units.title: A rejected commit goes back to its author
units.feedback:
REQUIRED

1. The fix-round agent can go around the gate, and build_commit would accept the result without noticing (src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py, the `commit` closure in `build_commit`). The fix agent is `run_claude`, which has `Bash(git *)` (ALLOWED, wiring.py:72). DISALLOWED and hooks/policy.py do not block `git commit --no-verify`, `git commit -n`, `SKIP=... git commit` or `git -c core.hooksPath=... commit`. The only thing stopping it is a sentence in COMMIT_FIX_PROMPT, and the fix round is exactly when an agent is most tempted to take that shortcut. If the agent commits on its own, the next `attempt()` finds nothing staged and returns None, so `commit` returns 0. For the `feat:` step, stack_runner counts `branch_commits`, so the bypassed commit goes on to review and push. That breaks the spec requirement 'The gate is never bypassed … under any circumstance'. Fix: in `build_commit`, read `git rev-parse HEAD` before each `fixer(...)` call and again after it. If HEAD moved, raise CommitRejected with a message saying the fix round committed on its own, instead of treating it as nothing staged. Add a test in tests/pipeline/test_commit_gate.py: a LINTER gate, and an Agent whose `edit` runs `git commit -q --no-verify -am x` (or `git add -A && git commit -n -m x`) in cwd. Assert that CommitRejected is raised and does not return 0. (Also denying `--no-verify`/`-n` in the policy hook is a reasonable extra, but the HEAD check is the one that catches every form, including SKIP and core.hooksPath.)

2. The bound is not actually tested (test_a_gate_that_never_accepts_fails_after_a_bounded_number_of_rounds). Task 1.3 says 'fails the unit after the fixed number of attempts', but the test asserts `1 <= len(agent.prompts) <= 10`, so raising COMMIT_FIX_ROUNDS to 9 would still pass. Import COMMIT_FIX_ROUNDS and assert `len(agent.prompts) == COMMIT_FIX_ROUNDS`. Also wrap the runner with the existing `Recorded` helper and assert that the number of `git commit` invocations is exactly `2 + COMMIT_FIX_ROUNDS` (the first try, the plain retry, then one per fix round). Assert every prompt contains LINT_OUTPUT, since each round must carry that round's gate output.

OPTIONAL

- `build_runner` passes `fix=run_claude` (the implement model) for every commit, including the rework commits at stack_runner.py:540/788 and the restack `adapt:` commit. The spec says the output goes to 'the agent that wrote the work'. The tool policy is the same, but the model is not. Either pass the rework runner for the rework commits, or say in the docstring and docs that the implement agent fixes every gate rejection.
- Fix rounds are Opus calls that skip `may_start` (the usage guard). There are at most 2 per commit, and a unit can make several commits. Consider checking `may_start` before each fix round, or at least note that the guard does not cover them.
- No test shows that build_runner wires the fix round to the same run_claude object (same allowed tools and hook settings) as the build run. A small test in tests/pipeline/test_wiring.py would stop a later refactor from quietly handing it a differently scoped runner.
- The `for fixer in [None, *([fix] * COMMIT_FIX_ROUNDS if fix else [])]` loop is clever enough to slow a reader down. An explicit plain retry followed by `for _ in range(COMMIT_FIX_ROUNDS if fix else 0)` would read more directly.

units.title: A branch that cannot be merged is sent back
units.feedback:
Checked against the predecessor as it is now (github-native-stacks/1, 6a1a10b, already on main). The conflict in cli/pipeline.py was resolved correctly: poll_all still keys each repo's snapshot by the abk.yaml repo name, now through state_path(inst.state_dir, repo), and cmd_status reads it by unit.repo, so both sides name the same file. None of the unit's tests asserts behaviour the predecessor removed or reshaped, and none duplicates its coverage. Each of tasks 1.1–1.4 has a test: test_github (recorded gh --json shape with MERGEABLE/CONFLICTING/UNKNOWN), the poller transition, undetermined and first-sight tests, and the status test driven through a real Poller. The four affected test files pass (215 passed). One required change, in the feedback text the rework is handed.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/events.py:676 — The conflict feedback tells the rework agent to "rebase onto it and resolve the conflict", but by the time REWORK_PROMPT runs, StackRunner has already restacked the branch onto its base (stack_runner.py:920-958: restack_onto, or _adapt if the restack conflicted). The instruction is false by then, and it asks the agent for a history rewrite the runner owns.
  Consequence: A unit reworked for a conflict reaches the rework step with a branch already moved onto the current base. It is then told to rebase. hooks/policy.py does not block git rebase, so the agent may rebase again itself, onto a base it picks, outside the restack/adapt bookkeeping (old_base, predecessor note, test accounting). Or it spends a rework run on a no-op and posts a reply on the PR claiming a rebase it did not do. docs/architecture.md:297 says the opposite: 'the restack at the start of the run does the rebase'.
  Done when: The CONFLICT_REASON branch of _requeue produces feedback stating the fact, not an instruction to rebase. For example: '<CONFLICT_REASON>: the branch has been moved onto its current base at the start of this run; check that the resolution kept this unit's behaviour and its tests pass, and do not rebase or reset the branch yourself.' test_a_conflict_is_reworked_as_a_conflict_not_the_old_review keeps its assertions and also asserts that the feedback does not contain 'rebase onto'.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/pr_poller.py:198 — The last definite answer is carried across the pipeline's own rework push. If the reworked branch still conflicts, for example because the trunk moved again during the rework, it goes False → (undetermined, kept False) → False. That is never a transition, so the unit is not sent back a second time.
  Consequence: A conflicted unit whose rework did not leave it mergeable stays in_review. Only the status mark shows it, and nothing reworks it again. The spec's 'still unmergeable → nothing further' does not address a new head in between, so this is a gap rather than a deviation.
  Done when: Optional, best taken with fresh-base-before-push: record the head sha in the snapshot, and treat a conflict on a different head sha than the one last dispatched as a new transition.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/forges/azure_devops.py:621 — _view never sets mergeable, so on Azure DevOps a conflict is never dispatched and never marked in status. Azure's mergeStatus ('conflicts' / 'succeeded' / 'queued' / 'notSet') maps directly to it.
  Consequence: An Azure-hosted installation gets none of this change's behaviour. That is safe (None dispatches nothing) but not stated anywhere.
  Done when: Map mergeStatus 'conflicts' → False, 'succeeded' → True and everything else → None in _view, with a test over a recorded pull request body. Or list it in the _view comment beside conversation and failing_checks as not yet read.

units.title: Replay a conflict resolution, and confirm it
units.feedback:
Round 2 check. R1 is done. `_replayed_files` now works from positive evidence: the `Resolved '<path>' using previous resolution.` lines in the rebase output. The binary-conflict test reproduces the case and passes, and the modify/delete test is kept. R2 is done: every marked file that was replayed is forgotten before the single abort, and a test covers two rejected replays. The optional docs sentence is in. I ran the module's 11 tests and they pass, including under a de_DE locale.

REQUIRED

1. `_UNTRANSLATED_ENV` takes a copy of `os.environ` when the module is imported, so the one git call that matters runs with a stale environment (src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/restack.py:57, used at the `rebase --onto` call in `move_branch_onto`). This rework introduced it, which is why it wasn't visible before. Two effects:
- Production: any environment change made after `restack` is imported never reaches the rebase. That includes HOME, GIT_* and PATH changes a long-running daemon or a later settings load might make. It is also the only git call in the module that behaves this way; every other call inherits the live environment.
- Tests: the autouse `isolated_git_config` fixture from round 1 item 4 sets GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM with monkeypatch at test time. That is after import, so the `rebase` call, the one that actually records and replays through rerere, still reads the developer's real global and system git config. That undoes item 4's isolation for exactly the call it was meant to isolate. `rerere forget` and the other calls do see the fixture's environment, so within one test they can read different configs.

Fix: build the environment at call time. Replace the module constant with a function such as `def _untranslated_env() -> dict[str, str]: return {**os.environ, "LC_ALL": "C", "LANGUAGE": "C"}` and pass `env=_untranslated_env()` at the rebase call. Keep the comment explaining why. The `{**os.environ, ...}` pass-through already appears in shell.py, verify.py and az.py, so this pattern is fine under the conventions.

Test: in tests/pipeline/test_restack_rerere.py, after import, `monkeypatch.setenv("GIT_COMMITTER_NAME", "restack-env-probe")` (plus GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL). Run a `move_branch_onto` that rebases cleanly, then assert that `git log -1 --format=%cn <branch>` equals `restack-env-probe`. That test fails against the current constant and passes once the environment is built per call.

OPTIONAL
- Nothing checks that the rebase really runs with LC_ALL=C. A test under a translated locale only proves something if that locale's git translations are installed, and passing under de_DE here proves nothing either way. A cheap guard: wrap `restack._shell_git` (or whatever `git` delegates to) in a recording spy, and assert that the `rebase` call's `env` has `LC_ALL == "C"`.

units.title: The planner joins small related sequential work
units.feedback:
The full suite passes (1952 passed) and the join rules, the store write and the `Separate:` parsing match the design. Three things need fixing before approval, and they share a cause: a carried group can be lost or mis-built when something outside `plan_all` reads a unit that a join has changed. The three cases are a build that started before a join was written, a re-plan of a change whose groups a started unit carries, and a re-plan of the carrying unit's own change.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:1055 — `build_unit` re-reads only the unit's state under the branch lock. It then builds the `unit` it was handed before the lock, so it can build a unit whose members a join has changed since, or one a join has removed.
  Consequence: Ticks overlap: the comment at lines 1050-1054 says so, and `reclaim_stale` exists because of it. Tick A takes `base/1` from its ready list (members `base:1`). Tick B's `plan_all` joins `feature` group 1 onto `base/1` under that branch lock and writes it. Tick A then takes the lock, sees `state == PLANNED`, and builds the stale `unit`, so `feature` group 1 is never built. The store now says `base/1` carries it, so when `base/1` merges, `_mark` ticks `feature` group 1 and `is_ready_to_archive('feature', ...)` is true. The change is archived with that work missing. When instead the unit taken in a join is in tick A's ready list, `store.get(unit.id)` raises `KeyError`. The generic handler logs `failed, KeyError` and then fails again recording the state, so the log misreports a unit removed on purpose.
  Done when: Under the branch lock, re-read the whole unit (`fresh = store.get(unit.id)`) and use `fresh` for `base_of`, `RunLog`, `build_runner` and `runner.run`. A missing unit (`KeyError`) ends with `skipped, it was joined into another unit` and returns True without touching the store. Add tests that call `build_unit` with a `Unit` captured before `store.join` was applied. One asserts the runner receives members that include the joined change's groups. The other asserts that a unit removed by a join is skipped and nothing is recorded as failed.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/planner.py:459 — `_in_flight_line` names the groups a unit builds (`builds`) only for unstarted units. Once a unit carrying another change's groups has started, the planner has no way to tell that those groups are taken.
  Consequence: `base/1` carries `feature` group 1 and is running or in review. `feature`'s tasks.md changes, so `feature` is planned again. The planner sees `- base/1 [app] spec/base/1 (in_review)` and `feature`'s tasks with group 1 unticked, and is told every group must be claimed by exactly one unit. So it claims group 1. `_check_groups` refuses that as already built, every attempt repeats it, and the change stops at `giving up until tasks.md changes`. The design requires that "the planner is shown the join as part of what is in flight". `test_planning_a_change_again_creates_no_unit_for_groups_another_unit_carries` covers only an unstarted carrier whose canned reply already leaves the group out.
  Done when: Put `builds` on every in-flight line, not only unstarted ones (keep the tier, estimate and dependency details unstarted-only if you like). Add a test where an `in_review` unit carries `feature` group 1 and `feature` is planned. It asserts the prompt line for that unit names `feature group(s) 1`.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_store.py:241 — When the carrying unit's own change is planned again and the plan drops that unit, `upsert` marks it `unplanned` along with its `joined` members. Nothing re-plans the carried changes, so their groups are orphaned.
  Consequence: `base/1` (planned) carries `feature` group 1. `base`'s tasks.md changes, and the new plan for `base` has no `base/1`, for example because the planner renumbers its units. `upsert(change='base')` demotes `base/1` to `unplanned`. `feature` is recorded as planned (`ok`), so it is never planned again. `link_needs` and `built` both skip `unplanned` units, so nothing builds `feature` group 1. Because `is_ready_to_archive` counts the `unplanned` unit through `carries`, `feature` never archives and nothing logs why. The planner cannot prevent this: when `base` is planned, its own planned units are left out of the context, so it is never shown that `base/1` carries anything.
  Done when: Constraint: an `unplanned` unit must never be the only holder of another change's groups. One fix: in `plan_all`, after `upsert`, for each unit just demoted that had `joined` members, remove those changes' records from `planned.json` so they are planned again next round, and log it. Add a test: store `base/1` carrying `feature:1`, plan `base` with a reply that omits `base/1`, and assert that `feature` is no longer recorded as planned, so the next `plan_all` asks the planner for it.

Optional:
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_store.py:210 — When the carrying unit's change is planned again, `upsert` keeps the unit's `joined` members but takes `estimated_lines` from the new plan, which estimates only the unit's own groups.
  Consequence: `base/1` at 100 lines takes 300 lines of `feature` and is recorded at 400. After `base` is planned again it reads 100 again, so a later join is checked against 100 + x instead of 400 + x and can pass the ceiling.
  Done when: When `joined` is carried over, keep the existing estimate. Either keep `existing.estimated_lines` or add the old surplus (`existing.estimated_lines` minus what the plan previously gave the unit's own groups) to the new estimate.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/units.py:404 — The unit-1 follow-up on `later_groups_by_change` is still open, and this change makes it reachable. A chain of joins can produce members `[a:1, b:1, a:3]`.
  Consequence: Each member is checked against its own highest group, so the `a:1` member reports `a` group 2 as later work even when group 2 sits before `a:3`, or has already merged. The boundary note then misleads the build.
  Done when: Compute each change's highest group once, across every member of that change, as the follow-up describes.
- [1.6] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/planner.py:516 — `plan_round` returns the units and passes the joins back by appending to a `joins` list the caller supplies.
  Consequence: This is a hidden output parameter: a caller that forgets to pass the list silently drops validated joins.
  Done when: Return the `Plan` (units and joins) from `plan_round`. Keep `parse_graph`'s list return for its existing callers.
- [1.7] tests/pipeline/test_unit_joins.py:299 — The refusal tests assert only that `"join"` appears in the output, not which rule refused.
  Consequence: Each variation does fail today if its rule is removed. But a variation that one day trips a different rule, such as `no such unit`, would still pass without exercising the rule it is named for.
  Done when: Give each `NEW_GROUP_REFUSED`/`CHAIN_REFUSED` entry the substring its `JoinRefused` message should contain, and assert that substring.

units.title: The switch: the graph is the only engine
units.feedback:
The graph now drives every tick, and the ported build, review, await and usage scenarios look sound. Four things block approval. (1) Converting units in flight gets two classic positions wrong. (2) The scheduler still reads `resume_from`, but nothing writes it any more. (3) Task 5.4 is only partly done: `resume_from` writers and the in-run `StoredUnit` fields remain while the docs say they are gone. (4) Many classic scenario tests of behaviour this change keeps were deleted and never ported. Task 5.5 is also incomplete: the changelog, configuration, cli and skill docs still describe ABK_ENGINE, reclaim_stale and the classic engine as current. Note: git commands needed approval in this environment, so the review reads the branch's files directly and compares deleted tests against the main checkout at /home/<redacted>/agent-build-kit.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/graph/convert.py:40 — A classic `verify` resume step is seeded `as_node=Node.TIER2`, so `after_tier2` routes straight to `verify_base` and a tier 2 unit never runs tier 2.
  Consequence: The classic runner recorded VERIFY before tier 2 ran (`checkpoint(VERIFY)` comes before `run_tier2` in the old `UnitRunner.run`; resuming at VERIFY ran tier 2 and then the base check). Take a tier 2 unit killed during its tier 2 run, or stopped at that checkpoint (store has `resume_from='verify'`, `tier='tier2'`). It converts, then `verify_base` → `push` → `open_pr`. Its branch is pushed and opened for review without tier 2 ever passing.
  Done when: VERIFY seeds a position whose next node is `tier2` for a tier 2 unit and `verify_base` otherwise. For example, `Node.PREPARE` with `base_commits=1, head_approved=True, tier2=tier2` lets `after_prepare` choose. A test in tests/graph/test_convert_in_flight.py stores a tier 2 unit at `verify` with its approval recorded, converts it, ticks, and asserts tier 2 ran before the push. Also add `("implement", Node.IMPLEMENT)` to the parametrized step list: it is one of the classic resume steps task 5.1 names and is not covered.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/graph/convert.py:49 — A `running` unit the classic engine left with no resume step and no feedback gets no thread. `reclaim_stale`'s requeue is gone, so nothing ever moves it again.
  Consequence: A classic run killed before its first `record_step` leaves state `running` with `resume_from=''`. Examples: during worktree setup, the fetch, or a restack whose conflict resolver is running. `_seed` returns None, so no thread is made. `resumable_units` needs a thread, `ready_units` only picks `planned`, and `reclaim_stale` was removed. The unit stays `running` forever, holds a place in `max_units_in_progress`, and blocks everything that depends on it.
  Done when: `_seed` gives any stored `running` unit without a thread a position: the step it names if it has one, otherwise `(None, {})` so it starts at `prepare`. The next tick then resumes it through `resumable_units`. A test (tests/graph/test_switch_tick.py style, through `cmd_tick`) stores a unit `running` with a branch, no `resume_from` and no feedback, runs one tick, and asserts the unit reaches `in_review` with its thread in `await_review`.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/units.py:457 — `in_progress`, `in_progress_label` and `_start_rank` recognise a paused build by `resume_from`, which no graph run writes, so a unit held before a step no longer counts as started.
  Consequence: `BuildPath.hold(PLANNED, ...)` (nodes.py:177 and 217: upstream went back, base moved, rebased twice) records `planned` with no PR and no `resume_from`, though the unit has a branch, commits and a thread. Under the classic engine the same hold wrote `resume_from=next_step`. Now `in_progress` is False, so the unit stops counting toward `limits.max_units_in_progress` and new units start past the limit. `_start_rank` also ranks it with brand-new units instead of ahead of them, against the order docs/architecture.md:137-139 describes. tests/pipeline/test_units_in_progress.py still passes only because it sets `resume_from` by hand, which no run does now.
  Done when: A planned or unplanned unit that a run has started counts as in progress and ranks 1, judged from something the graph does write. For example, a recorded `branch` (`prepare` sets it) or `pushed`/`approved`; or have the scheduler ask whether the unit has a thread. Fix the docstrings and docs/architecture.md:131-132 to match. A test drives a unit through the graph until it is held before a step, then asserts `in_progress(stored)` is True and that `ready_units` ranks it before a never-started unit. The test must not set `resume_from` itself.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/events.py:991 — Task 5.4 removes `resume_from`, but code still writes it and passes it through `set_state`. The comment on the field says nothing writes it.
  Consequence: `build_restack` writes `resume_from="rework_review"` at events.py:991 and :1063. The `resume_from=` keyword on `UnitStore.set_state` is still passed at nodes.py:199, 699 and 854, events.py:847, and cli/pipeline.py:1579 and 1584. `cmd_requeue` (cli/pipeline.py:1588-1589) still prints "resuming before <step>". unit_store.py:54-56 says "nothing in a run writes it", which is false. Because `convert_in_flight` runs on every tick, a restacked child without a thread is silently routed by the classic step through the converter, a coupling nobody will expect. That leaves the classic resume bookkeeping in place, against what task 5.4 and docs/unit-graph.md:482-484 say.
  Done when: Drop the `resume_from` parameter from `set_state`/`_record_state` and every call that passes it. Remove both writes in `build_restack`: the child goes `planned` and its run's `prepare` decides from the branch, as for any other unit. Drop the "resuming before" text in `cmd_requeue`. If the field stays at all, it is read only by `graph.convert`, which clears it once it has seeded the unit's thread. Fix the unit_store.py comment and the units.py module docstring (line 13) to match. Existing restack tests that assert `resume_from == 'rework_review'` change to assert the planned state and note.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_store.py:58 — `StoredUnit` keeps every in-run field: `approved`, `deferred`, `pending_replies`, `person_comments`, `predecessor_note` and `review_rounds`. Task 5.4 and the docs say they leave it.
  Consequence: Task 5.4 says to remove `StoredUnit`'s in-run fields. docs/unit-graph.md:94, 104-105 and 482-484 say in-run progress (review rounds, the approved commit, deferred follow-ups, pending replies, the predecessor note) leaves units.json for the checkpoint. The code keeps all of them in the store, and the nodes read and write them there. The document says something the code does not do.
  Done when: Move the in-run fields into `UnitRun` as task 5.4 asks. A field may stay in the store only where something outside a run must read or write it: `approved` for `build_restack` and the push gate, and `predecessor_note`, which `build_restack` writes. Where a field stays, docs/unit-graph.md (Who holds what, State, Moving the units in flight) names it and the reason, and the pull request says so. Once a field moves, `upsert` stops carrying it over.
- [1.6] tests/pipeline/test_review_verdicts.py:1 — Classic scenario tests of behaviour this change keeps were deleted and never ported to the graph, so that behaviour now has no test.
  Consequence: Task 5.4 removes only the tests of removed code; the design says the ported tests are what prove nothing was lost. The code behind these deleted tests still exists: `weigh_review`, `_round_budget_note`, follow-up recording, `mark_tasks`, `scope` and the boundary notes. Deleted from test_review_verdicts.py: every round is told its number and the final round says it is final; follow-ups are recorded against the change, survive a later push without duplicating, and are kept by a unit that stops between approval and push; a may-not-wait follow-up blocks approval and is never approved on the last round; spent rounds keep the follow-ups in the PR body; a multi-line follow-up stays one item. Deleted from test_joined_units.py: the build and review prompts name every carried change; the scope note treats carried groups as the unit's own; each change's groups are ticked in its own tasks.md; a failed joined unit unticks every change. Deleted from test_stack_runner.py with no graph counterpart (no match in tests/graph): the build, review and rework prompts name the later-unit boundary, and none is given when there is no later unit; the tests prompt asks for failing tests and no logic; a later review sees what earlier rounds asked and what was done; the default is three fix rounds, and the fix budget starts again each review round; an empty implement step against an exhausted window is a pause, not a failure, and is not a pause when usage is healthy; tasks are ticked only once through the loop, and a failed unit leaves them unticked; work is built on the remote trunk while the PR targets main; a tier 1 unit does not touch the local stack. A regression in any of these now passes the suite.
  Done when: Each listed behaviour has a test against the graph engine (tests/graph/, with `tests.graph_driver`/`runner_fakes` as test_remaining_paths.py does) or against the retained callable directly, asserting what the deleted test asserted. Then check every other test deleted from test_stack_runner.py, test_stack_runner_fresh_base.py, test_review_verdicts.py and test_joined_units.py the same way. Each one either tested removed resume bookkeeping (say which in the PR) or has a ported counterpart.
- [1.7] CHANGELOG.md:38 — The changelog has no entry for the switch, and two Unreleased entries describe the removed seam as current.
  Consequence: Task 5.5 asks for the changelog. Lines 38-53 say the graph behaviour exists only "behind `ABK_ENGINE=graph`" and that `ABK_ENGINE` (`classic` by default) picks the engine. Both are false on this branch. A reader upgrading learns nothing of: the first tick converting units in flight, `reclaim_stale`'s requeue and its `wip:` commit of a killed run's leftovers being gone, or a usage pause now leaving the unit `running` rather than `planned`.
  Done when: Rewrite those Unreleased entries to say the graph is the only engine and that `ABK_ENGINE` is gone (it was never released, so no deprecation window). Say that units in flight are moved onto threads on the first tick, and that a killed run is resumed rather than reclaimed, with no `wip:` commit of its leftovers. Say that a usage pause keeps the unit `running`, interrupted, until a tick the guard allows.
- [1.8] docs/unit-graph.md:184 — docs/unit-graph.md and the other docs still describe the classic engine, `reclaim_stale`, `checkpoint()` and `ABK_ENGINE` as current.
  Consequence: Task 5.5 asks for these to match what was built. False sentences: unit-graph.md:184 (`stack_runner.py`'s docstrings are the reference until this replaces them); :331, :355, :364 and :371 ("as the classic engine does" / "the classic handler" for what is now just the event handler's own behaviour); :333 ("on the graph engine"); :396 ("as `reclaim_stale` does now"); :398-401 (`reclaim_stale` leaves a running unit alone; it no longer exists); :420 ("as `checkpoint()` does now"); :292 ("the in-run fields `StoredUnit` carries today"); :474 ("happens once", while `convert_in_flight` runs every tick). docs/configuration.md:312 still documents `ABK_ENGINE`. docs/cli.md:31 and :46 say the tick reclaims units. docs/agent-runtimes.md:235, runtimes/base.py:121 and usage_guard.py:570 say `reclaim_stale` recovers an interrupted run. The abk-pipeline skill (SKILL.md:58) says a usage-paused unit is `planned` with a `paused before <step>` note; it is now `running` in an interrupt. docs/architecture.md:340-343 says the same.
  Done when: Each listed sentence describes the graph as built: the event handlers' behaviour named directly, a killed run resumed by the tick, a usage pause leaving the unit `running`, and conversion running on every tick but seeding only units with no thread. The `ABK_ENGINE` row is removed from configuration.md. Afterwards, a grep of docs/ and src/**/*.md for `reclaim_stale`, `ABK_ENGINE`, `classic engine` and `checkpoint()` finds only historical mentions, such as the Why section.

Optional:
- [1.9] src/agent_build_kit/graph/convert.py:37 — A converted unit is positioned after `prepare`, so its first run skips the fetch, the restack onto a moved base, the `running` state and the recorded base tip.
  Consequence: A unit converted at `review`, `tests`, `implement` or with waiting feedback runs that node with its store still `planned` and `start` unset. A base that moved before the switch is caught only at `verify_base`, after a review spent on the unmoved branch.
  Done when: Optional: position converted units so `prepare` runs first, with the routing hint in state that `after_prepare` honours; or accept the gap and say so in Moving the units in flight.
- [1.10] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/diagram.py:176 — The graph page's `paused-usage` class depends on a `paused before` store note, which the graph never writes.
  Consequence: A unit interrupted for usage is drawn `running`, and the paused-usage legend entry (and vocabulary.py:123) can no longer appear.

units.title: A dependency that must merge first: parse the merged qualifier, record merge_before, gate readiness, draw it
units.feedback:
The grammar, the store field, the `waiting_on` branch and the diagram edge are all in place, and the pipeline suite passes (1308 tests). Three things block approval: a readiness hole when the merge-gated dependency is `satisfied`, a `merge_before` in `link_needs` that can be lost within a tick and never shrinks, and task 1.6 (the docs), which was not done.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/units.py:366 — `waiting_on` checks `merge_before` against the ids that come out of `through_satisfied`, not against the unit's own dependencies. A merge-gated dependency in state `satisfied` is replaced by its own same-repo predecessor before the check runs, so the check is skipped and the ordinary same-repo rule applies to that predecessor.
  Consequence: I reproduced this with the graph [c/0 in_review, c/1 satisfied depends_on=(c/0,), d/1 depends_on=(c/1,) merge_before=(c/1,)], all in one repo. `waiting_on(d/1)` returns [], d/1 is in `ready_units`, and `base_of(d/1)` is `spec/c/0`. So d/1 starts stacked on an open PR. The spec allows it to start only once c/1 is 'satisfied with its work landed', which here needs c/0 merged. This is exactly the moving target the change exists to prevent.
  Done when: Apply the merge rule to each id in `unit.merge_before` before any satisfied look-through: it waits unless the dependency is MERGED, or SATISFIED and `satisfied_landed`. Run `through_satisfied` and the same-repo/cross-repo rules only on the remaining dependencies, so a gated id is never expanded. Add a test in tests/pipeline/test_units.py with the graph above that asserts `waiting_on(d/1)` is non-empty and d/1 is not in `ready_units`. Add a companion case with c/0 merged that asserts d/1 is ready with base `main`.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:746 — `link_needs` computes `held` per group from the `store.all()` snapshot taken before the loop, and it only ever adds. Two problems follow. (a) When one unit carries two groups that each have a `merged` Needs:, the second group's `set_merge_before` overwrites the first group's entry for that tick. (b) Removing `merged` from a Needs: line never clears the entry. `specification()` strips Needs: lines from the plan hash, so that edit never triggers a re-plan either.
  Consequence: (a) Take unit feature/5 carrying groups 5 and 6, where group 5 has `Needs: x group 1 merged` and group 6 has `Needs: y group 2 merged`. After the first tick, merge_before is (y/…,) only, and in that same tick the scheduler may start feature/5 stacked on x's in-review branch. (b) An author who drops `merged` to release a held unit finds it still held, and the only fix is editing units.json by hand. That contradicts design.md: 'Re-planning recomputes it from tasks.md like the rest of a unit's dependencies.'
  Done when: Build the gated set per unit across every change and group it carries, then write it once: `merge_before = the gated ids, in order, that are also in the unit's depends_on`, computed fresh from tasks.md rather than unioned with the stored value. merge_before comes only from `Needs: … merged`, so it can be authoritative. Extend the test in tests/pipeline/test_cli_pipeline.py to cover two things. First, a unit with groups 5 and 6, each carrying a `merged` Needs:, ends with both ids after a single `link_needs`. Second, after the `merged` word is deleted from tasks.md, another `link_needs` leaves merge_before == ().
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/skills/abk-authoring/SKILL.md:83 — Task 1.6 is not done. The abk-authoring skill, docs/architecture.md (around line 54) and docs/unit-graph.md's table of what stays outside the graph never mention the `merged` qualifier.
  Consequence: tasks.md 1.6 requires this documentation. Without it, the skill authors read to choose `Needs:` lines describes only `Needs: <other-change> group <n> — why`, so nobody learns the qualifier exists. docs/unit-graph.md also still omits the rule, which design.md says it should carry so that the unit-graph change does not have to.
  Done when: In SKILL.md's `Needs:` section, add the form `Needs: <other-change> group <n> merged — why`. Say what it does: the dependent waits for the merge, or for a satisfied dependency's work to land, even in the same repo, and then starts on the trunk. Say when to use it (a dependency still reshaping what this group builds on), and that `abk tags` rejects it on the change's own group. Add the same to the `Needs:` bullet in docs/architecture.md. Add a row naming merge-gated dependencies (`merge_before`, applied by `waiting_on`/`ready_units`) to docs/unit-graph.md's table of what stays outside the graph.
- [1.4] tests/pipeline/test_units.py:441 — Task 1.2 asks for a test that 'a stored unit without `merge_before` loads unchanged'. None exists. No test reads a units.json record written before this field.
  Consequence: A later change could make `merge_before` required, or rename it, and every existing installation's units.json would stop loading, with nothing in the suite failing.
  Done when: In the unit_store tests (tests/pipeline/), write a units.json record without a `merge_before` key into a UnitStore file and load it through `UnitStore.get`/`all`. Assert that it loads, that `merge_before == ()`, and that its other fields are what was written.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/work_graph.py:366 — `group_needs` is a second copy of `cross_change_needs`: the same loop over the same lines with the same regex, differing only in the item type. The code now has two parsers for one grammar, and the joins caller (cli/pipeline.py:831) still uses the old one.
  Consequence: A future change to how Needs: lines are read, such as a new qualifier or a heading rule, has to be made in both places. If only one is updated, the joins context and `link_needs` will disagree about the same tasks.md.
  Done when: Keep `group_needs` as the single parser. Either delete `cross_change_needs` and have the joins caller build `(n.change, n.group)` from `group_needs`, or make `cross_change_needs` a one-line projection of `group_needs`. Update tests/pipeline/test_work_graph.py to match.

Optional:
- [1.6] tests/pipeline/test_units.py:474 — The test name `test_a_merge_gated_dependency_is_waited_on_even_when_it_has_no_review_branch_yet` does not describe the test. Both dependencies are `in_review`, and what it actually checks is that only the gated one holds the dependent.
  Consequence: A reader looking for the 'no review branch yet' case will think it is covered when it is not.
  Done when: Rename it, for example `test_only_the_merge_gated_dependency_holds_the_dependent`.
- [1.7] tests/pipeline/test_work_graph.py:242 — The new tests import `Need` and `group_needs` inside the function bodies instead of at module top with the other work_graph imports.
  Consequence: This does not match the rest of the file's imports.
  Done when: Move the imports to the module's import block.
- [1.8] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/diagram.py:109 — The comment 'Dashed across repos: …' now sits above the `merge_before` branch, which is not about dashes.
  Consequence: It misleads the next reader about which branch the comment explains.
  Done when: Move the comment onto the `else` branch, or add one line explaining the thick `merged` edge.

units.title: Run the suite in parallel
units.feedback:
The poe/pyproject part (tasks 1.1–1.3) is correct. I ran `uv run poe test` once: 2322 passed in 25.37s in the parallel pass, and the serial pass deselected everything, exited 5 and was tolerated. Two task items in this unit's group are not done at all: 1.6 (the profile and CI use the same command) and 1.7 (AGENTS.md, docs and changelog). The branch has no evidence for 1.4/1.5, the ten repeated parallel runs. The one run I did was clean and no test needed marking `serial`, so I am not blocking on that. Say in the PR body how many repeated runs passed.

Required:
- [1.1] .github/workflows/ci.yml:38 — CI still runs the suite serially with `uv run --group dev pytest`. Task 1.6 says CI must use the same command as `poe test`.
  Consequence: CI runs a different command from the one developers and the change specify. It never runs the `serial` pass as its own pass, and it runs a serial-marked test inside the same single process as the rest. It also does not get the speed-up the proposal is for. Task 1.6 stays unmet.
  Done when: Change the `test` job's step to `uv run --group dev poe test`, so CI runs exactly the poe sequence: the parallel pass, then the serial pass. Add an assertion to tests/test_parallel_suite.py that loads `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and checks that the test job's run line invokes `poe test`. Without that test, the two commands can drift apart again.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/profiles/python_uv.py:143 — Task 1.6 says the python profile's test command uses the same command, but `_whole_repo_tests` still returns `uv run pytest -q`. The proposal says the profile 'gains the workers flag, so what a unit's tier 1 runs is what a developer runs'.
  Consequence: The pipeline's tier 1 for this repo, and for any repo with xdist, runs the suite in one process. That is the repeated cost the proposal set out to remove. The profile's tier 1 also runs `serial`-marked tests in the same command as everything else, so they are not separated the way the spec requires. Task 1.6 is unmet. The documented row in docs/toolchain-profiles.md:67 describes this command too.
  Done when: Do this test-first in tests/profiles/. When the repo declares `pytest-xdist` (the profile already parses pyproject via `_pyproject`/`_DEP_NAME`, including dependency-groups), `_whole_repo_tests` returns two commands mirroring `poe test`. The first is `uv run pytest -n auto --maxprocesses=8 -m 'not serial' -q`. The second is `uv run pytest -m serial -q`, and for it NO_TESTS_COLLECTED (5) must count as success, the same way tier2 treats it. A repo that does not declare xdist keeps exactly `uv run pytest -q`: adding `-n` unconditionally would fail with 'unrecognized arguments: -n' in every installation repo without the plugin. Tests assert both branches. Apply the same rule to the workspace member and root-tests commands, or state in the design why they are excluded. Update docs/toolchain-profiles.md lines 67–68 to match.
- [1.3] AGENTS.md:140 — Task 1.7 (update AGENTS.md's Running section, docs/ and the changelog) is not done.
  Consequence: AGENTS.md still describes `poe test` only as 'the suite'. It does not say that the suite now runs across workers, that a single `pytest <file>` stays single-process, or that `serial` marks a test that must run alone. The CHANGELOG has no entry for the new dev dependency `pytest-xdist` or for the new `serial` marker, while the Unreleased section records new dependencies elsewhere. docs/agent-runtimes.md:612 says 'Two markers keep slow tests out of the default suite' and does not mention the third marker, `serial`.
  Done when: AGENTS.md's Running comment for `poe test` says it runs in parallel workers (capped at 8) followed by a serial pass of tests marked `serial`. The Conventions test bullet says to mark a test `serial` when it cannot share a process, and that `pytest <file>` runs without workers. docs/agent-runtimes.md's marker section adds `serial`. CHANGELOG Unreleased gains an entry: `poe test` and CI run the suite with pytest-xdist (new dev dependency), the `serial` marker, and the profile's command change.

Optional:
- [1.4] tests/test_parallel_suite.py:52 — `has_workers_flag` treats any argument starting with `-n` as the workers flag. That includes unrelated long options such as `--n...` lookalikes or `-norecursedirs`-style strings, and `--numprocesses` is matched by prefix only.
  Consequence: This is not triggered by today's commands. A future option beginning with `-n` would make the serial-pass tests treat a non-worker invocation as parallel.
  Done when: Match `-n`, `-n<digits|auto|logical>`, `--numprocesses` and `--numprocesses=...` exactly, for example `re.fu<redacted>atch(r"-n(\d+|auto|logical)?|--numprocesses(=.*)?", arg)`.

units.title: Re-run cancelled checks instead of reworking
units.feedback:
The core is right. Cancelled checks are split from failing ones on both hosts, the poller dispatches its own event, and the count per head commit is stored, survives a new process and loads older units. Three things block approval. Azure DevOps still names a cancelled build as a failure in a mixed-outcome rework's feedback. The handler re-runs checks on a held unit. The forge `rerun_checks` operations, the only code that actually talks to the host, have no test and ignore a refusal. I ran tests/forges, tests/pipeline/test_rerun_checks.py, tests/pipeline/test_pr_poller.py and the leak check: 268 passed.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/forges/azure_devops.py:710 — `failed_check_logs` still loops over `self._failing_evaluations(...)`, which includes evaluations whose build ended `canceled`. Only `_said_on` was moved to `_split_evaluations`.
  Consequence: A mixed outcome on Azure DevOps: build 41 `canceled` and build 42 `failed`. `pull.failing_checks` is ("lint build",), but the rework's feedback also lists "CI build - build policy rejected" with its build link. The agent is told a cancelled check failed and reworks for it. The spec says it 'SHALL NOT send a unit back for rework because of one', and design.md lists 'the text handed to a rework for a real failure' as unchanged.
  Done when: `failed_check_logs` takes the failing half of `self._split_evaluations(repo, pull.number, run=run)` instead of `_failing_evaluations`. Add a test in tests/forges/test_cancelled_checks.py (or the Azure forge tests): with builds {41: canceled, 42: failed}, `AZURE.failed_check_logs(...)` names "lint build" and buildId=42, and does not contain "CI build" or buildId=41.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/events.py:812 — `on_rerun_checks` never looks at the unit's state. It re-runs checks and spends the count on a held (or satisfied) unit. The poller makes this likely: in `_dispatch_changes` it dispatches `rerun_checks` before the hold-label check, so a poll that sees `agent-hold` added together with a cancelled check does both.
  Consequence: A unit a person has held with `agent-hold`, whose CI is then cancelled: the runner asks the host to re-run the person's CI, which writes to a PR the person has taken over. docs/architecture.md says of `hold`: 'unit `held`; nothing automatic touches it again'. For a satisfied unit it re-runs CI on a pull request that is closing.
  Done when: After `_find`, a unit in HELD or SATISFIED state gets one log line ('rerun #N: <id> is held, leaving the checks') and the handler returns True without calling `rerun` or `record_check_rerun`. Add tests in tests/pipeline/test_rerun_checks.py: a stored unit set to HELD gets no rerun call and its `check_reruns` stays 0. Do the same for SATISFIED.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/forges/github.py:415 — `rerun_checks` ignores the `gh run rerun` return code, and `on_rerun_checks` records the count before it asks. A refused re-run is silent and still counts.
  Consequence: Two concrete cases: the token has no `actions: write` permission, or the run is already re-running. `gh run rerun` exits non-zero. The log still says 're-run 1 of 2', nothing runs, and once the count is spent the PR sits with cancelled checks and a log claiming re-runs happened. Elsewhere in this forge a refusal raises (`pr_files`; `close_pr`/`add_label` per docs/code-forges.md).
  Done when: GitHub `rerun_checks` raises RuntimeError naming the run and stderr when `result.returncode` is non-zero, as `pr_files` does. Azure's `az.json_out` call keeps whatever refusal behaviour it already has. `on_rerun_checks` calls `rerun(pull)` before `store.record_check_rerun`. On RuntimeError it logs 'rerun #N: the host refused: …' and returns True without counting. A handler test passes a `rerun` that raises and asserts the count is unchanged and the refusal is logged.
- [1.4] tests/forges/test_cancelled_checks.py:1 — No test exercises `GitHubForge.rerun_checks` or `AzureDevOpsForge.rerun_checks`. Every re-run test goes through a fake `rerun` callable or the `StandInForge` no-op. Nothing pins the commands sent to the host, which run ids or evaluation ids are picked, or that failed checks are left out.
  Consequence: The pipeline tests would still pass if GitHub re-ran the run behind a FAILURE check, re-ran nothing because `detailsUrl` parsing broke, or dropped `--failed`. They would also pass if Azure queued the failed build's evaluation or sent the wrong `--evaluation-id`. Task 1.3 asks for a test that the handler 'asks the forge to re-run the cancelled runs'.
  Done when: Add a GitHub test that patches `gh_json`/`gh` at the CLI boundary. The `statusCheckRollup` is shaped like `check()`: a CANCELLED CheckRun with detailsUrl .../actions/runs/123/job/9, a second CANCELLED job in the same run 123, and a FAILURE at runs/456. Assert exactly one call, `gh run rerun 123 --repo example/app --failed`. Add an Azure test that drives `AZURE.rerun_checks(AZURE_REPO, pull, run=run)` with evaluations for builds 41 (canceled) and 42 (failed), each with its own `evaluationId`. Assert exactly one `repos pr policy queue --id 16 --evaluation-id <41's evaluationId>` was sent. Use the GitHub fixture slug `example/app` (the test file's GITHUB_REPO is currently account `o`, name `r`).

Optional:
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/forges/github.py:401 — `rerun_checks` copies the rollup fetch, filter and run-id extraction from `failed_check_logs` line for line. Only the conclusion set differs.
  Consequence: The two copies can drift. A fix to how runs are found (say, a StatusContext with no detailsUrl) would have to be made twice. Not a behaviour bug today.
  Done when: A private `_runs_with(slug, pr, conclusions) -> tuple[list[dict], list[str]]` returns the matching checks and their sorted run ids. Both methods call it.
- [1.6] src/agent_build_kit/forges/azure_devops.py:154 — Every poll now makes one `az pipelines runs show` call per rejected build evaluation per open PR, including builds that failed for good and were already reported.
  Consequence: On an installation with many open red PRs, this adds az calls on every tick. It does not change behaviour.
  Done when: Optional: skip the lookup for a buildId already known to have failed, or note the cost in the docstring.
- [1.7] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/events.py:339 — design.md says that once the bound is spent, 'the log and the pull request's status line say "checks keep being cancelled by the host"'. Only the log says it.
  Consequence: A person looking at the PR cannot see why the runner stopped. The spec itself requires only the log, so this does not block.
  Done when: Optional: surface it on the PR's status line, or drop the status-line sentence from design.md.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/telemetry_cmd.py:81 — push-dashboard is registered with needs_installation=False, so the planning repo's .env, which the docs and the abk-config skill say holds ABK_GRAFANA_URL/_TOKEN/_FOLDER, is never loaded.
  Consequence: settings.reload(<planning root>/.env) only runs when main() loads an installation (installation.py:161/199). With False, Settings() reads `.env` from the process cwd only. Put ABK_GRAFANA_URL and ABK_GRAFANA_TOKEN in the planning repo's .env, as abk-config/SKILL.md and docs/configuration.md tell you to, then run `abk --config <planning>/abk.yaml telemetry push-dashboard` (or ABK_CONFIG, or run it from a subdirectory or another directory). It prints 'set ABK_GRAFANA_URL and ABK_GRAFANA_TOKEN' and exits 2 even though both are set where the docs say they go.

Add a test in tests/cli/test_telemetry_push_dashboard.py: a tmp planning dir holds a fixture abk.yaml and a .env with ABK_GRAFANA_URL=<fake url> and ABK_GRAFANA_TOKEN. The env vars are unset and the cwd is elsewhere (monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path / 'other')). `main(['--config', str(abk_yaml), 'telemetry', 'push-dashboard'])` returns 0 and the fake Grafana holds the dashboard.
- [1.2] docs/configuration.md:320 — The two new ABK_GRAFANA_* rows are separated from the environment-variable table by a blank line, so they are not part of it.
  Consequence: A Markdown table ends at a blank line. The two rows that follow have no header or delimiter row, so they render as a paragraph of literal `| ... |` text instead of table rows. The documentation task 1.5 asked for comes out as garbled text.

units.title: Report, summary page and archive roll-up
units.feedback:
Both earlier required points are fixed in the code. `refresh_usage` now catches `Exception`. Every ledger read goes through `read_lines`, which decodes with `errors="replace"`. `append_record` and `roll_up_change` share `ledger_lock`, and the roll-up reads the ledger once inside that lock. The lock file `usage-ledger.jsonl.lock` is already covered by `runs/*.lock` in the gitignore template, and `spans.record_line` appends through `append_record`, so no ledger writer is left unlocked. One thing still needs changing: the new concurrency test would also pass if `roll_up_change` took no lock at all.

- The archive-race test must also show that `roll_up_change` waits for the ledger lock, for example by asserting that the roll-up thread is still alive, or the ledger unchanged, while the test holds the lock.

Required:
- [2.1] tests/pipeline/test_usage_report.py:595 — `test_a_line_appended_while_a_change_archives_is_not_lost` checks that `append_record` waits for the lock, but nothing checks that `roll_up_change` does. If you delete `with ledger_lock(ledger):` from `roll_up_change`, the test still passes. The roll-up thread then reads, rewrites and swaps the ledger at once, while the test still holds the lock. The append is still blocked. Once the lock is released it writes into the new file, so `sess-late` survives and every add-marker line is a summary.
  Consequence: A regression that drops the roll-up's lock, which is the fix for finding 1.2, passes the suite. The ledger would then lose lines again whenever an archive runs alongside a build's append.
  Done when: In the `with ledger_lock(ledger):` block, after the `appended.wait(0.3)` assertion, also assert that the roll-up has not run while the lock is held. Either assert `rolling.is_alive()`, or check that the ledger still holds add-marker detail lines: `{x['kind'] for x in ledger_lines(ledger) if x['unit'].startswith('add-marker')} != {'summary'}`. With that assertion, removing the lock from `roll_up_change` makes the test fail.

units.title: Roll the ledger into metrics and the dashboard
units.feedback:
One required problem, in the dashboard and docs. The new ledger figures are added to the same `abk.agent.tokens` counter the runtime wrapper already writes, so a query that does not filter on `source` now counts every call's tokens twice. Everything else matches the change: cost and tokens by kind come from the same record the ledger writes, measured and estimated figures are separate series, there is a node histogram and a wait histogram by bucket, and no unit id, change name or session reaches a metric attribute. Turning telemetry off exports nothing, the four panels are there, and the docs and changelog are written. The new tests pass locally: 10 passed.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/telemetry/dashboards/pipeline.json:61 — The existing panel 8, "Agent tokens by kind", runs `sum by (kind) (increase(abk_agent_tokens_total[...]))` with no filter on `source`. `export_call` now adds a second series for every agent call to that counter. `runtimes/traced.py:54` writes kinds input/output/cache and no source; the ledger writes input/output/cache_read/cache_creation with a source. So the same call's tokens are summed twice.
  Consequence: Take one implement call with input=100, output=50, cache_read=1000 and cache_creation=200. Panel 8 shows input 200, output 100, cache 1200, plus separate cache_read 1000 and cache_creation 200. Input and output are doubled, and the cache tokens appear twice under different kinds. The design says the ledger is "one source and no second accounting", and this panel now does the second accounting. The new test only checks that queried metrics exist, so it cannot catch this.
  Done when: Make sure no dashboard query sums both series of `abk_agent_tokens_total`. The smallest fix is to restrict panel 8 to the runtime's series with `abk_agent_tokens_total{source=""}`; alternatively drop panel 8 in favour of the new panel 12. Add a test to `tests/test_dashboard_metrics.py`: every dashboard expression that queries `abk_agent_tokens_total` has a `source` matcher (`source=""` or `source!=""`) or groups `by` source. It should fail on the current panel 8.
- [1.2] docs/architecture.md:680 — The metrics table now lists `abk.agent.tokens` twice: line 675 with kinds input, output, cache, and line 680 with cache_read and cache_creation. Nothing says that summing the counter without a `source` filter counts each call twice.
  Consequence: Two rows for one instrument with different kind sets tell a reader they can query it freely. Anyone writing a query or alert on `abk_agent_tokens_total` without a `source` filter gets doubled tokens, the same bug as panel 8.
  Done when: Merge the two rows into one `abk.agent.tokens` row. It should say there are two series: the runtime's (role, model, kind input/output/cache, no source) and the ledger's (repo, tier, node, role, model, source, kind input/output/cache_read/cache_creation). It should also say that a query must select one of them by `source`.

Optional:
- [1.3] tests/pipeline/test_usage_metrics.py:98 — Nothing tests that a span with a `command` adds nothing, which is what the `elif not span.command` branch in `spans.export_span` is for.
  Consequence: If that branch were dropped, each tier 1 command's time would be counted again inside its node's time in `abk.node.duration`, and the tests would still pass.
  Done when: Add a test: `record_span` with `command="test"` (no `waited`) records no `abk.node.duration` or `abk.wait.duration` point.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_ledger.py:104 — A ledger record with no model is exported with `model=""`, while `runtimes/traced.py` labels the same case `model="default"`.
  Consequence: On one counter, `abk.agent.tokens`, the same unnamed model appears under two label values depending on the series, so a `by (model)` panel shows it split.
  Done when: Use `record.model or "default"` to match `traced.py`.

units.title: Azure DevOps over typed REST
units.feedback:
The REST port is well done overall. The domain mapping, label/draft/abandon/branch-deletion calls, the no-op base comparison, the bounded read pool, the subprocess-refusing fixture and the protocol-level httpx.MockTransport stand-in all hold up. Two things block approval: the az credential now expires partway through a tick, and policy evaluations are paged by a mechanism the fake invents. Note: I could not run git diff against main in this environment, so I reviewed the branch's files directly, compared them with the main checkout's pipeline/az.py, and read the change's proposal, design, spec and tasks.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/forges/azure_devops.py:223 — The az-session Bearer token is cached for the life of the process and never refreshed. The `_transport` docstring says the connection is 'rebuilt when its credential is read again (an `az` token expires)', but `transport.credential_for` caches per (forge, owner) indefinitely. `clear_credentials` is called only by tests, so the `held.credentials is not credentials` branch never fires in production.
  Consequence: A tick runs its unit builds in-process (cli/pipeline.py: ThreadPoolExecutor over `build_unit`), and a build is a long Claude Code session. With no PAT set, the first Azure call of the tick caches an Entra access token that lives about 60–90 minutes. After that, create_pr, post_status, set_draft and the rest answer 401, so `AuthError` fails the unit after its build succeeded. The removed `pipeline/az.py` fetched a fresh token for every call (`_authorization`) and every `az` subprocess authenticated itself, so this is a regression from what the code does on main.
  Done when: An az-sourced credential is re-read before it expires. Either read `expiresOn` (or `expires_on`) from `az account get-access-token -o json` and re-resolve when it is within a few minutes of expiry, or, on an `AuthError` from a credential whose source is `az account get-access-token`, drop that cache entry, re-resolve once and retry the call once. A PAT stays cached. The `_transport` docstring describes what actually happens. A test in test_azure_rest_auth.py has the fake `az` hand out a token that is then rejected (401 from the RestHost for that token), or an expired `expiresOn`. It asserts that the next call re-runs `az account get-access-token` and succeeds with the new Bearer. The changelog's 'read once per organisation' wording is corrected to match.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/forges/azure_devops.py:398 — Policy evaluations are paged by an `x-ms-continuationtoken` response header and a `continuationToken` query parameter. As far as I know, the published Policy Evaluations – List reference (7.1-preview.1) pages that endpoint with `$top`/`$skip` and documents no continuation token. The test fake (tests/forges/azure_rest_host.py `_evaluations`) implements exactly the token scheme the code assumes, so `test_evaluations_paged_by_continuation_token_are_all_read` tests the code against itself.
  Consequence: If the host caps a page and expects `$skip`, the loop sees no token after the first page, and a failing build evaluation on a later page goes unreported, so a red pull request reads as green. The spec requirement 'SHALL follow continuation tokens and paging parameters to the end' is then unmet for this endpoint, and the test cannot catch it.
  Done when: Check the paging scheme against the Policy Evaluations – List REST reference. If it is `$top`/`$skip`, page it the way `_pull_docs` does: request `$top`, add `$skip` by what has been read, and stop on a short page. Then make `RestHost._evaluations` page by `$top`/`$skip`, ignoring `continuationToken`, so the test asserts the skips the real host would need. If the reference does document the header, cite it in a comment beside `_failing_evaluations` and keep the code.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/forges/azure_devops.py:751 — `delete_remote_branch` ignores the answer to `POST git/refs`. Azure answers 200 with a per-ref `success` and `updateStatus` (for example `staleOldObjectId`, or a lock or policy refusal) rather than an HTTP error.
  Consequence: A refused ref delete reads as a deleted branch, and the branch is silently left on the remote.
  Done when: Parse the `value` list and raise a `TransportError` naming the ref and `updateStatus` when `success` is false. Add a test where RestHost answers `success: false` and the call raises.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/forges/azure_devops.py:1 — The module docstring still explains the decoding in terms of `%20` handed to `az repos --project`. No `az` call is made any more; the identity is now quoted into REST paths.
  Consequence: The next reader looks for an `az repos` call that does not exist.
  Done when: Reword the first paragraph so it says the identity is decoded once and quoted into each REST path.

units.title: GitHub through a typed client
units.feedback:
The test suite passes (forges, pipeline and cli: 1952 tests). The tests fake GitHub at the HTTP boundary (GitHubHost answers the raw REST/GraphQL bodies, Link headers, the 302 to log storage, label case rules), which is the right place, and they cover tasks 1.1 to 1.5. The one blocker is that the unit did not build what the change decided. The proposal, design, README and task 1.6 all name `githubkit` as the client, and none of them was revised. Because the tests already sit at the httpx transport layer, they should carry over almost unchanged once the client is githubkit (`transport=GitHubHost(...)`). If a person would rather keep the hand-rolled client, the change's proposal and design must be revised in the planning repo first: githubkit was a recorded decision, weighed against alternatives, and it should not be dropped silently.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/forges/github.py:312 — The unit does not use githubkit at all. It builds its own REST/GraphQL client on `forges/transport.Transport`, with hand-written models in `forges/github_models.py`, and adds no dependency. The change it implements decided otherwise: the proposal says 'GitHub operations run on `githubkit`', design §Client says `GitHub(auth, timeout=..., transport=..., auto_retry=..., http_cache=False)` per owner, the README says 'through the `githubkit` library', and task 1.6 says 'Add the dependency'. pyproject.toml is not touched, and nothing in the repo mentions githubkit.
  Consequence: AGENTS.md ('Code changes go through the spec process') says a code change is built as its OpenSpec change describes. Here the change's central decision is replaced without the change saying so. What the design chose githubkit for is lost: generated models from GitHub's OpenAPI description, which the design's Risks section relies on to catch model drift, and a maintained client. Instead, a hand-maintained GraphQL query and model set (`_LISTING`, `github_models.py`) now has to be kept right by hand. Tasks 1.6 and 1.7 ('the dependency notes') are left undone.
  Done when: 1. Add `githubkit` to pyproject.toml, pinned as the design's Risks section asks, and update uv.lock.
2. Build the per-owner client as `githubkit.GitHub(TokenAuthStrategy(credential_for('github', owner).token), timeout=settings.forge_timeout_seconds, transport=self.http, http_cache=False, auto_retry=<bounded by settings.forge_retries>)`, cached per owner the way `_transport` caches today.
3. Port the operations onto its typed REST methods and its `graphql` call, with the same paths and payloads the tests already assert. Keep `_base_missing`/`_reason`/`StackRefused(concurrent=status==409)` mapping from the githubkit `RequestFailed` response's status and body.
4. Keep the existing GitHubHost tests passing through `transport=`. Add a test that the client is constructed with `http_cache=False` and the configured timeout.
5. Name githubkit in docs/code-forges.md ('GitHub over REST and GraphQL'), docs/architecture.md and the changelog bullet, and add the dependency note task 1.7 asks for (httpx stays because githubkit uses it).

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/forges/github.py:371 — `list_prs` now reads every page of a repository's whole history; before, it read only the 100 most recent pull requests. Callers that want one unit's PR also go through it: `events.py:790` and `events.py:1563` call `list_prs(repo, head_prefix=branch)`, and `wiring.py:1017` does the same.
  Consequence: In a repo with 3000 pull requests, every such call is 30 GraphQL queries. Each page asks for 100 labels, 100 comments, 100 reviews and 100 check contexts per PR, so roughly 5 rate-limit points a page. Repeated per unit per tick, this can use up the 5000-points-an-hour GraphQL budget on a long-lived repo. The design does say 'Paging follows the cursor', so this is a scaling decision for a person, not a defect to fix in this unit.
  Done when: A person decides whether a later change should use GraphQL's `headRefName:` argument for the single-branch lookups, or bound the listing (for example by `states` or by age). Record it as a follow-up on the change.
- [1.3] tests/forges/test_github_rest_checks.py:170 — No test asserts that the signed log-storage URL is fetched without the GitHub token. `_job_log` builds a separate `httpx.Client` for it, and its docstring promises this, but nothing pins it.
  Consequence: A later refactor that fetched `location` through `self._transport(...)` would send the owner's bearer token to a third-party blob host, and every test would still pass.
  Done when: In the failed-log test, find the call GitHubHost recorded whose `host` is the storage host, and assert `'authorization' not in call.headers`.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/forges/github.py:1018 — `remove_label` swallows every `NotFound`, not only 'label not on the pull request'. A 404 because the credential cannot see the repo or the PR also returns normally, yet the docstring says 'any other refusal raises'.
  Consequence: Calling it with a credential from the wrong account reads as success, which hides exactly the silent-404 case that docs/code-forges.md §Authentication warns about.
  Done when: Swallow the 404 only when the body says 'Label does not exist' (from `error.body`), and raise any other 404. Or correct the docstring.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/forges/github.py:291 — `_JOB_LINE` contains a literal, invisible U+FEFF character where the old code wrote `\ufeff`. Separately, `_transport` replaces a cached `Transport` without closing the old one's httpx client.
  Consequence: The next reader cannot see that the regex strips a byte order mark, and an editor may silently drop the character. The second issue leaks one connection pool each time credentials are cleared, which is small.
  Done when: Write `\ufeff` in the pattern. Call `held.close()` on the replaced transport before storing the new one.

units.title: A cause on every state change, and readmission by it
units.feedback:
Task group 1 is mostly in place. Causes are written by the graph's boundary and rebase holds, the poller's rework, requeue, restack, merge and close. `_sent_back` and `effective_state` now decide from the cause. The note matchers are deleted and pinned by tests. `held_base` replaces the depth-hold regex. The touched test files pass (269 passed). Three things block approval: (1) the reviewer label hold writes no cause, so every post-cutover label hold is listed as a cutover leftover forever; (2) a unit that ends `held` is skipped without the cause being logged, which task 1.2 and the spec scenario ask for; (3) the docs and changelog say every state change records a cause, which the code does not do. One test is also missing: the push-node hold path needs to be in the table. Task groups 2 and 3 (event kinds, feedback source, outcome enums, rewriting prose-asserting tests) belong to later units and are not asked of this one.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/events.py:968 — The reviewer label hold records no cause, both in `on_hold` (events.py:968) and in the graph's HOLD event handler (nodes.py:1215). Neither `set_state(..., HELD, held_by=HeldBy.REVIEWER, ...)` call passes `cause=`.
  Consequence: `cmd_status` lists every `held` unit whose last entry has no cause under `no recorded cause:`. So any agent-hold label added after this change shows up there as a cutover leftover. The docs (cli.md, SKILL.md, architecture.md) tell the operator to fix it by holding it again from the PR. That writes another uncaused entry, so the unit can never leave the list. This also contradicts design.md, which says a reviewer hold redone by hand gets an entry that carries a cause.
  Done when: Add a cause for the label's hold to `Cause` (for example `REVIEWER_HOLD = "reviewer_hold"`). Pass it from events.py:968 and nodes.py:1215. Update `test_the_causes_are_the_fixed_set_the_design_names` and record the added value in the change's design.md in the planning repo. Add tests: (a) after `events.on_hold` on an `in_review` unit, the last history entry has that cause and `cmd_status` output has no `no recorded cause` line naming the unit; (b) the graph's HOLD event path records the same cause.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:668 — `_sent_back` returns early on `unit.state != PLANNED`, so a unit started this pass that ended `held` (toolchain, depth, review escalation, needs a human) is skipped without the cause being logged. Only `planned` units get the `not started again in this pass, stopped for <cause>` line.
  Consequence: Task 1.2 asks that a unit held for toolchain, depth or review escalation is not readmitted and that the skip is logged with its cause. The spec scenario 'A hold for another reason' (a toolchain hold) requires that the log says why. `test_a_held_unit_is_not_let_back_in_whatever_its_note_says` checks only the start count, so the missing log goes unnoticed.
  Done when: In `_sent_back`, also consider units in `started` whose state is `HELD` and whose last entry is later than their start. Never readmit them, and log them once per (id, at) with the same `stopped for <cause>` line. Extend `test_a_held_unit_is_not_let_back_in_whatever_its_note_says` to assert that `cause.value` appears in the captured output.
- [1.3] docs/architecture.md:372 — The docs and changelog overstate where causes are recorded. architecture.md says 'Every state change records a `cause`'; the CHANGELOG bullet says a recorded cause is kept 'on each state change'.
  Consequence: Both sentences are false for the code as written. No cause is written for running (nodes.py:450), in_review after the push (nodes.py:1143), satisfied (nodes.py:976/989/998), or the label hold (see the first finding). A reader trusting the docs would expect `cause` on those entries and get `None`.
  Done when: Reword both to what the code does, for example: every change that stops a unit, holds it or sends it back (and merge, close, release, failure) records a cause; entries for starting a run, reaching review or being satisfied carry none. Or add causes to those writers. Keep `abk status`'s filter consistent with whichever you choose.
- [1.4] tests/graph/test_hold_causes.py:77 — `HOLD_PATHS` leaves out one of the graph's boundary holds: the push node's `HostMoved` hold (nodes.py:1066, `not pushed: …`, `Cause.RESTACK_DEFERRED`).
  Consequence: Task 1.1 asks for a table over every hold path of the graph's rebase and boundary nodes. With this path missing, a change that tags it `BASE_CHANGED` or `REWORK` would make the pass readmit a unit whose branch the host moved, and no test would fail.
  Done when: Add a `HOLD_PATHS` entry that drives `push` to raise `HostMoved` while rounds remain (`state.spent` false). Assert the entry is `planned` with `Cause.RESTACK_DEFERRED` and a non-empty note.

Optional:
- [1.5] tests/graph/test_hold_causes.py:77 — No test pins the cause written by these holds: the review-node holds (needs-human at nodes.py:756, both escalations at nodes.py:783, rounds spent at nodes.py:1119), the poller-side restack writers in `build_restack` (events.py:1421/1451/1465/1496), and the toolchain hold in `_build_unit` (cli/pipeline.py:1500).
  Consequence: Nothing would fail if one of these writers recorded the wrong cause, for example one in `READMITTED_CAUSES`. The scheduling tests set causes through a fake builder rather than through these writers.
  Done when: Add each writer to a cause table, as `test_hold_causes.py` does for the boundary holds.
- [1.6] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_store.py:163 — `StoredUnit.cause` calls `Cause(value)`, which raises `ValueError` on a value it does not know.
  Consequence: If an installation pins back to an older release after a newer one wrote a new cause value, `abk status` and every tick crash on that store.
  Done when: Return `None` (and optionally log) for an unknown value, or document that a store is not readable by an older release.
- [1.7] tests/cli/test_tick_scheduling.py:163 — The `Builder` fake sets `held_by=HeldBy.TOOLCHAIN` for every `HELD` end, including DEPTH, NEEDS_HUMAN and the escalations.
  Consequence: The record the fake writes is unlike the real one, so a future rule keyed on `held_by` could pass here and fail for real.
  Done when: Map each cause to its real holder: DEPTH to `HeldBy.DEPTH`, the review causes to `HeldBy.REVIEW`, TOOLCHAIN to `HeldBy.TOOLCHAIN`.
