units.title: A failed tier 2 run lists the first error of every failed test
units.feedback:
Task 3.7 asked the builder to confirm what design.md marks UNVERIFIED. One item was whether pytest cuts a short-summary line to the terminal width. It does, under the flags this branch sends (see the first finding). The result belongs in design.md's UNVERIFIED paragraph and section 3 ("The command") of the planning repo's change; if the builder cannot edit that repo, put it in the PR description. Group 4 (the output file, `Full output:` line, run log and `abk status`) belongs to a later unit and is not expected here.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/profiles/python_uv.py:461 — The tier 2 command runs pytest with `-v`. At that verbosity pytest cuts every FAILED/ERROR summary message to the terminal width, and drops it entirely when the test id fills the line. So the listing this branch adds is cut or empty in a real run.
  Consequence: In the pinned pytest 9.1.1, `_pytest/terminal.py:1565-1571` (`_get_line_with_reprcrash_message`) keeps the whole message only when `running_on_ci() or config.option.verbose >= 2`. Otherwise it calls `_format_trimmed(" - {}", msg, tw.fullwidth - len("FAILED <id>"))`, which ellipsizes the message and returns None when even `...` does not fit. The gate runs on the developer host, not on CI, with output piped (width 80 unless COLUMNS is set). For a test id like `tests/integration/test_acp_build_unit.py::test_the_unit_is_built_reviewed_and_pushed_through_the_runtime` (over 80 characters), the line pytest prints is just `ERROR <id>`. `parse_test_failures` then returns `line=""`. A shorter id gets a message cut to the remaining width. The four full-run failures this group exists to show would be listed with no error at all. The changelog and docs/architecture.md also say each test is listed 'with its first failure line', which would be false.
  Done when: Make the python profile's tier 2 commands, both with and without members, use `-vv` instead of `-v`. This is pytest's documented way to keep the whole summary message. Keep `-rfE --tb=short`. Update `tests/profiles/test_python_uv_tier2_summary_flags.py` to assert `-vv`. Update `test_wiring.py:1077` and `test_wiring.py:1096`, which compare `[..., "-v"]` prefixes. Add a test that runs real pytest in a subprocess (`pytester.runpytest_subprocess`) with the flags taken from `PROFILE.tier2_commands(...)[0]` after `pytest`, with CI and GITHUB_ACTIONS unset and COLUMNS=80. Its test file should hold a test whose node id is over 80 characters and which fails with a message over 80 characters, plus a module fixture that errors. Feed the captured stdout to `PROFILE.parse_test_failures` and assert each entry's `line` is the whole first line of the exception message. Today's flags must fail that test.
- [1.2] tests/tier2_failure_fakes.py:21 — `FOUR_ERRORS` and `MIXED` are described as recorded `pytest -m local_stack -v -rfE --tb=short` output, but they are hand-written. Pytest at those flags never prints their summary lines: `ERROR tests/integration/test_unit.py::test_built - FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'svc-a'` is about 113 characters, and pytest would cut it to 80.
  Consequence: The parser tests (task 3.2, 'recorded pytest output') show the parser reading the lines the implementation expects, not the lines pytest prints. That is why the cut and empty messages in the first finding passed review. A later change to the flags or the pytest pin that changes the summary format would also pass these tests.
  Done when: Record the fixtures from a real run of pinned pytest with the tier 2 flags (after the first finding, `-vv -rfE --tb=short`), with CI unset, and paste that output verbatim, header lines included. Alternatively, build them in the test with pytester as the first finding describes. Fix the comment so it names the flags the output was recorded with.
- [1.3] tests/tier2_failure_fakes.py:108 — The change adds more copies of test drivers that already exist. `feedback_after_failing_tier2` repeats the failing-tier-2 run driver line for line, `gate`/`run_returning` repeat an existing Tier2Session-with-fake-runner helper, and `_checkout` repeats an existing checkout helper.
  Consequence: The run_unit-on-a-failing-tier-2 driver is now in three places: `feedback_after_failing_tier2` (tests/tier2_failure_fakes.py:108-128), `tests/pipeline/test_redaction_store_and_logs.py:100-129` and `tests/graph/test_tier2_failure_log.py:35-53`. Each builds the same RunLog, UnitStore and `Recorder(tier2_ok=False)`, and calls `run_unit` under `open_checkpointer`. A change to `run_unit`'s or `RunLog`'s signature must now be made three times. In the same way, `gate` + `run_returning` repeat `_tier_two` (tests/pipeline/test_redaction_store_and_logs.py:79-86), and `test_tier2_failures_redacted._run` writes the same `pyproject.toml` that `_tier_two` writes. `_checkout` in tests/pipeline/test_tier2_failures.py:68 repeats `_checkout` in tests/pipeline/test_tier2_projects.py:49.
  Done when: Keep one shared driver in `tests/tier2_failure_fakes.py`, or `tests/runner_fakes.py` beside `Recorder`. It runs a failing tier 2 unit with a given snapshot and returns what the callers need: the feedback, and the run-log directory for `test_tier2_failure_log`. Make `test_redaction_store_and_logs.py` and `test_tier2_failure_log.py` call it in place of their inline copies, and make `_tier_two` use `gate`/`run_returning`. Move `_checkout` beside them and use it from both tier 2 test files.

Optional:
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/profiles/python_uv.py:286 — The parser accepts every line after the summary mark that begins `FAILED ` or `ERROR `. Under `-vv`, pytest prints a multi-line exception message whole, so a continuation line that happens to begin with one of those words becomes an extra entry.
  Consequence: Take an assertion message whose second line starts `ERROR connecting to svc-a`. With `-vv`, that line follows the real entry in the short summary, and the listing gains an entry with test `connecting to svc-a`.
  Done when: Accept only lines whose id has the shape of a pytest node id (contains `::`, or is a path ending in `.py`). Alternatively, stop at the closing `=====` summary line and take a message's continuation lines as part of the entry before them. Add a test with such a message.

description.summary: When tier 2 fails, the python profile now lists every failed or errored test with the whole first line of its error, read from pytest's short summary.
changes: The python profile's tier 2 command runs pytest with `-vv -rfE --tb=short`, with or without workspace members. At lower verbosity pytest cuts each summary message to the terminal width, or drops it.

`parse_test_failures` reads the FAILED/ERROR summary entries in printed order. It caps each line's length, and skips continuation lines of multi-line messages, which only count as entries when they look like a node id.

A new test runs real pytest in a subprocess with the profile's own flags on an 80-column terminal, off CI, and checks that the parser gets each whole first line, including for a test id longer than the terminal.
The parser fixtures are recorded from the pinned pytest at the tier 2 flags instead of being written by hand.
The test drivers for a failing tier 2 run, the fake-runner gate and the checkout helper are each kept once in `tests/tier2_failure_fakes.py`, and the run-log, redaction and PR-body tests share them.

units.title: The full output of each tier 2 run is kept in a file named in the result

description.summary: Each tier 2 run's whole output, redacted, is now kept in a file under the state directory, and the tier 2 result, the unit's run log and `abk status` name that file, so the first error is never lost when the posted output is cut to its tail.
changes: Tier 2 appends each command's whole output (passing commands included) to `tier2-output/<change>-<nn>-<stamp>-tier2.log` after the command finishes. Each chunk is redacted as one piece before it is written, and a failed redaction writes the withheld notice on its own line.
The tier 2 result carries `output_file` and `output_withheld`, and its snapshot gains a `Full output:` line naming the file. The line also says when the content was withheld.

When tier 2 fails, the run log gets a line with the file path, even when the tail of the cut output would leave it out. For a failed unit, `abk status` shows the file named by the latest tier 2 snapshot in the unit's feedback.
Only the last three files of each unit are kept. Archiving a change, automatically or with `abk archive`/`abk verify`, removes that change's files and leaves those of changes with similar names.
docs/architecture.md, docs/configuration.md and the changelog describe the new directory.

units.title: Classify failed tier 2 tests and run the untouched ones once on the base
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:2480 — In production the session never gets a base, so nothing is classified and the base run never happens. `build_runner` builds `Tier2Session(...)` without `base=`, and `graph/nodes.py:1655` calls `r.run_tier2(cwd=self.tree())` without one either. `classify` therefore always returns early on `self._base is None` (wiring.py:1812), and `_judge` returns None.
  Consequence: On a real unit, a failed tier 2 run with an untouched failing test runs nothing on the base and `verdict` stays None. Only tests that build the session by hand with `base=` exercise the feature. The changelog bullet ('A failed tier 2 run now sorts its failed tests … and runs the untouched ones once … on the base'), the docs/architecture.md paragraph and `limits.tier2_base_runs` all describe behaviour no installation gets. Group 1's done-when ('a failed tier 2 run classifies … runs the untouched ones once on the base') is not met.
  Done when: Pass the base each run uses into the run, not into the constructor, because a restack can change `state.base` between runs. `Tier2Session.run(*, cwd, base=None)` takes it, the node calls `r.run_tier2(cwd=self.tree(), base=base)` with the `base = state.base or self.base` it already computes at nodes.py:1653, and `UnitRunner.run_tier2`'s type allows it. Remove the `or "HEAD"` fallback at wiring.py:1841, since a base is always present when `_judge` gets that far. Add a test that drives the `tier2` node (or `build_runner`'s `run_tier2`) with a fake runner and a temporary repo, and asserts that an untouched failing test is rerun in a worktree at the node's base. Today that test would fail.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:1841 — An error in the base step propagates out of `Tier2Session.run`, so a tier 2 failure becomes an exception. `worktree_at` calls `git_out(repo, 'worktree', 'add', …)`, which raises `CalledProcessError` when the add fails: an unresolvable base, git's lock on the shared `.git` held by another unit's worktree add (this add does not take the per-repo turn), or a full disk. `self._run` can raise `OSError`. Neither is caught.
  Consequence: Before this change, a failed tier 2 run always returned `(False, snapshot)` and the node saved the failure as feedback. Now any of the errors above makes `run_tier2` raise inside the node: the unit loses its tier 2 feedback and the run dies with a traceback instead of 'tier 2 failed'. The design ("anything else … a timeout: not proved pre-existing, so the unit broke it") says a base run that cannot answer leaves the unit failing as it does today. `test_a_base_run_that_raises_leaves_no_worktree_and_the_units_tree_unchanged` wraps the call in `contextlib.suppress(RuntimeError)`, so it passes either way.
  Done when: In `_judge`, catch `subprocess.CalledProcessError` and `OSError` from adding the worktree and from the base command. Log one line naming the error, and return a `Tier2Verdict` with every untouched failure in `broken` (or None, but pick one and document it). `run` then still returns `(False, snapshot)`. Change the raising test so it uses `OSError`, calls `gate.run` without `suppress`, and asserts that it returns `ok is False`, that the untouched tests are in `verdict.broken`, and that the worktree is gone. Add a test where the base sha does not exist, so `worktree add` fails, asserting the same outcome.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:1855 — The base run always reruns with the entry's first tier 2 command (`rerun(commands[0], ids)`), not the command that failed. For a workspace repo with members and no `projects`, `PythonUvProfile.tier2_commands` returns one command per member (`uv run --directory <member> --package <pkg> --isolated pytest -m …`) under a single entry. Every untouched id is then rerun in the first member's directory and package.
  Consequence: Take a workspace with members `a` and `b`. A test in `b` that fails on the unit and also fails on the base is rerun under `--directory a`. pytest reports the file as not found, and the test is classed `broken` instead of `pre_existing`. Pre-existing failures in every member except the first can never be recognised. The design says the ids are run with `serial_rerun_command(command, ids)` 'for the tier 2 command that failed'. No test covers a member-shaped repo or more than one command: all fixtures use the single no-member command.
  Done when: While building `outputs` in `run`, keep which command (and its `where`) named each failure, for example a mapping from test id to `(where, toolchain, command)` local to the run. Group the untouched ids by that command and run `serial_rerun_command(that_command, its_ids)` once per failed command, in `tree / where.relative_to(cwd)`. Add a test with a two-command entry (a members-shaped fixture, or a profile whose `tier2_commands` returns two commands) where only the second command's test fails. It should assert that the base run uses the second command's serial rerun and that the test comes out `pre_existing` when the base output names it.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/skills/abk-config/SKILL.md:141 — The new `limits.tier2_base_runs` field is documented in docs/configuration.md but not in the abk-config skill's `limits:` block. That block lists `tier1_repeat_runs` and stops there.
  Consequence: AGENTS.md, under 'Installation facts come from Installation/config.active()', says a new per-installation field is 'documented in the abk-config skill and docs/configuration.md'. An agent editing abk.yaml through the skill will not know the setting exists.
  Done when: Add `  tier2_base_runs: 1                # run the untouched failed tier 2 tests once on the base (0: off)` below the `tier1_repeat_runs` line, matching the docs/configuration.md line.

Optional:
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:1818 — `classify` reads the test id's file part as a path relative to the repo root. For a workspace member run through `uv run --directory <member>`, pytest prints ids relative to the member (`tests/test_x.py::t`), while `_changed_files` returns repo-relative paths (`<member>/tests/test_x.py`).
  Consequence: In a members-shaped repo, a failing test in a file the unit changed is classed untouched and is run on the base. If the base fails it too, it is recorded as `pre_existing`. Once group 3 parks units on pre-existing failures, such a unit would wait on a fix change for its own test. Only `projects` ids are prefixed today. Fixing this needs the profile to say where a command's ids are relative to, which is a design decision. Either do that here alongside the previous finding, or record it as a known limit in the docs and the change's design.
  Done when: Either resolve each id against the directory its command ran in (a profile hook, or the per-command mapping from the previous finding plus the profile's knowledge of `--directory`), with a members-shaped classify test, or state the limit in docs/architecture.md and the design's UNVERIFIED list.
- [1.6] docs/architecture.md:1049 — The design's UNVERIFIED item asks the builder to measure how long the clean base worktree takes on this repository's own tier 2 suite and to note it in docs/architecture.md, and task 1.6 says to confirm the UNVERIFIED places. The new paragraph has no such note.
  Consequence: A reader has no figure for what the base run costs on top of a failed tier 2 run, and the design's open question stays open.
  Done when: Add one sentence with the measured time (or say that it was not measured and why) to the new paragraph.
- [1.7] tests/pipeline/test_tier2_not_repeated.py:37 — The 'isolate is not called for a tier 2 command' part of task 1.4 is checked only by `spy.reruns == []`. That check is in a Tier2Session run whose only failure is the unit's own test, so no rerun would happen either way. The tier 1 test passes every command, so `isolate` is never reached there.
  Consequence: If tier 1 were changed to reach a tier 2 command through `isolate`, nothing here would fail.
  Done when: In the tier 1 test, have the fake runner fail the test command after lint with pytest output that names the tier 2 test. Then assert that `Spy.reruns` contains no command with the tier 2 marker and that `TIER2_COMMAND` was never run.

description.summary: When a unit's tier 2 run fails, its failed tests are sorted into the unit's own and the ones in files it left alone, and the untouched ones are run once on the unit's base to tell failures that were already there from ones the unit caused.
changes: A failed tier 2 run sorts its failed tests by owner. A test belongs to the unit when the branch changed its file, or changed a `conftest.py` beside it. Each untouched test is rerun once on the base, in a detached temporary worktree, while the same stack lock is still held, and `Tier2Session.verdict` records whose each failure is.
The tier 2 node passes in the base each run is against. If a restack moves the base, the next base run uses the new one.
Each failed tier 2 command is repeated on the base with only the tests it named, using the profile's serial rerun command. Workspace members are therefore rerun in their own directory.
If the base run cannot be made (the worktree cannot be added, or a command cannot start), the error is logged and nothing is proved: the unit still fails, and its untouched failures count as its own.
New setting `limits.tier2_base_runs` (default 1, 0 turns it off), documented in docs/configuration.md, docs/architecture.md and the abk-config skill.
Tier 2 tests are never repeated or isolated by tier 1's rerun machinery, and a test pins this.

units.title: Record pre-existing failures and write one previewed fix change each

description.summary: Adds a record of tier 2 tests that also fail on the base, and writes one fix change per such test without a model, previewed before it is written.
changes: A pre-existing failure is stored in `<state_dir>/preexisting-failures.jsonl` through a new generic `FailureRecord`, which the flake record now shares. `abk status` lists each one as `pre-existing:` with its count and fix change.

`untouched_failures.ensure_fix` makes sure, under a lock, that one open `fix-failing-<slug>` change exists per test id. It writes the proposal, design, tasks (one tier2 group at Priority 1) and spec without a model. A successor with a MODIFIED spec is written only after the earlier attempt is archived.

The ensure step reports `exists: <change>`, or `would write: <change>` then `wrote: <change>`. `abk tick --dry-run` prints the same preview line for each recorded failure, even when no unit is pending, and writes nothing.
The flake fix change is now also written at `Priority: 1`. The helpers that choose a fix change's name are public and shared by both kinds (`fix_change_name`, `open_fix_change`, `next_fix_name`).

The architecture doc, the CLI doc, the abk-pipeline skill and the changelog describe the new record, the fix changes and the preview output. An integration test checks that the written change and its successor pass `openspec validate --strict`.

units.title: Park a unit behind its fix change, resume at tier 2, and trim feedback
units.feedback:
The rebase onto the updated predecessor kept this unit's nodes.py additions intact: against main they only add lines, and the tier2 node still reads the same way around the new park. The 36 tests in the new files and in the neighbouring flake/fix-change files pass. Most of the tests still make sense against the predecessor as it is now. One test duplicates coverage the predecessor already has. Two of the tests the tasks ask for are missing an assertion. The Tier2Session base-run change has no test.

- The saved feedback still shows the snapshot's `**Failed:** N of M` count, which includes the pre-existing tests, and the `**Full output:**` path, whose file holds their output. The agent can still reach the untouched output through that file.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1694 — `wait_for_preexisting` copies the park tail of `wait_for_fix` (nodes.py:1288-1291) instead of reusing it: the note, then `self.hold(PLANNED, note, note, cause=Cause.GATED)`, then `r.store.set_gated_requeue(unit.id, RequeueReason.RESUME)`, then return. Task 3.6 says that hold and resume requeue should be 'reused'.
  Consequence: How a unit is parked behind a fix change now lives in two copies. A change to that park (a different cause, requeue reason or note handling) has to be made in both places, or tier 1 flakes and tier 2 pre-existing failures will park differently. This goes against the task text and the prior-art rule.
  Done when: Add one private method on BuildPath, e.g. `park_for_fix(self, note: str) -> Update`, that does the hold and sets the RESUME gated requeue. Have both `wait_for_fix` and `wait_for_preexisting` call it with their own note. The existing flake-parking and tier2-wait tests should pass unchanged.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/untouched_failures.py:229 — `wait_on_preexisting` repeats the loop in `flakes.wait_on_fix` (flakes.py:92-94): `for member in unit.members(): for group in member.groups: add_needs(...)`. The only difference is the reason text.
  Consequence: The rule for which groups of a unit get a `Needs:` line (every group of every member) is written twice. A change to it (say, members of another change, or only the unit's own groups) has to be made in both files, or flake waits and pre-existing waits will gate different groups.
  Done when: Extract one function in flakes.py, e.g. `add_needs_to_unit(inst, unit: StoredUnit, fix: str, reason: str)`, that runs the loop over `add_needs`. Call it from both `wait_on_fix` and `wait_on_preexisting`. Keep `add_needs` itself if anything else uses it; otherwise make it private again.
- [1.3] tests/graph/test_tier2_feedback.py:409 — Task 3.5 asks this file to also assert that 'the rework prompt made from the saved text holds none of an untouched test's output'. No test builds a rework or fix-checks prompt from the saved feedback.
  Consequence: The spec says every rework prompt made from the feedback is free of untouched output. If a prompt builder added the tier 2 snapshot or output file from somewhere other than the stored feedback (for example `fix_checks` reading `r.store.get(unit.id).feedback` and then adding more), the untouched test's output would reach the agent and this test file would still pass.
  Done when: Add a test that saves a mixed failure (own=OWN, old=OLD), then drives the unit's next round so the rework/fix-checks prompt is sent. The Recorder captures the prompt (as the existing claude:rework events do). Assert the prompt contains the OWN failure line and does not contain OLD_OUTPUT or 'assert in test_old'.
- [1.4] tests/pipeline/test_tier2_resume.py:737 — Task 3.4 asks this test to show 'that the restack's tier 1 path is unchanged'. The test only checks that restack comes before tier2 and tier2 before push. It says nothing about the tier 1 step a restack runs.
  Consequence: If the resume skipped or doubled the tier 1 run that a restacked unit gets (the moved-commit tier1 node), this test would still pass. The task's requirement goes unchecked.
  Done when: In the released run, assert the tier 1 event the restack path normally produces. For example `after.index("restack") < after.index("tier1") < after.index("tier2") < after.index("push")`, with `after.count("tier1") == 1` (or `tier1:whole_repo` if that is what the path runs), matching what `test_flake_parking.py::test_the_parked_unit_runs_tier_1_again_restacked_when_the_gate_clears` pins for the tier 1 park.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:1954 — `Tier2Session._judge` now fills `Tier2Verdict.command` (the base reruns joined with '; ') and `base_output` (the base runs' output, truncated to the last 4000 characters and redacted). No test checks either field. The wiring test builds its verdict with `verdict_of`, which sets them by hand.
  Consequence: The record's `command` and `base_output` (spec: each entry has 'the command' and the base run's result) come only from this code in production. If it regressed to `command=""`, dropped the output, or skipped the redaction, every test would still pass, because the only producer of a populated verdict in the tests is a fake.
  Done when: In tests/pipeline/test_tier2_base_run.py, with the existing `tier2_base_fakes` runner, assert that after a failed run with one pre-existing test, `session.verdict.command` equals the rerun argv joined with spaces (the `serial_rerun_command` output for the untouched ids) and `session.verdict.base_output` holds the fake base run's stdout. Add one case where the base output contains a secret-shaped value and assert it is redacted.
- [1.6] tests/graph/test_tier2_waits_for_fix.py:680 — `test_a_flake_fix_for_the_same_test_is_another_change_and_does_not_stand_in` only asserts `fix != flake_fix`. The predecessor already covers that in tests/pipeline/test_untouched_failures_change.py:118 (`test_it_is_a_different_change_from_the_flake_fix_of_the_same_test`). The 'does not stand in' part of its name is not asserted.
  Consequence: It adds no coverage over the predecessor. It would also pass if the unit gained no `Needs:` line on the fix-failing change because the existing flake line was taken as enough, which is exactly what 'does not stand in' claims to rule out.
  Done when: Either delete it, or make it test what its name says: after `on_preexisting(first, ..., wait=True)`, assert `waits_on(installation, "feature") == [flake_fix, fix]`, so the unit waits on both changes.

Optional:
- [1.7] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/untouched_failures.py:199 — `feedback_snapshot` drops the whole `<details>` output block whenever any failure is pre-existing, including the unit's own test's traceback. Its docstring says the output is 'kept only when no pre-existing test is in it', which reads as a check on the tail's content that the code does not make. The test named `..._saves_the_units_own_output_...` only asserts the one-line failure, not OWN_OUTPUT.
  Consequence: In a mixed failure the agent gets the unit's failing test id and its first line, but none of that test's output. A reader of the docstring or the test name would expect that output to be kept.
  Done when: Make the docstring, the test name and the behaviour agree. Either say the output block is dropped whenever a pre-existing failure exists (and rename the test to say 'failure line'), or keep the block when none of the pre-existing ids appear in it and add a test for that case.

description.summary: When tier 2 finds a failure in a test the unit did not touch, the unit is parked behind the change that fixes it, resumes at tier 2 once that change merges, and is never shown the untouched test's output.
changes: A unit whose tier 2 run fails only on pre-existing failures is held, gated, with a note naming the tests. Every group of every member gets a `Needs:` line on the fix change, written once per failing test. A flake fix for the same test is a different change, so the unit waits on both.

Parking for a tier 1 flake and parking for a tier 2 pre-existing failure share one `park_for_fix` step, with one gated hold and a RESUME requeue. The `Needs:` lines both write come from one `add_needs_to_unit` in flakes.py.

When the fix merges, the parked unit is restacked and runs tier 2 again in full, without another agent round. It runs tier 1 once only if the restack moved the branch, and it is parked again if the same untouched test still fails.

The tier 2 feedback saved for rework keeps the unit's own failure lines and names each pre-existing failure once. The output block is dropped whenever a pre-existing test failed, so no rework prompt carries an untouched test's output.
The tier 2 verdict now records the base rerun command and the base run's output, redacted and cut to its last 4000 characters, for the pre-existing failure record.

history.note: held before review: its base main was rewritten while it built

units.title: Several-process test spawns its processes and fork warnings fail the suite
units.feedback:
The spawn rewrite of the several-process test is sound. It passes serially and under `-n 4`, every process is joined or terminated, and the parked thread is released and joined. The guard is the problem: it does not work, and it hides the warning it is meant to catch. CPython raises the multi-threaded-fork DeprecationWarning after the fork has already happened. If a filter turns that warning into an exception, the interpreter swallows the exception instead of raising it. I checked this. With the branch's exact filter in a pytest.ini, a test that calls `os.fork()` and a test that uses `multiprocessing.get_context("fork")`, each with a parked thread alive, both pass with no warning in the summary. That happens on 3.14.6 (the repo's uv interpreter) and on 3.12.13 (CI's). Without the filter, both warnings appear in the summary. `python -W error::DeprecationWarning` on the same script also exits 0. So `interpreter_warns_on_threaded_fork()` is False on every supported interpreter, and the one behavioural test that would have shown this is always skipped. The spec sentence 'The pytest options SHALL turn the DeprecationWarning … into an error' cannot be met as written. Whoever revises the change in the planning repo should reword that requirement and design section 'The guard against regressions' to describe the hook-based mechanism below.

Required:
- [1.1] pyproject.toml:89 — The `error:This process .* is multi-threaded…:DeprecationWarning` filter does not fail a test that forks while threaded. It suppresses the warning instead, because CPython drops the error raised from this warning after the fork has happened.
  Consequence: A test that goes back to `get_context("fork")`, or any new `os.fork()` in a threaded test process, passes silently under `poe test` on 3.12 and 3.14. Before this branch the warnings summary at least printed the warning. The branch therefore removes the only signal that found the problem, and leaves task 1.3 ('fails if the context is fork') and the spec scenario 'A fork of a multi-threaded process fails the test' unmet.
  Done when: Remove the `error` filter entry. Fail the test from a hook in `tests/conftest.py` instead. For example, a `pytest_runtest_call` (or setup/call/teardown) hookwrapper that wraps the phase in `warnings.catch_warnings(record=True)`, sets `warnings.simplefilter("always", DeprecationWarning)` scoped to the fork message, and calls `pytest.fail(...)` naming the warning and its location when a recorded warning matches `This process .* is multi-threaded, use of fork\(\) may lead to deadlocks`. Other warnings must still reach pytest's summary: re-emit the ones that do not match with `warnings.warn_explicit`, or record only that message. Confirm by hand that the several-process test, switched temporarily to `get_context("fork")`, now fails.
- [1.2] tests/test_warning_filters.py:96 — `interpreter_warns_on_threaded_fork()` checks whether `-W error` makes the process fail, which never happens on any interpreter. The fork half of the behavioural test (task 1.2) is therefore always skipped, and the remaining tests pass whatever the guard does.
  Consequence: `test_a_test_that_forks_while_another_thread_is_alive_fails_with_the_warning` is skipped on 3.12 and 3.14 (confirmed: `SKIPPED … this interpreter does not warn`). `test_the_multi_threaded_fork_warning_is_an_error_in_the_pytest_options` checks only the config text. So the suite stays green while the guard is broken, which is exactly what happens on this branch. The skipif probe also runs a subprocess during collection in every xdist worker.
  Done when: Remove the probe and the skipif; every supported interpreter (>=3.12) emits the warning. Point the pytester tests at the real mechanism: load the repo's conftest hook into pytester, for example by making the hook a plugin module under `tests/` and passing `-p tests.<module>` or using `pytester.makeconftest` with its import. Then assert three things. A test that forks with a parked thread alive fails, and its output names `multi-threaded, use of fork() may lead to deadlocks`. A test that spawns passes. Another DeprecationWarning gives `passed=1, warnings=1`. Replace `fork_filter()`'s config-text check with a check that the hook is registered, or drop it if the behavioural tests cover it. The fork test must fail when the hook is removed.
- [1.3] tests/usage_asker.py:39 — `asking_in_a_process` keeps its own copy of the guard setup from `Host.__init__` in `tests/usage_host.py:89-92`: `CREDENTIALS_PATH = home / "no-credentials.json"`, `DEFAULT_ANCHOR_PATH = home / ".claude.json"`, and `config_module.activate(WorkspaceConfig(), None)`.
  Consequence: The two copies must change together. If `Host` starts faking another path, or renames the credentials file, the spawned child keeps the old setup. It then reads the developer's real files or a different file from the parent, and the test still passes.
  Done when: Add one function in `tests/usage_host.py` that returns the faked guard attributes for a home, e.g. `faked_paths(home) -> dict[str, Path]` for `CREDENTIALS_PATH` and `DEFAULT_ANCHOR_PATH`. `Host.__init__` applies them with `monkeypatch.setattr(usage_guard, name, value)` and the child with `setattr(usage_guard, name, value)`, so both read the same definition.

Optional:
- [1.4] tests/pipeline/test_usage_one_authority.py:97 — In the spawn test, the parent still calls `slow_endpoint(monkeypatch, calls, session=33.0)` but never asks for usage itself. The child's answer is written a second time, as the literal `{"session": 33.0}` at line 106.
  Consequence: The parent's patch does nothing, and the answer is stated twice. Changing one copy leaves the `("live", 33)` assertion depending on the other.
  Done when: Define the answer once (e.g. `ANSWER = {"session": 33.0}`), pass it to the child, and drop the parent's unused `slow_endpoint` call in this test.

description.summary: The several-process usage test now starts its processes with spawn instead of fork, and a test plugin fails any test that forks while another thread is alive.
changes: The test that sends twenty asks from several processes starts them with the `spawn` method, so it no longer forks a process that has a second thread, which can hang the child.

A new pytest plugin, `tests/fork_warning_guard.py`, registered in `tests/conftest.py`, records warnings during each test's setup, call and teardown. It fails the phase, naming the file and line, when CPython's 'multi-threaded, use of fork()' DeprecationWarning appears, and re-emits every other warning so it still reaches the summary.

`tests/test_warning_filters.py` runs the plugin in a separate pytest process and checks three outcomes: a test that forks with a thread alive fails and names the warning, a spawning test passes, and an unrelated DeprecationWarning is reported without failing. It also checks that the repo's own run loads the plugin.
The spawned asker and the in-process `Host` fixture both read the faked credentials and anchor paths from one function, `faked_paths(home)` in `tests/usage_host.py`.

units.title: The rules and the policy check cover the spellings of a command
units.feedback:
The global-option normalization, the wrapper-value stripping, the table and the per-spelling probe report all do what tasks 1.1–1.12 ask. The full pipeline, runtimes, hooks and forges suites passed (exit 0), and so did the leak guards, ruff and pyrefly. I also ran check_command by hand on edge spellings: `--repo=`, `-Ro/r`, `--method=PUT`, `-XPUT`, `timeout -s KILL 5`, `env -u X`, `--namespace x` and `--git-dir .git clean` are all refused, and pushing the unit's own branch with `-C` is still allowed. Three things block approval: one hole in the raw-API merge pattern, one test that task 1.2 asks for, and one changelog sentence that says more than the code does.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/forges/github.py:146 — The raw-API merge pattern `/pulls/\d+/merge$` is anchored at the end of the argument, so the same merge request with a query string or a trailing slash gets through.
  Consequence: Running check_command on `gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/1/merge?merge_method=squash` returns allowed=True (I ran it), and so does `gh api repos/o/r/pulls/1/merge/ -X PUT`. The host routes both to the merge endpoint, so an agent can merge a pull request through the raw API. That breaks the spec requirement that a merge through the host's raw API is forbidden as the merge command is.
  Done when: Change the path pattern so the match ends at the end of the argument, an optional `/`, or a `?`, for example r"/pulls/\d+/merge/?(?:\?|$)". Add a judge-only row to the raw-API merge class in `SPELLINGS`, with a new `SpellingName` such as `API_QUERY` and command `gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/1/merge?merge_method=squash`. `test_a_merge_through_the_raw_api_is_refused_with_the_method_either_side_of_the_path` then refuses it with 'never merges', and the existing read test still allows `pulls/1/comments` and `commits/abc123/check-runs`.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/command_spellings.py:423 — Task 1.2 asks for a test that the merge is refused with `--repo=<repo>` between `gh` and `pr`. The table has no such row, so no test checks the `=` form.
  Consequence: Task 1.2 and the spec scenario 'The host tool's repository option' (short, long, or with `=`) are unproven. The code refuses it today only because an unknown dash word is skipped as one token. If `GLOBAL_VALUED['gh']` or the skip rule were changed, `gh --repo=o/r pr merge 1` could be let through with no test failing.
  Done when: Add `Spelling(name=SpellingName.REPO_EQUALS, command="gh --repo=o/r pr merge 1", readers=JUDGE)` (a new enum member) to the merge class. `test_a_merge_is_refused_with_the_repository_given_before_the_subcommand` then refuses it, and `test_a_gh_read_is_allowed_with_the_repository_option` allows `gh --repo=o/r pr view 1`. Also add the row to `test_the_judge_also_reads_the_two_word_forms_and_the_landings`.
- [1.3] CHANGELOG.md:14 — The entry says the policy check 'now attempts each of these spellings in its one prompt'. It attempts only the table's probe rows.
  Consequence: The probe does not attempt the two-word `--git-dir .git` and `--work-tree .` forms, `HEAD:main`, `master`, `--method PUT`, the hard-reset and branch-delete `-C` spellings, or any wrapper spelling, `sudo -u root` included; those are judge-only rows. An operator reading the changelog would believe the live check covers them.
  Done when: Reword the sentence so it states what the probe sends. For example: 'The policy check now also attempts the global-option spellings of the amend, the push to the default branch and the force push, the repository-option spellings of the merge and two raw-API merge spellings, all in its one prompt, and reports, per class and spelling, which one an agent ran without asking.'

Optional:
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/acp.py:150 — The same 'probe rows of the table' comprehension is written four times: `PROBE_CLASSES` here, `probed()` and two inline copies in tests/pipeline/test_command_spellings_table.py (lines 38, 90 and 103 of the file), and `table_rows()` in tests/runtimes/test_acp_probe_spellings.py.
  Consequence: A change to how a row is chosen for the probe (a new `Reader`, for example) needs four matching edits.
  Done when: Add one `probe_rows()` that yields (label, spelling) pairs, either in `command_spellings` or in tests/spelling_rows.py beside `judge_rows`, and use it in all four places.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/forges/github.py:145 — A merge through the host's GraphQL endpoint (`gh api graphql -f query='mutation { mergePullRequest(...) }'`) is still allowed, and `DeniedRequest` (command, method, path) cannot express a rule that looks at the request body.
  Consequence: The spec's wording ('a merge requested through the host's raw API SHALL be forbidden') covers this; the design limits the rule to REST paths. Closing it means deciding how to match a request body.
  Done when: A person decides whether `DeniedRequest` gains a body pattern, or whether the GraphQL merge is recorded as out of scope in design.md.
- [1.6] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/acp.py:1708 — The probe report uses the bare string "plain" twice (`spelled.get(command, "plain")` and `result.spelling == "plain"`) instead of `SpellingName.PLAIN`, and `SpellingResult.spelling` is typed `str`.
  Consequence: If the enum value is renamed, the report silently stops recognising plain rows.
  Done when: Use `SpellingName.PLAIN.value`, or type `SpellingResult.spelling` as `SpellingName`.
- [1.7] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/acp.py:147 — The comment says each probe command is harmless even if run, because the probe worktree has no remote. The new `gh -R o/r ...` and `gh api ... repos/o/r/...` rows name a repository outright, so an agent that runs them without asking sends real requests to the code host with the installation's token.
  Consequence: The requests are not destructive, since the token has no rights on `o/r`, but the comment no longer describes what the probe does.
  Done when: Correct the comment to say that these rows reach the host if run but cannot act there.

description.summary: The command policy and the live policy check now cover the other ways an agent can type a forbidden git or gh command: global options before the subcommand, a wrapper's option values, and raw-API merges.
changes: git global options (`-C`, `-c`, `--no-pager`, `--git-dir`, `--work-tree`, joined or as separate words) and gh's repository option (`-R`, `--repo`, `--repo=`) are skipped before the policy reads the subcommand. An amend, a push or force push to the default branch, a hard reset, a branch force-delete or a PR merge spelled this way is refused.
A privilege or environment wrapper's option value (`sudo -u root`, `env -u X`, `timeout -s KILL 5`) no longer hides the command it wraps.

A merge through `gh api` is refused for PUT or POST to `/pulls/<n>/merge`, whether the method is given explicitly or implied by fields. A trailing slash, query string or fragment does not get it through. Reads through the raw API stay allowed.
A shared table in `pipeline/command_spellings.py` lists each forbidden class's spellings and marks which ones the judge reads and which the probe sends. `probe_rows()` gives the probe's rows.
The ACP runtime's policy-check probe sends the table's probe rows in its one prompt and reports, per class and spelling, which one an agent ran without asking.

units.title: Doctor and init name the spelling; documentation
units.feedback:
The production change is small and correct. `policy_check.describe` is one rendering that both `cli/doctor.py` and `cli/init.py` call (all three init call sites). It falls back to `unenforced` for a cached report that has no per-spelling results; the existing UNENFORCED tests in tests/cli/test_doctor.py:500 and tests/cli/test_init.py:316 exercise that fallback. The docs and the folded changelog bullet match the code: MAX_AGE is 15 minutes, and wrappers and directory changes are JUDGE-only rows in command_spellings.py. What blocks approval is in the new tests: two copied helpers, one assertion that cannot tell refused spellings from unrefused ones, and the passing case that task 2.1 asks for. Task 2.2's 'a check that could not run prints a note and caches nothing' is already covered by tests/cli/test_init.py:441 and the behaviour did not change, so it is not raised.

Required:
- [1.1] tests/cli/test_doctor_policy_spellings.py:47 — The doctor test only checks that each command string appears somewhere in the detail. It never checks that the refused ones are shown as refused, or that classes with nothing let through are left out. Its fixture also carries only one class, while a real report has a result for every probe row.
  Consequence: A `describe` that listed all of a class's commands under 'not refused', or that printed every class including fully refused ones, would still pass. Task 2.1 requires that the test 'groups the class's other spellings as refused'. The same weakness is in tests/cli/test_init_policy_spellings.py:82. tests/runtimes/selectable.py:78 builds a three-row report by hand, where the real `_probe` (runtimes/acp.py:1705) returns one SpellingResult per `probe_rows()` entry across every class.
  Done when: Build `spelling_report()` from `command_spellings.probe_rows()`: one SpellingResult per row, all refused except the amend class's DIRECTORY spelling, with `unenforced` derived the way acp.py:1715 derives it. Then assert the exact rendered text in both tests, e.g. that `policy.detail` equals "amending a commit: not refused as `git -C . commit --amend --no-edit`; refused as `git commit --amend --no-edit`, ..." listing the class's other probe spellings in table order. Also assert that no other class label (such as 'merging a pull request') appears in the detail.
- [1.2] tests/cli/test_doctor_policy_spellings.py:22 — The test redefines `which_all` and an `answer` run-fake, and builds its own planning repo and abk.yaml. tests/cli/test_doctor.py already provides `Answers` (line 36), `which_all` (73), the `workspace` fixture (85), `by_name` (117) and `select_runtime` (379).
  Consequence: This is a second copy of the doctor test helpers. Seven sibling files (test_doctor_union_rule, _environment, _replay, _grafana, _secrets, _changelog, forges/test_github_api_url) import `Answers, which_all` from tests.cli.test_doctor instead, so the two copies have to change together.
  Done when: Delete the local `answer` and `which_all`. Import `Answers, which_all` (and `workspace`, `select_runtime`, `by_name` if wanted) from tests.cli.test_doctor, matching the existing doctor test files. Write the runtime entry with `select_runtime(workspace, "loose", "    policy_fix: [scripts/constrain-agent.sh, --strict]\n")` as test_doctor.py:504 does.
- [1.3] tests/cli/test_init_policy_spellings.py:25 — The `stubs` autouse fixture and the `app` fixture copy tests/cli/test_init.py:60-84. The setup inside the test copies the `loose` fixture at test_init.py:300-313: init `--yes`, append the runtime entry, select. The copied `stubs` also drops the original's guards that fail on an unexpected prompt or an unasked fix.
  Consequence: This makes a second copy of the init test fixtures. A change to how init is stubbed (a new external call to fake) must be made in both places, or this file starts calling the real thing. The file already imports `fake_claude, fake_openspec, init_args` from tests.cli.test_init, so the rest is copied for no reason.
  Done when: Reuse the fixtures from tests.cli.test_init: import `stubs`, `app` and `FIX`, or move `stubs`, `app` and a report-parametrised form of `loose` into a shared helper module that both files import. Then build the spelling case through that shared fixture, passing `spelling_report()` in place of UNENFORCED, rather than repeating the setup inline.
- [1.4] tests/cli/test_doctor_policy_spellings.py:33 — Task 2.1's second half is missing: 'with every spelling refused it passes'.
  Consequence: Task 2.1 asks for this case and no test covers it. A report with per-spelling results, all refused and ok=True, is never run through doctor. A change that made doctor fail, or print, whenever `results` is non-empty would go unnoticed.
  Done when: Add a test in this file. It selects a runtime whose report is the full table with every SpellingResult refused (ok=True), and asserts that the 'runtime policy' check has status 'ok'.

Optional:
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/policy_check.py:77 — `describe` is a new public function with no unit test of its own. It is covered only through doctor and init, and its fallback path (a report without results) is covered only incidentally by older tests.
  Consequence: If the doctor or init tests are later refactored, the fallback for a report cached before per-spelling results existed could break without any failing test.
  Done when: Optionally add tests/runtimes/test_policy_check_describe.py (or similar). It should assert describe's output for a report with results, and that a report with only `unenforced` gives the joined labels.

description.summary: When an agent runtime refuses one spelling of a forbidden command but not another, `abk doctor` and `abk init` now show it by class and by spelling, through one shared rendering.
changes: `policy_check.describe` renders a policy report as one clause per forbidden class that has an unrefused spelling: the spellings that got through first, then the class's other spellings marked as refused. Classes with every spelling refused are left out.
A cached report that has no per-spelling results falls back to the joined list of unenforced class labels.
The 'runtime policy' check in `abk doctor` and all three of `abk init`'s policy messages use this one rendering, so the operator sees the same text before being asked to run the installation's fix.

The tests build a policy report from the real probe table, with one result per probe row, and check the exact text doctor and init show. They also check that doctor passes when every spelling is refused.
The docs and the changelog bullet describe the per-spelling report.

units.title: A redaction function replaces known secret values by name
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/redaction.py:93 — `gather` reads the process environment directly with `os.environ.get(name)` to resolve the `redact` list, and separately parses the planning root's `.env` with `dotenv_values`. That puts a second environment and `.env` reader outside `settings.py`.
  Consequence: AGENTS.md (Conventions, 'Types are pydantic models'): 'Env config is pydantic-settings (`settings.py`); no `os.environ` reads elsewhere.' The new module breaks this rule. It also re-parses `.env` on its own while the settings module already owns that file (`settings.reload(env_file)`). So the two can disagree, for example on which `.env` was loaded or about a later reload.
  Done when: Move the lookup into `settings.py` as one public function, e.g. `settings.named_value(name: str, env_file: Path | None) -> str` (process environment first, then the `.env` file). `redaction.gather` calls it for each `installation.config.redact` name. `redaction.py` then imports neither `os` nor `dotenv`. `test_each_source_is_held_under_its_own_name` keeps passing unchanged: it covers both a `.env` name (LISTED_VAR) and a process-environment name (FROM_PROCESS).
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/config.py:244 — The change adds a new `RuntimeConfig.env: dict[str, str]` field, commented 'Environment variables the runtime's agent is started with'. Nothing reads it except `redaction.gather`. It is never merged into an agent's environment: `AgentRequest.env` and `child_environment` in runtimes/base.py and claude_code.py's `request.env` only ever carry the gateway key.
  Consequence: An installation that sets `runtimes.claude_code.env: {SOME_VAR: value}` gets a key the schema accepts and the comment says reaches the agent, but the agent never sees it. The comment is false and the setting does nothing. The CHANGELOG bullet also lists `runtimes.<name>.env` as if it were an existing setting. AGENTS.md also requires a new config field to be 'documented in the `abk-config` skill and `docs/configuration.md`'. Neither mentions `runtimes.<name>.env`, and no later task group of this change adds it: task 4.3 documents only `redact`.
  Done when: Make the field true to its comment, or don't add it. Either (a) pass `runtime_config(...).env` into the spawned agent's environment where the runtime builds its request (beside the gateway key in `AgentRequest.env`), with a test that a variable set there is in the agent's environment, and document the key in `docs/configuration.md` and the abk-config skill. Or (b) leave the field out, drop the `runtimes.*.env` source from `gather`, the test and the changelog bullet, and record in the planning repo's change (design/spec) that no such source exists today. Whichever is chosen, no accepted key may claim a behaviour the code lacks.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/redaction.py:76 — `gather` imports the private `installation._resolve` inside the function to resolve each `verify.env` provider one at a time. This reaches into another module's internals. cli/doctor.py:58 already does the same, so it is existing practice, not new.
  Consequence: There are now two outside callers of a private name, so a change to `_resolve` has to be checked against both. Low risk today.
  Done when: Optionally give `Installation` a public method that resolves `verify.env` per name and reports which names failed, e.g. `verify_env_each() -> tuple[dict[str, str], list[str]]`. Have both `redaction.gather` and doctor use it.
- [1.4] tests/test_redaction_set.py:119 — `test_a_minted_gateway_key_is_registered_under_gateway_key` registers into the process-global active redactor, whatever an earlier test in the same worker left there, and never restores it. Other tests also replace the global through `make_installation`.
  Consequence: The test relies on shared global state left by earlier tests. Since keys are random it does not fail today, but the minted key stays in the active set for later tests in that worker.
  Done when: Optionally start the test with `redaction.activate(redaction.Redactor({}))` through a fixture that restores the previous redactor afterwards.

description.summary: Adds a redaction set: activating an installation gathers its known secret values by name, and a function replaces them in any text with `[redacted:<NAME>]`.
changes: Activating an installation now builds a redaction set from four sources: the `verify.env` values, the credential settings, and the variables named in the new `abk.yaml` `redact` list (read from the process environment first, then the planning repo's .env).

A new `redaction` module replaces each known value with `[redacted:<NAME>]` and token-shaped strings with `[redacted:token-shape]`. Values shorter than 8 characters are not replaced, and printing the set shows only names.
When a value's provider fails, the value is left out and one warning names it without showing the value.
Each gateway key minted for a run is registered in the active set under `gateway-key`.
`settings.named_value` is the one place that looks up a named variable from the environment or the .env file.

units.title: Stored and printed output is redacted before it is written
units.feedback:
1.1, 1.3 and 1.4 are done, and each has a test that fails without its fix. In the tier-2 test, the 1500-character cut falls 10 characters inside the value. The builder's reason for redacting the ledger through one redact_leaves call holds: one call logs exactly one line. 1.2 is open on one point only. The rework now runs every string field of a ledger record through redaction, including the fields readers use to identify and classify a record. When redaction fails, a usage record then disappears from accounting. The point below is small and local, so one more round should be enough.

Still open from earlier rounds:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_ledger.py:137 (reported open) — `append_record` redacts the serialized JSON line, not the record's string fields. A failed redaction only replaces `outcome`, so every other string field is written raw.
  Consequence: (a) A known value containing `"` or `\` (passwords often do) appears JSON-escaped in the line, so the exact-substring match misses it and the value is written to the ledger. (b) `record_line` also writes `Span` records (spans.py:50, free-text `cause` and `command`) and `Sample` records. When redaction raises, `model_copy(update={'outcome': WITHHELD})` leaves `Span.cause`/`command` and `UsageRecord`'s other strings raw, and adds a stray `outcome` to a `Sample`. That breaks 'the usage ledger's text fields' and 'When redaction raises, the text SHALL NOT be stored'.
  Done when: Before dumping, redact each top-level `str` field of the record with `redact_text`, e.g. `record.model_copy(update={name: redact_text(value) for name, value in record if isinstance(value, str)})`, then dump that. A field whose redaction failed then becomes the notice on its own, and the whole-line `== WITHHELD` special case goes. Tests: (1) a known value containing `"` in `outcome` gives a line where `json.loads(line)['outcome'] == 'died: [redacted:NAME]'` and the raw value is absent; (2) with `known(broken=True)`, recording a `Span` whose `cause` holds SECRET writes a line without SECRET whose `cause` is the notice.

Required:
- [2.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_ledger.py:137 — When redaction fails, `append_record` replaces every string field with the notice. That includes the fields that identify and classify a record (`kind`, `at`, `unit`, `node`, `session_id`, …), so readers can no longer use the line.
  Consequence: Take a redactor that raises while `record_call` writes a UsageRecord with tokens and cost. The line is written with `kind` set to `[redaction failed: text withheld]`. `grouped_records` (usage_ledger.py:334) skips any line whose `kind` is not `agent`, so `read_ledger`, `usage_report` and serve/metrics silently drop that call's tokens and spend. If such lines were read, every failed record would share the same `unit`, `node` and `session_id`, so they would merge into one call or replace each other. Spans lose their `kind` the same way. Round 1's version replaced only `outcome` and kept the record readable. The spec requires the run to go on with only the text withheld (a tier-2 result keeps its counts and loses only its output). Here, the failure removes the record's numbers instead.
  Done when: In `append_record`, keep the fields that identify and classify a record exactly as written, and redact every other top-level `str` field in the same single `redact_leaves(..., where='ledger')` call. The kept fields are at least `kind`, `at`, `unit`, `node`, `change`, `session_id`, `started` and `ended`. Pipeline-set labels such as `repo`, `tier`, `role`, `model`, `runtime` and `waited` may also be kept. Name the kept set once as a module constant with a comment saying why. Free text (`outcome`, `cause`, `command`) stays redacted. Extend `test_a_failed_redaction_withholds_a_ledger_line`, or add a test: with `known(broken=True)`, `record_call` a UsageRecord that has `input_tokens` set and an `outcome` holding SECRET. Assert that `read_ledger(_ledger_path())` returns a record with the original `unit` and `input_tokens` and `outcome == NOTICE`, that SECRET is absent from the file, and that exactly one failure line is logged.

Optional:
- [2.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:1752 — A multi-command tier-2 run now calls `redact_text` once per command. With a broken redactor it logs one failure line per command, not one per result.
  Consequence: A tier-2 entry with three commands and a raising redactor logs three `redaction failed in tier-2 output` lines. Nothing leaks, but this departs from the spec's 'one log line'. The existing test runs a single command, so it does not catch this.
  Done when: Optional: collect each command's output, then redact all of them in one `redact_leaves([...], where='tier-2 output')` call before slicing. Or accept one line per command and leave it as is.

description.summary: Known secret values are redacted from what the pipeline stores and prints: feedback, run logs, transcripts, printed output, the usage ledger, and the tier-1, tier-2 and verify results. If redaction itself fails, only the affected text is withheld and the run goes on.
changes: Agent transcripts and run logs replace known secret values by name before they are written, including every string inside a tool call's input.

Usage ledger lines redact their free-text fields (such as outcome, cause and command) one field at a time, so values containing quotes or backslashes are still caught. Fields that identify or classify a record (kind, unit, session id and the like) are kept, so a failed redaction never drops a record's tokens or cost from accounting.
Tier-1, tier-2 and verify output is redacted before it is truncated, so a cut can never leave part of a secret. A tier-2 run across several commands is redacted in one pass.
`abk verify` redacts a verification's detail once, so both the printed output and verified.json are clean.

When redaction raises, the affected text is replaced by a withheld notice. Exactly one warning is logged, naming where it happened and the exception type but never the text or the exception message. Counts and verdicts are left as they were.

units.title: Posted text and rework prompts are redacted, and the set's leaks are guarded
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/forges/github.py:326 — `comment_exists` still compares the caller's unredacted body with the redacted body the host now holds, so the duplicate-post check never matches a body that held a secret or a token-shaped string. The same is true in `forges/azure_devops.py:498` (`comment.content == body`) and `forges/local.py:195` (`c["body"] == body`).
  Consequence: Take a reply or close reason whose body contains a known value or a `ghp_…`/`sk-…`-shaped string. `post_comment`/`post_reply` store `[redacted:…]`. Then `pr_replies._held` (pipeline/pr_replies.py:203), `close_pr` (pipeline/wiring.py:1509) and `ResilientForge._landed` (forges/resilient.py:131, which calls `comment_exists` with the original args after an unconfirmed create) all look for the original text, find nothing and post again. Every repeat or retry leaves a duplicate comment on the PR.
  Done when: In all three forges, redact `comment_exists`'s `body` the same way the write methods do: apply the decorator to it, renaming `redacted_writes` to something like `redacted_text` since it no longer covers only writes, or redact `body` at the top of each method. Add a test, at least for the local forge and the GitHub fake host: inside `known()`, `post_comment(body=f"... {SECRET} ...\n{MARKER}")`, then `comment_exists(repo, pr, MARKER, same_body)` returns the posted id and not None.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:488 — `_weak_secrets` re-walks the redaction sources on its own: the `verify.env` loop through `_resolve` and the `redact` loop through `named_value` with the same `env_file` rule. That copies `redaction.gather` (redaction.py:71-91).
  Consequence: The two copies must change together. Adding a source to `gather` (for example the `runtimes.*.env` values the design lists) or changing how a `redact` name is looked up would leave doctor warning about a different set from the one actually redacted. It also resolves every command provider again, so the subprocess runs once more per doctor run, on top of `_verify_env`.
  Done when: Keep one enumeration in `redaction.py`, for example a public `sources(installation)` that yields `(name, value | None)` per source, or have `gather` record the short and unset names on the `Redactor` (names only). Use it from both `gather` and `_weak_secrets`, so doctor reports exactly the names the set skips as too short or unset. `tests/cli/test_doctor_secrets.py` keeps passing unchanged.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1297 — The fix-round prompt (`redact_text(..., where="fix prompt")`) is redacted, but no test covers it. Both cases in `test_rework_redaction.py` go through the requeue/rework path at line 1443.
  Consequence: If the line-1297 call is removed, no test fails. A check-fix agent could again be given feedback saved before this change with a value in it.
  Done when: Add a case to `tests/graph/test_rework_redaction.py` that drives a tier-1 fix round (feedback with SECRET saved outside `known()`, then a failing check that leads to the fix node). Assert that the fix prompt holds `[redacted:NAME]` and that the stored feedback is unchanged.
- [1.4] tests/forges/test_forge_redaction.py:603 — The Azure status test only asserts that SECRET is absent. Unlike the GitHub status test, it never checks that the replacement was sent.
  Consequence: It would still pass if the Azure `post_status` dropped or emptied the description, so it does not show the text was redacted rather than lost.
  Done when: Also assert that `SAID_REPLACED` is in `written`.

description.summary: Text the pipeline sends to a code host and the prompts it gives rework agents are now cleaned of known secret values and token-shaped strings, and `abk doctor` warns about secrets the redaction set cannot protect.
changes: Pull request titles and descriptions, comments, replies and commit statuses go through the redaction set in the GitHub, Azure DevOps and local forges before they are sent or stored. If redaction fails, the text is withheld instead of being posted.
The duplicate-post check (`comment_exists`) redacts the body it compares in the same way. A comment that held a secret is still recognised as already posted, so retries do not post it twice.
Rework and fix-round prompts are built from redacted feedback, while the feedback saved in the unit store stays as it was.
The redaction module now lists each secret source once (`sources`). From that list it builds the set and records which names are too short or unset.
`abk doctor` warns, by name and never by value, about a `verify.env` or `redact` variable under 8 characters and about a `redact` name that is not set.
New guard tests check that the set's values do not leak, and the changelog bullet for this change now covers posted text, rework prompts and the doctor warning.

units.title: The operator can redact history already saved
units.feedback:
The command, docs and changelog cover what group 4 asks for, and the tests drive the real config path: a literal verify.env value through `main`. Three things block approval. The rewrite can lose a running tick's writes. The secret-bearing `.pre-redact` copies sit in a directory the operator commits. The name reporting duplicates the redactor's matching and resolves every provider a second time.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/redact_history_cmd.py:157 — `--apply` rewrites `units.json` with a plain `path.write_text(clean)`. It does not take the store's lock and does not write aside and rename. The ledger, run logs and transcripts get the same unlocked read-then-overwrite.
  Consequence: The state directory is live. `tracks/runner.py:536` says a tick 'may be rewriting right now', and the pipeline runs unattended on a timer. Suppose a tick's `UnitStore._write` lands between this command's `read_text` and `write_text`. The command then writes back the stale text and that store update is lost: a unit's state, PR or pushed sha reverts. The design says this command exists because a bad hand edit of `units.json` loses the store. The store's own unlocked readers can also see a half-written file, which is the case `unit_store.py:431-435` is written to avoid. The same applies to lines appended to the ledger or an open run log or transcript between the read and the write: they are lost.
  Done when: Rewrite `units.json` inside `file_lock(units.json.lock)`, the lock `UnitStore` uses at `unit_store.py:366`; prefer a named `UnitStore` method or accessor over rebuilding the lock path. Re-read the file inside the lock. Write each changed file aside and `os.replace` it into place, as `usage_cmd._write` (`cli/usage_cmd.py:242`) and `UnitStore._write` do. Append-only files cannot be locked against appenders, so make `--apply` refuse with a non-zero exit and a one-line message unless `pipeline.pause.pause_in_force(state_dir)` holds, and say so in `docs/cli.md`. Add a test that `--apply` without a pause in force changes nothing and exits non-zero.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/redact_history_cmd.py:156 — Each `<file>.pre-redact` copy holds the secret. The copies sit in the state directory, which the operator commits, and nothing ignores or flags them. The docs also never say that the earlier `units.json` versions in git history still hold the value.
  Consequence: The planning repo's `.gitignore` template commits `units.json` and does not ignore `runs/transcripts/`. It ignores only locks, `unit-logs/` and the ledger. So `runs/units.json.pre-redact` and `runs/transcripts/*.pre-redact` show up as untracked files. The operator's next `git add runs/`, made to commit the redacted `units.json`, also commits and pushes the original secret. That is a new leak, caused by the command meant to clean up. `docs/cli.md` says the command 'redacts what was saved' and is silent on git history, so an operator can wrongly believe the value no longer exists in the planning repo.
  Done when: Add `*.pre-redact` under the state directory to the packaged planning-repo `.gitignore` template, with the same 'move this line if planning.state_dir is changed' note. With `--apply`, print one line after the file list saying the `.pre-redact` copies hold the original values, must not be committed, and are the operator's to delete. In `docs/cli.md` add one sentence: earlier versions of `units.json` in the planning repo's git history still hold the values and are not rewritten. Extend `test_apply_replaces_the_value_in_every_saved_file_and_keeps_a_copy` to assert the warning line is printed and contains no secret.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/redact_history_cmd.py:135 — `_names_in` re-implements the redactor's matching: a non-empty value, `len >= MIN_LENGTH`, then a substring test. To feed it, `cmd_redact_history` calls `redaction.sources(inst)` again after `redaction.gather(inst)` has already called it.
  Consequence: The matching rule now has two copies, in `Redactor._compile` (`redaction.py:55`) and here. They must change together, and a later change to one makes the dry-run report differ from what `--apply` replaces. Calling `sources()` twice resolves every `verify.env` provider twice, so a `from: command` provider's argv runs twice (`installation.py:179`). If that command returns a different value the second time, a rotating token for example, the reported names and the replaced values disagree. The report also leaves out `token-shape` whenever any named value matched in the same file, so a file holding both reports only the name.
  Done when: Add a public `Redactor` method, for example `found(text) -> tuple[str, ...]`. It returns the sorted names whose values the compiled pattern matches, plus `token-shape` when `_TOKEN_SHAPE` matches. Use it in the command, and delete `_names_in` and the second `sources()` call. Add a test in `tests/` for the redaction module: text holding a known value and a `ghp_`-shaped token yields both names. Add a CLI test: a file holding only a token-shaped string is reported as `token-shape`.

Optional:
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/cli/redact_history_cmd.py:150 — The match runs on raw file text, but `units.json`, the ledger and the transcripts are JSON. A value with a character JSON escapes (`"`, `\`, a control character, or non-ASCII under the default `ensure_ascii`) is stored escaped and is never found.
  Consequence: Such a secret survives `--apply`, and the second dry run reports nothing. The operator is told the history is clean when it is not.
  Done when: Either also search for each value's JSON-escaped form (`json.dumps(value)[1:-1]`) in the JSON files, or say in `docs/cli.md` that a value containing a quote, backslash or non-ASCII character is not found in the JSON files.

description.summary: Adds a temporary `abk redact-history` command that finds known secret values in the pipeline's saved history and, with `--apply` while the pipeline is paused, replaces them safely.
changes: `abk redact-history` builds the same set of known secrets the pipeline uses. For each of `units.json`, the run logs, the transcripts and the usage ledger it prints the secret names found (never the values), plus `token-shape` for unconfigured token-shaped strings. By default it writes nothing.

`--apply` replaces the values, keeps each original as `<file>.pre-redact`, and warns that those copies hold the secrets and must not be committed. It refuses with exit 1 unless a pipeline pause is in force.

`units.json` and the ledger are rewritten under the locks their writers take (new `UnitStore.locked()`, existing `ledger_lock`). Every rewrite goes to a scratch file and is renamed into place, so concurrent store updates and readers are not lost or shown half-written files.
`Redactor.found(text)` reports which configured names, and whether a token shape, `redact` would replace, so the command does not duplicate the matching rule.

The planning-repo `.gitignore` template ignores `runs/**/*.pre-redact`. `docs/cli.md` and the changelog describe the command, the pause requirement, that git history is not rewritten, and that JSON-escaped values are not found.

units.title: A Needs line starts the dependent on the parent's branch

description.summary: A `Needs:` line becomes a plain dependency: a dependent in the same repository starts on the parent's branch once the parent is in review, and the word `merged` is deprecated and reported with a warning.
changes: `link_needs` no longer turns `Needs: ... merged` into a merge gate. On the next tick it clears any gate an earlier version stored, so a dependent in the same repository starts on the parent's branch once the parent is in review. A dependent in another repository still waits for the merge.
`abk tags` and `abk check` print one warning for each `Needs: ... merged` line that names another change, saying the word is deprecated. They still exit zero.
A `merged` line that names the change's own group is still an error, not a warning. One shared parse (`group_needs` → `merged_needs` → `names_own_change`) decides which of the two a line gets.
`Need` records the line number it was read from, so warnings and errors can name the line.
Tests that pinned the old gate behaviour are replaced by tests in tests/cli/test_needs_starts_on_parent_branch.py. These run the real store and `link_needs`, and check the CLI warnings.
A changelog bullet under Unreleased describes the change and the deprecation.

units.title: A Needs line added to a started unit is an ordinary dependency

description.summary: A `Needs:` line added to a unit that has already started now acts as an ordinary dependency: the running unit finishes its current step and then stops, and requeued or sent-back units wait for the parent and restack onto its branch.
changes: A running unit's upstream and base checks now read the unit as stored, not as it was when the run began (`as_stored` in wiring.py). A `Needs:` line linked mid-run lets the current step finish, then stops the unit with `upstream_went_back` or `base_changed`. It resumes on the parent's branch.
Requeueing a failed or held unit whose parent is not yet in review leaves it planned and gated through `waiting_on`. It no longer starts on a stale base.
A unit sent back for rework is parked only when it waits on an unmerged parent in another repository. A same-repo parent that is not yet reviewed leaves the unit's cause as rework.
Wait messages in `abk status`, requeue and sent-back notes now say "to merge" after a parent in another repository.
The `Needs:` line written for a flaky-test fix no longer carries the deprecated `merged` word.
The tick test driver and `graph` fixture moved into tests/tick_driver.py and tests/graph/conftest.py, where the new graph tests share them.

units.title: The merge gate is removed and the graph marks a Needs dependency

description.summary: Removes the merge gate (`merge_before`), so a `Needs:` dependency is now an ordinary dependency: the graph marks it and the stored key is dropped on load.
changes: The merge gate is removed from scheduling. A `Needs:` dependency is applied by `waiting_on`/`ready_units` like any other: a same-repo parent in review releases the dependent onto the parent's branch, and a cross-repo parent must merge first.

A units.json written by an earlier release that still carries `merge_before` loads through both the tick's store and `abk serve`, which no longer fails on it. `StoredUnit` drops the key whatever its value, and the next write leaves it out.

The unit graph draws a `Needs:` dependency as a thick edge labelled `needs` (`==>|needs|`), while the planner's own dependencies stay plain arrows. The mark is recomputed from tasks.md each tick and does not affect scheduling.
On the web unit page the 'Merge gates' list is gone, and each dependency on the Status tab now links to its unit. The API's unit detail and the recorded fixtures no longer carry `merge_gates`.
The docs (architecture, cli, configuration, unit-graph), the abk-authoring and abk-pipeline skills, and the changelog bullet now describe `Needs:` without the merge gate.

units.title: A network or provider outage parks the unit and does not fail it

description.summary: An agent run that ends because the network or the model service is down now parks its unit and retries it later instead of failing it.
changes: The claude runtime raises a typed `NetworkUnavailable` when a failed run's words show a DNS, route or connection failure (strong or weak sign) and no HTTP status. It names the host and port the run called, honouring a base-URL override, and reports the call's spend first. The ACP runtime raises it for a strong sign only.

A new connectivity probe (`pipeline/network_probe.py`) looks up and connects to the called host and to a control group (the forge hosts plus `limits.network_control_hosts`). A weak sign then becomes `network_unavailable`, `service_unavailable` or an ordinary failure. A strong sign parks without asking the probe, and a probe that errors never parks.

A parked unit is `planned` with its step, branch, thread, feedback and round counts kept. It is counted as interrupted, not failed, and resumes at the same step, continuing its session if it had one, after the shared 1/2/5/10/30-minute backoff that the code-host parking also uses (renamed `PARK_BACKOFF`).

`abk status`, the tick log and the Mermaid graph say 'waiting for the network' or 'waiting for the model service' beside 'waiting for the code host'. The graph also shows the step and the time the unit may run again.
An outage during a restack's resolver run aborts the rebase and is deferred, not reported as a conflict, and a scheduled track moves on to its next project.

New limits `network_probe_timeout_seconds` (default 5) and `network_control_hosts` (default `one.one.one.one`, `dns.google`) are validated at load, shown by `abk config --show`, and documented in the docs, skills and changelog.
