units.title: Service 5xx/529 parks the unit up to a cap, and a network outage pauses agent runs

description.summary: A model service that answers 5xx or 529 now parks the unit instead of failing it, up to a configurable cap, and a network outage writes a pause that holds agent runs until a control host connects again.
changes: A Claude run whose closing event carries a status of 500–599, or the CLI words 'API Error: <status>' when the event has none, raises ServiceUnavailable. 4xx, 429 and refusals still come back as a failed result.

A ServiceUnavailable parks the unit as `service_unavailable` without running the probe, and charges no review or check round. The tick records it as interrupted. A run of such parkings is capped by `limits.service_unavailable_attempts` (default 5), and the next one after the cap fails the unit with its error text and step.

Parking a unit for the network writes a `network` pause. While it stands, no unit starts and nothing is planned, and `abk status` shows 'waiting for the network — <reason>'. Only a tick whose control host connects ends it, whatever its deadline, and a probe that cannot run counts as reachable.

The restack conflict resolver, the merge-event restack and the scheduled track phases treat a model-service outage like a network outage. The branch is left alone and the child is deferred, not marked as a conflict, and the track goes on to its next project.
The changelog's outage bullet, docs/agent-runtimes.md, docs/unit-graph.md, docs/architecture.md and the abk-pipeline skill describe the status rule, the cap and the `network` pause.

units.title: A refused read with headroom allows a start on an estimate

description.summary: When the usage endpoint refuses or cannot be read, the usage guard now allows starts based on an estimate built from the last good reading kept, instead of pausing, while that estimate leaves ample room.
changes: When the endpoint cannot be asked (a refusal, a cool-down, an error, or the minimum interval), each window is estimated as the kept reading plus a per-unit allowance for every unit that has spent or been admitted since. A window that has reset is estimated from its reset plus the most it could have climbed since.

A start is allowed only while both windows' estimates plus `usage_headroom_margin_pct` stay under their thresholds, and at most `usage_estimate_max_starts` units start on one reading. A good read clears the admitted list.

Only a start that actually happens is recorded: the per-step gate in the build graph and each track name themselves through a `starting` context. The round's decision, the resume time and status record nothing, so a unit's later ledger record is counted once.

New settings: `usage_unit_allowance_pct` per window (10 for the session, 2 for the week), `usage_headroom_margin_pct` (5) and `usage_estimate_max_starts` (3). They are documented in docs/configuration.md, the abk-config skill and docs/architecture.md.
`abk status` prints the estimate line from the reading held, with no call, when the reading is past its keep time and the endpoint cannot be asked. Refusal reasons name the estimate.
The cool-down kept in the cache file is now read through one shared helper by the guard, status and `rate_limit_note`.

units.title: A refusal that asks for no wait does not widen the interval

description.summary: A usage-endpoint refusal that names a retry time of zero no longer widens how long a usage reading is kept, and the ceiling on that time drops from 60 to 30 minutes.
changes: When working out how long to keep a usage reading, a refusal with `Retry-After: 0` is skipped. Refusals with no `Retry-After` or an unreadable one still double the time, and a longer retry time a refusal names is still respected.
`usage_cache_max_minutes` now defaults to 30 instead of 60. A higher configured value is still honoured.
The `abk status` line for the usage cache now says when the last refusal asked for no wait and did not widen the time.
The cool-down after a refusal whose retry time is zero or unreadable stays the five-minute default, and tests now pin this.
The architecture doc, configuration doc, abk-config skill and changelog describe the new default and the no-wait rule.

units.title: A dependency that would close a cycle is dropped or refused
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/cycles.py:98 — `drop_cycle_edges` checks the whole stored graph for a cycle, including cycles that have nothing to do with the plan. When it finds one, it returns early, drops no planner edges and reports that cycle as this plan's error.
  Consequence: The spec expects the store can already hold a cycle that an older version wrote (the scenario 'A cycle already stored'). Take stored planned units `old-a/1 -> old-b/1 -> old-a/1` and plan an unrelated change `add` whose planner edge `add/1 -> other/1` closes a cycle with stored `other/1 -> add/1`. `find_cycle(graph)` returns the old-a/old-b cycle first. The plan keeps the edge that closes the cycle, so the new deadlock is stored, which breaks 'A planner edge never closes a cycle with stored work'. `plan_all` also logs `add: cannot be ordered ... old-a/1 -> old-b/1 -> old-a/1` and sets `PlanResult.cycle`, so `abk replan add` exits 1 over a cycle in another change. While that one stale cycle sits in the store, every plan of every change goes unguarded and every replan fails.
  Done when: Check the advisory edges with `path_between` whether or not the fixed edges contain a cycle (`path_between` already handles cycles through `seen`). Put in `CycleDrops.cycle` only a fixed-edge cycle that passes through one of the plan's units, for example by running `find_cycle` only over the nodes reachable from the plan's unit ids, or by checking `path_between(graph, u, u)` for each plan unit. Add a test in tests/pipeline/test_cycles.py: stored `old-a/1 <-> old-b/1` plus stored `other/1 -> add/1`, and a plan `add/1 -> other/1`. Assert that `add/1`'s edge is dropped, naming `add/1 -> other/1 -> add/1`, and that `result.cycle == ()`. Add a second case where an unrelated stored cycle and a plan with no closing edge give `cycle == ()`, the plan unchanged.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/cycles.py:54 — The change adds a second cycle finder (`find_cycle`, plus `path_between`) next to the DFS in `_check_dependencies` (src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/planner.py:429-449). The two can drift apart in how they visit and name a cycle.
  Consequence: Two cycle detectors with different output formats have to be kept in step. Task 1.8 and the design ask for a new `find_cycle` and say to leave the in-plan check as it is, so this is not a required finding.
  Done when: Optionally have `_check_dependencies` call `find_cycle` over the plan's own edges and raise the same PlannerError message.
- [1.3] tests/cli/test_link_needs_cycles.py:71 — `test_a_refused_needs_is_logged_once_in_each_pass` calls `link_needs` twice without `reported` and asserts two lines. What it pins is that a refusal is logged again in each new pass. It does not show 'once in a pass'; test_tick_refused_needs.py does that.
  Consequence: The name tells a reader that once-per-pass suppression is tested here, which is not true.
  Done when: Rename it to something like `test_each_call_without_a_pass_set_logs_the_refusal_again`, or pass one shared `reported` set to both calls and assert one line.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:3535 — `cmd_replan` exits non-zero on any refusal `link_needs` returns, including refusals for changes the replan did not touch.
  Consequence: A `Needs:` cycle between two other changes makes every `abk replan <any change>` exit 1 until someone edits that tasks.md. The spec's wording allows this, but it can make a successful replan of an unrelated change look like a failure.
  Done when: Optionally count only refusals whose unit or cycle includes a unit of `to_plan`, or print a line explaining why the exit code is non-zero.

description.summary: Keeps the unit graph free of new dependency cycles. Planner-proposed edges that would close a cycle with stored or declared work are dropped, and `Needs:` edges that would close one are refused.
changes: Adds `pipeline/cycles.py`. `find_cycle` gives deterministic cycle detection over any dependency graph. `drop_cycle_edges` tries a plan's advisory planner edges one at a time against stored and declared `Needs:` edges, ignores finished units, and drops each edge that would close a cycle, naming that cycle.

During planning, dropped planner edges are logged. A cycle made only of `Needs:` and stored edges that runs through the plan's own units is reported as an error while the plan still stands. A stale cycle elsewhere in the store neither disables the guard nor counts against an unrelated plan.

`link_needs` checks each `Needs:` edge before adding it. If the edge would close a cycle, it refuses it, leaves the unit's other dependencies and its stored edges alone, and logs the refusal once per pass. It returns the refusals.
`abk replan` exits non-zero when the plan reports a fixed-edge cycle, or when a refused `Needs:` cycle runs through a change being replanned. A tick logs these and carries on.
A replan replaces an unstarted unit's stored dependencies with the plan's, so a stale cycle-closing edge goes away. A started unit's dependencies are never changed.

units.title: A cycle is reported before planning, in the status, and avoided by the planner
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/cycles.py:170 — `deadlocks` builds its graph from every unit that is not merged, closed or unplanned, using the raw `depends_on` edges. So a cycle that runs through a unit that is running, in review, or satisfied gets reported as units that 'wait on each other and cannot start', even when one of them can start.
  Consequence: Take `a/1` in review in repo app, depending on `b/1`, and `b/1` planned in app, depending on `a/1`. `waiting_on(b/1)` (units.py:532-534) is empty because a same-repo parent in REVIEWED does not block, so `b/1` is in the ready queue. Yet `abk status` prints `deadlocked: a/1 -> b/1 -> a/1 (… cannot start)` and also lists `b/1` as 'in the cycle'. Worse, when a pass starts nothing for a real reason (the queue limit, a failed parent), `_nothing_started_reason` (cli/pipeline.py:1757) returns 'nothing can start: deadlocked: …' in place of the true reason. The spec scopes this to 'planned units wait on each other'.
  Done when: Make `deadlocks` take only units in PLANNED state, with edges to the parents `waiting_on(unit, units)` returns, so that a cycle is reported only when every member is truly stopped from starting by the next member. Add a test in tests/cli/test_deadlock_status.py: `a/1` in_review and `b/1` planned in the same repo, depending on each other. Assert that status prints no `deadlocked:` line and that a pass which starts nothing because the queue is full still says 'queue is full'.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/cycles.py:205 — `needs_cycle` re-implements `names_own_change` (work_graph.py:537) inline as `need.change != change.lower()`. It also uses the un-lowercased directory name for source nodes but the lowercased `need.change` for target nodes.
  Consequence: There are two copies of the 'a Needs: names its own change' rule, and they must change together. A change directory with any uppercase letter produces source nodes (`Foo group 1`) that never match target nodes (`foo group 1`), so a real cycle through it goes unreported.
  Done when: Call `names_own_change(need, path)` to skip a `Needs:` line on the change's own group, and build every node from `path.parent.name.lower()` so source and target names agree.
- [1.3] docs/unit-graph.md:1 — Task 2.10 is not done. The branch adds no 'Cycles' section to docs/unit-graph.md, does not touch the planning paragraph of docs/architecture.md (around line 130), adds nothing about `deadlocked:` to the status section of src/agent_build_kit/skills/abk-pipeline/SKILL.md, and says nothing in the `Needs:` section of the abk-authoring skill about a cycle being an error that `abk tags` finds.
  Consequence: The group's tasks list these docs explicitly. AGENTS.md says docs describing code a change builds belong in that change's tasks so the two land together. Without them, an operator reading the abk-pipeline skill has no explanation for the new `deadlocked:` status line, and an author has no guidance on the new `abk tags` error.
  Done when: Add the four doc edits named in task 2.10: a 'Cycles' section in docs/unit-graph.md (dropped planner edge, refused `Needs:`, `abk tags`/`abk check` error, `deadlocked:` in status, nothing broken automatically), a sentence in docs/architecture.md's planning paragraph, a `deadlocked:` entry in the abk-pipeline skill's status section, and a line in the abk-authoring skill's `Needs:` section saying a cycle across changes is an error that `abk tags` reports.
- [1.4] tests/cli/test_needs_cycle_tags.py:400 — Two negative cases the tasks name have no test. Task 2.1 says 'a change whose `Needs:` lines form a chain or a diamond is clean'. Task 2.5 says 'a chain of planned units with no cycle is never reported as deadlocked'. Neither is tested.
  Consequence: A `needs_cycle` or `deadlocks` that reports a shared parent or a diamond as a cycle (for example by treating a node it has already finished as still being on the current path) would pass every test on this branch. Every positive test has a true cycle, and the only negative status test removes an edge from a two-cycle.
  Done when: In test_needs_cycle_tags.py, add a test with three changes whose `Needs:` form a chain (c needs b, b needs a) and a diamond (d needs b and c, both need a). Assert that `abk tags --all` exits 0 and prints no 'Needs: cycle'. In test_deadlock_status.py, store a chain and a diamond of planned units and assert that status prints no line containing 'deadlocked'.

- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:537 — The per-unit `  deadlocked: …` and `  w/1 … waits on …` lines are printed after `_ready_queue_lines`, but outside its output. When nothing is ready, the 'ready queue (start order):' header is never printed, so the indented lines appear under whatever was logged before them.
  Consequence: In the common deadlock case (nothing else ready), status shows indented lines with no heading. They read as belonging to the previous section.
  Done when: Either give these lines their own heading (for example 'cannot start:') when there are any, or fold them into `_ready_queue_lines` so they always sit under a header.
- [1.6] tests/pipeline/test_planner_cycle_rule.py:524 — The test splits the prompt on blank lines. The rules list is one paragraph, so `rule[0]` is the whole rules block, and `"through" in rule[0]` can be satisfied by any other rule's wording.

- [1.7] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:1650 — `_deadlocked_unit_lines` reports only units that depend directly on a cycle member. A unit two steps behind (waiting on `w/1`, which waits on `a/1`) gets no reason.
  Consequence: A unit transitively behind a deadlock shows no deadlock reason in status.

description.summary: Finds dependency cycles between units and between changes' `Needs:` lines. It reports them before planning and in `abk status`, and stops the planner from creating them.
changes: `abk tags` and `abk check` report as an error a cycle formed by the `Needs:` lines of two or more changes together with the order of each change's consecutive groups. The error appears under each change on the cycle, and change names are compared without regard to case.

`abk status` prints a `deadlocked: A -> B -> A` line for each cycle of planned units that block each other. Under a `cannot start:` heading it then lists each unit in the cycle and each planned unit waiting on one, directly or through other units. A unit that can start, such as one whose same-repo parent is in review, is never reported.
When a tick's pass starts nothing, it gives `nothing can start: deadlocked: …` ahead of any other reason, but only for a true deadlock, so reasons such as 'queue is full' still show otherwise.
The planner prompt says an unstarted unit must not depend on the change being planned, even through other units.

`docs/unit-graph.md` gains a Cycles section. `docs/architecture.md` and the abk-pipeline and abk-authoring skills now describe the dropped or refused edges, the `abk tags` error and the `deadlocked:` status line.

units.title: A fresh reading in Claude Code's own cache is used before the endpoint is asked
units.feedback:
The step itself is in the right place: before `_too_soon` and `fresh()` in `decide_start`, with `claude-json` left out wherever `cache` is. Two things block approval. First, the status command prints the block's age twice. Second, the freshness test lets a block beat a newer reading of the guard's own when `usage_claude_cache_minutes` is set above the cache time. Both fixes are small. I ran the five changed or new test files (81 passed); I did not run the full suite.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_guard.py:834 — `_fresh_claude_block` puts the age into `UsageReading.source` (`"claude.json, 6m old"`). `abk status` already adds the age itself (`cli/pipeline.py:464`: `f"usage: {_usage_line(reading)} ({reading.source}, {age}m old)"`), so the status line comes out as `(claude.json, 6m old, 6m old)`.
  Consequence: The spec's 'The label' scenario requires the status command to end `(claude.json, 6m old)`. A fresh block makes `held_usage()` and `refreshed_usage()` return this reading, so `abk status` prints the age twice. The same applies after `_noted`: `claude.json, 6m old (rate limited until …), 6m old`. The CHANGELOG and architecture.md say the status line shows `(claude.json, 6m old)`, which is false. The only status test (`test_the_status_command_s_readings_prefer_a_fresh_block_without_a_call`) checks `"claude.json" in reading.source` and never looks at the printed line, so the duplication goes unnoticed.
  Done when: Leave the block's `source` as `claude.json` and add the age only to the decision's reason. Rename `_labelled` to take the age, or format `(claude.json, {minutes}m old)` there, so `decide_start`'s reason still ends `(claude.json, 6m old)`. The status command's existing `({source}, {age}m old)` then prints `(claude.json, 6m old)`. Update `test_usage_one_authority.py:152` back to `"claude.json"`. Add a test that runs the status command (as `tests/cli/test_status_usage_estimate.py` does) with an old guard reading and a block fetched six minutes ago. It should assert the usage line ends `(claude.json, 6m old)` exactly once, and that no endpoint call is made.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_guard.py:826 — The guard's own reading only takes precedence while it is younger than the kept interval. Once it is older, any block within `usage_claude_cache_minutes` wins, even a block observed earlier than the guard's reading.
  Consequence: The spec requirement 'A fresh reading in Claude Code's own cache is used before the endpoint is asked' says the guard SHALL decide from the block only when it 'is fresher than the reading kept in the guard's own cache, a tie going to the guard's own'. Example: `usage_claude_cache_minutes: 30`, `usage_cache_minutes: 15`, a guard reading 20m old at session 90% and a block 25m old at 50%. The older, lower block allows the start, although usage only rises within a window. The test `test_a_window_above_the_stale_age_does_not_use_a_block_older_than_it` (lines 147-151) pins this wrong behaviour: a 50m-old block beats a 40m-old guard reading and is asserted to decide.
  Done when: In `_fresh_claude_block`, return None whenever `held` is not None, has not passed a reset, and `block.observed_at <= held.observed_at`, whatever the held reading's age. Drop the `current_cache_interval(...).kept` clause and the now-unused `calls_file` parameter. In the test at line 147, make the guard reading older than the block (e.g. 55m) so the block still decides. Add a case with window 30, a guard reading 20m old and a block 25m old: the block is not used and the guard's own path runs, and no `claude-json` line is recorded.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_guard.py:822 — Every `decide_start`, `held_usage` and `refreshed_usage` now parses all of `~/.claude.json`. Before this change it was read only as the fallback after a failed call.
  Consequence: The file holds Claude Code's per-project history and can be large, so each start decision in a tick now parses it. This is a cost, not a wrong result.
  Done when: Optional: when `usage_claude_cache_minutes` is 0, return before reading the file, so turning the step off also removes the read.

description.summary: The usage guard now decides from a fresh reading in Claude Code's own cache, when that reading is newer than the guard's own, before asking the usage endpoint.
changes: `decide_start` checks Claude Code's cached usage block before the minimum-interval and endpoint paths. When the block is younger than `usage_claude_cache_minutes` (capped at the stale age), comes from the current window, and is strictly newer than the guard's kept reading, it decides the start with no call. It is recorded as a `claude-json` call.
A block no newer than the guard's own unreset reading is never used, however old that reading is, because usage only rises within a window.
When `usage_claude_cache_minutes` is 0, the step is skipped and Claude Code's cache file is not read.
`held_usage` and `refreshed_usage`, which the status command uses, also prefer a fresh block, so `abk status` shows `(claude.json, Nm old)` with the age once and makes no endpoint call.
A start decided from a block ends its reason with `(claude.json, Nm old)`, both when it allows the start and when it refuses it.

units.title: A failed unit waiting on another unit does not hold a place

description.summary: A failed unit that is waiting on another unit no longer holds a place under `limits.max_units_in_progress`, so failed waiters cannot fill the queue and keep their prerequisites from starting.
changes: `in_progress` no longer counts a failed unit whose `waiting_on` set is non-empty. The unit stays failed, the pipeline never requeues it, and it counts again once nothing it waits on is pending. New helpers `failed_waiting` and `failed_waiting_units` in `pipeline/units.py` name this case.
The "queue is full" line in `abk status` and the tick log adds "N failed waiting not counted" after the blocked count.
`abk status` prints a `failed, waiting on <units>: <unit> (<repo>)` line for each such unit, after the blocked lines.
The Mermaid graph labels such a unit `failed, waiting on <units>`.

The architecture, configuration and unit-graph docs, the abk-config and abk-pipeline skills, and the changelog describe the new counting rule. The shared test helper `status_lines` takes an optional in-progress limit and records unit states.

units.title: The policy step, --policy-only and --policy-fix; doctor shares the probe

description.summary: Makes `abk init`'s runtime policy check a guided step. The step can run alone on an existing installation through `--policy-only`, and `abk doctor` reports the same results.
changes: `abk init` runs a guided policy step right after abk.yaml is written, so anything it records lands in init's commit. Before a fix runs, the step prints the fix and each unrefused class and spelling. It then runs the fix with its output on the terminal, checks again, and reports what is refused now. A fix that changes nothing is reported as such.

Runtimes declare `policy_check_prompts_agent` (True for the protocol runtime, False for Claude Code). When a check would send the agent a prompt, init says it spends tokens and asks first. Declining records `runtimes.<name>.policy: unchecked`.
An agent with no known fix gets a three-way choice that is asked again until it is answered: rely on abk's own protocol layer, supply a fix command (recorded as `policy_fix`), or continue unchecked.

New flags: `abk init --policy-only` runs only the policy step on an existing installation and exits 0, 1 or 2. `--policy-fix ARGV` validates, records and uses a fix. `--run-policy-fix` lets `--yes` run a configured fix, which `--yes` alone never does.

`abk doctor` lists other usable runtimes and warns when a selected entry is documented only, using a shared `DOCUMENTED_ONLY` prefix and `Candidate.documented_only`. For an entry marked unchecked it warns without probing, and its hint says to run `--policy-only` and then remove the marker.
docs/cli.md, docs/agent-runtimes.md, the abk-config skill and the changelog describe the step, the flags and their exit codes.

units.title: The real abk init against a stand-in agent

description.summary: Live-stack tests that run the real `abk init` as a process against a recording stand-in agent, checking the runtime choice, model selection, confirmation and policy-fix flows without any model call.
changes: Runs `abk init` on an isolated machine (its own PATH, HOME and config dir) with a stand-in protocol agent installed under a known agent's program name. The tests check that the runtime list puts the usable agent first, gives reasons for the others, and records the choice in abk.yaml.

Checks that models advertised by the agent are offered with the current one as the default and the choice is written. An agent that advertises no models leaves the roles empty, and answering no at the confirmation writes nothing.
Checks that `--yes` with several usable agents, or with none, names the problem and writes nothing.

Drives `abk init --policy-only --policy-fix` against a scratch agent configuration. A fix that closes an unrefused spelling is reported as refused afterwards and exits 0; a fix that changes nothing says so and exits 1.

Every run asserts the stand-in was sent no prompt, so the suite spends no tokens. The conventions-workspace init test now runs with a `claude` stub on its own path, so it no longer depends on the host's agents.

units.title: A planning attempt is not spent on an outage, and a failed plan keeps its reason
units.feedback:
The unit covers tasks 4.1 to 4.9: the wait record, the due rule in `plan_all` and `_needs_planning`, the network pause and its release, the bounded and redacted reason, and the replan and status lines. The new tests and the rest of `tests/cli/` pass (817 passed). Two things block approval. First, the service-wait cap counts waits that came through the probe path. Second, the test fakes repeat the outage error builders that already exist in the unit-parking tests.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:2412 — `_plan_wait` caps a `ServiceUnavailable` against `waits`, but `waits` also counts network waits and probe-path service waits. So waits from the probe path count toward the `limits.service_unavailable_attempts` cap.
  Consequence: Take `service_unavailable_attempts: 3`. A change records three network waits (a strong sign, or a weak sign the probe sorts), and then the planner returns a 529. `waited` is 3, which is not below the cap, so `_plan_wait` returns None and the 529 is recorded as an ordinary failed attempt on its first status. Tasks 4.3 and 2.3 say waits from the probe path are not capped and that only the fourth *consecutive* status is a failure. The unit path follows that rule: `store.count_service_attempt` (pipeline.py:3356) is only incremented in the `ServiceUnavailable` branch. The plan path does not. `test_a_wait_found_by_the_probe_is_not_capped` never mixes the two kinds, so it misses this.
  Done when: Give the plan record its own count of status waits, e.g. `service_waits`. Increment it only when the error is a `ServiceUnavailable`, carry it across waits of the same hash, and compare that count, not `waits`, against the cap. `waits` stays as it is for the backoff. Add a test with the cap at 3: one or more network waits (strong sign), then three `ServiceUnavailable` calls, each past its `until`. All three must be recorded as `service` waits with `attempts` 0, and only the next `ServiceUnavailable` is an ordinary failed attempt. Update the docs/architecture.md sentence on the cap if the field is named there.
- [1.2] tests/cli/plan_outage_fakes.py:16 — `API`, `WORDS` and `network()` copy `API`, `WORDS` and `outage()` in tests/pipeline/test_network_outage_parking.py:36-41 word for word. `service()` repeats the `ServiceUnavailable` builder in tests/pipeline/test_service_outage_parking.py:45.
  Consequence: There are now two copies of the outage fakes, the CLI's error text and the API host, for the plan path and the unit path. A change to how a runtime words or types the error (for example the claude_output 'API Error' wording the earlier follow-up asks to pin to a recorded fixture) must be made in both copies, or the two paths are tested against different inputs.
  Done when: Keep one copy. Either make plan_outage_fakes.py (or a neutral shared module such as tests/outage_fakes.py) the only home of `API`, `WORDS`, the network-error builder and the service-error builder, and have test_network_outage_parking.py and test_service_outage_parking.py import from it. Or have plan_outage_fakes import `outage`, `API` and `WORDS` from test_network_outage_parking, as test_plan_outage_wait.py already does for `Probe`. Assertions do not change.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:1017 — `_release_network_waits` reads planned.json with `_planned_hashes` outside `planned.lock` and then writes whole records back through `record_plans`, so it can overwrite a record that changed in between.
  Consequence: Suppose `abk replan feature` records `ok: True` between this function's read and its write. The tick then writes back the old waiting record with `until` set to now, and the next round plans the change again, an extra model call. `record_plans` says it exists so that "a command beside a planning pass loses neither's update".
  Done when: Do the read-filter-write under the same lock. For example, let `record_plans` (or a sibling) take a function from the current records to the updates, so the filter on `waiting == "network"` runs on what is read under the lock.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:3810 — `_plan_state` indexes `record['since']` and `record['until']` and parses them directly. `_plan_waiting` tolerates a missing or unparsable `until`; this function does not.
  Consequence: A hand-edited or truncated planned.json entry with `waiting` but no `since` makes `abk status` and a bare `abk replan` raise KeyError or ValueError, while the tick treats the same record as due.
  Done when: Read both with `.get` and show the state without the time when it is missing or unreadable, matching `_plan_waiting`.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:2576 — Once one change records a network wait and writes the network pause, `plan_all` goes on to call the planner for each remaining change in the same round.
  Consequence: During a confirmed network outage, a round with several changes to plan makes one failing planner call (and possibly one probe) per change, and records a wait for each. Under the pause the next tick would make none of these calls.
  Done when: Optionally, once a `network` wait is recorded in a round, skip the remaining changes as `skipped`. They are planned on the tick that clears the pause.

description.summary: When planning a change hits an internet or model-service outage, the plan waits instead of using up an attempt, and a plan that fails keeps a short, redacted reason.
changes: A planner error caused by an outage (an HTTP 5xx/529 status, or a network failure that is either a strong sign or confirmed by the control probe) is recorded as a wait with its cause, start time and next try. The attempt count is not touched, and the change is not planned again until the next try is due.

Status waits are counted on their own (`service_waits`) and capped by `limits.service_unavailable_attempts`. After the cap, the next status error counts as an ordinary failed attempt. Network waits are neither counted toward the cap nor capped.

A network wait writes a `network` pause. The tick whose probe clears that pause makes every network-waiting plan due at once, through a read-modify-write of the plan records under their lock (`update_plans`). The other changes in the same round are skipped until then, except under a forced replan.
A failed plan keeps a bounded, redacted reason. Ordinary failures, successes, edits to tasks.md and `abk replan --forget` end a wait.
`abk status` and `abk replan` show a waiting change as waiting for the network or the model service, with its times and with attempts marked as not used. A record missing its times is still shown.

units.title: The recommended policy is one table in the kit

description.summary: Adds the kit's recommended command policy for build agents as one tested table of deny globs per forbidden class, with its glob dialect, coverage and gaps documented.
changes: runtimes/recommended_policy.py adds RECOMMENDED. For each forbidden class (merging a PR via `gh pr merge`, via the raw API or via GraphQL; amending a commit; pushing to main/master; force pushing, which the push globs cover) it lists the deny globs and the samples the globs must refuse and must allow.

It adds a reference matcher `matches`, with the glob dialect stated in DIALECT: fnmatch, case-insensitive, anchored, checked against the whole command and each segment of a compound command. It also adds `patterns(extra)`, which returns the recommended globs followed by an installation's extras, with none repeated.

It records the classes it leaves uncovered (UNCOVERED, each with a reason), the commands the globs refuse even though they are harmless (KNOWN_FALSE_POSITIVES), and the commands that do a forbidden thing without being caught (KNOWN_GAPS).

Tests hold the table to the policy check's spellings table: every row with a glob reader must be a refused sample of its class, the commands a build needs must be allowed, and every class the check attempts without a glob must be listed as uncovered.
docs/agent-runtimes.md gains a 'Recommended policy' section, and CHANGELOG.md gains one Unreleased bullet for it.

units.title: abk policy patterns and show, and the installation's extra patterns

description.summary: Adds `abk policy patterns` and `abk policy show`, which print the kit's recommended deny policy for a build agent, and a per-runtime `policy_extra` list in abk.yaml for the installation's own extra patterns.
changes: `abk policy patterns` prints the recommended command globs one per line, as a JSON array or as a YAML list. Each format loads back to the same list, and an empty selection prints an empty list, never a blank line.

`--class LABEL` (repeatable) limits the output to the named classes. An unknown label exits 2 and lists the valid labels. A class whose globs belong to another class prints no globs and a note on stderr naming the class that covers it.

`--extra` adds the selected runtime's `runtimes.<runtime>.policy_extra` patterns. With no loadable installation it exits 2 with the underlying config error, for example naming a blank `policy_extra` entry.

`abk policy show` prints each class with its globs, the classes the policy does not cover and why, the known false positives, and the glob dialect. It also says that `abk doctor`, not this command, runs the policy check.
abk.yaml gains `runtimes.<runtime>.policy_extra`, a validated list of non-blank globs. It is documented in docs/configuration.md, docs/cli.md, the abk-config skill and the changelog.

units.title: The apply engine and the first known agent's applier

description.summary: Adds an engine that merges the kit's recommended deny patterns into a known agent's own YAML configuration by inserting lines into the original text, and gives the first known agent a verified recipe for it.
changes: A known-agent row can carry an optional `ApplyPolicy` descriptor: the home variable and its default, the config file, the format, the deny-list key path, the YAML version used to read bare scalars, an optional recommended toolset, and how the row was verified. Only the first known agent has one.

`runtimes/policy_apply.py` adds the recommended patterns (then any extras) that the deny list lacks. It parses the file read-only and splices the new items into the original text, copying the last item's indentation and quote style. A missing list or section is inserted as a small block. Every other byte, including line endings, stays the same.

Shapes it cannot handle by insertion (an inline list, a single string, null, an alias, an anchor or tag, a flow mapping, several documents, a non-mapping top level, a file that does not parse) are refused with the file, key and reason, and nothing is written. Every splice is parsed again and written only if it equals the original plus the added patterns.

Writes back up the original once to `<file>.abk-backup` and go through an atomic temporary file that keeps the file's mode. A dry run returns the diff without writing. An absent file is reported, naming the home variable, and is never created. A second run changes nothing.
The agent's recommended toolset is replaced only when asked, by editing that list's lines as text, and is reported from and to.
Adds `ruamel-yaml` as a dependency, a docs section in `docs/agent-runtimes.md`, and a changelog sentence noting that no command runs the engine yet.

units.title: abk policy apply, a configuration-aware show, and doctor's fix text

description.summary: Adds `abk policy apply`, which merges the kit's recommended deny globs into a known agent's own configuration. `abk policy show` now compares that configuration with the recommendation, and `abk doctor` points at `abk policy apply` when the agent has an applier.

Exit codes: 0 when written, nothing to change, or a dry run; 1 when declined; 2 for usage or configuration problems.

`abk policy show` now reads the selected agent's configuration and lists the missing globs by class, plus any missing `policy_extra` entries. It counts entries that are not the kit's and shows the toolset recommendation against the current list. An absent, unreadable or wrong-shaped file is reported by its path.

Choosing the agent: the agent comes from the runtime's command through the new `known_agents.agent_for_command`, or from `--agent` for a wrapper the table does not recognise. `--runtime` picks another configured runtime. An unknown name, or no installation without `--agent`, is a usage error.

When a class is unenforced, `abk doctor` suggests, in order: the installation's `policy_fix`, the runtime's own advice, `abk policy apply` for an agent with an applier, then `abk policy patterns` plus the `policy_fix` key to set.

The engine's `held()` now refuses a deny value that is present but not a list, instead of treating it as empty. A write that fails after confirmation is reported as an error with exit 2 rather than a traceback.
docs/cli.md, docs/agent-runtimes.md and the abk-config skill describe the new command and doctor's fix order.

units.title: abk init's policy step offers the kit's recommended policy
units.feedback:
The code path follows the design's order: the installation's policy_fix first, then the kit's applier, then the existing choices. It is shared by the end of `abk init` and `--policy-only`, and the tests cover 5.1–5.4 without clock, thread or port hazards. Two things block approval. Task 5.6's documentation was not done, and the step that writes the configuration and reports it is copied from `abk policy apply`.

Required:
- [1.1] docs/cli.md:518 — Task 5.6 is not done. Only the changelog bullet was written; docs/cli.md, docs/init.md, docs/agent-runtimes.md and the abk-pipeline skill do not describe the built-in fix in init's policy step.
  Consequence: Task 5.6 requires these documents. docs/cli.md:518-530 now states something false: it says the step offers a fix only when `runtimes.<name>.policy_fix` is set, and that 'An agent with no fix offers three choices'. An agent with an applier is now offered the kit's recommended policy instead. The three-choice menu also gained the `abk policy patterns` line, which the doc does not list. 'With `--yes` a configured fix is only printed' does not say that the same rule now covers the built-in fix.
  Done when: docs/cli.md's policy-step bullet should give the order: the configured `policy_fix`, then (with no policy_fix and an agent the kit can write to) the kit's recommended policy. For that fix the step shows the file and the diff, asks 'apply the kit's recommended policy? [y/N]', applies the deny list only, checks again and prints what is refused. The doc should say that an absent configuration prints 'not found' and `abk policy patterns`; that the toolset is left alone and `abk policy apply --toolset` is named; and that the unknown-agent menu mentions `abk policy patterns`. The `--yes`/`--run-policy-fix` bullet should say the built-in fix also needs `--run-policy-fix`. docs/init.md's description of the policy step needs the same order. docs/agent-runtimes.md needs the passage 'a machine with the kit and the agent and nothing else' going from a failing check to a passing one through `abk init --policy-only`. The abk-pipeline skill's list of init's policy flags needs to say what `--run-policy-fix` now authorises and name `abk policy apply`/`patterns`.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/init.py:401 — `_apply_builtin` copies `cmd_policy_apply`'s write-and-report block. Both call `policy_apply.apply(descriptor, home, extra[, toolset])`, catch `(ApplyRefused, OSError)` and print to stderr, then print 'backed up the original to …' and 'added N patterns to …'. Compare init.py:401-408 with cli/policy_cmd.py:250-257. The resolve-home and dry-run/ABSENT/UNCHANGED steps before them follow the same sequence (init.py:375-391 against policy_cmd.py:217-233).
  Consequence: There are now two copies of how the kit writes the recommended policy and tells the person what it did. A change to what is reported after writing (for example, naming the classes the added globs cover, or a new error that must be caught) has to be made in both. If it is made in one, `abk init` and `abk policy apply` report the same write differently.
  Done when: Extract one function in cli/policy_cmd.py (or runtimes/policy_apply.py, if it does not print) that applies the policy and prints the backup and 'added N patterns' lines, returning the result or None on ApplyRefused/OSError after printing the error. Both `cmd_policy_apply` and `_apply_builtin` call it. Existing tests stay green unchanged.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/init.py:380 — The dry-run `policy_apply.apply(..., dry_run=True)` catches only ApplyRefused. An OSError while reading the agent's configuration (an unreadable file, or a home that is a file) propagates out of `abk init` as a traceback.
  Consequence: The rest of the step is built so that init carries on when a check cannot be had (`_policy` swallows and reports). An unreadable agent configuration aborts init, including a full init before research, propose and the commit.
  Done when: Catch `(ApplyRefused, OSError)` around the dry run as well, print the error and the `abk policy patterns` hint, and return False.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/cli/init.py:375 — `_apply_builtin` reloads abk.yaml and builds a second Installation just to get `env_file`, though `_policy_step` already built `Installation(loaded, planning)` at line 425.
  Consequence: This is an extra parse of the config, and a second place that constructs the installation from the file.
  Done when: Keep the Installation that `_policy_step` builds and pass its `env_file` (or the installation itself) to `_apply_builtin`.

description.summary: When the agent refuses too little and the installation has no fix of its own, `abk init`'s policy step now offers to apply the kit's recommended deny policy as the fix, sharing one apply-and-report path with `abk policy apply`.
changes: When the runtime does not refuse a forbidden command class, the policy step picks a fix in this order: the installation's `runtimes.<name>.policy_fix`; otherwise, for a known agent the kit can write to, the kit's recommended policy; otherwise the existing choices.

For the built-in fix, init shows the configuration path and the diff and asks `apply the kit's recommended policy? [y/N]`. On a yes it writes only the deny list (backing up the original), checks again and prints each class and spelling as refused or not. A spelling still not refused is named, with the note that the agent's matcher may be what lets it through.

If the agent's configuration is absent, init reports `not found` and points to `abk policy patterns`. The build-run toolset is never changed, and init names `abk policy apply --toolset` for that. The menu for an agent the kit cannot write to now mentions `abk policy patterns`.
With `--yes`, the built-in fix, like a configured one, runs only when `--run-policy-fix` is also given. Without it, init names the unrefused classes and exits 1 under `--policy-only`.

`abk policy apply` and init share `preview` and `write_recommended` in cli/policy_cmd.py. As a side effect, `abk policy apply` now reports an unreadable configuration during the preview with exit 2 instead of a traceback.
docs/cli.md, docs/init.md, docs/agent-runtimes.md, the abk-config skill and the changelog describe the built-in fix.

units.title: The allowance of each window is calibrated from the recorded history

description.summary: Each tick calibrates the usage allowance a unit is assumed to spend in the session and weekly windows from the installation's recorded readings and ledger, and uses that in place of the flat defaults when a start is allowed on an estimate.
changes: Each tick takes a high quantile of the points gained per unit across recent pairs of usage readings and keeps it in usage-allowances.json. The figure is clamped between a per-window floor and twice the default, and it is only used when there are enough pairs.
The usage guard's estimate reads the kept calibrated figure for each window. It falls back to the configured allowance when there is no calibration or too few pairs.
If the calls file or the ledger cannot be read, or the result cannot be written, the kept result is left as it was. A calls file that does not exist counts as an empty history.

New abk.yaml settings: `usage_unit_allowance_pct` now takes `auto` or a whole number, plus `calibrate_usage_allowances`, `usage_allowance_quantile`, `usage_allowance_window`, `usage_allowance_min_pairs` and a per-window `usage_allowance_floor_pct`.
`abk status` prints which allowances are in force and the pairs behind them.
The session and weekly window lengths are defined once in usage_allowances.py and shared by calibration and the guard's reset arithmetic.
