description.summary: The tick's scheduling pass now treats each project's build workers as a separate pool, both when it starts units and when it resumes them, and its wait reasons and usage samples report per project.
changes: A pass fills each project's build workers up to `max_concurrent_stacks` on its own, so a busy project no longer takes workers another project could use.
A unit is resumed only within its own project's free workers. Units held by a run in flight count against that project, not against a shared total.
A ready unit whose project has no free worker gets the full-queue wait reason, not a generic wait.

Each usage sample totals the limit, the cap and the free workers over the projects that still have an unfinished unit. Merged, closed, satisfied and unplanned units do not count, and the worker pool is sized from the same set of projects.
Counting units per project now goes through one shared function, `count_by_project` in pipeline/units.py, so the scheduler and the readiness checks count the same way.
The changelog bullet for the global/project limits split now also describes the per-project pass.

units.title: Each project has its own restack lane

description.summary: The restack lane is split into one lane per project, so each project has its own `project_limits.max_concurrent_restacks` workers and its own queue, and a busy project no longer holds back another project's restacks.
changes: `build_restack_lane` now returns a `RestackLanes`. It makes a `RestackLane` for a project the first time a unit of that project is handed over or found owed, and routes each unit to its project's lane.
Each project's lane is capped at `project_limits.max_concurrent_restacks` and queues its own extra units, so a full lane in one project does not delay a restack in another project of the same repo.

Each lane writes its own record file in the state directory (`record_path`). `abk status` and the graph page read every `restacks*.json` file, including the single file the previous version wrote, and show the totals.
`finished()` completes when the next restack in any lane ends. `drain()` joins every lane's threads and returns only when no lane has work running or waiting, even if every lane was already idle.
The tick, round, refresh and dispatch code takes a `Lane` protocol in place of the concrete `RestackLane`, and the changelog's existing limits bullet now describes the per-project lanes.

units.title: The graph page nests a subgraph for each project of a repo that has several
units.feedback:
The rendering itself is sound: the nesting, the indentation, the id scheme, the edges and the legend all follow the spec. But none of the callers that write the real page pass the new `projects` mapping, so the half of the rule about declared projects never reaches the page. One test also checks a project title loosely enough that a wrong title would still pass. Separately, the two `recorder.tier1` -> `recorder.unit_test` edits in tests/graph/ fix fixtures that the merged rename broke. They are fine.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/diagram.py:281 — `write_page` takes no `projects`, and none of its callers pass declared projects. So the real graph page never counts the projects a repo declares: only the projects of units in view decide whether it nests.
  Consequence: Spec unit-graph-page says a repo has more than one project 'among those it declares and those of its units in view', and task 10.1 asks that 'a repo whose units are all in one declared project but declares two still nests it'. In practice, a repo whose abk.yaml declares project `web`, with every unit in view in `web`, is drawn flat on the page written by `refresh_graph` in `store_for` (cli/pipeline.py:343), `cmd_graph` (cli/pipeline.py:807), `_refresh_graph_page` (cli/pipeline.py:3979) and `diagram.main` (diagram.py:321). The new tests pass only because they call `render_mermaid` and `render_markdown` with a hand-built mapping. That also makes two sentences false: the docs/unit-graph.md line 'those it declares and those of its units in view', and the CHANGELOG bullet's claim for repos that declare several projects.
  Done when: Add `projects: Mapping[str, Collection[str]] | None = None` to `write_page` and forward it to `render_markdown`. Pass the installation's declared projects at all four call sites; `declared_projects(inst.repos)` in pipeline/work_graph.py:58 is the existing accessor, and cli/pipeline.py already imports it. That accessor leaves out the root (`project_tags` drops `.`), so the counting in `render_mermaid` must be correct for its real output shape, not only for the `(".", "web")` shape the tests hand in. A repo declaring `web` (so `{"app": ("web",)}`) with units only in `web` must nest. A repo declaring none (`{"app": ()}`) with one unit in an undeclared project must stay flat, as test_diagram_single_project already pins. Either count the root whenever a repo declares another path, or have the callers add it; then state the chosen contract in the `render_mermaid` docstring. Add a test that goes through `write_page` (or `cmd_graph`) with a fixture installation whose `app` repo declares `web` and whose units are all in `web`, and asserts that the written page holds a nested `["web"]` subgraph inside `subgraph app`.
- [1.2] tests/pipeline/test_diagram_projects.py:33 — The title check for the `web` project, `"web" in enclosing["b"][1]`, matches the subgraph id `app__project__web`, so it passes whether or not the title is `web`.
  Consequence: Task 10.1 and the spec require the nested subgraph to be 'titled with the project's path'. If the title were dropped (`subgraph app__project__web` with no `["web"]`) or wrong, this test would still pass. The check on line 32 for `.` has the same `or` weakness: `endswith(".")` would accept a bare id.
  Done when: Assert the titles exactly: `enclosing["a"][1].endswith('["."]')` and `enclosing["b"][1].endswith('["web"]')`.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/diagram.py:114 — The `render_mermaid` docstring describes `graph` and `restacking` but not the new `projects` parameter: whether it is keyed by repo, whether it includes the root `.`, and that it only decides when to nest.
  Consequence: The next caller has to read the counting expression to learn which shape to pass. Passing the wrong shape (root included or not) silently changes whether a repo nests.
  Done when: Add a sentence saying what `projects` maps (repo -> declared project paths, in the shape `declared_projects` returns or whatever contract finding 1 settles on) and that it only decides whether a repo is drawn nested.

description.summary: The unit graph page draws a nested subgraph for each project inside a repo that has more than one project, counting both the projects the repo declares and those of its units in view.
changes: Inside each repo's subgraph, units are grouped into a nested subgraph per project, titled with the project's path (`.` for the root), when the repo has more than one project.

A repo counts as having several projects if its abk.yaml declares a project besides the root, even when every unit in view sits in one project. A repo that declares none and whose units are all in one project stays flat.

`write_page` takes the declared projects, and every path that writes the real page passes the installation's declared projects: store refresh, `abk graph`, the tick's graph refresh and the diagram module's own entry point.
Tests cover the nesting, the exact subgraph titles, and a page written through `abk graph` for a repo whose units are all in one declared project.

units.title: The text edit that moves the limits renames the key and moves three settings
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/config_migrate.py:128 — Any existing `project_limits` block causes a refusal whenever a setting would move, even when the settings don't overlap. The spec only refuses the same setting already being in `project_limits`.
  Consequence: The spec's refusal list is exhaustive: refuse 'when … [the file] already holds the same setting in `project_limits`'. Take `project_limits:\n  max_concurrent_stacks: 2\nglobal_limits:\n  max_units_in_progress: 5\n`, which is a half-migrated file that unit 5's loader refuses with a pointer. `migrate` raises `project_limits: project_limits is already set, move the settings into it by hand` instead of moving `max_units_in_progress`. This is the 'already on the new names with one left behind' scenario, and the user is left with a file that neither loads nor migrates.
  Done when: When `project_limits` is a block mapping and none of its keys overlap the moving ones, append the carried lines after its last content line (`_end(lines, its_line, its_col) + 1`). The carried lines keep their own indentation, so refuse with a reason if the existing block's child indentation differs from the moved lines' indentation, or if the block is flow style. If `project_limits` is null, give it the moved lines. Keep the existing refusal for an overlapping key. Add a case to `tests/test_config_migrate_text.py`: a disjoint `project_limits` block before `global_limits` ends with the moved setting appended under it, and the result passes `_verify`.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/config_migrate.py:110 — If the `limits` block is an alias of a mapping anchored elsewhere, `migrate` crashes with IndexError instead of refusing.
  Consequence: Input `base: &b\n  max_units_in_progress: 5\nlimits: *b\n` crashes with `IndexError: list index out of range`. The aliased node's keys sit on the `base` lines, those lines get deleted, and then `lines[block_line]` is out of range. The spec requires refusing an anchor or alias with the key and a reason, and unit 12's command would show a traceback instead of exit 2. A related case: `limits: &l\n  max_units_in_progress: 5\n` is only caught by the generic `_verify` message ('would differ … more than the move'), not by a reason about the anchor.
  Done when: Before editing, refuse with `ConfigMigrateError` naming the block key and saying it has an anchor or an alias when `_MARKED.search(_strip_comment(lines[block_line]))` matches. Also refuse when any moving key's line falls outside the block's own lines (`block_line < key.start_mark.line <= _end(lines, block_line, col)`). Add `limits: *b` (with an anchored base) and `limits: &l` blocks to CASES in `tests/test_config_migrate_refusals.py`, each with key pattern `limits` and reason `anchor|alias`.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/config_migrate.py:155 — An empty `limits:` block (null value, written with nothing after the colon) is refused. The rename writes `global_limits: {}`, but `_expected` keeps the value null.
  Consequence: Input `limits:\nrepos: {}\n` is refused with 'the edited text would differ from the file in more than the move'. It is a valid file needing only the rename, and no refusal in the spec covers it. `limits: ~` happens to work only because the `~` is left on the line.
  Done when: Write `{}` only when something moved and nothing is left, e.g. `_renamed(..., empty=bool(moving) and not left)`. A bare `limits:` then becomes `global_limits:` and verifies as null. Add a test in `tests/test_config_migrate_text.py` that `limits:\nrepos: {}\n` migrates to `global_limits:\nrepos: {}\n` with `moved == ()`.
- [1.4] tests/test_config_migrate_verified.py:55 — `test_a_result_that_would_differ_is_never_returned` passes whatever the code does. It returns on `ConfigMigrateError` and otherwise asserts the document is equal.
  Consequence: Task 11.4 asks for 'a migration whose result would differ is refused'. The test passes if `_verify` is deleted, as long as the edit happens to be right, and it passes on a refusal for an unrelated reason. Nothing pins that the verification step refuses.
  Done when: Assert the refusal: `with pytest.raises(ConfigMigrateError, match='differ'): migrate(text)` for the block-scalar input. Today `_region` lifts `    # part of the text` as a comment and `_verify` refuses, so this holds now and fails if the check is removed.

Optional:
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/config_migrate.py:18 — The module imports the private helpers `_end`, `_insert`, `_lines` and `_strip_comment` from `runtimes/policy_apply.py`.
  Consequence: Two modules now depend on helpers whose names say no one outside should rely on them. A refactor of `policy_apply` has no signal that `config_migrate` breaks. Task 11.5 explicitly allows a pure move into a shared module.
  Done when: Move the line helpers (`lines`, `end`, `insert`, `strip_comment`, plus `indent`/`content`/`marker`, which `end` uses) into a small shared module under public names, with both `policy_apply` and `config_migrate` importing from it and no behaviour change to `abk policy apply`.

description.summary: Adds a text-level migration that renames a root `limits` block to `global_limits` and moves the three scheduling settings into `project_limits`, leaving every other byte of the file unchanged.
changes: `migrate(text)` renames `limits` to `global_limits`, writing `global_limits: {}` only when every setting moved out. It moves `max_units_in_progress`, `max_concurrent_stacks` and `max_concurrent_restacks` into a new `project_limits` block placed straight after it, carrying each setting's end-of-line comment and the comment lines above it.

When `project_limits` already exists as a block (or bare null) with no overlapping setting, the moved lines are appended to it. A setting already present there, or a block that is anchored, flow-style or indented differently, is refused with the key and a reason.

It refuses, with `ConfigMigrateError` naming the key, a block that is an alias or carries an anchor, settings not written under their block, flow-style blocks, multi-line values, anchors or merge keys on moved settings, and files holding both `limits` and `global_limits`.
Before returning, it checks that the edited text parses to exactly the old document with the keys renamed and moved, and refuses anything else.

The line helpers for editing YAML as text (splitting lines, finding a node's end, inserting lines, stripping comments) now live in a shared `yaml_lines` module used by both `abk policy apply` and the migration.

units.title: abk config --migrate shows the change, asks, writes once with a backup, and is idempotent
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/config_cmd.py:27 — `_confirmed` is a second copy of `policy_cmd._confirmed` (src/agent_build_kit/cli/policy_cmd.py:230). It makes the same `yes(input(question))` call, treats EOFError as no, and adds only a terminal check.
  Consequence: The rule for asking a yes/no question at the terminal (how a reply is read, EOF counts as no) now lives in two private functions that must change together. The review rules treat a duplicate that the change introduces as required.
  Done when: Keep one public function for asking, for example `confirmed(question) -> bool` beside `yes` in init/runtime_choice.py, which does the input/EOF handling. Use it from both policy_cmd and config_cmd. config_cmd adds its no-terminal rule at the call site (`sys.stdin.isatty() and confirmed(...)`) or through a keyword on the shared function, so `abk policy apply` behaves exactly as before.

units.title: An acceptance or narrow unit waits for every earlier unit of its change, computed at run time

description.summary: An acceptance or narrow unit now waits for, stops for and follows every earlier unit of its change. The rule is worked out at run time from the change's units, not from the dependencies stored on the unit.
changes: `waiting_on` holds a unit flagged `acceptance` or `narrow` until every earlier, non-`unplanned` unit of its change is reviewed, merged or satisfied in its own repository, or merged (or satisfied and landed) in another repository, even when those units are not among its stored dependencies.
A running acceptance or narrow unit stops with the cause upstream went back when such an earlier unit in its repository goes back to planned, failed, held or closed (`build_upstream_incomplete`).

`follow_predecessors` sets an acceptance or narrow unit in review back to planned, naming the earlier unit, while that unit's branch is changing. Ordinary units are still moved only by their own parents.
The rule only adds waits: base, depth, open parents and second open parents still come from the stored dependencies. A unit with no flag, or flagged `contract`, behaves as a plain chain does.
New helpers in `pipeline/units.py`: `unit_number`, `earlier_units` and `followed_dependencies`. `run_log` and `transcript` now take a unit's number from `unit_number`.

Tests cover the rule over in-memory graphs, over a real `UnitStore`, and over a store fixture in the pipeline's shape, checking that reducing it to direct dependencies leaves every flagged unit's waits and `ready_units` unchanged.

units.feedback:
Task group 1 is mostly done: 28 tests pass, ruff and pyrefly are clean, and the leak and ecosystem guards pass. Four required points remain, all small and local. One is a correctness gap: with no side named, a mixed archive entry is never refused. One is a porcelain parser that repeats an existing one and is weaker. Two are small duplicates or shadowed names. What the command prints (counts, the exit code) and copying belong to groups 2–4 and are not asked of this unit.

  Consequence: Example: a source whose only mixed item is `archive/2026-01-02-x`, with groups `[app]` and `[lib]`. `plan_split(source, 'app')` gives `refusals == ()`, so the run goes ahead and the entry stays in the source without anyone choosing a side. The spec ('Without --allow-mixed the run SHALL refuse'; an archive entry 'SHALL be classified … the same way') and design.md §Mixed changes require a refusal. The comment states something the code does not do.

The change name is the entry name with its leading `YYYY-MM-DD-` removed; that change already refuses. Name the entry and its repos in the refusal. Fix or remove the comment to match. Add a test in tests/split/test_select_mixed.py: a source whose only mixed item is an archived entry, `plan_split(source, 'app')` with no side, gives exactly one `RefusalKind.MIXED` refusal whose line names the entry and `lib`. The existing `test_with_no_side_the_plan_refuses_and_names_the_change` must keep exactly one refusal, because its archived `mixed` entry is named for the active `mixed` change.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/split/select.py:312 — `uncommitted` parses `git status --porcelain` itself without `-z`. `pipeline/workspaces.py:140` `_porcelain` already parses `--porcelain -z --untracked-files=all` and handles rename and copy entries correctly.

A staged rename under openspec/ prints as `M openspec/a.md -> openspec/b.md`, one bogus path. A file with a space or non-ASCII character in its name prints C-quoted (`M "openspec/a b.md"`), not as its path.
  Done when: Give the parser a public name and let it take a pathspec: move `_porcelain` into `pipeline/shell.py` as `porcelain(path, *pathspec)`, or make it public in place, and have workspaces use it too. Then build `uncommitted` from its `(code, path)` pairs, mapping a code to `??`, `D` or `M` as now. description.summary: Adds the planning half of splitting a planning repo: for a chosen repo, or one of its projects, it works out which changes, archive entries, specs and units would move to a new planning repo, which stay, and what blocks the split.
changes: `split.select.plan_split` sorts each active change and each archive entry by the repo tags on its task groups. Each one moves, stays, is mixed, or cannot be read; an archive entry without a tasks.md is reported as unclassified. A `--project` path is checked against the projects the repo declares and normalised the same way.

A mixed change, or a mixed archive entry, is refused when no `--allow-mixed` side is chosen. An archive entry is not refused a second time when it is named after an active mixed change that already refuses. Choosing `source` or `destination` decides where mixed items go, and choosing `destination` is refused when the destination lacks a repo the item uses.
Spec capabilities are sorted into moved, shared and unowned. A unit is refused if it builds both a change that moves and one that stays, or if it is still running, in review or held.
The plan lists the uncommitted files under the specs and state directories as `M`, `??` or `D` lines with their exact paths, and gives None when the source is not under git.

Two existing helpers become public so the split can reuse them: the null-separated `git status --porcelain` parser is now `pipeline.shell.porcelain` (also used by workspaces), and the project-path normaliser is now `work_graph.tag_path`.

units.title: The copy: files, unit records and plan records, a dangling edge refused, and scrub
units.feedback:
Group 2 is mostly in place: files, records, plan records, the preflight and the scrub seam all exist, and the 55 tests under tests/split and tests/pipeline/test_unit_store_import.py pass. Two things block approval. First, the dangling-edge preflight gets the `Needs:` lines wrong in both directions. It misses a staying change whose `Needs:` names a moved change, and it refuses a moved change whose `Needs:` names an archived change. Second, the change adds three copies of logic that already has, or should have, one home. Groups 3 and 4 (the command, the config splice, --remove and the docs) belong to later units and are not asked of this one.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/split/copy.py:125 — The reverse edge check only looks at staying unit records. It never checks a staying change's `Needs:` lines that name a moved change, although design.md ("a staying unit or change whose edge points at something moved") and task 2.4 ask for both.
  Consequence: Take a source with `stays/tasks.md` containing `Needs: moves group 1`, where `moves` is the change being moved. preflight returns no warning, and with remove=True no error. After group 4's --remove the source has no `changes/moves/tasks.md`. The tick skips a `Needs:` whose target tasks file is missing (cli/pipeline.py:1655-1658), so the staying group stops waiting for a dependency that never merged in this repo, and nothing told the person.
  Done when: In preflight, for every active source change not in plan.changes_moved, read its needs with `group_needs(tasks)`. Each Need whose `change` is in plan.changes_moved becomes a line naming the staying change, the `Needs:` target and its group, and saying it moves. Add it to `warnings` without remove and to `errors` with remove, the same way the unit edges are handled. Add a test to tests/split/test_dangling_edges.py: a staying `[lib]` change has `Needs: moves group 1`, and the test asserts one warning naming both changes without remove and one error with remove=True.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/split/copy.py:114 — The moved-change `Needs:` check parses tasks.md line by line with NEEDS_LINE. That re-implements `work_graph.group_needs` (pipeline/work_graph.py:596), which already gives the lowercased change, group and line, scoped to group headings.
  Consequence: There are now two parsers of `Needs:` lines that must change together. They already differ: the copy here also counts a `Needs:` line that sits above the first group heading, and group_needs and the tick ignore it. So the split can refuse an edge the pipeline never acts on.
  Done when: Replace the loop at copy.py:114-123 with `for group, needs in group_needs(source.changes_dir / name / "tasks.md").items(): for need in needs: ...`, using need.change and need.group in the message. Drop the NEEDS_LINE import.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/split/copy.py:117 — A moved change's `Needs:` naming a change that is already archived, or has no active tasks.md, is refused as dangling. The pipeline treats such a line as satisfied: cli/pipeline.py:1656-1657 only waits when `changes/<target>/tasks.md` exists.
  Consequence: Take a moved change with `Needs: done group 1`, where `done` was finished and sits in `changes/archive/2026-01-01-done`. preflight reports `... names done, which is neither moved nor in the destination` and carry_out raises CopyRefused. The edge is inert, so the only way past the refusal is to edit the change's tasks.md by hand.
  Done when: Count a `Needs:` target as dangling only when the source has an active `changes/<target>/tasks.md`, the target is not in plan.changes_moved, and the destination has no `changes/<target>/tasks.md`. This mirrors the tick's own test at cli/pipeline.py:1656. Add a test to test_dangling_edges.py: a moved change needs an archived change, and preflight returns no error.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/split/copy.py:178 — The plan-record hash `sha256(specification_text(...))` is written out inline. That makes a fourth copy of the formula the tick already has three times (cli/pipeline.py:1175, 2680, 3007).
  Consequence: If the tick's hash ever changes (another normalisation in `specification`, a different digest), copy.py keeps writing the old form. Every split change then fails `record.get("hash") != digest` in has_work and gets planned again, which defeats task 2.3. Text handling already differs: the tick hashes `tasks.read_text()`, which turns CRLF into LF, while the copy hashes `bytes.decode()`, which keeps CR. A CRLF tasks.md therefore gets a hash the tick never matches.
  Done when: Add one public function in cli/pipeline.py, for example `plan_digest(tasks: Path) -> str`, returning `hashlib.sha256(specification(tasks).encode()).hexdigest()`. Use it at the three existing sites, and in carry_out over the destination's `changes/<name>/tasks.md` after the files are written. test_copy_plans.py keeps passing unchanged.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/split/scrubbing.py:24 — `PLACEHOLDER = "<redacted>"` repeats the default `replacement` of `scrub_terms.scrub_text` (scrub_terms.py:129). scrub_counts depends on the two staying equal.
  Consequence: If scrub_text's default replacement changes, scrub_counts counts the old string, so the plan reports 0 (or negative) substitutions while files and records are still being changed.
  Done when: Define the replacement once in scrub_terms.py as a public constant (for example `REPLACEMENT = "<redacted>"`). Use it as scrub_text's default and import it in scrubbing.py in place of PLACEHOLDER.
- [1.6] src/agent_build_kit/split/copy.py:62 — The filter for moved unit records, `[u for u in UnitStore(source.state_dir / "units.json").all() if u.id in plan.units_moved]`, is written twice: here in `_records`, and again in `scrubbing.scrub_counts` (scrubbing.py:82-84).
  Consequence: Which records the copy imports and which ones the scrub counts report on are two copies that must change together. If group 4 changes the selection (for example, records already in the destination), the counts the plan prints stop describing what is written.
  Done when: Add `moved_records(source, plan) -> list[StoredUnit]` to split/select.py next to `moved_files`. Use it in copy._records and in scrubbing.scrub_counts.

Optional:
- [1.7] src/agent_build_kit/split/copy.py:179 — The tasks file is looked up with the hard-coded key `Path("changes") / name / "tasks.md"` instead of being derived from the installation's paths.
  Consequence: This is correct today, because changes_dir is always specs_dir/changes. But it is a second statement of that layout, and changes_dir_under (installation.py:31) owns it.
  Done when: Use `(source.changes_dir / name / "tasks.md").relative_to(source.specs_dir)`. This becomes moot if the plan_digest fix reads the destination file directly.

description.summary: Adds the copy step of splitting a planning repo. It writes one code repo's changes, archive entries, specs, unit records and plan records into a destination installation, checks for conflicts and dangling dependency edges before writing anything, and can scrub installation terms along the way.
changes: carry_out copies the moved changes, archive entries and specs into the destination. It skips files that are already there and identical, keeps file modes, and imports the moved unit records into the destination's unit store.

Each moved change whose plan succeeded in the source gets a plan record in the destination. Its hash comes from the tick's own formula, now in one public plan_digest function, so the destination's tick does not plan the change again.

preflight finds every problem before the first write: files or unit records that differ in the destination, and unit edges, joins or a moved change's `Needs:` lines that point at something neither moved nor in the destination. A `Needs:` naming an archived or inactive change counts as satisfied, as it does in the tick.

Edges from what stays into what moves are reported: staying unit records' depends_on/needs, and staying changes' `Needs:` lines. They are warnings normally and errors when the source copy is going to be removed.

With scrub on, the moved files and unit records have the installation's terms replaced. scrub_counts reports how many files and records would change and how many substitutions there would be, using the same record selection and replacement string as the copy.

units.title: The command: dry run by default, a checked destination, and the destination's repo entry
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/split/config_edit.py:10 — add_repo_entry imports seven underscored helpers from init/scaffold.py (_block_end, _child_indent, _indent_of, _key_at, _key_line, _read_lines, _top_level_end) and `_replace` from runtimes/policy_apply.py. It then re-implements three sequences that already exist there: (a) `_block` repeats add_project's lookup of the repo block (scaffold.py:286-295: find the `repos:` line, take the child indent, call _key_at, call _block_end); (b) the parse-and-compare check (config_edit.py:100-106) repeats scaffold.py:327-332; (c) back up once, then _replace (config_edit.py:108-112) repeats policy_apply.py:518-523.
  Consequence: Each pair now has two copies that must change together, and the private names have a caller outside their module that nothing warns about. If add_project's block lookup is fixed (for example for a quoted key or a tab-indented file) and config_edit's copy is not, add_repo_entry splices into the wrong place. Changing the backup rule in policy_apply leaves the split writing the old way.
  Done when: Give scaffold a public repo-block lookup, e.g. `repo_block(lines, repo) -> tuple[start, end, indent] | None`, used by both add_project and add_repo_entry. Expose the parse-and-compare as one public function used by both, e.g. `checked(path, updated_text, expected) -> None` raising on mismatch. Give policy_apply a public `backup_and_replace(path, text) -> Path | None` used by both its apply path and add_repo_entry. Import only public names: either make the line helpers public in scaffold or move them into one shared module that both import. The existing tests must keep passing unchanged.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/planning_cmd.py:35 — Which plan records move is decided twice: `_counts` filters with `recorded.get(name, {}).get("ok")`, and copy.py:189 has the same filter. `_removals` (line 52) skips the filter and prints `would remove plan record <name>` for every moved change.
  Consequence: With `--remove`, a moved change that has no plan record (or one with ok false) is counted as 0 plan records but listed as a plan record to remove, so the dry run contradicts itself. The count and carry_out will also drift apart when either filter changes.
  Done when: Add one function in split/copy.py, e.g. `moved_plan_records(source, plan) -> tuple[str, ...]`, holding the `ok` filter. carry_out, `_counts` and `_removals` all use it. Add a test: one moved change with a record and one without, run with `--remove` and no `--apply`; assert `plan records: 1` and exactly one `would remove plan record` line, naming the change that has the record.
- [1.3] tests/cli/test_planning_split_destination.py:58 — test_a_destination_that_is_the_source_is_refused asserts only that `"source" in err`. The fixture root is `tmp_path / "source"`, so every error message that echoes the path contains `source`.
  Consequence: The test passes regardless of the message. It would still pass if the check were removed and a later step failed with exit 2 for another reason, as long as that message printed the path, e.g. a missing-file or not-loading error about the same directory.
  Done when: Assert the phrase the check prints, e.g. `assert "is the source" in err`, or make the assertion independent of the path some other way.
- [1.4] tests/split/test_config_add.py:101 — Both parametrized refusal cases (a flow-style source block and a flow-style destination `repos:`) are rejected by the block lookup before the splice runs. The parse-and-compare check at config_edit.py:100-106 is never exercised, although task 3.3 asks that 'a result that does not parse to the old document plus the block' be refused.
  Consequence: Deleting the parse-and-compare check, or comparing against the wrong expected document, leaves every test green. A splice that produces broken YAML would then be written to the destination's abk.yaml.
  Done when: Add a case that gets past the lookup and fails only at the check. For example, a block-style source where `lib: &base` holds path and slug, and `app:` has `<<: *base` plus its own `path:`. The spliced text then has an undefined alias. Assert ConfigEditError naming the destination file and `app`, the destination text unchanged, and no `.abk-backup` file.
- [1.5] tests/cli/test_planning_split_plan.py:1 — No test runs `abk planning split --apply` against a valid destination. Group 3's Done-when says that with `--apply` the command copies and adds the repo's entry to the destination's `abk.yaml`, and planning_cmd.py:120-127 (carry_out, the add_repo_entry call that writes, the `copied ...` line, exit 0) is not exercised.
  Consequence: The test suite would not catch the command dropping the add_repo_entry call, passing the source and destination paths in the wrong order, or calling carry_out with the wrong scrub flag.
  Done when: Add an in-process CLI test on the `trees` fixture with `populated(source)`. Run `split(source, '--repo', 'app', '--to', str(destination), '--apply')` and assert: exit 0; the moved change's files exist under the destination's specs directory; the destination store holds the moved unit ids; `yaml.safe_load(destination/'abk.yaml')['repos']['app']` equals the source's entry; `abk.yaml.abk-backup` holds the original; the source tree is unchanged (snapshot_tree); a `copied` line is printed.

Optional:
- [1.6] src/agent_build_kit/split/select.py:381 — load_destination goes through installation.load_config, which calls `settings_module.reload(<destination>/.env)`. From then on the process-wide settings are the destination's, including `settings.config`, which planning_cmd.py:74 reads to find the source config.
  Consequence: When the destination has a `.env`, everything after the destination is loaded runs with its settings: the source config lookup when `--config` is absent, and the scrub and copy steps. The design says the destination is 'not made the active installation', but its settings in effect are.
  Done when: Either load the destination with `config.load` and skip the `.env` reload, or reload the source's `.env` afterwards. Derive the source config path from what main already located rather than from settings read after the reload.
- [1.7] src/agent_build_kit/split/config_edit.py:104 — The spec says the new text must 'parse to the old document plus the block and to load'. Only the parse-and-compare is done; the result is never validated as a WorkspaceConfig (config.load / model_validate).
  Consequence: I found no input that loads in the source and fails in the destination, so this is the spec's wording rather than a failure I can reproduce.
  Done when: After the compare, validate `loaded` with `WorkspaceConfig.model_validate` (or config.load on the text) and raise ConfigEditError naming the file when it fails.

description.summary: Adds `abk planning split`. It does a dry run by default, which counts and lists what would move to another planning repo. With --apply it copies the repo's changes, specs, unit records and plan records into a checked destination, and splices the repo's entry into the destination's abk.yaml.
changes: `abk planning split --repo R --to DIR` checks the destination, which must exist, load, carry the same rules and not be the source. It then prints counts of changes, archive entries, specs, units, plan records and config entries, and lists refusals. Nothing is written without --apply.
With --remove, the dry run also lists what would be removed from the source. A plan record is listed only for a moved change that has an ok record, through the shared moved_plan_records.

With --apply, the command copies the files and records. It then adds the repo's block to the destination's abk.yaml as text, reindented to the destination's style, after a one-time `.abk-backup`. A layout it cannot follow, or a result that does not parse to the old document plus the block, is refused and nothing is written.

init/scaffold.py now exposes repo_block, checked and its line helpers publicly, and runtimes/policy_apply.py exposes backup_and_replace. add_project, the policy apply and the split's config edit share these instead of keeping copies.

units.title: --remove takes out only what moved, a second run changes nothing, and the docs say how

description.summary: `abk split --apply --remove` takes out of the source planning repo only what moved to the destination, a second run changes nothing, and a run killed part way through removal is finished by the next run.
changes: With `--remove`, the split deletes the moved unit records and plan records from the source state first, then the moved files, leaving everything that stays untouched.

Files are removed one directory at a time: capability specs first, then changes, then archive entries. Within each directory `tasks.md` goes last, and a directory is pruned once its files are gone. A killed run therefore always leaves the files that tell the next run what moved.

A rerun after a kill at any point during removal returns 0, removes what is left, and drops the moved repo's entry from the source `abk.yaml`. A test kills the run at every unlink on the fixture to cover this.
A directory a killed run left with no files is also pruned, and running the split again once it is done changes nothing.
The docs and the changelog bullet describe how `--remove` and reruns behave.

history.note: rounds spent with work outstanding: Both earlier points are fixed for the scenarios they named. The per-directory removal opened a new kill window, though. A capability spec is moved only because the changes that own it are moving, and those changes are now removed before the spec. A run killed in between leaves the spec in the source

units.title: Scrub terms come from one function, skip the root's own name, and read a local list
units.feedback:
Both round-1 findings are fixed. The provider loop no longer adds a home-directory term of its own, so a provider file's directory comes only from the filtered `_config_paths` loop. Bare dotfile names such as `.env` are no longer terms. The new tests cover the planning root at <home>/plan, the `.config` tool directory and `.secretdir/.env`. The leak test now builds its patterns from `TOOL_DIRS`, which removes a second copy of that list. One new problem came in with this rework: the idempotence change to `scrub_text` stops it scrubbing some terms at all.

Required:
- [2.1] src/agent_build_kit/scrub_terms.py:134 — To make a second pass idempotent, `scrub_text` now drops every term that appears inside the replacement string, so those terms are never scrubbed at all.
  Consequence: Any term that is a substring of `<redacted>` is left in the output verbatim: `act`, `red`, `ted`, `dact`, `redact`, `acted`, and so on (3+ characters is the minimum term length, so a repo, host or person named `ted` or `red` qualifies). `scrub_text("an act of act", ["act"])` now returns `an act of act` unchanged. That breaks the spec requirement (scrub-check spec, 'One function defines the terms, and one scrubs text with them') that `scrub_text` SHALL replace each term. Stored text scrubbed through it in later units would leak exactly those names. The new test `test_a_term_inside_the_replacement_does_not_break_idempotence` (tests/cli/test_scrub_text.py:36) only checks once == twice, so it passes on this leaking output.
  Done when: Keep every term and make an existing placeholder match itself. Build the alternation with `re.escape(replacement)` first, then the terms longest first. Every match is replaced with `replacement`, so a placeholder already in the text is consumed whole and re-emitted unchanged, while every term is still replaced. Remove the term filter and the early return on an empty `ordered`. In the test, also assert `once == "an <redacted> of <redacted>"` (the term is replaced) before asserting that the second pass equals `once`.

description.summary: Deriving an installation's scrub terms is now one shared function with a matching text scrubber. It no longer flags the planning root's own name, and it reads a local list of terms to add or remove.
changes: `scrub_terms.py` now builds the scrub term list on its own: repo names, owners, verify.env keys, provider file names, longer literal values, the home directory name and dot-directories under home. `abk scrub-check` and later callers all use this one function instead of a private copy inside the CLI.

The planning root's own directory name is no longer a term. A provider file such as `<home>/plan/.env` no longer adds `plan`. Bare dotfile names and tool directories such as `.config` are skipped too.
A local list in the planning repo can add terms or remove derived ones, so an installation can tune the list without touching the framework.

`scrub_text` replaces every term case-insensitively, longest first, with `<redacted>`. That includes terms that are pieces of the placeholder itself. Running it again on its own output changes nothing.
The structural leak test builds its tool-directory patterns from the shared `TOOL_DIRS` constant instead of keeping a second copy of the list.

units.title: An ignored abk.local.yaml is merged over abk.yaml and errors name their file

description.summary: An optional, ignored `abk.local.yaml` beside `abk.yaml` is merged over it when the configuration loads, so facts about a particular installation can stay out of a public checkout.
changes: Loading the configuration deep-merges `abk.local.yaml` over `abk.yaml`. Mappings merge key by key. Lists, scalars and `null` from the overlay replace the base value whole.

Schema and YAML errors name the file the failing key came from, either the base file or the overlay. A single file that sets both `limits` and `global_limits` is refused, and the error names that file. The deprecated `limits` spelling is renamed in each file before the merge, so two files that spell it differently still merge.
The rename and the 'both are set' refusal for the deprecated root `limits` key now live in one shared function (`_alias_limits` in config.py). The model validator and the file loader both use it.
`abk config` reports on stderr which top-level keys the overlay set, and `abk config --path` prints the overlay's path after `abk.yaml` when an overlay exists.
Nothing that writes configuration writes the overlay, and redaction passes the overlay's values through like any others. Tests cover merging, errors, the CLI output and redaction.

units.title: The leak test reads planning content, and init ignores the local list and says where facts go
units.feedback:
Unit 3 covers its tasks, and the 29 tests in the three new and changed test files pass, as does ruff. Four small points block it: a missing sentence in init's closing output, a test whose fixture passes whether or not the property holds, and two duplicates this change introduces. There is no openspec/ or abk.yaml in this checkout, so task 3.5 has nothing to scrub here. Templates/gitignore now holds both `runs/**/*.pre-redact` and `*.pre-redact`; group 5 removes the first, so I have not raised it.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/init.py:805 — Init's closing output does not say that a planning repo that plans only itself needs no other repo entries. Only the planning context template says it.
  Consequence: The consumer-facts-in-env requirement says init SHALL say this 'in the planning context template and in its closing output'. Task 3.3 asks for it in both too. The output gives only the .env sentence, and the test checks the one-repo sentence only in `context`, so nothing catches its absence from the output.
  Done when: Step 4 of the closing output (or a line next to it) also says that a planning repo that plans only itself needs no other repo entries in abk.yaml. In tests/cli/test_init_local_ignore.py::test_the_output_and_the_planning_context_say_stack_facts_go_in_the_env_file, the `no other repo entries` assertion runs for both `context` and `output` inside the loop.
- [1.2] tests/test_leak_scan_planning_content.py:52 — The 'run log under the state directory is not read' test uses files the scan's suffix filter skips anyway (`.log`, `.jsonl`).
  Consequence: Neither `.log` nor `.jsonl` is in `TEXT`, so the test still passes if `runs` is added to `SCANNED`, or if `files()` reads all of `runs/`. It does not check the requirement that ignored state, other than the unit store, is not read.
  Done when: Use a fixture with a suffix the scan reads, e.g. `runs/unit-logs/feature-1.json` or `runs/ledger.json`, containing HOME_LINE, next to a clean `runs/units.json`. Assert `leaks(tmp_path) == []`. That fixture fails if anything under `runs/` other than `units.json` is scanned.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/init/scaffold.py:608 — `_ensure_ignored` is a third copy of 'append the lines an ignore file lacks, with a newline separator'. The other two are `pipeline/scratch.py:87-92` and `tracks/runner.py:404-410`.
  Consequence: The three copies already differ: scratch strips each line before comparing, the other two do not. A fix to the read/compare/separator logic has to be made in three places that drift apart, and the next caller will add a fourth.
  Done when: Make one shared function, e.g. `append_missing_lines(path, lines) -> bool` (returns whether it wrote), in a common module such as `pipeline/file_lock.py` beside `atomic_write_text`, or in a small text-file helper module. It reads the file once, compares stripped lines, adds the separator newline only when needed, and creates a missing file. Scaffold's `_ensure_ignored` (it then only records `written`), `scratch.py` and `tracks/runner.py` all call it, and its own test covers a missing file, a file with no trailing newline and a line already present.
- [1.4] tests/installation_leaks.py:125 — The hit format `f"{path.relative_to(root)}:{number}: {line.strip()[:100]}"` and its loop over files and lines now appear four times: `hits`, `leaks`, and the inline comprehensions in `test_every_github_slug_belongs_to_a_fixture_owner` and `test_every_azure_organisation_belongs_to_a_fixture`.
  Consequence: The spec fixes the report as path, line and clipped line, so changing that format means editing four copies together. This change adds `leaks` as a new copy and moves the two test loops onto the new module without folding them in.
  Done when: Have `hits` take a line predicate (`Callable[[str], object]`) or a pattern. `leaks` becomes `hits(root, lambda line: any(s.search(line) for s in SHAPES) or foreign_slug_owners(line) or foreign_azure_orgs(line))`, and the two tests call `hits(ROOT, foreign_slug_owners)` and `hits(ROOT, foreign_azure_orgs)`. The format string is then written once.

Optional:
- [1.5] tests/test_no_installation_leaks.py:102 — `test_planning_content_leaks_nothing` runs `leaks(ROOT)`, which re-checks the per-pattern tests above it over the same files.
  Consequence: `SCANNED` and `ROOT_FILES` now include the planning content, so every hit fails two tests and the suite reads the repo once more. Nothing new is covered for this checkout.
  Done when: Drop it, or keep it and remove the per-pattern tests it repeats. `leaks` stays the tested entry point for the temporary-tree tests.
- [1.6] tests/installation_leaks.py:148 — `repo_path_leaks` calls `repo.get` without checking the entry is a mapping.
  Consequence: An `abk.yaml` with `repos: {app: null}`, or a non-mapping `repos`, raises AttributeError, so the test errors instead of reporting a finding or passing.
  Done when: Skip entries that are not dicts, or treat them as `path: .`, e.g. `if not isinstance(repo, dict): continue`.

description.summary: The structural leak scan now also reads an installation's committed planning content. `abk init` ignores the local scrub list and tells the user that stack facts go in the ignored .env.
changes: The leak scan moves into `tests/installation_leaks.py` and also reads `openspec/`, `abk.yaml` and the tracked `runs/units.json`. Ignored state such as run logs and ledgers is not read. Each hit is reported as path, line and clipped line, a format now written in one place.
A new check fails when a tracked `abk.yaml` gives a repo a path outside the checkout. It names the repo key, not the path, and skips repo entries that are not mappings.
`abk init` adds the local scrub list and `*.pre-redact` files to the planning repo's ignore file, appending only lines that are missing.

Init's closing output and the planning context template both say that stack facts go in the ignored .env, read through `from: env-file` entries. They also say a planning repo of one repo needs no other repo entries.

A new shared `append_missing_lines` helper in `pipeline/file_lock.py` appends only the lines an ignore file lacks. It is now used by init's scaffolding, the worktree scratch exclude and the tracks runner's raw-output exclude.

units.title: Doctor warns before an installation's facts are committed to a public repository
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:624 — The owner comparison and its `.` exemption read `inst.config.repos`, the loaded configuration with `abk.local.yaml` already merged in, instead of the committed text that `_committed_facts` parsed a few lines above.
  Consequence: The spec (public-config-doctor: 'read the committed file's own text (parsed directly, not through the loader)') and task 4.1 ('does not use the loader') both require the committed text. Concrete case: the committed abk.yaml holds only `app` with path `.`, and the ignored abk.local.yaml adds `platform` with slug `other/platform`, which is exactly the use the Unreleased changelog recommends for the overlay. Doctor then warns `repos.platform is owned by another account than the origin` and tells the user to move a value that was never committed. It also works the other way: an overlay that sets a committed foreign repo's `path` to `.` hides a real finding.
  Done when: Iterate the `repos` mapping of `document` (the parsed committed text). Take the `.` exemption from that entry's own `path`, and take the account from that entry, for example by validating it with `RepoConfig.model_validate(entry)` and calling `forges.get(cfg.forge).identity(cfg)`, skipping entries that fail to validate. Never take it from `inst.config`. Add a test in tests/cli/test_doctor_public_content.py: the committed abk.yaml holds only the `.` entry, and an abk.local.yaml beside it adds a repo with slug `elsewhere/app`. Assert that the check is `["ok"]`. Group 7 deletes this test along with the overlay.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:663 — `_local_files` globs `*.pre-redact` under `inst.state_dir` and calls `copy.relative_to(root)`, but `planning.state_dir` may be absolute and outside the planning root (config.py:113, 'Relative to the planning root unless absolute').
  Consequence: With `planning.state_dir: /var/abk-runs` (or any directory outside the root) holding `units.json.pre-redact`, `relative_to` raises ValueError and the whole of `abk doctor` crashes. If that line is avoided, `git check-ignore` on a path outside the repository exits 128 and the code reports the copy as 'not ignored', even though a file outside the repository cannot be committed to it.
  Done when: Consider only copies that resolve inside the git toplevel (`_public_content` already computes it; pass it in), and skip the rest. Pass the path to git relative to that toplevel, or relative to the root when the copy is under it. Add a test in tests/cli/test_doctor_local_ignored.py: `planning.state_dir` is set to an absolute `tmp_path / "elsewhere"` holding `units.json.pre-redact`, and the planning `.gitignore` ignores `scrub.local` only. Assert that `run_doctor` returns and the check is `["ok"]`.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:667 — A tracked `*.pre-redact` copy gets the fix 'add `*.pre-redact` to .gitignore'. That does not untrack a committed file. The equivalent `scrub.local` branch handles this case and gives `git rm --cached`.
  Consequence: When a copy was committed, `git check-ignore` reports it as not ignored, so the user adds the ignore line, runs doctor again, and gets the same warning with no hint that `git rm --cached` is needed.
  Done when: Check `_is_tracked` first, as for `scrub.local`, and give 'git rm --cached <name>, and add `*.pre-redact` to .gitignore'. Add a test that commits a copy with `git add -f`.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:619 — `home in value` matches every string containing a slash when the home directory is `/` (a container with no home), and any value starting with `/root` when HOME is `/root`.
  Consequence: On such a host, every path-like value in abk.yaml produces a false `holds a home-directory path` warning.
  Done when: Only use `str(Path.home())` when it is not `/`, and match it as a path prefix (the home directory followed by `/` or the end of the string), not as a substring.

description.summary: `abk doctor` gets a `public content` check that warns, without any network call, when a planning repository's committed files would expose installation facts or hold files that must stay ignored.
changes: When `abk.yaml` is tracked, doctor reads the committed file's text directly, not through the loader. It warns about any repo path that leaves the checkout and any value holding a home-directory path. A home directory counts only as a path prefix, and a home of `/` matches nothing.

Doctor warns about committed repo entries owned by a different account than the planning repository's `origin`. The entry for the checkout itself (path `.`) is exempt, and repos that only the ignored `abk.local.yaml` adds are not judged.
Doctor warns when `scrub.local` or a `*.pre-redact` copy (in the planning root or the state directory) is tracked or not ignored, and says how to untrack it or add it to `.gitignore`.
Redaction copies outside the git toplevel, such as those in an absolute state directory elsewhere, are skipped instead of crashing doctor or being reported as not ignored.
A planning root that is not a git repository, or whose `abk.yaml` is untracked, gets a single `ok` with the reason.

units.title: abk scrub-store rewrites home paths in stored text
units.feedback:
Group 5 is implemented and the targeted tests pass (113 passed across the five new or changed test files, test_redact_history, the leak test and tests/split). Three things block approval. The new store rewrite copies a per-record text mapping that already exists. The new command keeps a second list of the home roots. And the shared test fixture gets past the leak test by adding itself to the leak test's exempt list instead of building its strings in pieces, as the existing doctor test does. Docs (docs/cli.md and the skill) belong to group 6, a later unit, and are not asked for here.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_store.py:593 — `UnitStore.rewrite_text` re-implements the per-record text mapping that `split/scrubbing.scrub_record` (src/agent_build_kit/split/scrubbing.py:47-67) already does: the same feedback/guidance/predecessor_note/stack_refusal fields, and the same history-note comprehension with a different guard (`"note" in entry` here, `isinstance(entry.get("note"), str)` there). `REWRITTEN_TEXT_FIELDS` also becomes a third list, walked by `scrub_store_cmd._counts`.
  Consequence: There are now two copies of 'which free-text fields a stored record has'. A text field added to `StoredUnit` (or the `description` that scrub_record already covers and rewrite_text does not) has to be added in both, or the split scrub and `abk scrub-store` silently disagree about what they clean. The guards already differ: a history entry whose note is not a string makes `rewrite_text` call `fn` on a non-string, while `scrub_record` skips it.
  Done when: Add one public function in pipeline/unit_store.py, for example `with_text(unit, fn) -> StoredUnit`, that maps `fn` over REWRITTEN_TEXT_FIELDS and each string history note (use the isinstance guard). `rewrite_text` calls it per record. `scrub_record` calls it and then applies `fn` to `description` itself, keeping the split's current behaviour. tests/split and tests/pipeline/test_unit_store_rewrite_text.py keep passing unchanged.
- [1.2] tests/installation_leaks.py:53 — `scrub_store_support.py` is added to the leak test's `SELF` exemption so that its literal `/home/someone/...` and `~/work/...` strings pass. The exemption works by basename and switches off every shape (home paths, slugs, anecdotes, noreply) for that file.
  Consequence: AGENTS.md ('Two checks keep it that way') relies on tests/test_no_installation_leaks.py as the structural guard. This weakens it for a whole fixture file, so a real home path, slug or anecdote added to that file later would not be caught. The repo already avoids this: tests/cli/test_doctor_public_content.py:14-15 builds `HOME = "/" + "home" + "/someone"` 'so that this file does not itself look like a leaked path'.
  Done when: In tests/scrub_store_support.py, build LINUX, MACOS and TILDE (and FEEDBACK from them) by concatenation, as test_doctor_public_content.py:15 does. Drop the module docstring's note about SELF and remove "scrub_store_support.py" from `SELF`. tests/test_no_installation_leaks.py must still pass.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/scrub_store_cmd.py:23 — The home roots `("home", "Users")` are written out again here, while src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:569 already has `_HOME_ROOTS = ("/" + "home" + "/", "/" + "Users" + "/")` for the same change's doctor check. The tilde lookbehind `(?<![\w/])~/` is also a second copy.
  Consequence: The doctor's public-content warning and the scrub that is meant to clear it have to agree on what a home path is. A root added to one (another OS's home root, for instance) leaves doctor warning about a path that scrub-store will never rewrite, or the reverse.
  Done when: Define one public `HOME_ROOTS` (bare names or `/x/` form) in src/agent_build_kit/scrub_terms.py beside `TOOL_DIRS`. Build both `doctor._HOME_PATH` and `scrub_store_cmd.HOME_PREFIX` from it, with no other spelling of the roots left in either module. Existing doctor and scrub-store tests keep passing.

Optional:
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/cli/scrub_store_cmd.py:27 — The new module-level `scrub_text(text)` has the same name as `scrub_terms.scrub_text(text, terms)` (re-exported by cli/scrub.py and split/scrubbing.py) but does something different. It also makes the scrub_terms module docstring ('anything that scrubs stored text uses it through `scrub_text`') misleading.
  Consequence: The next reader importing `scrub_text` can get the home-path pass when they meant the term pass, or the reverse.
  Done when: Rename it to `scrub_home_paths` (or keep it private), and adjust the scrub_terms docstring to say the home-path pass is separate.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/cli/scrub_store_cmd.py:24 — `[^/\s]+/?` swallows punctuation after a bare user directory. `see /home/someone, then` becomes `see <home>/ then` and a quoted `'/home/someone'` loses its closing quote. The spec says only the home prefix is replaced and every other term stays.
  Consequence: Feedback text loses a comma, quote or paren wherever a path ends at the user directory.
  Done when: Limit the user-directory segment to name characters, for example `[\w.-]+`, and add a test case `(/home/someone)` → `(<home>/)`.
- [1.6] src/agent_build_kit/cli/scrub_store_cmd.py:35 — The dry run gives one line per history entry (`<uid> history note: 1 path(s)` repeated) instead of one count per record and field, as the spec's dry-run requirement words it.
  Consequence: A unit with several history notes holding paths prints several identical-looking lines.
  Done when: Sum the history-note counts per unit and yield one `history note` row.
- [1.7] src/agent_build_kit/cli/redact_history_cmd.py:28 — `copy_of` and `paused_or_refused` now live in a command whose HELP says it is 'temporary: removed once every installation has run it', and the lasting `scrub-store` imports them from there.
  Consequence: Deleting redact-history later breaks scrub-store's imports unless someone moves the helpers first. Task 5.5 prescribed the sharing, so this is optional.
  Done when: Optionally move the two helpers to a lasting module (for example beside `pause_in_force` in pipeline/pause.py) and import them from both commands.

description.summary: Adds `abk scrub-store`, which replaces home-directory paths in the stored unit records with `<home>/`. It shares what a home path is with `abk doctor`'s public-content check, and shares the per-record text mapping with the split scrub.
changes: `abk scrub-store` counts home paths in each record's free-text fields and history notes, one row per field. With `--apply`, and only while the pipeline is paused, it rewrites them to `<home>/` and keeps the original as `units.json.pre-redact`. Paths under tool directories such as `~/.claude` are left alone.
A single `with_text` function in the unit store says which free-text fields a record has. Both `UnitStore.rewrite_text` and the split's `scrub_record` use it.
The home roots and the tilde prefix are defined once in `scrub_terms.py`. `abk doctor`'s home-path warning and `abk scrub-store` both build their patterns from them.

The original-copy suffix and its ignore pattern live in `pipeline/original_copy.py`, and the refuse-unless-paused check lives in `pipeline/pause.py`. `abk redact-history`, `abk scrub-store`, `abk doctor` and `abk init` all use these shared definitions.

units.title: Planning root role, pipeline marker and one sync routine
units.feedback:
Ran the two new test files and the guards (helpers-defined-once, one-definition-per-pattern, shared-commit-helper, no-installation-leaks, ecosystem-names, shared-patterns). All 59 pass. The sync logic matches the design's steps 1-5: the per-worktree git dir is checked for unfinished operations, HEAD on a branch is refused, the tip is fetched or taken from the local branch, and the merge is ff-only. Nothing is stashed, reset or deleted. Two required points block approval: the common-dir lookup now exists in two copies, and the rule that the repo entry's branch wins rests on a hard-coded "main" with no test.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/planning_sync.py:50 — `_git_path(root, "--git-common-dir")` repeats the existing `_common_dir` at `src/agent_build_kit/cli/pr_cmd.py:30`. Both run `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir` and resolve the result, returning None on failure. The search for the checkout that shares a repository's common dir also exists three times: `planning_mode` (planning_sync.py:99-103), `_in_repo_default_branch` (planning_sync.py:112-116) and `pr_cmd._repo_name` (pr_cmd.py:27).
  Consequence: Two copies of 'which repository is this path in' must change together. Later units (repository name, `Installation.checkouts` mapping, doctor) will need the same lookup and will pick one of the two copies or add a third. If `pr_cmd` and the planning mode disagree about a worktree, a command treats the same path as in-repo in one place and not in the other.
  Done when: Add one public function, e.g. `common_dir(path: Path) -> Path | None`, beside `is_repo` in `pipeline/planning_repo.py` (or in `pipeline/shell.py`). It returns None for a missing directory or a non-repo, as `pr_cmd._common_dir` does. Use it in `planning_sync` and in `pr_cmd` (delete `_common_dir`). Also add one helper in planning_sync, e.g. `in_repo_name(inst) -> str | None`: the name of the listed repo whose checkout shares the root's common dir. `planning_mode` and `_in_repo_default_branch` should both use it instead of each looping over `inst.checkouts`. Existing pr_cmd tests and the new mode tests must still pass.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/planning_sync.py:115 — `_in_repo_default_branch` decides that the repo entry 'says otherwise' with `branch != "main"`, a hard-coded copy of `RepoConfig.default_branch`'s default (config.py:795). No test covers this path: every fixture uses `main` with origin HEAD `main`.
  Consequence: The design (step 3) says the in-repo repo's `default_branch` wins, as verify's does, and verify uses `repo.default_branch` unconditionally (verify.py:241). Example: `abk.yaml` sets `default_branch: main` for the in-repo repo, but `origin/HEAD` points at `develop`. The sync fetches and fast-forwards to `origin/develop`, while verify (group 6) requires `main`, so the two disagree. The override branch has no test, so deleting it or inverting the check would still pass the suite.
  Done when: Make an explicitly set repo entry win. Either use `"default_branch" in repo.model_fields_set`, or take the entry's value outright, as verify does. Do not compare against the literal "main". Add a test in `tests/pipeline/test_planning_sync.py`: the in-repo repo is configured with `default_branch: trunk`, the bare origin has both `main` and `trunk` with origin HEAD on `main`, and a new commit is published to `trunk` only. Assert the outcome is SYNCED and the worktree's HEAD equals the `trunk` tip.

Optional:
- [1.3] tests/pipeline/test_planning_sync.py:209 — `test_a_separate_root_is_put_on_the_default_branch_and_pulled` ignores the `SyncResult` returned by `sync_planning`.
  Consequence: A regression that pulls but then reports STOPPED or SKIPPED would pass this test. Group 2's tick would then fail every separate installation.
  Done when: Assert `result.outcome == SyncOutcome.SYNCED`.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/planning_sync.py:69 — `write_pipeline_marker` writes `worktree` exactly as given, but the design says the marker holds the absolute path.
  Consequence: A caller passing a relative path writes a marker that every other worktree and cwd resolves differently. That makes no installation live, or the wrong one.
  Done when: Write `worktree.resolve()` (or reject a non-absolute path) so the stored value is always absolute.
- [1.5] tests/pipeline/test_planning_sync.py:84 — `test_a_worktree_ahead_of_the_tip_is_logged_and_left` and `test_a_diverged_worktree_is_stopped_with_both_commits_intact` set `user.email`/`user.name` in the worktree. `init_repo` already set them in the shared repository config, which a linked worktree reads.
  Consequence: These are noise lines that suggest a worktree needs its own identity.
  Done when: Drop the two `git config` calls in each test.

description.summary: When the planning root lives inside a code repository, the pipeline now tells that layout apart from a separate planning repo, records which worktree belongs to the pipeline, and brings the planning worktree up to date through one sync routine.
changes: The planning root is classified as separate, the pipeline's own worktree, or a person's working copy. The classification asks git whether a listed repo's checkout shares the root's common git directory.
A pipeline marker file in the common git directory names the pipeline's worktree, so every worktree of the repository sees the same one.

One sync routine either fast-forwards the planning worktree to the default branch's tip or stops with a reason: on an unfinished merge, rebase or similar, on a checked-out branch, or on a divergence. It never stashes, resets or deletes anything. A worktree that is ahead is logged and left alone.
For a planning root inside a code repo, the default branch comes from that repo's `default_branch` setting, as verify reads it, not from origin's HEAD.
Finding which checkout a path belongs to is one shared helper (`common_dir`, `repo_sharing` in planning_repo.py), and `abk pr` uses it too.

units.title: Tick and tracks sync the pipeline worktree and settle on a detached HEAD

description.summary: When the planning repo is one of the workspace's own repos, a tick and every track now first bring the pipeline's planning worktree up to date. They make and push their bookkeeping commits from a detached HEAD, and a working copy that someone is using is left untouched.
changes: `abk tick` brings the planning worktree up to the default branch's tip before it reads any state. If the sync has to stop (for example, HEAD is on a branch someone is keeping), the tick prints one line and ends without changing anything.
Tracks sync the pipeline worktree before they pull or choose a project. The planning repo's own project is not pulled, but its phase still runs.

A phase records the HEAD it started from and makes its commit on the detached HEAD, then pushes it to the default branch. If the push is rejected, it fetches, rebases once and pushes again. A second rejection, or a rebase that conflicts, is reported, and the commit is kept.
A phase that leaves HEAD on a branch is moved back to a detached HEAD at the recorded commit. If HEAD no longer contains the recorded commit, the run stops and commits nothing.
A tick or phase run in someone's working copy leaves its branch and files as they were: nothing is committed or pushed, and the run log stays untracked.

units.title: install-timers creates the pipeline worktree and marker

description.summary: `abk install-timers` run from a repository that is also the planning repo now runs the timers in a separate detached worktree of that repository, recorded in a pipeline marker, so ticks never touch the person's working copy.
changes: From a working copy, `install-timers` creates (or reuses) a detached worktree at `<data dir>/<repo name>/planning` at the default branch tip (origin's, or the local branch with no origin). It writes the pipeline marker in the common git directory and renders every unit with that worktree as `WorkingDirectory`. Run again from either the working copy or the worktree, it reports every unit unchanged.

It refuses a directory in the way that is not a worktree of this repository, and a default-branch ref that does not exist, naming the path or the `git fetch` to run, before any marker or unit is written. A worktree deleted by hand is refused with `git worktree prune` advice.

A reused worktree that is clean is moved to the tip through the same sync the tick uses. A dirty one is left where it is, with a note saying why. A worktree without `abk.yaml` gets a note that it is not on the default branch yet.

`--remove` takes off the units and the marker and leaves the worktree, printing its path and the `git worktree remove` command, or `git worktree prune` advice when it is gone. Both install and remove also take off units an earlier version pointed at the working copy itself.

The command output names the worktree it created or reused, where the units point, and the `--config <worktree>/abk.yaml` to use from the working copy. A separate planning repo installs exactly as before.
Small shared helpers come out of existing code: `data_home()` in `installation.py`, and `default_tip_ref()` and a public `in_repo_default_branch()` in `planning_sync.py`.
