units.title: Repository-derived names, worktree root and env file
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/installation.py:247 — `load_config` still reads `path.parent / ".env"` directly instead of going through the new `env_file` rule. In a pipeline worktree, the settings that `config.load` and `Installation.__init__` read come from no `.env` at all.
  Consequence: A pipeline worktree is a fresh checkout and never has its own `.env`, because `.env` is untracked. So `load_installation(worktree/abk.yaml)` calls `settings_module.reload(None)`. `config.load` then checks the runtime without the `ABK_RUNTIME` from the main working tree's `.env`. `Installation.__init__` reads `settings.worktree_root` (line 57) before `activate()` reloads with the right file, so an `ABK_WORKTREE_ROOT` set in the main working tree's `.env` is ignored and unit worktrees go to the default. That is the main case this group exists for. It also makes the changelog sentence 'a `.env` the worktree lacks is read from the main working tree' false for both settings.
  Done when: Put the rule in one function, for example `env_file_for(root: Path) -> Path` in installation.py: the root's own `.env`, or the main working tree's `.env` when the root is the pipeline worktree and has none. Use it in both `Installation.env_file` and `load_config`, with no second copy. Add a test in tests/test_installation_in_repo.py: a pipeline worktree with no `.env`, and a main working tree `.env` that sets `ABK_WORKTREE_ROOT=<tmp dir>`. Assert that `load_installation(config_path=worktree / 'abk.yaml').worktree_root` is that dir, and that the same holds when it is constructed through `load_config`.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/tracks/runner.py:215 — Task 4.4 says to list every direct reader of `repo.path` that bypasses `Installation.checkouts` and move it. That was not done, so the new relative-path rule and the working-copy mapping apply to some callers and not others.
  Consequence: Direct readers remain at:
- src/agent_build_kit/tracks/runner.py:215 (`eligible_projects`, which already has `inst`)
- src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/units.py:184 (`local_ref` → `has_origin(checkout)`)
- src/agent_build_kit/replay/review.py:43
- src/agent_build_kit/forges/local.py:108-109 and :132
- src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:115, 154-155, 181, 842, 999
- src/agent_build_kit/cli/changelog_cmd.py:38
- src/agent_build_kit/scrub_terms.py:96 and 103
With `repos.app.path: .` in the pipeline worktree, these resolve `.` against the process cwd, not the planning root. With an absolute path naming the person's working copy, tracks run, and doctor checks, the working copy instead of the pipeline worktree, which is what the change is meant to stop. The changelog sentence 'a relative `repos.<name>.path` is relative to the planning root' is false for these callers.
  Done when: Every pipeline, track, forge and doctor reader of a repo's checkout gets the path from `Installation.checkouts`, or from one shared function it uses: `inst.checkouts[name]` where an installation is at hand, or an accessor reached through the active installation for `units.local_ref` and the local forge. Init-time readers that run before an installation exists (init/scaffold.py:809, cli/init.py:233) may stay, each with a one-line reason. Add a test that the track runner's `eligible_projects` returns the pipeline worktree for `path: .` and for the absolute working-copy path, with the process cwd set to some other directory.
- [1.3] tests/test_timers_names_in_repo.py:13 — The new test helper `pipeline_worktree(base, repository)` copies `in_repo` in tests/planning_worktree_support.py:36: init a repo, commit, `git worktree add --detach`, `write_pipeline_marker`. The only difference is a repository name parameter.
  Consequence: The two fixtures that build a pipeline worktree have to change together. A change to how the marker or worktree is set up (for example an origin, or the `runs/units.json` seed) will reach one and not the other.
  Done when: Give `working_copy_of` and `in_repo` in tests/planning_worktree_support.py a `name: str = "app"` parameter. Place the worktree so that two names can live under one base, for example `base / f"{name}-planning"`, or keep `base / "planning"` when the name is `app`. Use `in_repo(tmp_path, name=...)` in test_timers_names_in_repo.py and delete `pipeline_worktree`.

Optional:
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/installation.py:117 — In a pipeline worktree, `checkouts` is a property that runs `git rev-parse` two or three times per repo on every access.
  Consequence: `inst.checkouts` is read at dozens of call sites, several of them inside per-unit loops. A tick in a pipeline worktree spawns many redundant git processes for an answer that cannot change during the installation's life.
  Done when: Compute the mapping once in `__init__` or with `functools.cached_property`, since the config is frozen.

description.summary: When the planning repo is also a code repo, abk reads its settings and finds its repositories' checkouts the same way from the main working tree and from the pipeline worktree.
changes: When the pipeline worktree has no `.env` of its own, it reads the main working tree's. This now applies to config loading too (`load_config`), so `ABK_RUNTIME` and `ABK_WORKTREE_ROOT` set there take effect from the worktree.
A relative `repos.<name>.path` is resolved against the planning root, not the process's current directory.

From the pipeline worktree, a repo path that names a worktree of the planning repo's own repository resolves to the pipeline worktree itself. Tracks, doctor and the pipeline then work there and not in the person's working copy.

Every reader of a repo's checkout uses one mapping: `Installation.checkouts`/`checkout_of`, or `config.active_checkout` for leaf modules with no installation. That covers the track runner, doctor checks, replay cassette review, changelog lookup, scrub terms, `units.local_ref` and the local forge.
The test fixtures for building a pipeline worktree are now one shared helper that takes a repository name.

units.title: Live installation notice and refusing commands in a working copy
units.feedback:
The dispatch helper, the doctor check and the changelog bullet match group 5. Two things block approval. Task 5.2 asks for two tests that are not in the file. The new check for an explicitly named config reads the environment directly, against the repo's settings convention, and so disagrees with how the config is actually found.

Required:
- [1.1] tests/cli/test_live_installation.py:42 — Task 5.2 asks for two tests that are missing: one that the pipeline worktree runs tick/track/verify/archive (and status) with no notice and no refusal, and one that with no marker each command runs as before. The `installed(..., marker=False)` parameter was added for the second test but nothing uses it.
  Consequence: Suppose a regression makes `live_notice` fire in the PIPELINE_WORKTREE role, or with no marker at all (for example, `planning_mode` compared without `.resolve()`, or `live_pipeline_worktree` ignoring a missing marker). Every timer tick would then exit 2 and do nothing. Every test in the file still passes, because each one runs only from the working copy with a marker present.
  Done when: Add two parametrized tests over COMMANDS plus `status`. (a) With `installed(tmp_path)` and `monkeypatch.chdir(live.worktree)`, and no `--config` and no ABK_CONFIG: `main(argv) == 0`, the patched command ran (`calls == [name]`), and stdout+stderr contain neither the worktree notice nor 'not the live'. (b) With `installed(tmp_path, marker=False)` and chdir to the working copy: `main(argv) == 0`, `calls == [name]`, and no notice is printed. For `status` in (b), assert that `working-copy-only/1` is listed.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/__init__.py:107 — `explicit` reads `os.environ.get(CONFIG_ENV)`. The config itself is found through `settings.config` (`installation.load_installation` passes `config_path or settings_module.settings.config`), and that setting is pydantic-settings with `env_file=".env"`.
  Consequence: AGENTS.md, under Conventions, says: 'Env config is pydantic-settings (settings.py); no os.environ reads elsewhere.' Because the two checks read different sources, they can disagree. Take ABK_CONFIG set in a `.env` that settings reads (or settings reloaded through `settings.reload(env_file)`). The installation was loaded from that named config, but `explicit` is False, so `abk tick` in the working copy refuses even though a config was named. The spec says it runs, naming that the config is not the live one.
  Done when: Compute `explicit = args.config is not None or settings.config is not None`, using `agent_build_kit.settings.settings`, the same source `load_installation` uses. Drop the `os` import. In the ABK_CONFIG test, set the variable in a way the settings object sees: monkeypatch `settings.config` or reload it, following how other tests set settings.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/__init__.py:112 — The refusal (exit 2) prints its message to stdout. The error a few lines above in the same function prints `abk: ...` to stderr.
  Consequence: A script or unit that runs `abk tick` and keeps only stderr records a silent exit 2. The tests accept either stream, so nothing pins it.
  Done when: Print the refusal with `file=sys.stderr`. Keep the status notice and the 'not the live' notice on stdout.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/cli/__init__.py:106 — The three `if notice ...` branches repeat the same conditions. `live_notice` also lives in `cli/__init__`, so `doctor._live_installation` has to import it lazily from the package to avoid a cycle.
  Consequence: The dispatch is harder to read than the rule it carries, which is: notice → print; if not explicit, return 0 for status and 2 otherwise. The lazy import hides a dependency.
  Done when: Write it as one `if notice: print(...); if not explicit: return 0 if args.command == 'status' else 2`. Consider moving `live_notice` beside `live_pipeline_worktree` in `pipeline/planning_sync.py` so that doctor and the CLI import it normally.

description.summary: When a planning working copy's installation is live in a separate pipeline worktree, abk says so, and the commands that write pipeline state refuse to run in the working copy unless a config is named explicitly.
changes: `abk tick`, `abk track`, `abk verify` and `abk archive` run in a working copy whose marker names a live pipeline worktree now exit 2. They print the `abk --config <worktree>/abk.yaml <command>` to run instead (or say to set ABK_CONFIG) and do nothing.
`abk status` in such a working copy prints where the installation is live and exits 0 instead of listing the working copy's own store.
Naming a config on the command line or through the ABK_CONFIG setting runs the command anyway, with a notice that this config is not the live installation.
`abk doctor` reports which pipeline worktree the installation is live in when it is run from such a working copy.

The pipeline worktree itself, and any working copy with no marker, run every command as before with no notice. The shared `live_notice` helper in pipeline/planning_sync.py decides all of this for both the CLI and doctor.

units.title: Verify in the pipeline worktree exempting planning paths

description.summary: `abk verify` can now verify a change whose repo is the planning repo itself, run from the pipeline worktree.
changes: For a repo that is the planning repo, run in the pipeline worktree, verification accepts a HEAD detached at the default branch's tip, where before it refused anything not on the default branch.

In place of `git pull`, it runs the planning sync to bring the worktree to the fetched tip. A stopped sync fails verification with the sync's reason, and if HEAD still lacks tip commits afterwards (for example with `self_pull` off), it refuses and names them.

The specs directory, the state directory and the graph and usage pages are left out of that repo's uncommitted-changes check. Any other tracked change, including `abk.yaml`, still holds verification. `Installation.planning_paths` exposes those paths.
What the planning sync says is kept in the verification detail.
For every repo, a `git status` that fails now holds verification, where before it read as a clean tree. Other repos otherwise keep their branch check, their dirty check and their pull.

units.title: Planning commits limited to planning paths
units.feedback:
All five earlier points are done and the new tests pass when I run them. One new problem remains, in the commit rework. A rename under the planning paths gets half-committed, because the name-only diff detects renames and lists only the new path. The fix is one flag and one test.

Required:
- [2.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:814 — With `only`, the list of paths to commit comes from `git diff --cached --name-only`. That command detects renames by default (`diff.renames`, on since git 2.9) and prints only the new path for a rename. So `git commit -- <names>` commits the added file but not the deletion of the old one.
  Consequence: Take an in-repo planning root where a session renames or moves a file under openspec/, for example moving `openspec/changes/feature/design.md` to `openspec/changes/feature/notes/design.md` with mostly the same content. `porcelain` gives both paths and `git add -A -- old new` stages a delete and an add. The name-only diff then prints only `.../notes/design.md`, and the commit holds just the new file. The commit pushed to the default branch now has the file twice. The old path's deletion stays staged after the commit, so the tree is not clean, and the next planning commit picks up an unrelated deletion. This was not visible in round 1: it came in with the rework of 1.1, and round 1's prescription for that fix missed it.
  Done when: Add `--no-renames` to the name-only diff: `git diff --cached --name-only --no-renames -- *only`. A rename is then listed as both its old and new paths, and `git commit -- <names>` records the deletion and the addition. Add a test in tests/pipeline/test_wiring_commit_only.py. Move a committed file under openspec/ to a new path with its content unchanged, then call `build_commit(only=("openspec",))("docs: plan", cwd=repo)`. Assert the result is 1. Assert HEAD's commit names both the old path (deleted) and the new one, for example with `git show --name-status --no-renames HEAD`. Assert `git status --porcelain` shows nothing under openspec/.

Optional:
- [2.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:779 — The docstring says that with `only`, whatever else the tree holds 'stays modified and unstaged'. But a file that was already staged outside the pathspecs now stays staged, which is the point of the 1.1 fix.
  Consequence: A reader of the docstring would expect a file staged outside the pathspecs to come back unstaged. It stays staged, as `test_a_file_already_staged_outside_the_pathspecs_is_not_committed` asserts.
  Done when: Reword the docstring, for example: 'nothing else is staged, checked or committed, and what else the tree holds is left as it was: modified files stay modified, and staged ones stay staged.'

description.summary: Commits made in a working copy whose planning files live in the code repository now take in only the planning paths, and leave the rest of the tree as it was.
changes: `build_commit` takes an `only` set of pathspecs. With it, the commit stages, gate-checks and commits only the changed paths under those pathspecs. Other files keep their state: modified files stay modified, and staged files stay staged.
With `only`, "nothing to commit" means nothing is staged under the pathspecs. A file staged only outside them makes the call return 0 and leaves HEAD where it was.
Renames and moves under the planning paths are committed whole, as a deletion of the old path and an addition of the new one, so the commit never holds the file twice and the tree is left clean.

Planning commits from attach, workspace setup and the chat server's planning flow pass the planning paths when the planning root sits inside the code checkout. A separate planning repository still commits every file.
Tests cover the scoped commit, the planning-path wiring and the chat planning count. They run against real git fixtures, and shared helpers live in tests/planning_paths_support.py.
The changelog has an entry saying that planning commits stay limited to planning paths.

units.title: planning.publish direct or branch
units.feedback:
Three things block this. A later phase's planning branch picks up the files an earlier phase already published. The test task 8.3 asked for, where the sync stops when the content differs, is missing. The test in task 8.1 that the setting has no effect never reads the setting, and nothing covers the working-copy case. The rest matches the spec: the setting, the push and pull request to the default branch, putting HEAD back, and clearing landed files before the fast-forward. The design.md UNVERIFIED notes (task 8.4) live in the planning repo and are not judged here.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/tracks/runner.py:557 — Under `branch`, a later phase's commit picks up the files every earlier phase already published, because `_publish_branch` leaves them uncommitted in the worktree and `commit_bookkeeping` stages them all again with `git add -A -- <state>/**/*.md`.
  Consequence: Say a run's health phase publishes `runs/track-health.md` on `planning/<run>-app-health` and resets HEAD, so the log is now untracked. The improve phase then commits that log as well, and its `planning/<run>-app-improve` pull request repeats the health phase's files. This repeats on every later run until each pull request lands, because the sync stays CURRENT and the untracked files stay. When two phases both edit `tracked-issues.md`, the second pull request holds both edits; once the first lands, the second conflicts on the shared lines. The spec says each pull request holds the phase's own commit.
  Done when: Under `branch`, a phase's commit holds only what that phase wrote. One way: before the phase runs, or before staging, record which state Markdown is already dirty, and stage only paths whose content changed since then. Add a test in tests/tracks/test_runner_publish_branch.py that runs two phases in one run under `branch` and checks that the second `planning/...` branch shows only the second phase's log (`git show --name-only`), not the first's.
- [1.2] tests/pipeline/test_planning_sync_published.py:43 — There is no test for the case where the local file differs from the landed content, which task 8.3 and the spec scenario 'A file that differs' require.
  Consequence: If `_clear_landed_files` deleted or restored a file whose content does not match, for example by dropping the `hash-object` comparison, every test would still pass. A person's local edits would then be thrown away when a published pull request lands.
  Done when: Add a test: write a log locally with one content, land the same path with other content through `publish_elsewhere`, and run `sync`. Check the outcome is the stopped one with a non-empty reason, HEAD has not moved, and the local file still holds its own content. Add one case for a tracked file, modified locally with content that differs from what landed: it is kept and the sync stops.
- [1.3] tests/test_config_planning_publish.py:64 — `test_it_has_no_effect_on_a_separate_root` only checks `planning_mode`, which never reads `planning.publish`. It passes whatever the runner does with the setting, and the working-copy case task 8.1 asks for is not tested at all.
  Consequence: Suppose `commit_bookkeeping` dropped its `detached` guard and published to a branch in a working copy. No test would fail. This test cannot fail on any publish behaviour.
  Done when: Remove this test, or replace it with one that runs a phase through the runner. Put it in tests/tracks/test_runner_publish_branch.py beside the existing separate-root test. Set up a working-copy installation (in-repo, no live pipeline worktree) with `publish: branch`, and check that `host.created` is empty, origin has no `planning/*` branch, and its default branch has not moved.

Optional:
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/tracks/runner.py:616 — The `repo_name is None` return in `_publish_branch` can never run, and it would push a branch silently without opening a pull request. `PIPELINE_WORKTREE` mode already guarantees `in_repo_name` is not None.
  Consequence: Anyone reading it may think a branch can be pushed without a pull request. If it ever did happen, nothing would be logged.
  Done when: Log a line naming the pushed branch before returning, or pass the repo name in from the caller, where the mode is already known.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/tracks/runner.py:614 — A change proposed under `branch` is left untracked in the pipeline worktree's `openspec/changes/` after the reset, so the tick can plan it before its pull request is reviewed.
  Consequence: Opening a pull request for a proposed change is meant to let someone review it before it lands. The worktree's tick reads `openspec/changes/` from disk, so it may treat the proposal as live while the pull request is still open.
  Done when: Decide whether the planner should skip a change that is published but has not landed. Record that in the change's design, or make it a follow-up.

description.summary: Adds a `planning.publish` setting so that, in a pipeline worktree, a phase's planning bookkeeping can be published as its own branch and pull request instead of being pushed straight to the default branch.
changes: With `planning.publish: branch`, a phase's commit of run logs and tracked issues is pushed to `planning/<run>-<project>-<phase>` and a pull request to the default branch is opened. HEAD is then reset so that the next sync is a fast-forward.

Within a run, each later phase commits only the state files it changed. Files an earlier phase published and left uncommitted in the worktree are left out by comparing content hashes taken before the phase.
When the planning repo has no code-host repo to open a pull request against, the push is logged as made with no pull request.
Planning sync clears local files that match content landed by a published pull request, and stops while keeping the local copy when the content differs.
The setting has no effect in a separate planning root or a working copy, and tests at the runner level cover both cases.

units.title: Doctor knows an in-repo installation
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:95 — _planning_publish reads the forge's empty `merge_guard` answer as 'protected', and LocalForge.merge_guard (src/agent_build_kit/forges/local.py:126) always returns "". So an in-repo installation on `forge: local` with the default `planning.publish: direct` now gets a FAIL saying main is protected and abk's commits cannot land.
  Consequence: A repo listed with `path: .` and `forge: local` (a supported forge, docs/code-forges.md:19) with `planning.publish` unset makes `abk doctor` fail 'main is protected and planning.publish is direct'. That is false: nothing on any server guards a local repo, and direct pushes work. It is a doctor failure the user cannot fix, because the advice is wrong. Before this change the same answer was only a misleading 'ok: main is protected' line in _merge_guards.
  Done when: LocalForge.merge_guard returns a non-empty reason, e.g. f"no server guards {branch}: the local forge keeps pull requests in the state directory", so both _merge_guards (info) and _planning_publish (ok for direct) read it as unguarded. Add a test in tests/cli/test_doctor_publish_conflict.py. It builds an in-repo installation whose repo sets `forge: local` and does not register a stand-in forge. It asserts the 'planning publish' check is 'ok' with publish=None. Add a forge test asserting LocalForge.merge_guard returns a non-empty string.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:113 — _pipeline_worktree calls the marker 'ok' when the named path is any existing directory (`named.is_dir()`). The spec (planning-in-repo-init, '`abk doctor` accepts a repo that is the root') says ok only when it names an existing worktree of the repository, and a warning when it is stale.
  Consequence: Two cases are reported 'ok' instead of the stale-marker warning: a marker naming a directory that is left over after its worktree was pruned, or one that was reused for something else, or one that is a worktree of a different repository. abk install-timers is the fix in both cases.
  Done when: Use the existing `is_worktree_of(named, common_dir(inst.root))` from src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/planning_repo.py:69 in place of `named.is_dir()`. Add a test in tests/cli/test_doctor_in_repo.py that writes the marker naming a plain existing directory that is not a git worktree (`write_pipeline_marker(root, tmp_path / 'plain')` after mkdir). It asserts the 'pipeline worktree' check is 'warn' with 'abk install-timers' in its fix.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:96 — The ok detail is the same f"{publish}; {branch} is not protected against it" in two cases, and in one of them it says the opposite of what the forge reported.
  Consequence: With `planning.publish: branch` and a protected main (the spec's 'Protected and branch' scenario), doctor prints 'ok planning publish: branch; main is not protected against it', but main *is* protected. The user is told a false thing about their branch protection.
  Done when: Split the ok branch. When guard is non-empty (unprotected), the detail is f"{publish}; {guard}". When guard is "" and publish is branch, the detail is f"branch; {branch} is protected, so abk publishes through a pull request". Extend test_branch_with_a_protected_default_branch_is_ok to assert 'is protected' in found.detail and 'not protected' not in found.detail.

Optional:
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:93 — Telling 'cannot say' apart from 'unprotected' depends on `guard.startswith("cannot tell")`. That phrase is shared by the github and azure_devops forges and by _guard_of, but the Forge.merge_guard contract (forges/base.py:353) does not mention it.
  Consequence: A forge, or an edit to one, that phrases an unreadable answer differently has it read as 'unprotected'. The check then reports ok instead of the info line the spec requires.
  Done when: Make the three outcomes explicit: protected, unguarded with a reason, or unknown with a reason. That means either a small result type from _guard_of, or documenting the 'cannot tell' prefix in Forge.merge_guard's docstring as the contract.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:108 — `is_repo(inst.root)` in _pipeline_worktree is redundant. in_repo_name only returns a name when common_dir(inst.root) is not None.
  Consequence: The check does nothing; it only makes the next reader wonder which case it guards.
  Done when: Drop the `or not is_repo(inst.root)` and the import, or keep it with a comment if a case exists that in_repo_name does not cover.

description.summary: `abk doctor` now recognises an installation whose planning lives inside one of its code repos (a repo with `path: .`) and checks the things specific to that layout.
changes: A new 'planning publish' check compares `planning.publish` with what the forge reports about the default branch. It fails when `direct` meets a protected branch and says 'info' when the forge cannot be asked. Otherwise it is 'ok', and the detail says whether the branch is unguarded or protected and published through a pull request.

A new 'pipeline worktree' check reads the pipeline marker. It is 'ok' only when the marker names a real worktree of the same repository. When it names a missing directory, a plain directory or a worktree of another repository, it warns and points to `abk install-timers`.

The local forge now reports that no server guards its branches, instead of an empty answer that read as 'protected'. The merge-guard and planning-publish checks therefore treat a local repo as unguarded.
The Forge protocol now documents that a merge_guard reason beginning 'cannot tell' means the host could not be asked, and doctor reads it as such.
Tests cover each publish/protection combination, an in-repo installation on the local forge, and stale or foreign pipeline markers.

units.title: Unit worktree cannot write planning paths
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/acp.py:901 — This branch adds `ToolPolicy.planning_paths` but only the Claude Code runtime uses it. The ACP runtime takes the same `ToolPolicy` and checks file writes itself in `_resolve_target`, which `write_text_file` (line 1085) and the edit-permission check (line 874) both call. That method checks only the worktree and `specs_dir`, so it never reads `planning_paths`.
  Consequence: Take an installation whose build runtime is ACP and a unit whose repo is the planning repo. Its agent can write `abk.yaml`, `runs/units.json` or `openspec/changes/<c>/tasks.md` in its worktree, through `fs/write_text_file` or an edit permission request, and the write is allowed. The spec requirement 'A unit worktree of the planning repo cannot write the planning paths' (the tool policy SHALL deny) then holds for only one runtime. The new CHANGELOG bullet also says these writes 'are refused', which is false for ACP units. No later task group (11–17) covers the ACP runtime.
  Done when: In the ACP client, keep the policy's planning paths, for example `self._fenced = tuple(self._worktree / p for p in policy.planning_paths)` when there is a policy and a worktree. In `_resolve_target`, after the specs check and only while `_scoped`, return None for a candidate that `is_relative_to` any of them. Make the `write_text_file` refusal reason name the planning paths and say to report `BLOCKED: <what and where>`. Add a test under `tests/runtimes/`, next to the existing ACP client write tests, with a `ToolPolicy(planning_paths=("openspec", "runs", "abk.yaml"))` and a real worktree. It should assert that `write_text_file` and an edit permission request are refused for `abk.yaml` and `openspec/changes/x/tasks.md`, and allowed for `src/module.py` and `tests/fixtures/x/abk.yaml`. It should also assert that with an empty `planning_paths` the `openspec/x.md` write is allowed.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/hooks/policy.py:382 — The planning paths go into the hook's shell command joined by commas and without quoting. A configured `state_dir`, `specs_dir` or page path containing a space or a comma would break the argument parse or split one path into two.
  Consequence: Suppose `planning.graph_page: "docs/unit graph.md"`. The hook command gets an extra argument, argparse exits with an error, and every tool call in that unit's run fails at the hook. The existing `--planning-state-dir` and `--planning-change-dir` flags have the same shape, so this follows the surrounding pattern rather than adding a new kind of problem.
  Done when: Optional: pass each path through `shlex.quote`, or repeat the flag once per path with `action="append"`, and do the same for the existing path flags.

description.summary: When a unit's repo is the planning repo, its agent cannot write the pipeline's planning paths in its worktree. These are the specs, the state, the generated pages and abk.yaml. Both the Claude Code hook and the ACP runtime refuse the write and tell the agent to report BLOCKED.
changes: `ToolPolicy` carries `planning_paths`. The pipeline fills them in for a unit whose repo is the planning repo, so its agent cannot write those paths in its own worktree.

The Claude Code PreToolUse hook takes `--planning-paths` and refuses a write under any of them. The refusal says to report `BLOCKED: <what and where>`. Every other path stays writable, including a nested fixture that happens to be called `abk.yaml`.
The ACP client applies the same fence. Its file writes and its edit permission requests are refused for a planning path, with the same BLOCKED wording.

The hook command shell-quotes the path flags (`--specs`, `--planning-repo`, `--planning-state-dir`, `--planning-change-dir`, `--planning-paths`), so a path with a space or another special character stays one argument.
A changelog bullet says that the planning paths are refused to such units.

units.title: locate ignores a unit worktree's abk.yaml
units.feedback:
The behaviour matches the spec's `locate()` requirement and task group 11. All twelve tests pass locally, each in its own tmp_path, with no clock or thread use. One thing blocks approval: the new check copies two git queries the pipeline already has, one of them line for line. The design.md correction in 11.3 lives in the planning repo, not on this branch, so I could not review it here. The docs (`docs/configuration.md` 'Locating abk.yaml') and the changelog belong to groups 15 and 16, so they do not block this unit.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/config.py:1234 — `own = git(tree, "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-dir", check=False)` followed by `Path(own.stdout.strip()).resolve()` copies the private `_git_dir` in src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/planning_sync.py:52-54: the same argv, the same returncode check and the same resolve.
  Consequence: There are now two copies of how a worktree's own git directory is found, and they must change together. If `_git_dir` changes, for example to handle a bare repository or a `.git` file indirection the way design.md's UNVERIFIED notes anticipate, the unit-worktree check in `locate` and the sync's unfinished-operation check in `_sync_worktree` (planning_sync.py:135) will disagree about whether a directory is a linked worktree.
  Done when: Move `_git_dir` to `pipeline/planning_repo.py` as a public `git_dir(path) -> Path | None` beside `common_dir`, with a docstring like common_dir's. Use it in `planning_sync._sync_worktree` and in `config._not_a_unit_worktree`, so the check reads `own = git_dir(tree); common = common_dir(tree); if own is None or common is None or own == common: return found`. No copy of the rev-parse --git-dir argv should remain in config.py.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/config.py:1238 — Reading the checked-out branch with `git(tree, "symbolic-ref", "--short", "-q", "HEAD", check=False).stdout.strip()` adds a sixth inline copy of the same query. The others are planning_repo.py:52, planning_sync.py:140, wiring.py:311 and restack.py:742, plus a timeout-carrying variant at runtimes/acp.py:956.
  Consequence: Every place that reads 'the branch this tree has checked out, or empty when detached' must stay in step. The detached-HEAD meaning matters here in particular: the spec's 'A detached unit worktree' scenario depends on an empty string meaning detached, and that is now spelled out independently in several places.
  Done when: Add `current_branch(path: Path) -> str` to `pipeline/planning_repo.py`, returning the short branch name or "" when HEAD is detached. Use it in config.py's new check, and at least in its siblings planning_repo.py:52 (`restore_default_branch`) and planning_sync.py:140 (`_sync_worktree`), the modules this change already depends on. wiring.py:311 and restack.py:742 may follow but are not required.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/config.py:1239 — The unit-branch prefix comes from `read_base(found)`, the committed file alone, so it ignores the local overlay beside abk.yaml that `load()` merges (config.py:1365-1369).
  Consequence: Suppose an installation sets `git.branch_prefix` only in its overlay, say `agent/`. The pipeline then creates `agent/<change>/<n>` branches, but `locate` matches against the committed default `spec/`. A hand-run `abk` in such a unit worktree silently adopts the worktree's abk.yaml, which is exactly what this requirement forbids. If the overlay is git-ignored, the unit worktree has none, so the right prefix may only be readable from the pipeline worktree's overlay.
  Done when: Read the prefix from the merged base and overlay mapping (the same merge `load` does, without validation), or document in the docstring that the overlay's `git.branch_prefix` is not consulted. Either way, a test with an overlay setting the prefix should pin whichever behaviour is chosen.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/config.py:1233 — The check uses `found.parent`, so a nested `abk.yaml`, such as a test fixture inside a unit worktree, is also replaced by the pipeline worktree's file when `locate` runs from inside that fixture directory.
  Consequence: A unit agent that runs `abk config --path` or a similar command from a fixture directory holding its own abk.yaml gets the live installation's file, not the fixture's. The spec's fence requirement treats a nested abk.yaml as an ordinary file, but this redirect does not.
  Done when: Either apply the redirect only when `found.parent` is the worktree's top level (compare it with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`), or state in the docstring that any abk.yaml inside a unit worktree is redirected. Add a test for the chosen case.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/config.py:1229 — `config.py` is the leaf the rest import, and it now does function-local imports of `pipeline.planning_sync`, which imports `installation`, which imports `config`. The local import exists only to break that cycle.
  Consequence: Nothing breaks today, but config's import surface now runs through the pipeline package, and a top-level import added there later would turn this into an import-time cycle.
  Done when: Optional: move `marker_path`, `read_pipeline_marker` and `MARKER_NAME` into `pipeline/planning_repo.py`, which imports only `shell`, and re-export them from planning_sync. config.py would then import from a module that does not reach `installation`.

description.summary: When abk.yaml is found inside a unit worktree (a linked worktree on a `<prefix><change>/<n>` branch), locating the installation now uses the pipeline worktree's abk.yaml instead, and the git queries for a worktree's own git directory and checked-out branch now each live in one shared helper.
changes: Locating abk.yaml ignores a unit worktree's own copy. When the found file is in a linked worktree on a unit branch, the live pipeline worktree's abk.yaml is used instead, and an error is raised when there is no live pipeline worktree.
The unit-branch test uses the `git.branch_prefix` from the committed abk.yaml. A tree on a detached HEAD, or on a branch outside that shape, keeps its own file.
`pipeline/planning_repo.py` gains `git_dir(path)` (a worktree's own git directory, or None) and `current_branch(path)` (the short branch name, or "" when detached).

The planning sync's check for unfinished operations, `restore_default_branch`, wiring's unit-branch lookup, restack's `adopt_host_head` and `abk pr`'s branch lookup now use these helpers instead of inline git commands.

New tests in tests/test_config_locate_unit_worktree.py cover each case using real git worktrees under tmp_path: a unit worktree, a detached unit worktree, a non-unit branch, a custom prefix and no live pipeline worktree.

units.title: Specs dir from config, and repo hooks and CI scope
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] scripts/ci_scope.py:25 — `changed_paths` runs `git diff --name-only BASE HEAD`, which detects renames by default (diff.renames has been on by default since git 2.9) and lists only the new path of a renamed file. A file moved from code into a planning path therefore shows up only under its planning name.
  Consequence: A PR that runs `git mv src/agent_build_kit/foo.py openspec/foo.py` (or moves any code or test file under `openspec/` or `runs/`) produces only `openspec/foo.py` from `--name-only`. The script prints `code=false`, the `test` and `integration` jobs are skipped, and the skipped jobs satisfy the required checks, so a change that deletes a module merges without the suite running. Group 14's done criterion is that the test jobs are skipped only when nothing outside the planning paths changed.
  Done when: Pass `--no-renames` to the `git diff` in `changed_paths`, so a rename lists both the deleted source path and the added destination path. Add a case to `tests/test_repo_gates.py`: in the temporary repo, commit a file under `src/`, then `git mv` it to `openspec/` in the head commit. Assert `scope_output` is `code=true`. `scope_output` writes new files and cannot express a rename today, so the test needs a variant or helper that runs `git mv`.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/init.py:774 — The same proposing loop now reports `kept {specs_dir}/changes/<change>/` but still prints `wrote openspec/changes/{change}/`. The dry-run plan (line 216 `propose: openspec/changes/...`) and `init/propose.py` (the prompt text at lines 108/112/150 and the error at line 347) also still name `openspec/changes`.
  Consequence: With `planning.specs_dir: specs`, the lookup reads `specs/changes/<change>`, but the propose agent is told to write under `openspec/changes/<change>/`. A rerun of `abk init` would not find what the first run proposed and would propose it again. Task 13.3 names only `CHANGE_DIR` and init's lookup, so this is beyond the group's stated scope, but it is the same literal in the same flow.
  Done when: In a follow-up (or a later unit), pass the configured specs directory through `propose` and use it in its prompt text, its error message, the `wrote` line and the dry-run plan line.
- [1.3] scripts/ci_scope.py:15 — The planning paths are hardcoded here as a second copy of the list that `Installation.planning_paths` (per the design) returns.
  Consequence: If this repo's `specs_dir`, `state_dir` or page names ever change, the CI scope and the pipeline's notion of planning paths drift apart. The duplication is understandable, since the scope job runs before `uv sync`.
  Done when: Leave a comment pointing at the canonical list, or have the script read the four names from `abk.yaml` when it exists.

description.summary: The runner and `abk init` find a change under the configured specs directory instead of a hard-coded `openspec`, and this repo's pre-commit hooks and CI are scoped to how the pipeline uses the repo.
changes: The unit runner now builds a change's directory and its follow-ups file path from `planning.specs_dir` (the new `change_dir_of` in `stack_runner.py`), so a specs directory with another name works.
`abk init` checks for an existing proposed change under the configured specs directory, and its `kept` message names that directory.
Pre-commit skips the pipeline's state directory `runs/`, so model-written logs and the unit store are not rewritten or rejected. `abk.yaml` is outside that directory and is still linted.

CI has a new `scope` job that runs `scripts/ci_scope.py` over the changed paths. The test and integration jobs run only when something outside the planning paths changed (`openspec/`, `runs/`, the two generated docs pages, `abk.yaml`), and when they are skipped they still satisfy required checks.
The scope check turns off git's rename detection, so a code file moved into a planning path still counts as a code change and the test jobs run.
Tests cover the specs directory in the runner and in init, the hook exclusion, the workflow's lack of a path filter, and the scope script against real temporary git repos, including moves.

units.title: abk init recognises a repo that is its own planning repo

description.summary: `abk init` now recognises when the planning directory sits inside one of the code repos it is given, and sets that repository up in place instead of making a nested planning repo.
changes: `abk init . --repo .` (or a planning subdirectory with `--repo .`) writes the repo's path relative to the planning directory. A single `holds_planning` rule makes this decision for both the config draft and the in-repo check.

In that mode init creates no nested git repository, leaves existing files and the unit store as they are, and commits nothing. It lists each file it wrote, or prints 'planning repo: nothing to write' on a rerun.

The state-directory ignore lines go into `.gitignore`, and a planning orientation goes into AGENTS.md (or else CLAUDE.md). Both are marker blocks that a rerun refreshes in place, and a CRLF `.gitignore` gets a CRLF block.

A guidance file whose markers do not pair up, or that is not valid UTF-8, is refused by name in the planning path. The code-repo changelog block now skips a non-UTF-8 file and leaves its bytes as they are, where it used to rewrite the file with replacement characters.
A separate planning directory is still laid out, committed and printed exactly as before, and a test now pins that.

units.title: Documents describe the in-repo planning mode

description.summary: Documents the in-repo planning mode, where the planning repo is also one of the code repos. They cover its three roles, how the pipeline worktree is synced and published, and the two settings that govern it.

It also says a working copy points at the live worktree and refuses the state-writing commands unless a config is named.

init.md describes `abk install-timers` creating or reusing the detached pipeline worktree and printing its path.

units.title: Rules, skills, templates and changelog for in-repo planning
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/templates/planning-orientation.md:13 — The in-repo orientation block doesn't say that a session edits specs and state but not the code, or how to run the pipeline from a working copy. It is the orientation `abk init` writes when a repo is its own planning repo (scaffold.py `_orientation`, line 688), and this unit left it unchanged.
  Consequence: Group 16's done criterion says the planning orientation template must say 'an interactive session does not edit the code but may edit specs and state'. For a repo that is both the planning repo and a code repo, the only orientation `abk init` writes is planning-orientation.md. `planning-CLAUDE.md` is written only in the separate-repo branch (scaffold.py lines 773-781). An agent opening an in-repo installation reads 'the pipeline builds changes into it' and nothing more. It isn't told not to apply a change to the code by hand. It isn't told that `abk tick` refuses in the working copy (cli/__init__.py line 87 to 92) and that `abk --config <worktree>/abk.yaml tick` is the command to run.
  Done when: Add a short paragraph to planning-orientation.md. Changes are written under `{prefix}{specs_dir}/changes/` in the working copy and committed. A session does not edit the code to apply a change: the pipeline builds it. Ticks and tracks run in the pipeline worktree that `abk install-timers` makes, and from the working copy the command is `abk --config <worktree>/abk.yaml tick`, which `abk status` prints. Any literal brace must be doubled, because the template goes through str.format. Extend tests/test_templates_planning_in_repo.py with a test that formats planning-orientation.md the way `_orientation` does (or calls the public init path that renders it) and asserts the output names 'pipeline worktree' and '--config' and says the code is not edited by hand.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/templates/planning-CLAUDE.md:4 — The new sentence 'It may also be one of those code repos.' is in a template that scaffold.py writes only for a separate planning repo (the `else` branch at lines 773-781). The in-repo case writes planning-orientation.md instead. Every installation that receives this file is one where the sentence is false.
  Consequence: An agent reading a separate planning repo's CLAUDE.md may think code lives there too. The template also still ends with 'Run `abk tick`', which would be refused in an in-repo working copy if the sentence were true.
  Done when: Drop the sentence, or reword the opening so it describes this repo without saying the planning repo is never a code repo. For example: 'This repo holds the specs, the pipeline state and the run logs of an `abk` workspace that builds {repo_names}.' That still passes the SEPARATION test.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/skills/abk-pipeline/SKILL.md:58 — The list of stop reasons leaves out two that `_sync_worktree` produces: a failed fetch (planning_sync.py line 200), and a fast-forward refused because a local file differs from what lands (line 213, the published-file case from group 8). The fix steps don't cover a modified file in the way.
  Consequence: A person who sees `planning sync stopped: error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten` gets no matching cause or fix from the skill.
  Done when: Add 'a fetch from origin that failed' and 'a file in the pipeline worktree that differs from what the default branch brings'. For the second, the fix is to commit it to the default branch or remove it.
- [1.4] AGENTS.md:5 — The rewrapped opening line is about 120 characters, while every other line in the paragraph wraps near 78.
  Consequence: It's only cosmetic: the paragraph reads unevenly in plain text.
  Done when: Rewrap the opening paragraph at the file's usual width.
- [1.5] tests/test_skills_planning_in_repo.py:42 — The first regex `planning sync stopped.{0,400}(diverged|means)` matches the word 'means' right after the quoted line, so it would pass even if the stop reasons were never explained.
  Consequence: A rewording that drops the explanation of what a stop means would still pass.
  Done when: Assert on a reason the code really emits, such as 'diverged' and 'unfinished', not 'means'.

description.summary: Updates the packaged skills, templates, rules and changelog so that an installation whose planning repo is also one of its code repos is described correctly, and tells a session in that working copy how to work there.
changes: When `abk init` sets up a repo as its own planning repo, the orientation it writes now explains that changes are written and committed in the working copy, and that the code is not edited by hand. It also says ticks and tracks run in the pipeline worktree that `abk install-timers` makes, reached from the working copy with `abk --config <worktree>/abk.yaml tick`.
The separate planning-repo CLAUDE template no longer claims the planning repo may also be a code repo.

The abk-pipeline skill explains every reason the planning sync can stop: diverged commits, an unfinished merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert, a stray branch, a failed fetch, and a file that differs from what the default branch brings. It says how to fix each one.
The AGENTS.md opening says the planning repo may itself be one of the code repos.
New tests check that the templates and skills keep saying these things.

units.title: A scratch planning-in-repo installation runs end to end

description.summary: Makes a planning-in-repo installation on the local forge run end to end: verify sees the files a local pull request changed, tracks accept local-forge repos whatever their origin, and an acceptance test drives a scratch installation through tick, verify and track publishing.
changes: The local forge records where each pull request's branch left the trunk (its fork point) beside its tip, and moves both on a rework or rebase. `pr_files` lists the files in that range, NUL-separated and without rename detection. units.title: The account is one setting with stated rules, and every claude the pipeline starts is told it

description.summary: Adds a per-installation Claude Code account setting (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or `ABK_CLAUDE_HOME`, from the process or the installation's `.env`) and makes every claude the Claude Code runtime starts, and the sessions page, use that account directory.
changes: A new `claude_account` module reads the account directory from the existing `claude_home` setting. It expands `~`, refuses a relative path with a message naming the value, the variable and where it came from, treats an empty value as unset, and can report which name and place supplied the value.

With an account set, every `claude` the Claude Code runtime starts (builds, planner, restack resolver, tracks, chat turns, init research) gets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir>` on top of any gateway entries or inherited value. With none set, nothing is added and calls are unchanged.
`refresh_login` runs its `claude` with the process environment plus the account variable when an account is set, so the login it refreshes belongs to that account.
The sessions page lists, opens and resumes sessions from the account's `projects` directory. A session of the default account answers 404 while another account is set.
Tests pin the precedence rules, the value rules, that abk.yaml has no key for the account, and that the test suite never inherits a developer's own account setting.
The changelog gains a bullet saying how to run an installation on its own Claude Code account.

units.title: The usage guard reads the account's credentials and state file
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_guard.py:956 — The pause reason for an unknown reading still says "neither the usage endpoint nor ~/.claude.json could be read". With an account set, the file this change makes the guard read is `<dir>/.claude.json`, so the reason now names a file the guard never opened.
  Consequence: Take an installation with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/srv/acct` whose endpoint read fails and which has no block in `/srv/acct/.claude.json`. `decide_start` pauses with a reason that sends the operator to `~/.claude.json`. That is the default account's file, which this change says must never be read when an account is set. The sentence was true before this change and is false after it.
  Done when: Build the reason from the path actually read, e.g. `f"usage is unknown: neither the usage endpoint nor {_state_file()} could be read"`. With no account this still prints the default path, and with an account it prints `<dir>/.claude.json`. Add one case to `tests/pipeline/test_usage_guard_account_state_file.py`: with `host.use_account()` and no block, nothing kept and the endpoint failing, `decide_start(...)` has `may_start` false and a reason containing `str(account / '.claude.json')` and not `str(usage_guard.DEFAULT_ANCHOR_PATH)`.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_guard.py:31 — The module docstring still gives the fallback source as `~/.claude.json`'s `cachedUsageUtilization`, without saying it is the account's state file when one is set.
  Consequence: Someone reading the module learns the old rule. No behaviour depends on it.
  Done when: Say "Claude Code's state file (`<account dir>/.claude.json` with an account set, else `~/.claude.json`)".

description.summary: With a Claude Code account (config directory) set, the usage guard reads that account's credentials and `.claude.json` state file instead of the default account's, and its messages name the file it actually read.
changes: With an account directory set, the fallback usage reading (`cachedUsageUtilization`) comes from `<account dir>/.claude.json` and never opens `~/.claude.json`. With no account set, the default file is used as before.

Start decisions, held readings and refreshed readings (`decide_start`, `held_usage`, `refreshed_usage`, `read_cached_usage`) all use the account's state file. An account with no cached block gives no reading, whatever the default file holds.
When usage is unknown, the pause reason names the state file the guard tried to read: the account's when one is set, else `~/.claude.json`.
The `usage_guard` module docstring now describes the fallback source as Claude Code's state file for the active account.

New tests in `tests/pipeline/test_usage_guard_account_state_file.py` fail if the default state file is opened while an account is set. A shared `Host.use_account` / `refuse_default_state_file` helper in `tests/usage_host.py` supports them.

units.title: A kept reading belongs to one account, status names it, and other-account sessions start afresh
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] tests/pipeline/test_usage_calls_account.py:91 — Task 4.2 and the spec scenario 'The rate figures read every line' ask for both `derive_rate` and `cache_interval` over a record of two accounts. The test only checks `derive_rate`; it never calls `cache_interval`.
  Consequence: If someone made `cache_interval` (usage_calls.py:209) filter by account or stop at the last account change, refusals logged under the other account would no longer double the interval. The spec forbids this (the design says counting every call is the safe side), and no test would fail.
  Done when: Add a test that writes a record with a refusal line (outcome REFUSED, no Retry-After) under account `<a>`, then lines under `<b>`, with the setting `<b>`. Call `cache_interval(calls, now=..., base=B, maximum=M)` and assert the interval is 2*B, the doubled value, so the refusal from `<a>` still counts.
- [1.2] tests/pipeline/test_usage_allowances_account.py:387 — Task 4.3 and the spec scenario 'One account throughout' cover a record whose lines all name `<a>` and also one whose lines all name none. Only the named-account case is tested.
  Consequence: With no account set, `since_last_change` has to keep the whole record when every line's account is None. If it went wrong for None (a truthiness or `is` slip, or treating None as 'a different account'), every installation without an account would lose its calibration, and no test would catch it.
  Done when: Add a test with no setting (`settings.claude_home = None`) over the same `old + new` record with `account` left as None. Assert that `refreshed(...).pairs_available == 10 + ENOUGH`, the same as the single-account result.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/usage_cmd.py:58 — `abk usage replay` builds `pairs(calls, ...)` from the whole record and calibrates each prefix with `calibrate_pairs`. Only its last line goes through `calibrated_allowances`, which drops lines from before the account change.
  Consequence: With a record that switches from `<a>` to `<b>`, the replay counts the gap from the last `<a>` reading to the first `<b>` reading as a usable pair. Its gain is meaningless, and the earlier allowances it shows mix both accounts. Its last line, which is filtered, then disagrees with the rows above it.
  Done when: Either filter `calls` with `since_last_change(calls, claude_account.account_key())` in `cmd_usage_replay`, or make `pairs`/`consecutive_readings` never pair two readings whose `account` differs. The second would fix both callers in one place.

description.summary: Usage readings now record which Claude account they came from. Allowance calibration and `abk usage replay` start over after a change of account, while the call-rate and cache-interval figures keep counting every line.
changes: Each line of the usage call record names the account (the configured Claude home) it was read under. Older lines that name none still load, with no account.

Allowance calibration pairs only the readings after the last change of account, so readings from one account are never paired with another's. A record that stays on one account, or never names one, is calibrated whole.
`abk usage replay` uses the same restart: its rows, counts and allowances line come only from readings after the last change of account.
The call-rate figures and the usage cache interval still count every line across accounts. A refusal recorded under the previous account still doubles how long a reading is kept.
Status names the account a kept reading belongs to, and a session belonging to another account starts fresh instead of reusing that reading.

units.title: User skills, doctor, the template and the docs for the account
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/claude_code.py:448 — `account_report` calls `claude_account.home()` (and `environment_entry()`) without catching the `ConfigError` that `_configured()` raises for a relative value, so `abk doctor` crashes on exactly the misconfiguration it should diagnose.
  Consequence: With `ABK_CLAUDE_HOME=accounts/second` in the planning repo's `.env` (the spec's own 'A relative value is refused' scenario), `abk doctor` dies with a Python traceback from `_runtime` -> `_account` -> `account_report`. Nothing in `run_doctor` or `cli.main` catches it, because `main` only guards `load_installation`. So none of the later checks print. Every other doctor step that can hit a `ConfigError` (`config`, `worktree root`) turns it into a FAIL line.
  Done when: `account_report` (or `_account` in doctor.py) catches `ConfigError` and returns one `AccountLine(status="FAIL", detail=str(error), fix="write an absolute path for <name>")`, without running `auth status`. Add a test in `tests/cli/test_doctor_claude_account.py`: with `ABK_CLAUDE_HOME=relative/dir` in the `.env`, `run_doctor` returns normally, the `runtime account` check is FAIL and names the value and `ABK_CLAUDE_HOME`, `run.asked == []`, and checks after the runtime check (for example `telemetry`/`skills`) are still present.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/claude_code.py:498 — `_logged_in` copies `refresh_login`'s expression for handing a `claude` the account's environment: `**({"env": child_environment(None, entry)} if entry else {})` at line 185.
  Consequence: Two copies of the rule for how a side `claude` call (not a build) is started in the account must now change together. If one copy changes (always pass `env`, or add an entry), the doctor login check and the token refresh would ask different accounts.
  Done when: One module-level helper in `claude_code.py` (for example `_account_run_kwargs()`, returning `{"env": child_environment(None, entry)}` when `claude_account.environment_entry()` is non-empty and `{}` otherwise) is used by both `refresh_login` and `_logged_in`. The existing tests (`test_claude_refresh_login_env.py`, `test_the_login_question_is_asked_with_the_accounts_variable`, `test_the_default_account_says_so_and_asks_without_a_variable`) keep passing unchanged.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/claude_code.py:452 — The login command shell-quotes the claude argv but not the directory: `f"{name}={value}"` is unquoted.
  Consequence: An account directory with a space or shell metacharacter prints a fix line that does not run as written, even though the spec calls it 'the exact command'.
  Done when: Write `f"{name}={shlex.quote(value)}"`. Add a test with a directory containing a space whose printed fix, passed through `shlex.split`, gives `["CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=<dir>", "claude", "auth", "login"]`.
- [1.4] tests/cli/claude_auth_fakes.py:480 — `account_lines` selects checks by `"account" in check.name`, which also matches doctor's existing `gh account` check.
  Consequence: If a fixture ever produces a `gh account` line, the positive tests would read a check that is not the runtime account check, and `all(status in (ok, info))` could fail or pass for the wrong reason.
  Done when: Filter on `check.name == "runtime account"`.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/claude_code.py:456 — When the account directory does not exist, the early return also skips the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` warning.
  Consequence: A person fixing a missing directory sees the token warning only on the next doctor run. This is minor because the spec's scenario for the token assumes an existing account.
  Done when: Optionally compute the token warning before the existence check and append it in both branches.

description.summary: Lets an installation run Claude Code under its own account directory and has the user-facing tools report, check and document that account.
changes: `abk doctor` adds a 'runtime account' check. It names the account directory and where the setting came from, and says whether `auth status` reports it logged in. It fails with a login command you can paste, shell-quoted, when the directory is missing or not logged in.
A relative ABK_CLAUDE_HOME no longer crashes `abk doctor`. It is reported as one FAIL line naming the value and the variable, and the remaining checks still run.

Doctor warns when CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is set beside a non-default account, because the usage guard would otherwise read the wrong credentials. The warning also appears when the account directory is missing.
The token refresh and doctor's login question start `claude` in the configured account through one shared rule, so both always ask the same account.
The user skills, the planning-repo template and the docs describe how to point an installation at its own Claude Code account.

units.title: Runtime tags and collection-time tag rule
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] tests/test_runtime_tag_rule.py:163 — Task 1.3 asks that a parametrised live-stack test whose parameters each carry a different runtime tag 'collects as separate items each with its one tag'. The test only checks that two item ids appear (`test_drives_one[claude]`, `test_drives_one[acp]`). It never checks which tag each item carries.
  Consequence: If parameter marks were dropped, or applied to both items (for example a plugin or helper that copies marks to the function), both ids would still collect with ret 0 and this test would pass. Selecting by runtime (`-m runtime_acp`) would then pick the wrong items or none, and nothing here would catch it. That is a missing_test the task asked for.
  Done when: Let `collect` in tests/runtime_tag_collection.py take the `-m` expression as an optional argument, defaulting to "". The parametrised test should then collect the same file under `-m runtime_acp` and assert that only `test_drives_one[acp]` is listed, and under `-m runtime_claude_code` that only `test_drives_one[claude]` is listed. Checking each item's `runtime_tags` some other way would also do.
- [1.2] tests/test_runtime_tags_registered.py:12 — `PREFIX = "runtime_"` duplicates `tests/runtime_tags.py:13` `PREFIX`, which this same change adds.
  Consequence: The two copies have to change together. If the plugin's prefix were changed, the drift test would still compare registered markers under its own copy and pass, while the plugin silently checks a different prefix.
  Done when: Import `PREFIX` from `tests.runtime_tags` in tests/test_runtime_tags_registered.py and delete the local constant.

Optional:
- [1.3] docs/agent-runtimes.md:834 — The list's intro says 'Two markers keep slow tests out of the default suite, and a third keeps a test out of the parallel pass'. The list now also holds the `runtime_<name>` and `dev_stack` markers (and already held `replay`), so the count no longer describes what follows.
  Consequence: The sentence is false for the list it introduces.
  Done when: Reword the intro so the count is not tied to the list, for example 'The markers the suite uses:', or note that the runtime tags and `dev_stack` select within the live-stack tests rather than excluding from the default suite.

description.summary: Live-stack tests can now name the agent runtime they drive with a registered runtime tag, and collection rejects a live-stack test that carries two different runtime tags or an unregistered marker.
changes: Registers `runtime_claude_code`, `runtime_acp` and `dev_stack` as pytest markers. Turns on `--strict-markers`, so a mistyped or unregistered marker fails collection instead of quietly selecting nothing.

Adds a collection-time plugin (`tests/runtime_tags.py`, loaded from `tests/conftest.py`). It reads each item's markers from the test, its class, its module and its parameters, and fails collection for any `local_stack` item with more than one distinct `runtime_*` tag, naming every such item and its tags.
A parametrised live-stack test can give each parameter a different runtime tag. Each parameter becomes its own item, and selecting by a runtime marker picks only the matching item.
A drift test checks that the registered `runtime_*` markers match the runtimes the package knows about.
Documents the runtime markers, the one-tag rule and strict markers in the docs' test-marker section, and adds a changelog entry under Unreleased.

units.title: One builder makes the tier 2 selection and every tier 2 command takes it
units.feedback:
Task groups 2.1 to 2.5 are covered. The builder, the base re-run keeping the expression, the optional listing hook and `selection_unavailable` all match the tier2-runtime-tags requirement and the design's 'One expression, a listing hook for the rest'. The new and profile tests pass (138 passed). Two things block approval: the listing hook gives the wrong answer for any repo whose pytest addopts already carry `-q`, and the serial-split check is a second copy of an existing helper.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/profiles/python_uv.py:476 — `selected_tests` asks for the listing with `-q`, which stacks on a `-q` already in the repo's pytest addopts. pytest then prints per-file counts instead of test identifiers, and the hook returns an empty list ("nothing selected") when it should return the selected tests.
  Consequence: I checked this against real pytest. With `addopts = "-q"` in the repo's pyproject, `pytest --collect-only -q` prints `test_x.py: 2` (verbosity -2) and no `path::test` lines. `selected_tests` filters on `"::"`, so it returns `[]` with exit status 0. Per the design, parking (group 7) would read that as 'the blocked runtime holds no test' and pass a run that skipped the blocked runtime's tests. Attribution would find no group for a failure. This is the 'pass that checked nothing' the design says must never happen. The fake `Runner` in tests/profiles/test_python_uv_tier2_selection.py prints whatever the test hands it, so the tests pass whatever verbosity the argv asks for.
  Done when: Ask for an absolute verbosity rather than a relative one: replace the trailing `-q` with `--verbosity=-1`, which overrides an addopts `-q` (checked: it prints node ids under `addopts = "-q"`). Also drop any `-q` or `-v` left in `words`. Add a test that builds a fixture repo in tmp_path with `[tool.pytest.ini_options] addopts = "-q"` and a test file with two tests (one marked `runtime_acp`, markers registered). Have it call `PROFILE.selected_tests` with `run=subprocess.run` against real pytest, using a root-level command such as `[sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", ...]` or one `_pytest_program` recognises, and assert it returns exactly the `runtime_acp` test's identifier. Optionally, as a second guard, return None when the exit status is 0 but no identifier was parsed while the output reports tests collected.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/profiles/python_uv.py:449 — The check for tier 1's serial/parallel split in `serial_rerun_command` (`expression in ("serial", "not serial") or expression.endswith((" and serial", " and not serial"))`) is a second copy of `_is_serial_pass` at python_uv.py:158-162. That function already tests the same `-m serial` / `... and serial` shape that `test_commands` (python_uv.py:378-379) builds.
  Consequence: Two copies of the rule 'this `-m` is tier 1's serial split' now have to change together. If the split's wording in `test_commands` or `_marker_selection` changes and only one copy is updated, tier 1's serial re-run either keeps a `not serial` expression and re-runs nothing it should, or `tolerates_exit` stops tolerating an empty serial pass.
  Done when: Pull one helper out of `_is_serial_pass`, for example `_is_serial_split(expression) -> bool`, covering both the `serial` and `not serial` halves. Have `_is_serial_pass` (serial half only) and `serial_rerun_command` (both halves) call it, so there is one copy of the split's wording.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/tier2.py:64 — `tier2_selection` accepts an `only` runtime that is also in `blocked`. It returns `"<marker> and not runtime_X and runtime_X"`, which selects nothing.
  Consequence: Suppose a resume or a scheduled variant for runtime X is built while X is blocked. Its run selects no test. pytest exits 5 (no tests), which tier 2 may treat as a clean no-test outcome, rather than the caller being told the request contradicts itself.
  Done when: Refuse `only` when it is in `blocked`, raising a ValueError that names it the same way an unknown name is refused, and add a case to tests/pipeline/test_tier2_selection.py. Or document that `only` overrides `blocked` and drop it from `left_out`.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/profiles/base.py:175 — The `ListsSelectedTests` docstring does not say that `expression` replaces the command's own `-m`, which is what the python profile does (the test asserts `-m runtime_acp` alone).
  Consequence: A group 7 caller that passes a bare tag (`runtime_acp`), as the design's parking description suggests, lists tagged tests outside the repo's tier 2 marker as well. Nothing in the protocol warns them to combine the tag with the marker.
  Done when: State in the protocol docstring that `expression` replaces the command's marker expression and is not ANDed with it, so a caller wanting the marker's tests of one runtime passes `<marker> and runtime_<name>`.

description.summary: Adds one builder for the tier 2 test selection, so every tier 2 command takes the same marker expression, plus an optional profile hook that lists which tests an expression selects.
changes: `tier2_selection` in pipeline/tier2.py builds the tier 2 marker expression from the base marker, the blocked runtimes and an optional single runtime (or `base`). It refuses unknown runtimes, blocking `base`, and asking for a runtime alone while also blocking it, and names the runtime in each case.
`selection_unavailable` reports when a profile cannot list what a selection holds, so callers do not treat 'unknown' as 'nothing selected'.

A new optional profile protocol, `ListsSelectedTests`, lists the test ids a command would run under a given expression. The expression replaces the command's own marker expression rather than being ANDed with it. It returns an empty list when nothing is selected and None when the listing fails.

The python-uv profile implements the listing with pytest's `--collect-only --verbosity=-1`, so it still prints test ids in repos whose addopts carry `-q`. It drops summary, duration and relative-verbosity flags and prefixes ids with the `--directory` path.
The serial re-run of a failed tier 2 command keeps its marker expression. Only tier 1's serial/parallel split is dropped, and one helper (`_is_serial_split`) now holds the split's wording.

units.title: Runtime lists in the configuration and the blocked set from configuration plus state file
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/tier2_blocks.py:257 — A file entry whose `until` has no time zone makes `blocked_runtimes` raise TypeError. It should count as an unreadable file.
  Consequence: `_Entry.since` and `_Entry.until` are plain `datetime`, so pydantic accepts an ISO string with no offset, such as `"until": "2031-01-01T00:00:00"`. Line 257 then compares it with the aware `now` and raises `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`. I reproduced this against this branch with a hand-written `tier2-blocked.json`. `write_block` has the same gap: it accepts a naive `until` or `now` from any caller and writes it. The spec says a file that cannot be read SHALL block nothing and SHALL be reported as unreadable. Instead, every caller crashes: the tier 2 runs, status and doctor in later units, and the scheduled tick.
  Done when: Make `_Entry.since` and `_Entry.until` `pydantic.AwareDatetime` (`AwareDatetime | None` for `until`). A naive value then fails validation in `_read`, which returns None, so the file reads as `unreadable=True` and blocks nothing. `write_block` then refuses a naive `until` or `now` with a ValidationError before it takes the lock. Add a test to `tests/pipeline/test_tier2_blocks.py`: write a `tier2-blocked.json` holding one entry with an `until` that has no offset, call `blocked_runtimes`, and assert `blocked == {}` and `unreadable` is true, with no exception.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/config.py:105 — A runtime configured under the key `base` makes `base` a known name, so the three lists accept it.
  Consequence: With `runtimes: {base: {}}` and `tests.tier2_runtimes: [base]` the file loads, although the spec says the name `base` SHALL be refused. `tier2_variants` would then return `("base", "base")`, and `tier2_selection` refuses `base` as a blocked name at run time instead of when the file loads.
  Done when: Refuse `base` explicitly in `_tier2_runtime_lists`, using `tier2.BASE_GROUP` or a shared constant, whatever `runtimes` configures. Alternatively, refuse `base` as a key under `runtimes`. Add a test for whichever you choose.

description.summary: Adds installation-wide and per-repo lists of tier 2 runtimes to abk.yaml, and works out which runtimes are blocked from the configuration plus a state file.
changes: abk.yaml accepts `tests.runtimes_blocked`, `tests.runtimes_allowed` and `tests.tier2_runtimes` at the top level, and `tests.tier2_runtimes` per repo. A name that is not a known runtime is refused when the file loads. So are the reserved group name `base`, a name listed twice, and a runtime that is both blocked and allowed. The error names the setting and lists the known runtimes.

A new `tier2_blocks` module reads `tier2-blocked.json` in the state directory. A runtime is blocked if the configuration blocks it or the file holds an unexpired entry for it. A runtime the configuration allows is never blocked; it is reported as overridden. The module also reports entries for unknown runtimes, and reports a file it cannot parse as unreadable, in which case the file blocks nothing.

Entries in the state file must carry times with a time zone. A hand-written file with a time that has none reads as unreadable instead of crashing. `write_block` refuses such a time before it takes the lock or writes anything.
`write_block` writes one runtime's entry atomically under a file lock and replaces any earlier entry. It refuses a deadline when the source is `command`.

`tier2_variants` gives the groups a scheduled tier 2 run covers for a repo: `base` first, then the repo's own runtime list, or the top-level list when the repo sets none. The `base` group name is now one shared constant in `config.py`.

units.title: Edit the blocked and allowed lists in abk.yaml as text

description.summary: Adds a text-level editor that adds a runtime name to, or removes one from, the `tests` blocked and allowed lists in abk.yaml, keeping the rest of the file as it is and refusing layouts it cannot edit safely.
changes: `add_runtime` and `remove_runtime` edit one list under `tests` in abk.yaml as text. They keep comments, ordering and formatting, and create the key or the `tests` block when it is missing.

The editor refuses layouts it cannot edit safely: duplicate keys, anchors, aliases or tags on `tests`, flow-style `tests`, multi-line flow lists, values that are not lists, and files that do not parse. Each refusal raises `ConfigTextEditError` with the reason.

Before writing, the edited text is reloaded and checked to give exactly the expected lists. If it does not, the edit is refused and nothing is written: no backup and no temporary file are left behind.
The file is written atomically and keeps its original permission mode.
