units.title: `abk tier2 hold`, `release` and `status` change both places and show what is held
A tier 2 run leaves out blocked runtimes, names parked ones and attributes failures

description.summary: A tier 2 run can now leave blocked agent runtimes' tests out, report which runtimes it parked, and attribute each failed test to its runtime group.
changes: Tier2Session takes a blocked set and an optional single runtime. Every tier 2 command runs under one marker expression that leaves the blocked runtimes out, or runs only the one runtime when a parked group is resumed.

Before running, the session finds by listing (collect-only) which blocked runtimes hold a test the run would have executed, and records them as `parked` on the result. A listing that fails parks the group and logs why. Under own scope with nothing else to run, the session runs no command and takes no stack lock, including for parametrized tests and tests inside a project.
A result with a parked runtime is never shown as a complete pass. The snapshot and the commit-status description name the parked runtimes.

Each failed test carries its runtime group: `base`, a runtime name, or `unknown` when a listing could not say. The group comes from one listing per command and runtime, with project prefixes stripped so failures inside projects are attributed correctly.
A repo whose tier 2 runs through its dev stack script, or whose profile cannot express a selection, runs whole and logs that it cannot leave the blocked runtime out.

units.title: A unit with a parked group waits for the runtime and resumes only that group

description.summary: A unit whose tier 2 run left out a blocked runtime's tests now waits, held planned, until that runtime is usable. It then reruns only the tests left out on the same commit, and no commit status is ever posted for tests that did not run.
changes: When a passing tier 2 run parked a blocked runtime, the tier 2 node holds the unit planned with the new cause `runtime_blocked`. Its note names each runtime and why it is blocked, and the unit store records the parked runtimes, the commit and the snapshot. Nothing is pushed or posted, and there is no feedback, fix round or failure record. A run that failed in other groups still fails as before.

On resume, if the head is still the stored commit, the node reruns only the parked groups, each through `run_tier2(only=...)`. If the head moved, it reruns the whole run. If a group is still blocked the unit parks again and keeps the results of the groups that passed. On a pass it clears the stored parking and posts one status, with a snapshot that includes the first run's result.

`Tier2Session.run` takes an `only` for one call, which the next call does not inherit. A group that is still blocked is parked without running a command or taking the stack lock. The result records which group the run was limited to.
`build_runner` computes the blocked runtimes once per run, passes them to the session, and gives the node `tier2_result` and `tier2_blocks`.
`post_status` refuses a result with parked runtimes. A status for a run limited to one group says '(<group> tests, completing an earlier run)'.
A new `awaits_release` check keeps a unit parked for a runtime, or a gated requeue, out of a tick's round. `abk status` reports such a unit as blocked.

units.title: A parked unit is released when its splits are usable and shown while it waits
Failures and the gate belong to a runtime
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:2411 — No test covers how the groups a run executes are worked out, or that they reach the gate. `Tier2Session.runtimes()`, the `tier2_runtimes=lambda: tier2.runtimes()` wiring in `build_runner` (wiring.py:3501) and the `runtimes=r.tier2_runtimes()` argument in `BuildPath.tier2` (nodes.py:1715) are never exercised. Every gate test in tests/pipeline/test_untouched_failures_runtime.py hands `build_on_tier2_gate` a tuple it built itself (FULL_RUN, WITHOUT_ACP, CLAUDE_ONLY), and the graph tests leave `tier2_runtimes` at its default of None, which means every group.
  Consequence: Task 10.2 asks that the gate not hold a run that left a blocked runtime out for that runtime's fix, and 10.4 asks that the runtimes the run executes reach the gate. The suite would still pass if any of these were broken: `- left_out` dropped from `runtimes()` (a blocked acp would still hold the run), the `_only` branch returning every group, the `tier2_runtimes=` line left out of `build_runner`, or `runtimes=` dropped from the node's call. In each case an open acp fix holds a unit whose run leaves acp out. Nothing in the suite would catch it.
  Done when: Add tests that reach the real path. (a) Test `Tier2Session.runtimes()` on a session built the way the existing tier 2 selection tests build one (tests/pipeline/test_tier2_selection.py or test_tier2_runtime_groups.py). Assert: with `blocked=["acp"]` it returns `base` and every known runtime except acp; with nothing blocked, acp is included; with `only="acp"` it returns `("acp",)`; with `only="base"` it returns `("base",)`. (b) Add a graph test in tests/graph/test_tier2_runtime_gate.py that opens an acp fix with `planning.open_fix(OLD, group="acp")` and ticks a whole-scope unit with the real gate (`build_on_tier2_gate`). Assert that `tier2_runtimes=lambda: ("base", "claude_code")` lets tier 2 run with no `Needs:` line and the unit not gated, and that `tier2_runtimes=lambda: ("base", "acp")` parks the unit waiting for the fix. Removing `runtimes=` from nodes.py should then fail the test.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1769 — Some pre-existing failures are now skipped by `on_preexisting`: those whose runtime is unknown or blocked. When at least one other failure parks the unit, `wait_for_preexisting` still names every `verdict.pre_existing` test in `preexisting_waiting_note`, the skipped ones included.
  Consequence: A verdict holds a base failure and an unknown-group failure. The unit parks with a note saying it waits for a fix of the unknown-group test, but no change was written for that test. In the real path `classify` already sends unknown-group failures to `own`, so this mainly matters through fakes or a runtime blocked between the run and the record.
  Done when: Build the note only from the failures whose `on_preexisting` returned a fix, for example by zipping `verdict.pre_existing` with `fixes`.

description.summary: Tier 2 failures on the base are attributed to the runtime group of the failing test, and the open-fix gate only holds a unit for fixes in groups its run actually executes.
changes: Before tier 2 runs, the gate is told which groups the run executes: the base group plus every known runtime not blocked, or only the single group the run is limited to. An open fix for a runtime the run leaves out no longer holds the unit.
`Tier2Session.runtimes()` works out those groups from the run's selection, and `build_runner` passes them through to the graph node, which hands them to the gate.
A pre-existing failure whose runtime is unknown or blocked gets no fix change and is treated as the unit's own failure, with its output given as feedback.
When a unit waits for fixes of failing base tests, its waiting note names only the tests that actually got a fix change.

units.title: Post-merge verification waits for a held split instead of passing without it
The scheduled run is one change per variant

description.summary: The scheduled tier 2 run now writes one change per configured runtime variant, plus the base variant, for each repo. Each variant is due on its own schedule.
changes: When a repo's tier 2 run is due, `write_due` writes one `scheduled-tier2-<repo>-<date>-<variant>` change for the base group and one for each configured `tier2_runtimes` entry.

Each variant's due date comes from the latest change of that same variant, open or archived. A variant that has never run is due at once, while the others wait for their period. A change name with no variant suffix counts as `base`.
`scheduled_parts` reads both the date and the variant from a change name, and replaces the base-only `scheduled_date` helper.
Each written change's proposal, design and single tasks group name its variant. The task heading reads 'Run the `<variant>` group of the full tier 2 suite on the default branch'.
An integration test checks that every variant's change, including runtime names with underscores, passes `abk check` and `abk tags` against the real OpenSpec CLI.

units.title: abk tier2 hold, release and status change both places and show what is held
units.feedback:
Group 6 has most of what it needs: the commands, the status and doctor lines, and tests for each scenario in the spec. Two things block approval. First, `hold` and `release` only edit the top-level `tests.e2e_splits`, but task 6.1 asks them to cover every declaration of the split, and a split a repo declares under its own `tests.e2e_splits` is refused or missed. Second, `release` changes the state file before it changes the configuration, so a failed configuration write leaves the two out of step and then reports that nothing was written. I could not run anything here because my shell commands were refused, so the findings come from reading `set_hold`, `tier2_splits`, `declared_splits` and the wiring callers.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/tier2_cmd.py:172 — `hold` and `release` only edit `tests.e2e_splits` at the top level (`set_hold(path, None, ...)` in `_editable`, `cmd_tier2_hold` and `cmd_tier2_release`). They never edit a declaration under `repos.<name>.tests.e2e_splits`, but task 6.1 says to set `hold: true` "on every declaration of the split" and to remove any `hold: false` found.
  Consequence: Case 1: a split declared only in a repo's own splits (`repos.app.tests.e2e_splits.acp`). `_known_split` accepts it, because `declared_splits` includes repo-own splits. Then `_editable` raises "`acp` is not a split declared at tests.e2e_splits", so `abk tier2 hold acp` fails, and the by-hand line points at `tests.e2e_splits`, which is the wrong place. Case 2: the split is declared at both levels and a repo's own entry carries `hold: false`. `hold` only touches the top level, so that repo's units still run the split (wiring.py:3453 judges holds per repo through `tier2_splits(repo, ...)`, and `held_splits` treats the file entry as overridden there). Case 3: `release` leaves a repo-own `hold: true` in place. Also, `prior` in `cmd_tier2_hold` is read from the first declaration in `declared_splits`, which need not be the declaration that was edited, so the rollback can write back the wrong value.
  Done when: Work out every place the split is declared: the top level if `config.tests.tier2_splits` declares it (or it is `rest`), and each repo whose own `tests.tier2_splits` is not None and declares it (or it is `rest`). Pass each such repo name as `location` to `set_hold`. Run every edit on the scratch copy in `_editable` first, so that any refusal writes nothing. For rollback, save the file's original text before editing and write that text back, instead of calling `set_hold` again with a single `prior`. The by-hand message names each place to edit. Tests in `tests/cli/test_tier2_cmd.py` with a fixture where `app` declares its own `acp` with `hold: false`: (a) `hold acp` exits 0, `load(config).repos['app'].tests.tier2_splits['acp'].hold is True` and no `hold: false` is left; (b) `release acp` then returns the file to its text from before the hold, apart from the removed `hold: false`, which stays removed; (c) a split declared only under a repo can be held and released.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/tier2_cmd.py:238 — `cmd_tier2_release` calls `remove_hold` on the state file before `set_hold` on the configuration. If the real `set_hold` then fails, the entry is already gone, and `_refuse_edit` still prints "nothing was written".
  Consequence: `_editable` runs on a copy in a temporary directory, so it can pass while the real write still fails. For example, the planning directory cannot be written, so the backup copy or `mkstemp` in `backup_and_replace` raises OSError, which becomes `ConfigTextEditError`. The file entry has then been deleted, `hold: true` is still in `abk.yaml`, and the user is told nothing changed. That breaks the spec's "both are written or neither" (tier2-runtime-blocks). An OSError from `remove_hold` itself is also not caught and would end the command with a traceback.
  Done when: Use the same order as `cmd_tier2_hold`. Edit the configuration first. Then call `remove_hold`, catching ValueError and OSError. On failure, write back the configuration's original text and print that nothing was released. Add a test: `remove_hold` fails (an unreadable `tier2-held.json`, for example `{not json` with `hold: true` set in the config), release exits non-zero, and both the configuration text and the state file are byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/tier2_holds.py:118 — `declared_splits` keeps the first declaration of each name, so `abk tier2 status`, `abk status` and `abk doctor` report the hold of only one declaration. The pipeline judges holds per repo.
  Consequence: Example: repo `app` follows the top level, where `acp` has no hold, and repo `platform` declares its own `acp` with `hold: true`. `platform`'s units leave `acp` out (wiring.py:3453), but all three commands show `acp` as usable, and `abk status` prints no held line. The spec requires one line for each held split. A `hold: false` on a later declaration is likewise never reported as overriding the file.
  Done when: Have `declared_splits` combine the holds of all declarations: held if any declaration has `hold: true`, overridden if any has `hold: false`. Alternatively, report holds per repo where the declarations differ. Add a test with the two-repo fixture above: `tier2 status` shows `acp` as held, and `abk status` prints its line.
- [1.4] CHANGELOG.md:114 — The changelog says `abk status` shows "a file entry the configuration overrides". It does not: `held_status_lines` lists only the held splits.
  Consequence: The sentence "`abk status` and `abk doctor` show the held splits and a file entry the configuration overrides" is false for `abk status`. Only `abk tier2 status` and `abk doctor` report the override.

description.summary: Adds `abk tier2 hold`, `release` and `status`. A hold sets `hold: true` in `abk.yaml` and writes the `tier2-held.json` entry, both or neither. `abk status` and `abk doctor` show what is held.
changes: `abk tier2 hold <split> [--reason]` sets `hold: true` at every place the split is declared: the top-level `tests.e2e_splits` and each repo's own `tests.e2e_splits`. It removes any `hold: false` and then writes the state-file entry. If any edit refuses or the state file cannot be written, the configuration's original text is put back and nothing is held.

`abk tier2 release <split>` removes the `hold` lines at every declaration, then removes the command's file entry (a gate's entry is left alone). If the file entry cannot be removed, for example because the file is unreadable, the configuration is restored and nothing is released.

`abk tier2 status`, `abk status` and `abk doctor` read holds across every repo's declarations through one function, `current_holds`. A hold declared only under one repo now shows as held, and `abk status` prints one line for each held split.

The changelog bullet describes which commands show held splits and which also show a file entry the configuration overrides, and says that a split declared under a repo's own `tests` is held and released there.

units.title: Parked units are released when their splits are usable, and post-merge verification waits for a held split
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:1763 — The release step, the status lines and post-merge verification decide whether a split is held from `current_holds`, which merges every repo's declarations. The unit's own tier 2 run decides per repo, with `held_splits(tier2_splits(repo, config), state_dir, now=...)` in `pipeline/wiring.py` around line 3452. The two can disagree about whether a split is held for a given repo.
  Consequence: A repo's own splits may carry `hold`, and `declared_splits` combines them: true if any repo says true, otherwise false if any says false. Example 1: the file holds `acp`, `app` sets `acp: {hold: false}`, and `platform` sets no hold. A `platform` unit parks on `acp`, because in its own view the split is held. `_releasable_split_units` sees `acp` as released (the combined hold is false and overrides the file), so it resumes the unit every round. The unit's run parks it again each time, which breaks 'released once per hold' and spends a requeue and a tier 2 run every round. Example 2: `platform` sets `acp: {hold: true}` and `app` does not. In `verify_change` (`pipeline/verify.py` line 245), `app`'s verification leaves `acp` out and is skipped every round whenever `app`'s change has an `acp` test. The change is never archived, even though `app`'s own tier 2 runs `acp`. `_split_wait_lines` (line 1775) reports the hold from the same combined view, so status can show a reason that does not apply to the unit's repo.
  Done when: Add one named function in `pipeline/tier2_holds.py`, for example `repo_holds(config, repo, state_dir, *, now=None) -> Holds`, returning `held_splits(tier2_splits(repo, config), state_dir, now=...)`. Use it in `wiring.py` (replacing the inline call), in `_releasable_split_units` and `_split_wait_lines` with `inst.repo(unit.repo)`, and in `verify_change` once per repo instead of filtering the combined `current_holds`. Add tests: in `test_release_split_held.py`, a two-repo installation where the file holds `acp` and only the other repo sets `acp: {hold: false}`; the parked unit of the repo that does not override is not released. In `test_verify_split_holds.py`, a repo whose own split is not held is not skipped when another repo's config holds that split name.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/verify.py:89 — `_base_selection` writes pytest `-m` boolean syntax (`"{marker} and not {exclude}"`) in framework code. It is a copy of `profiles/python_uv.py:743`.
  Consequence: AGENTS.md, under 'Toolchain facts come from the profile' and 'Framework code is language- and tool-independent', says expression syntax belongs to the profile. A profile with a different selector syntax, such as a node-shaped one, would be handed a pytest expression as its base marker. The two copies of the dev-stack exclusion would also have to be changed together.
  Done when: Remove `_base_selection` and let the profile render the whole expression. For example, express the dev-stack exclusion as an extra `none_of` entry on the selection (`build_selection(repo.tests.tier2_marker, splits, held=held)` followed by `model_copy(update={'none_of': (*selection.none_of, exclude)})` when `dev_stack_marker` is set). `profile.expression` already renders `none_of` as `not <tag>`. Use the same selection in `_held_live_tests`. The existing assertions in `test_verify_split_holds.py` (`local_stack and not dev_stack and not runtime_acp`) should pass unchanged.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/verify.py:133 — `_runs_in` duplicates `_run_in` in `cli/tier2_cmd.py:46`. Both run a listing command from a directory under an env so that a profile's `list_tests` can call it with only the command.
  Consequence: Two copies of the listing runner now have to change together. They have already drifted: the `tier2_cmd` copy forwards the caller's kwargs, while this one discards them.
  Done when: Extract one public helper, for example `listing_runner(run, directory, env)` in `pipeline/tier2.py`. Use it from both `verify._held_live_tests` and `tier2_cmd._check_repo`, and delete both private copies.

Optional:
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/verify.py:149 — When a listing fails, or the profile cannot list tests (`list_tests` returns None), the held split counts as holding no test. The verification then runs with that split left out and can pass without it.

- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/units.py:758 — `in_progress` checks the cause with `getattr(unit, "cause", None) == "split_held"`, a string literal standing in for `Cause.SPLIT_HELD`. `unit_store.awaits_release` encodes the same fact with the enum.

description.summary: Units parked because a tier 2 split is held are released once that split is usable for their own repo, and post-merge verification leaves held splits out and waits when a held split has a live test among the change's files.
changes: Each pass, a planned unit parked for held splits is requeued, once per hold, when none of the splits it waits on is still held for its own repo. Holds are read from that repo's split declarations and the held file.
`abk status` shows one line for each parked unit, saying which split it waits for and why (reason, deadline, where the hold is written), or that it has been released and resumes this round.

Post-merge verification builds its live-test selection through the profile, leaving out the held splits and the dev-stack-only tests. Each repo is judged against its own holds, so a split held in one repo does not hold back another.
When a held split has a live test among a change's files, or its listing fails, verification is skipped for the round before anything is pulled or deployed. It runs again once the split is released.
A single shared `listing_runner` runs a profile's test listing from the right directory under the verify environment, for both `abk tier2` checks and verification.

units.feedback:
Point 1.2 is done. The branch assertion now prints the tick's output and the unit's run log, and no longer prints the exit code, which was always 0. The new pause assertion makes a tick the usage guard holds fail at the first tick, with the guard's reason. Points 2 and 3 of the person's request are still met: the ACP hold is untouched, and each parameter keeps exactly one runtime tag. Moving test_acp_session_step.py into the default suite and dropping its test of which module holds the helper is fine. Point 1.1 is still open. The builder says it did not find the cause, and the commit message records none. Reading the code turns up a concrete one that matches the failure exactly: a 1.9-second tick that exits 0 and starts no agent. It is set out in the finding below.

Still open from earlier rounds:
- [1.1] tests/integration/test_graph_unit.py:152 (reported open) — The claimed cause, an `ABK_RUNTIME` inherited from the host's environment, does not match the failure being fixed. So the `"ABK_RUNTIME": runtime` line is not a fix of the cause, and the cause was not found.
  Consequence: In the saved tier 2 log, `assert built.returncode == 0` passed: the child tick exited 0 in 1.9s, and the run then failed at `git log` (exit 128). An inherited `ABK_RUNTIME=acp` with no `runtimes.acp` entry cannot produce that. `config._check_runtime` (src/agent_build_kit/config.py:1579) raises ConfigError because `AcpRuntime.requires = ("command",)` (runtimes/acp.py:1262), so the tick would exit non-zero. The only other value is `claude_code`, which is what the variant wants anyway. So the next tier 2 run of `runtime_claude_code` will fail the same way, and the person's request ('Fix the cause') is not met.
  Done when: Trace, by reading the code, the paths on which `abk tick` under `claude_code` exits 0 with no agent start. Rule out what the ACP variant shares: the same run planned and started its agent, so the OpenSpec CLI, the fake host and the planning setup work. What is left is specific to claude_code. Check the usage guard (`usage_guard.current_usage` / `read_live_usage` / the start decision), which only the claude_code start consults: a refused, unreadable or over-threshold reading holds the start and the tick exits 0. Also check the Claude account the child gets: `runtime_scratch` copies `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/`ABK_CLAUDE_HOME` only when they are in os.environ, and the tier 2 process may have neither. Check `claude` on PATH. Then make the scratch installation give the claude_code child what it needs, or, if the guard's refusal is a legitimate host condition, make the test fail at the first tick with the guard's stated reason. Either way, a tick that starts nothing must fail at that point with the reason in the message, not at `git log`. Keep `ABK_RUNTIME` pinned if you like, but record the cause you found in the commit message.

Required:
- [2.1] tests/runtime_scratch.py:56 — The claude_code scratch gives its child `abk tick` the Claude account only when the account is in this process's os.environ. An account the installation names in its planning repo's `.env`, which is a documented place for it (claude_account.py:1-7, settings.reload with Installation.env_file), never reaches the child. The child then reads the default ~/.claude credentials, the guard's usage reading comes back None, and `may_start_unit` refuses with 'usage is unknown'. The tick pauses and exits 0 with no agent. This is the likely cause of the failure the person asked about, and nothing here fixes or detects it ahead of the tick.
  Consequence: The tier 2 runner starts pytest with `{**os.environ, **verify_env}` (cli/tier2_cmd.py:59-60; pipeline/wiring.py:3491). `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/`ABK_CLAUDE_HOME` is loaded into abk's settings from the planning `.env`, not into os.environ. So `env.update({n: os.environ[n] for n in claude_account.NAMES if n in os.environ})` copies nothing. The child runs with cwd set to the scratch planning repo, which has no `.env`. So `claude_account.is_default()` is true there, `_credentials_path()` is ~/.claude/.credentials.json, `read_oauth_token` returns None, `current_usage()` gives None, and `may_start_unit` refuses (usage_guard.py:962-969). `_may_build` then writes paused.json and returns 'usage' (cli/pipeline.py:1308-1316). With the new assertion the next run fails with that reason instead of at `git log`. But the cause is unchanged, so `runtime_claude_code` still cannot pass on a host whose account is set in `.env`. The person asked for the cause to be fixed, and round 1 asked for the cause found to be recorded.
  Done when: In `runtime_scratch`, for a runtime other than acp, give the child the account the host's own settings resolve, not only what os.environ holds. Take it from `claude_account.environment_entry()` when the test process has loaded the installation's settings. If nothing names an account, fail fast with `pytest.fail` before any tick, the same way the ACP branch fails on a missing `<redacted>`. Fail when none of these holds: the account variable is in os.environ, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is in os.environ, or the default credentials file the child will read exists. The message must say to name `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in `verify.env`. Add a default-suite test in tests/test_runtime_scratch_setup.py: with no account variable, no token and a missing credentials file (point HOME at tmp_path), `runtime_scratch('claude_code', ...)` fails naming `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `verify.env`; with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set, the returned env carries it. Record in the commit message that the cause traced is the account named only in the planning `.env` not reaching the child, so the guard refused on an unknown usage reading. If a live run shows a different cause, record that one.

units.title: The provider table reads usage through an optional extra's library, and a gate command answers for the rest
units.feedback:
The parsing, the month fallback, the gate command runner, the extra and the lock all match the spec. All 51 tests in the five new files pass here, and the lock check passes. Three things block approval. First, the provider table has no row model; task 2.6 and the spec require one. Second, the reader's tests use a hand-made namespace instead of the library's own summary type, which tasks 2.1 and 2.3 and the design require; the real type takes `adjustments` as a dict, and the tests pass a list. Third, one test from task 2.3 is missing. Separately, the changelog adds a second bullet for this change instead of folding the text into the bullet group 1 already wrote. Task 2.7's design corrections live in the planning repo and cannot be checked from this branch.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/providers.py:23 — There is no `Provider` row model. `PROVIDERS` is a tuple of names, and `read_usage` ignores `name`: every name goes to `_read_modal`, and no row carries a hint.
  Consequence: Task 2.6 asks for 'the `Provider` row model (how to read, parser, hint), the `modal` row'. The spec says 'Each row SHALL give how to read usage, how to turn the result into a reading ... and a hint for a person whose reading fails', and design.md says 'Adding a provider is adding a row and a reader'. As built, `read_usage("anything", ...)` silently reads the modal billing. Group 5's doctor needs 'the table's hint' and has none to read. Adding a second provider means editing `read_usage`'s body instead of adding a row.
  Done when: Add `Provider(Frozen)` with the reader (`Callable[[], object]`), the parser (summary, budget, now → `ProviderReading | ProviderUnknown`) and `hint: str`. Make `PROVIDERS` a mapping `{"modal": Provider(read=read_modal_summary, parse=..., hint=<the text in _MODAL_MISSING>)}` and keep `names()` as `sorted(PROVIDERS)`, so config.py:672 keeps working. `read_usage` looks the row up by `name`, uses `read or row.read`, and returns `ProviderUnknown` naming the table's names for a name the table lacks. description.summary: Adds a table of providers whose usage a split's gate can read through an optional extra's library. Each reading comes back as a percent of a budget over a billing window, or as unknown with a reason. A gate command can answer instead when no provider row fits.
changes: `runtimes/providers.py` adds a provider table. Each `Provider` row gives how to read usage, how to parse the result and an install hint, and the table has one `modal` row. `read_usage` returns a `ProviderReading` (amount, whole percent of the budget rounded up, window) or a `ProviderUnknown` with a reason that has been redacted.
The billing window comes from the summary's start and end. A missing, epoch, empty or backwards window falls back to the clock's calendar month in UTC.

A provider name not in the table, a budget of zero or less, a missing library (the reason gives the install hint), a failed call, or a missing or invalid `metered_cost` all give an unknown reading, not an error.

`run_gate_command` runs a configured command without a shell. Exit 0 means usable; any other exit is held, with the first line of output (redacted and capped) as the reason. A timeout or a failure to start gives unknown.
A new optional extra, `modal`, brings the provider's library and the `acp` extra. The development group installs it, the lock holds it, and the existing changelog bullet for this change says so.
A suite-wide fixture fails any tier 1 test that reaches the real provider's library.

units.title: A provider's month is a window the same ramp judges, and its reading is cached per split
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_guard.py:1548 — The cache entry is keyed only by the split's name. It does not record which gate produced it (provider name and budget, or command argv), so an answer taken under one gate configuration is replayed under a different one for up to `usage_cache_minutes`.
  Consequence: Three cases go wrong. (1) A split's gate is switched from `provider` to `command` while a provider reading is cached: `_gate_cached_result` returns the `ProviderReading`, `_gate_answer_result` takes the provider branch, and `assert provider is not None` raises AssertionError. The evaluation that group 4 puts in every tick round would then crash. (2) Switched from `command` to `provider`: the cached `GateCommandResult` answers the provider gate with no figures. (3) The spec scenario 'Usage falls': `budget_usd` is raised from 200 to 400 with a reading cached. The stored `used_pct` of 87 is judged again, so the hold stands for up to 15 minutes, and the reason reads '173.04 of 400 USD, 87% used', which contradicts itself. `test_raising_the_budget_turns_87_percent_into_44_and_lifts_the_hold` passes `refresh=True`, which bypasses the cache, so this goes untested.
  Done when: Store with each entry what it was taken for: the provider name and `budget_usd`, or the command argv. In `_gate_cached_result`, treat an entry whose key differs from the current `gate` as no reading. Alternatively, keep `used_amount` and recompute the percent from the current budget, but a source mismatch must still be no reading. Add tests to tests/pipeline/test_provider_cache.py: (a) a provider reading cached, then `gate_result` with `GateConfig(command=[...])` one minute later runs the command once and returns its result without raising; (b) a reading cached at budget 200 (87%), then `gate(budget=400)` one minute later without `refresh` gives used_pct 44 and state usable when standing; (c) a command result cached, then a provider gate asks the reader.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_guard.py:1450 — Task 3.5 asks for reuse of `relief_at` and task 3.3 says the provider window is judged by the same `threshold_at` and `relief_at`. The standing-hold lift is instead written inline as `used_pct + band.resume_buffer_pct > threshold`, a second statement of the room rule that `relief_at` (line 454) already holds, and no test pins `relief_at` for the provider window.
  Consequence: If the room rule changes in `relief_at`, the Claude Code resume moves and the provider lift does not. A patched `relief_at` changes nothing for a provider, while task 3.3 says it should.
  Done when: Either derive the lift from `relief_at(window, now=now, limits=...)` being at or before `now`, keeping the 84/85 boundary test green, or extract the 'usage plus buffer' room predicate into one function that both `relief_at` and `provider_decision` call. Either way, extend test_provider_window_shared_ramp.py so that patching the shared piece changes both results.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_guard.py:1549 — The gate-usage lock is held across the provider's network call, and the provider reader has no timeout.
  Consequence: If the provider library hangs, every other reader blocks on the `flock` for as long as the hang lasts. That includes the cached `abk status` path, which the spec says asks no provider, and other ticks. A command gate is bounded by `timeout_seconds`; a provider reading is not.
  Done when: Bound the provider call, for example by running the reader under `gate.timeout_seconds`, or read the cache under the lock, release it for the fetch, and take it again to write. Either one keeps a cached reader from waiting on a slow provider.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_guard.py:1442 — `provider_decision` builds `Limits(session=band, weekly=band)` twice, once for `threshold_at` and once for `_threshold_note`. It only works because `Limits.band` sends any name other than 'session' to `weekly`.
  Consequence: The next reader has to work out that 'billing' falls into the weekly slot. If `Limits.band` ever matches 'weekly' explicitly, the provider window silently breaks.
  Done when: Build one `Limits` value in a local variable with a comment saying the provider's single band fills both slots, or give `Limits` a named constructor for a one-band window, and use it for both calls.
- [1.5] tests/pipeline/test_provider_window_shared_ramp.py:58 — `Window(name="billing",  # type: ignore[bad-argument-type]`: since `Window.name` is now `str`, the ignore is stale. Left in place, it reads as though a provider name were still a type error.
  Consequence: It contradicts the very thing the test asserts, that `Window` accepts a provider window name.
  Done when: Remove the ignore comment.

description.summary: A provider's monthly spend becomes a usage window that the same threshold ramp as the Claude Code windows judges, and each split caches its gate's answer for a while.
changes: A provider reading (amount used against `budget_usd` over a billing window) is judged as a `Window` by the shared `threshold_at` ramp. A new hold starts at used >= threshold. A hold already standing lifts only when `relief_at` offers room, the same rule the Claude windows resume on.
No allowance, estimate or staleness rule is applied to a provider reading, and once the window it assumed has ended the reading answers `unknown`.

`gate_result` evaluates a split's gate (a provider or a command) through a per-split cache in `<state_dir>/gate-usage.json`. A good answer is kept for `usage_cache_minutes`, and never past its window's end. An unknown answer is kept for `usage_stale_retry_minutes`. `refresh` bypasses the cache.
Each cached answer records what it was taken for: the provider name and budget, or the command argv. Changing a split's gate, or raising its budget, reads afresh instead of replaying an old answer.
The cache file is read and written under a file lock that is not held during the provider call or command, so a slow provider does not block readers of the cache.
A held provider result's reason names the provider, the amount used and the budget, along with the percent used and the threshold note.

units.title: The gate result is a held-split entry with source gate, written and lifted each round

description.summary: Each tick round now evaluates every e2e split that has a usage gate and records the result as a `gate`-source entry in the held-split set, holding, renewing or lifting it without touching holds from other sources.
changes: A split whose gate reads over its threshold is held with source `gate` until the provider window ends (or one cache time for a gate command). The hold is renewed on later rounds and lifted when a reading shows room.
Holds set by hand or by a configured `hold: true` are never overwritten or removed by the evaluation, including on splits the configuration releases with `hold: false`.
An unreadable gate writes nothing by default. Under `on_unknown: hold` it writes or renews a short retry hold, but never shortens a standing gate hold.
`abk tick --dry-run` reports `would hold` / `would lift` and writes neither the held set nor the gate usage cache (gate_result gained a `persist` flag).
The test fixture `parked_split_support.installation` can gate both declared splits, and the tick CLI tests build on it instead of a second copy.

units.title: Status and doctor show a split's gate usage; documents, skills and changelog describe the gate

description.summary: `abk status` and `abk doctor` report each test split's usage gate (figures, threshold, state and where the figure came from), and their judgement matches the tick's.
changes: `abk doctor` checks each gated split: the provider library is installed (or the gate command exists), a fresh reading can be taken without the cache, and what it says. A gate hold that still stands is shown as information, and an unknown reading is a warning.
The doctor judges a split under a standing gate hold with the same rule as the tick, so a reading inside the resume buffer stays held.
A provider error shown by the doctor is redacted with the installation's own secrets (its `.env`, `verify.env` and redact settings).
`abk status` takes a split's state word from the held set: `held` for a gate hold, or `held (<source>)` for another source.
Without `--refresh`, `abk status` shows the last recorded reading for the gate whatever its age, with its figures and real age. It says 'not read yet' only when no reading exists.

units.title: The configuration declares a repo's tier 2 splits, each a name and a selector, and rest is the tests in none

description.summary: Adds `tests.tier2_splits` to the configuration: each split has a name, a `marker` and an optional `hold`. The tests in no declared split form the implicit split `rest`.

units.title: The selection is built over the declared splits and the profile translates each selector
units.feedback:
Tasks 2.1–2.3 (the tests) are largely in place, and `build_selection` matches what 2.1 asks for. But the code half of group 2 isn't done. Task 2.4 is only partly done and task 2.5 not at all: the old runtime-name builder, `RUNTIME_TAG_PREFIX` and the `selected_tests` hook all remain, and the live tier 2 run still goes through the old path. So nothing the pipeline runs uses the new selection yet, and the changelog describes behaviour the tool doesn't have.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:2421 — Task 2.5 is not done. `Tier2Session` doesn't take the repo's splits, and still builds its expression, its parking listings and its failure attribution from runtime names. `_selection` (2421–2431) calls `tier2_selection(..., configured=active().runtimes)`. `_park` (2457) calls `tier2_selection(self._marker, [], only=name)`. `_groups` (2513) builds `f"{self._marker} and {RUNTIME_TAG_PREFIX}{name}"` over `known_runtime_names`. `run` (2539) and `_selection` call `selection_unavailable` without `splits`.
  Consequence: The group's done-when says "no framework code builds a name from a split", and task 2.5 says Tier2Session builds through the builder and the profile. As it stands, a repo that declares `tier2_splits` with a marker that isn't `runtime_<name>` gets its held split left out under the wrong marker, or not at all. And `build_selection`/`PROFILE.expression` have no production caller, so they're dead code as far as the pipeline goes.
  Done when: `Tier2Session` is given the repo's splits (from the config function group 1 added). `_selection` returns `build_selection(marker, splits, held=self._blocked, only=self._only)`, and each command's `-m` text comes from `profile.expression(marker, selection)`. `_park` lists each held split via `build_selection(..., only=name)` plus `list_tests`. `_groups` lists the failed ids under each declared split's selection (falling back to `rest`/`unknown` as now). `run` and `_selection` pass `splits=` to `selection_unavailable`. The repo's existing Tier2Session tests (e.g. tests/pipeline/test_tier2_runtime_groups.py and the parking/base-run tests) still pass with splits matching the kit's runtimes, with unchanged expected `-m` text.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/tier2.py:106 — Task 2.4 says to replace `tier2_selection` and remove `RUNTIME_TAG_PREFIX` and the runtime registry from the selection. Both are still here (lines 46–47 and 106–130), next to the new `build_selection`.
  Consequence: There are two selection builders with different name sets: runtime names plus `base`, and split names plus `rest`. Any change to selection semantics now has to be made in both, and the old one keeps building `runtime_<name>` tags, which is what the group's done-when forbids.
  Done when: Delete `tier2_selection` and `RUNTIME_TAG_PREFIX` once wiring uses `build_selection` (finding 1), and drop the now-unused imports (`known_runtime_names`, and `BASE_GROUP` if nothing else in the module needs it). `grep -rn 'RUNTIME_TAG_PREFIX\|tier2_selection' src/` finds nothing.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/profiles/python_uv.py:475 — Task 2.4 says to rename the listing hook `selected_tests` to `list_tests`, taking the selection, and add selector kinds and `expression(marker, selection)` to the profile protocol. Instead, `list_tests` was added as a thin wrapper that forwards to `selected_tests`. The `ListsSelectedTests` protocol in profiles/base.py:175 still declares only `selected_tests(command, expression)`, with a docstring telling callers to pass `<marker> and runtime_<name>`. `selection_unavailable` reads `selector_kinds` through `getattr` rather than a protocol.
  Consequence: The profile now has two public listing entry points with the same behaviour, and the protocol, the thing a second profile would implement, doesn't describe `selector_kinds`, `expression` or `list_tests`. A node or other profile author following base.py would implement the old hook, and `selection_unavailable` would still report it unable.
  Done when: Rename `selected_tests` to `list_tests(command, selection, *, run, among)` in the python profile, with no second method. Update the protocol in profiles/base.py to declare `selector_kinds`, `expression(marker, selection)` and `list_tests`, with a docstring free of `runtime_<name>`. `selection_unavailable` and `_lister` in wiring use the protocol. The test doubles that define `selected_tests` follow the rename.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/tier2.py:60 — On a selection from `build_selection`, `Tier2Selection.expression` is always the bare marker, even when splits are left out or one runs alone. The real text exists only through `profile.expression(...)`. The class docstring still describes "the marker expression of one tier 2 run, the runtimes it leaves out and the group it runs alone".
  Consequence: Code that reads `selection.expression`, as `_park` does today at wiring.py:2477 (`self._selection().expression`), would get `local_stack` for a selection that holds `acp` and list or run every tier 2 test, including the held ones.
  Done when: Remove the `expression` field from `Tier2Selection`; the profile renders it. Rewrite the docstring in split terms (marker, any_of, none_of, left_out, only, empty). Every caller gets the text from `profile.expression`.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/profiles/python_uv.py:466 — `expression` renders an empty selection (every split, `rest` included, held) as the bare marker, which selects every tier 2 test. `test_every_split_held_selects_nothing_and_says_so` checks only the `empty` flag, never what a profile makes of it.
  Consequence: If every split is held, `build_selection(..., held=[all, 'rest'])` followed by `PROFILE.expression(...)` gives `local_stack`, so the run executes exactly the tests that were all held. The opposite of what was asked.
  Done when: `expression` (and so `list_tests`) raises a `ValueError` naming the held splits when `selection.empty`, and the caller in Tier2Session reports nothing to run instead of calling it. Add a test in tests/profiles/test_python_uv_tier2_selection.py asserting that `PROFILE.expression('local_stack', selection(held=['acp','claude_code','rest']))` raises.
- [1.6] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/tier2.py:133 — `selection_unavailable` keeps a second, legacy path for `splits=None` ("a caller not yet moved to splits") that checks `ListsSelectedTests`. Once Tier2Session passes splits (finding 1), no caller uses it.
  Consequence: Two rules for when a profile can apply a selection (has the hook, or reports the `marker` kind) disagree for the node profile with no splits declared. Which reason a run logs depends on whether the caller remembered to pass `splits`.
  Done when: Make `splits` a required argument, remove the `splits is None` branch, and have both wiring call sites pass the repo's splits.
- [1.7] CHANGELOG.md:10 — The added sentence says a tier 2 selection is built over a repo's splits and the profile turns each selector into what the test runner takes. Tier 2 runs still build from runtime names (finding 1).
  Consequence: A user who declares splits per this bullet will find held splits aren't left out by the marker they declared.

description.summary: A tier 2 run's selection is now built from the repo's declared splits, and the toolchain profile turns it into what the test runner takes, replacing selections built from runtime names.
changes: A new builder makes the tier 2 selection from a repo's splits, a set of held splits and an optional split to run alone (`rest` included). It returns the marker, the selectors to require or leave out, the splits left out, and an `empty` flag for when every split is held. Unknown names, or a split that is both held and run alone, are refused.

The profile protocol gains `AppliesTier2Selection` (selector kinds, `expression(marker, selection)`, `list_tests(command, selection, ...)`). The python profile renders the same `-m` text as before for the same sets, and raises on an empty selection instead of selecting every tier 2 test.

`Tier2Session` takes the repo's splits from configuration. It builds its run expression, the listings for parked held splits and the attribution of failed tests from those splits' declared markers, never from `runtime_<name>` tags.

`selection_unavailable` requires the repo's splits. A repo that declares none is never reported unable. Otherwise a profile that lacks the `marker` selector kind, or a repo whose dev stack script runs tier 2, is reported with the reason.
The old runtime-based `tier2_selection` and `RUNTIME_TAG_PREFIX` are gone, and the changelog says how tier 2 selections are now built.

units.title: A test is in at most one split, found by listing and reported by abk tier2 check
units.feedback:
Both round-1 points are done. `tier2_work` gives the CLI and `tier2_scope` one list of (where, toolchain, commands). Listings now run per project with `cwd` and the verify env, and the new tests cover two projects, a node project and the no-name path. One regression came in with the rework: the new `_run_in` wrapper throws away the keyword arguments the profile passes to `run`, and against the real `subprocess.run` that breaks every listing.

Required:
- [2.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/tier2_cmd.py:30 — `_run_in` drops the caller's kwargs (`**_`), so `capture_output=True, text=True` from `PythonUv.list_tests` (python_uv.py:504) and `registered_selectors` (python_uv.py:526) never reach `run`. In this command `run` defaults to the bare `subprocess.run`. `Tier2Session._lister` can drop them only because its `self._run` defaults to `wiring._run`, which adds capture and text itself.
  Consequence: Run `abk tier2 check app` for real. pytest's `--markers` and `--collect-only` output goes to the terminal and `result.stdout` is None. For a listing that exits 0 or 5, `result.stdout.splitlines()` raises AttributeError and the command crashes with a traceback instead of printing the splits. The check this unit adds cannot run outside the tests. This was not visible in round 1, because the wrapper is new in this rework (before it, `run` was passed straight through with the profile's kwargs). The CLI tests' `Pytest` fake returns text stdout whatever kwargs it gets, so they pass either way.
  Done when: Make `_run_in` forward the caller's kwargs and add its own on top: `def run_in(argv, **kwargs): return run(argv, **{**kwargs, "cwd": where, **env})`. Then make the `Pytest` fake in tests/cli/test_tier2_check_cmd.py behave like `subprocess.run`: return `stdout=None` unless the call has `capture_output=True` and `text=True`. That way the existing listing and count tests fail when the kwargs are dropped. Add an assertion in `test_every_listing_runs_in_the_checkout_under_the_verify_env` that every recorded call carries `capture_output=True` and `text=True`.

Optional:
- [2.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/tier2_cmd.py:21 — `_run_in` copies the logic of `Tier2Session._lister`'s inner `run` and of the `_test_env` construction (wiring.py:2332, 2464-2465): run from `where` with `{**os.environ, **verify_env}` merged in only when an env exists.
  Consequence: Two copies of how tier 2 runs a listing command must change together. The kwargs bug above shows they can already drift.
  Done when: Optionally extract one public helper in wiring (for example `run_from(where, env, run)`), with the kwargs forwarded correctly, and use it in both places.

description.summary: Tier 2 splits are checked so that a test falls in at most one split, by listing each split's tests with the toolchain, and `abk tier2 check <repo>` reports the result.
changes: `abk tier2 check <repo>` lists each declared split's tier 2 tests, plus the rest split. It prints a count per split and a finding for any test that more than one split selects, and exits non-zero when there are findings.

Each listing runs once per declared project, from that project's directory and under the installation's verify env, the same way a real tier 2 run takes its commands. The CLI and the tier 2 scope share one list of (directory, toolchain, commands) from `wiring.tier2_work`.
When a profile cannot apply a marker selection in a project, the check reports that the split cannot be applied, instead of listing.
A repo with no declared split prints that every tier 2 test is in the rest split and exits 0.
The profile's listing calls keep their `capture_output`/`text` arguments through the CLI's run wrapper, so the check works against the real `subprocess.run`.

units.title: The held set is the configuration's hold and the state file together, the configuration wins, and a gate may write an entry

description.summary: Tier 2 holds now apply to splits, not runtimes: a split is held when the configuration says `hold: true` or the state file `tier2-held.json` holds it, and the configuration wins either way.
changes: The held set combines each split's `hold` setting in `tests.tier2_splits` with the entries in `tier2-held.json`. `hold: false` overrides a file entry and reports it as overridden. A file entry for a split nothing declares is reported as unknown, and a file that cannot be read holds nothing.

Writing a hold is atomic and done under a lock. Only an entry whose source is `gate` may carry a deadline, and an entry whose deadline has passed no longer holds. Removing a hold reports whether there was one, and refuses to touch a file it cannot read.
The `tests.runtimes_blocked` and `tests.runtimes_allowed` settings and the old `tier2-blocked.json` file are no longer read. `pipeline/tier2_blocks.py` is replaced by `pipeline/tier2_holds.py`.

The unit runner and parked units report the splits held now with their reasons. Handling of a preexisting failure looks up the unit's repo through the installation, so an unknown repo gets an error that names the known ones.

units.title: A split's hold is edited in abk.yaml as text
units.feedback:
I ran the edited test file and the two guard tests (93 passed) and probed `set_hold` with a scratch script. I checked the port's decisions on this file's tests against the merged predecessor (the config now reads `e2e_splits`, with `tier2_splits` as its old name, and a repo whose own splits are None follows the top-level ones). Most retirements and adaptations hold: the new tests cover what each retired one did. Three problems block approval. (1) A real behaviour bug: the repo-level `rest` case. (2) The reload-check test can no longer fail. (3) The CRLF retirement rests on a claim that is not true. The changelog sentence is folded into the existing bullet and is accurate.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/config_text_edit.py:112 — Holding `rest` at a repo that has no `tests.e2e_splits` of its own creates one holding only `rest`. That silently drops every top-level split the repo inherited.
  Consequence: Input: `tests:
  e2e_splits:
    acp: {marker: m}
repos:
  app:
    path: /a
`, then `set_hold(path, 'app', 'rest', True)`. Verified: it writes `repos.app.tests.e2e_splits: {rest: {hold: true}}`. `config.tier2_splits` (config.py:360-361) uses a repo's own mapping instead of the top-level one once it is not None. So `app` no longer has an `acp` split, and its `acp` tests fall into `rest`, which is now held. One command meant to hold `rest` for one repo actually holds every e2e test that repo has and removes its named splits. A related symptom: holding `acp` at the same repo is refused with `declared: rest`, which is misleading because `acp` is declared at the top and that repo follows it.
  Done when: When `location` names a repo with no `tests.e2e_splits` (or `tier2_splits`) of its own, `set_hold` refuses for every split, `rest` included, and changes nothing. The reason says the repo follows the top-level `tests.e2e_splits`, so the hold should be set there, or the repo's own splits declared first. Add a test: from the fixture above, `set_hold(path, 'app', 'rest', True)` and `set_hold(path, 'app', 'acp', True)` each raise `ConfigTextEditError` matching that reason, and the file is byte-for-byte unchanged with no backup. `test_hold_on_rest_at_a_repos_own_splits_appends_there` stays as is, since its repo has its own splits.
- [1.2] tests/config/test_config_text_edit.py:1038 — `test_an_edit_is_written_only_when_it_reloads_to_the_expected_hold` accepts either outcome, and all four of its layouts edit successfully, so the reload refusal is never exercised.
  Consequence: Task 5.4 requires a test that 'an edit whose result does not give the expected `hold` is refused and not written'. I ran all four TRICKY layouts through `set_hold` and each one was written. If the `reloaded != expected` check in `_write` were deleted, this test, and the whole file, would still pass. A text edit that corrupts a neighbouring value would then be written to `abk.yaml`.
  Done when: Add at least one layout where the text edit really misfires and assert the refusal. The check must raise `ConfigTextEditError` matching `expected hold`, leave the file byte-for-byte unchanged, and leave only `abk.yaml` in the directory. Verified example: `tests:
  e2e_splits:
    acp:
      marker: |+
        text


repos: {}
` with `set_hold(path, None, 'acp', True)`. A second one is `set_hold(path, None, 'rest', True)` on the same text. Both are refused today with 'the edit did not give the expected hold'. The current try/except test can stay for the layouts that must edit correctly. For those it should assert that the edit succeeds, because they do succeed today, rather than allowing a refusal.
- [1.3] tests/config/test_config_text_edit.py:612 — `test_crlf_new_block_is_crlf` was retired on the grounds that 'the created-mapping tests cover line endings', but none of the created-mapping tests uses CRLF.
  Consequence: The spec requires that every line ending stays as it was, including when `rest` creates a missing `tests` or `e2e_splits` mapping. Only the in-place insert is tested with CRLF (`test_crlf_line_endings_are_kept`). If `_create` or `_insert` wrote `
` instead of `eol`, a CRLF file would end up with mixed endings and no test would fail. The retirement's justification is false.
  Done when: Add a test: `planning:
  path: /p
`, then `set_hold(path, None, 'rest', True)`. The resulting bytes must equal `original + 'tests:
  e2e_splits:
    rest: {hold: true}
'`, which is what the code produces today. Folding this into `test_crlf_line_endings_are_kept` as a parametrized case also works.

Optional:
- [1.4] tests/config/test_config_text_edit.py:462 — Most fixtures still write the old key `tier2_splits`, and the `splits()` helper reads only `tier2_splits`. Only two tests use the current `e2e_splits` key.
  Consequence: The predecessor made `e2e_splits` the current name and `tier2_splits` the old one. Most of this file now exercises the fallback path, and the lookup of the current key is checked only by `test_an_entry_under_the_current_key_is_edited_in_place` and the tests that create the mapping. A regression in the primary lookup would be caught narrowly. This is not wrong, but AGENTS.md asks new names to use the new spelling.
  Done when: Switch `BLOCK`, `REPO_AND_TOP` and the `splits()` helper to `e2e_splits`. Keep one explicit test (the current-key test, renamed) showing that a file written with `tier2_splits` is edited under that key.

description.summary: Adds a text editor for `abk.yaml` that sets, changes or removes a split's `hold` in `tests.e2e_splits` (or a repo's own splits) while keeping every comment, line ending and other line byte-for-byte.
changes: `set_hold(path, location, split, value)` sets a split entry's `hold` to true or false, or removes it, at the top level or under a named repo. It edits block entries and one-line flow entries in place.
Holding `rest` creates any missing `tests`, `e2e_splits` and `rest` mappings. Removing the hold from a `rest` entry that holds nothing else removes the whole entry.

It refuses, writing nothing, in these cases: undeclared splits, unknown repos, a repo that has no splits of its own and follows the top-level ones, duplicate keys, anchors and aliases, multi-line flow entries, flow-style parents, read-only or unparseable files, and any edit whose result does not reload to the expected `hold`.
A file that still uses the old `tier2_splits` key is edited under that key. Line endings (LF or CRLF), a missing final newline and the file mode are all kept.
The first edit copies the original once to a backup beside the file. A request that changes nothing reports that and leaves the file alone.

units.title: A tier 2 run leaves out held splits, names the parked ones and attributes each failure to its split
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] tests/pipeline/test_tier2_split_groups.py:381 — The two run-limited-to-one-split tests now check only `ran.runs[0]`. The old `[command] = ran.runs` asserted that the only command run carried the split's selection; the new form ignores every command after the first.
  Consequence: Task 6.4 asks for a test that a run limited to one split runs only that split's selection. Both `test_a_run_limited_to_one_split_runs_only_that_splits_selection` (line 381) and `test_a_run_limited_to_rest_leaves_every_declared_split_out` (line 421) now make a test fail (`failing=[ACP]` / `failing=[PLAIN]`), so the base re-run adds a second command. That is presumably why the unpacking was relaxed. But with only `runs[0]` checked, a regression would pass both tests if it ran the whole marker on the base re-run, or ran a second head command under a different selection, for a limited run.
  Done when: In both tests, assert that every command run carries the limited selection: `assert [expression_of(c) for c in ran.runs] == [expected([], only="acp")] * len(ran.runs)` (and `only=REST_SPLIT` in the rest test). Also assert that the base re-run happened, for example `len(ran.runs) == 2`, or that one run's cwd is not `repo`. Keep the existing assertions on `f.split`.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:2480 — Task 6.5 renames blocked runtimes to held splits, but the rename leaves the old wording in this group's code and tests: the `_park` docstring ('The blocked runtimes holding a test…'), the `run` docstring at line 2562 ('a group still blocked'), the log line at 2577 ('tier 2 parked {only}: still blocked'), and the test names `test_with_acp_blocked_…`, `test_the_blocked_group_…` and `test_a_blocked_runtime_with_no_own_test_…`.
  Consequence: A reader sees two words for one idea. The log line is something an operator reads, and it says 'blocked' where the configuration and state file now say 'held'.
  Done when: Say 'held split(s)' in those docstrings and in the log line ('still held'), and rename those test functions to say held/split. The resume wording at line 2562/2577 may instead go with group 7, which renames the resume.
- [1.3] tests/pipeline/test_tier2_split_groups.py:448 — `test_a_held_rest_with_no_test_in_none_of_the_splits_parks_nothing` is a double negative that reads as the opposite of what it asserts.
  Consequence: The next reader has to decode the name to learn the case: the unit's own tests all belong to a declared split, so a held `rest` holds nothing the run would execute.
  Done when: Rename it, for example `test_a_held_rest_parks_nothing_when_every_own_test_is_in_a_split`.

description.summary: A tier 2 run now reasons in declared splits rather than runtime groups: it leaves out held splits, parks the ones holding tests it would have run, and attributes each failure to its split.
changes: Every tier 2 command leaves out the held splits by their declared selection. When a held split holds tests the run would have executed (found by listing without running), it is parked and named in the result instead of being counted as a pass.

A run limited to one split, or to `rest`, runs only that selection. The base re-run of a failed test keeps the same selection, and a call limited to a split that is still held is parked again without running or taking the lock.

Each failure is attributed to the split found by listing it under each split's selection. A failure that can't be placed is recorded as unknown and is not classified. Results stored under the older group key are read as their split.
When every split is held, nothing runs and no selection expression is built. A held `rest` parks only the tests that belong to none of the declared splits.
The runtime-group tests become tests/pipeline/test_tier2_split_groups.py, written in splits and `held`, and the shared tier 2 fakes are updated to match.

units.title: A unit whose own tests include a held split waits for the split and resumes only that split

description.summary: This renames the tier 2 park from a blocked runtime to a held split, in the unit store and the graph node. Units stored under the older names still read correctly.
changes: A unit whose own tier 2 tests fall in a held split is now held planned with the cause `split_held`. Its note names the split and the hold's reason, and it waits with "waiting for tier 2 split <name>".

The unit store's parking field is now `parked_splits`, written by `set_parked(unit_id, splits, sha, snapshot)`. A resume runs only the parked splits on the stored commit and clears the parking once they pass.
A stored unit written with the older cause `runtime_blocked` or field `parked_runtimes` reads as `split_held` with the same names in `parked_splits`. The next write keeps only the new field.
`awaits_release` treats a `split_held` unit as waiting for release, so a tick still never starts a parked unit.
The node, status and store tests are renamed to splits, and a new `tests/pipeline/test_unit_store_split_park.py` pins how older records are read and that writes use only the new names.
The unreleased tier 2 splits changelog bullet now names the new cause and field and says the older names are still read.

units.title: A failure and the open-fix gate belong to a split, and a held split never records a failure
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:2430 — Tier2Session.runtimes() is kept beside the new splits() instead of being renamed to it. Nothing in src calls it any more; build_runner now wires tier2_splits=lambda: tier2.splits(). Three tests still pin it: tests/pipeline/test_tier2_split_groups.py:487-513 (test_the_groups_a_run_executes_leave_out_the_blocked_runtimes, ..._are_every_one_when_nothing_is_blocked, test_a_run_limited_to_one_group_executes_only_that_group). They assert the old 'base' + known_runtime_names() shape. The new splits() has no direct test anywhere. tests/graph/test_tier2_split_gate.py hands the node a fake `tier2_splits` lambda, so it never runs Tier2Session.splits(). splits() also repeats the `REST_SPLIT if self._only == BASE_GROUP else self._only` mapping that _selection already has at line 2455.
  Consequence: Task 8.4 asks for the scope decision to give the splits the run executes 'under that name', which is a rename. As written, the only tested 'what does this run execute' method is dead code still reading known_runtime_names(active().runtimes). The method the gate actually gets is untested. A regression in splits() would pass the suite. Examples: it returns held splits, it leaves out `rest`, or it returns 'base' for a resume limited to the untagged group. In production that means the gate holds a run for an open fix of a split it left out, or does not hold a run of `rest` for a `rest` fix (task 8.2). The base→rest mapping now sits in two places that must change together.
  Done when: Delete Tier2Session.runtimes() and drop the now-unused known_runtime_names import from wiring.py if nothing else uses it. Repoint the three tests in test_tier2_split_groups.py at splits() over SPLITS, renamed to say split/held. Assert: with 'acp' held, splits() is the declared splits less 'acp' and still includes 'rest'; with nothing held it is every declared split plus 'rest'; with only='acp' it is ('acp',); with only='rest' it is ('rest',) (and only='base' also gives ('rest',) while the older name is still read). Put the base→rest mapping of `_only` in one place, e.g. a small private property, and use it in both splits() and _selection().

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/untouched_failures.py:202 — The local variable in _proposal is still called `runtime_line` even though it now writes 'It belongs to the `<split>` split's tests.'
  Consequence: The next reader looks for a runtime concept that this code no longer has.
  Done when: Rename it to `split_line`.

description.summary: Tier 2 failures and the open-fix gate are now kept per split, and a held split never records a failure.
changes: Each tier 2 failure is recorded under the split whose tests produced it, and an older result stored under the 'base' group key is read as belonging to the `rest` split.

The open-fix gate decides whether to hold a run by checking the splits that run will execute, which `Tier2Session.splits()` reports. That is the one split a resumed run is limited to (the older name 'base' maps to `rest`), or otherwise every declared split that is not held, `rest` included.
A split that is held is left out of the run, so it never records a failure for the unit.

`Tier2Session.runtimes()` and its derivation from the known runtime names are removed. The split a run is limited to is now worked out in one place and used both for the splits the run reports and for its test selection.
When a failure is proposed as a fix for an untouched test, the proposal names the split that test belongs to.

units.title: The scheduled run is one change per declared split and rest, each due and open on its own
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/tier2_schedule.py:55 — `scheduled_parts` now reads any `-base` suffix as `rest`, but a split may still be declared with the name `base`. `_tier2_splits_declared_well` (config.py:1152) accepts `base` because it matches `[a-z0-9_]+` and is not `rest`. So the schedule can never find that split's own changes.
  Consequence: Take `tests.tier2_splits: {base: {marker: m}}`. On the first tick `write_due` writes `scheduled-tier2-app-<today>-base` for split `base`. That change then reads as `rest`, so `rest` says `exists:` and never gets a change of its own while it stays open. On the next tick of the same day, `_open_changes(..., 'base', ...)` finds nothing (every `-base` name reads as `rest`) and `_archived_dates` finds nothing either, so it calls `_write_change` with the same name again. `root.mkdir(parents=True)` then raises FileExistsError inside the lock, and the tick fails. On each later day it writes another `-base` change. This breaks the spec's rule that the due and open checks are per repo and split, with no second change written for a (repo, split) while one is open.
  Done when: Refuse `base` as a split name when the file loads, in `_tier2_splits_declared_well`, in both the top-level map and a repo's own map. The message names the setting and says `base` is reserved as the older name of `rest`. Add a test (for example in tests/config/test_tier2_runtime_lists_refused.py or the splits config test) asserting that `tests.tier2_splits: {base: {marker: runtime_base}}` and `repos.app.tests.tier2_splits: {base: ...}` each raise a ValidationError naming the setting and `base`.

Optional:
- [1.2] tests/tier2_schedule_fakes.py:66 — `archived` and `open_change` still take a parameter called `variant`, and it defaults to `"base"`. So by default they write the legacy `-base` name, not `-rest`.
  Consequence: Any test calling them without a split is quietly testing the legacy-alias path, not the current name, and the old word `variant` stays in a helper the change rewrote.
  Done when: Rename the parameter to `split` and default it to `REST_SPLIT`. Tests that want the legacy name pass `"base"` explicitly.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/config.py:729 — Task 9.5 says to delete `BASE_GROUP` and the registry-based names (`known_runtime_names`), but both are still defined. They are still used by wiring.py (Tier2Session, failure attribution) and untouched_failures.py, which belong to groups 6–8, not yet built.
  Consequence: This is not wrong today: deleting them now would break code those groups own. But nothing records that the deletion moved, so task 9.5 will be ticked while part of it is undone.
  Done when: Record in the change's follow-ups (or the tasks of groups 6/8) that `BASE_GROUP` and `known_runtime_names` are deleted when the last caller is renamed, and update the comment at config.py:728 so it no longer calls `base` a reserved runtime name.

description.summary: The scheduled tier 2 run now writes one change per declared split and one for `rest`, and each is due and open on its own. The old runtime lists are refused when the config loads, naming `tests.tier2_splits` as their replacement.
changes: Scheduled tier 2 changes are named `scheduled-tier2-<repo>-<date>-<split>`, with `-rest` for the tests in no split. The due and open checks run per (repo, split), so a newly declared split runs at once while the others wait out their period.
An older scheduled change with no suffix, or one ending `-base`, is read as the `rest` split. An installation's in-flight and archived changes still count.
`base` can no longer be a split's name, at the top level or in a repo's own `tests.tier2_splits`. The config is refused at load because `base` is reserved as the older name of `rest`.

`tests.tier2_runtimes`, `tests.runtimes_blocked` and `tests.runtimes_allowed` are refused at load, at the top level or per repo. Each error names the `tests.tier2_splits` setting that replaces it, and `abk config show` no longer prints them.

units.title: The kit's own splits are installation configuration, and a test keeps split and runtime names out of the framework
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] tests/test_tier2_names_not_in_framework.py:155 — The scan leaves out two parts of the mechanism that task 10.1 names. For the profile protocol it scans `ToolchainProfile`, the general profile, which has no tier 2 member. The tier 2 protocols, `AppliesTier2Selection` and `ListsRegisteredSelectors` in profiles/base.py, are not scanned. The failure record, `pipeline/untouched_failures.py`, is not in MODULES either.
  Consequence: Spec tier2-splits says no code of the tier 2 mechanism may name a runtime or a `runtime_` marker, and task 10.1 lists the record and the profile protocol. Today, adding `runtime_acp` or `"claude_code"` to `AppliesTier2Selection.expression` or `ListsRegisteredSelectors.registered_selectors`, or to the per-split record in untouched_failures.py, passes the test. That is exactly the leak the requirement exists to catch.
  Done when: Add `("profiles/base.py", "AppliesTier2Selection")` and `("profiles/base.py", "ListsRegisteredSelectors")` to CLASSES. Keeping `ToolchainProfile` there is fine. Add `"pipeline/untouched_failures.py"` to MODULES, and fix the module-list comment to match. I checked these by running the test's own `words`/`tokens` over them, and they have no hits today, so the test still passes.
- [1.2] tests/test_tier2_names_not_in_framework.py:217 — The only test asserts `hits == []` over the real source. Nothing shows the scanner can find a name, and nothing shows the provider table would be flagged if it were not exempt. The spec's scenarios 'A name in the framework' (fails naming the module and the name) and 'The provider table' (exempt) are not tested.
  Consequence: Suppose `words()` stopped yielding string constants, or `tokens()` split `runtime_acp` into `runtime` and `acp` and the `startswith` check stopped matching. `forbidden()` could also come back empty after a registry change. In each case the test still passes, because an empty hit list is the passing state. The test would pass whatever the source contains.

Add a test that parses a snippet with a string `"acp"`, a name `runtime_claude_code`, an argument named `modal` and a decorator `@runtime_checkable`.
