units.title: The buffer and rounds settings
Buffer and rounds settings, and the verdict's size step
units.feedback:
Groups 1 and 2 are in place and their tests pass: I ran 363 tests across tests/config, tests/cli/test_doctor*.py and tests/pipeline/test_verdict_{size,drivers}.py, all green. The settings, the load-time check against the reading limit, the doctor warnings and the size step's threshold all behave as the spec says. One correctness problem blocks approval: the way a reviewer's driver text is turned into group numbers, explained in the finding below.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/verdict.py:164 — `_driver_groups` only recognises a driver written exactly as `group N` (`_GROUP_DRIVER.fu<redacted>atch`). Any other text is treated as a file name and matched as a plain substring of each group's task text (`driver.strip() in g.text`). Common spellings the reviewer will produce therefore give the wrong groups or none.
  Consequence: The reviewer prompt (wiring.py:697-700) asks for drivers as `["group or file"]` and shows no exact form. I ran these through `compute_verdict` with groups whose text reads like a real tasks.md group. A driver of `3` returned (1, 3): it matched group 1 because group 1's text contains `rounds of 3` / `about 280`. A driver of `group 3: the size step` returned (), and so did `groups 2 and 3`. Real task text always holds digits (`3.1`, `Estimate: about 360`), so a bare-number driver matches almost every group, and a titled driver matches none. The wrong drivers are then stored on the split request. Later groups (7 and 8) build the planner's pins and the plan check from them, so the split either pins unrelated groups at the earned tier or pins nothing, against the spec ('the outcome SHALL be hold-and-split, carrying ... the reviewer's drivers as groups').
  Done when: Read a driver as a group when it starts with an optional `group`/`task group` (any case) and a number, with anything after the number ignored. For example, `re.match(r"(?:task\s+)?(?:groups?\s+)?(\d+)\b", driver, re.I)` turns `3`, `Group 3`, `group 3: the size step` and `group 3 (verdict)` into 3. Only a driver that is not a group reference is treated as a file. Match a file against a group's text as a whole path token, not a substring: the driver must be bounded by start/end, whitespace or backticks, so `charge.py` does not match inside `surcharge.py` and a digit never matches. Add cases to tests/pipeline/test_verdict_drivers.py, using group texts that contain digits like real ones (`- [ ] 1.1 ... Estimate: about 360 changed lines`): `3` → (3,), `group 3: the size step` → (3,), and `charge.py` against a group naming `src/billing/surcharge.py` → ()

Optional:
- [1.2] tests/pipeline/test_verdict_size.py:87 — `test_a_repos_override_is_the_ceiling_used` passes a hand-built `CeilingsConfig` straight to `compute_verdict`. It never merges a repo override through `ceilings_in_effect`, so it shows only that the ceilings argument is used, not that a repo's override is the one in effect.
  Consequence: If a caller passed the workspace ceilings instead of the repo's merged ones, this test would still pass. The wiring is group 3's work, so this is not blocking here.
  Done when: Build the ceilings with `ceilings_in_effect(config.repos['app'], config)` from a `WorkspaceConfig` in which the app repo sets `review.ceilings.full: 1000`, and pass that to `compute_verdict`. Alternatively, cover the merge in group 3's wiring test.
- [1.3] CHANGELOG.md:10 — The bullet says 'The review verdict can now say a unit is over its earned tier's buffered ceiling'. Nothing on this branch passes ceilings to `compute_verdict` yet: `verdict_record.py:64` calls it without them. So no user can see that behaviour.
  Consequence: A reader of the Unreleased notes expects verdicts that flag oversized units. Until group 3 lands, none do.
  Done when: Either reword that sentence to describe groundwork, or leave it for a later unit of this change to fold into the same bullet once the hold is wired.

units.title: Piece ids and superseding a held unit in the store
Piece ids, store supersession and superseded readers
units.feedback:
Groups 5 and 6 are mostly in place and the new tests pass (98 passed together with the leak check). Three things block approval. Superseding leaves a stale `merge_needs`. The web server's run-log reader still breaks on a piece's id, so it lists no logs for a piece. The id parsing and log-prefix code is now spread across several copies. Two smaller points: several readers in task 6.1 have no tests, and some docstrings were not updated.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_store.py:1484 — `supersede` re-points `depends_on`, `needs`, `waited_on` and `superseded_by`, but not `merge_needs`. A dependent whose `Needs:` line waits for the merge keeps the superseded id there.
  Consequence: Take `app/5` with `needs=("app/3",)` and `merge_needs=("app/3",)`. After `store.supersede("app/3", [app/3-s1, app/3-s2])` it has `needs=("app/3-s2",)` and `merge_needs=("app/3",)`. That breaks the field's documented rule that `merge_needs` is a subset of `needs` (units.py:160). `waiting_on` then skips `app/3` because it is superseded (units.py:376-381), so the merge hold on the pieces is lost until the next `link_needs` recomputes the field. Until then `app/5` can start before `app/3-s2` has merged. This misses the spec's requirement that superseding re-point "every other unit's dependency and `Needs:` target that named it".
  Done when: Add `merge_needs` to the fields `_repoint_references` rewrites, or re-point it in `supersede`. In `tests/pipeline/test_unit_store_supersede.py`, give `app/5` `merge_needs=(HELD_ID,)` in `store_of`, and assert in `test_a_dependent_is_re_pointed_to_the_last_piece_in_dependency_and_needs` that `dependent.merge_needs == (LAST,)`.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/serve/server.py:196 — `_run_name` and `_run_files` read the last segment of an id as an integer: `int(number)` and `number.isdigit()`. A piece `app/3-s1` therefore has no run logs in the web view, although its logs are now written as `app-03-s1-...`.
  Consequence: Task 5 says "nothing that reads an id's last segment as an integer breaks". The spec says each unit's run logs are "found by its own id". For unit `app/3-s1`, `_run_files(inst, "app", "3-s1")` returns `[]` because `"3-s1".isdigit()` is false, and it would raise in `int("3-s1")` without that guard. The web view shows no runs for every piece of a split.
  Done when: Build the pattern from the same prefix function run_log uses (see the next finding) instead of `int(number):02d`. Drop the `isdigit` guard, or replace it with a check that `unit_id_parts` accepts the id. Add a test under `tests/serve/` that writes run logs for `app/3` and `app/3-s1` with `RunLog`, then asserts the server's runs for each id list only that unit's files.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/transcript.py:71 — The change adds copies of id parsing instead of having one. `transcript._id_prefix` and `run_log._unit_prefix` (run_log.py:65) each build `<change>-NN<suffix>-`, and serve's `_run_name` is a third, stale copy. `units.unit_id_parts` says it is "the one place an id is taken apart", but `unit_ids._number` (unit_ids.py:33) already takes an id's leading integer with its own regex.
  Consequence: The run-log and transcript file-name formats have to change together, and they are now kept in two (three, counting serve) places. The serve copy has already drifted (previous finding). The docstring claim of being the one parser is false while `unit_ids._number` exists, so the next change to the id form will miss one of them.
  Done when: Expose one public prefix function, e.g. `unit_file_prefix(unit_id: str) -> str` in `run_log.py` (or `units.py`), and use it from `run_log._unit_prefix`, `transcript._prefix`/`_id_prefix` and `serve/server.py:_run_name`. Make `unit_ids._number` call `unit_id_parts(unit_id)[0]` instead of `_LEADING_NUMBER`, so `unit_id_parts` really is the one parser.
- [1.4] tests/pipeline/test_superseded_readers.py:1 — Task 6.1 asks for tests that a superseded unit's groups are not taken, are not required to still be in `tasks.md`, that it occupies no slot, and that the graph shows it closed with its pieces. None of these exist. Only archive, `waiting_on`, upsert and status are tested.
  Consequence: Four rows of the design's reader table go unpinned: `_STARTED`/`_taken_groups`/`_gone_groups`, `in_progress`/`start_room`, and graph/web. If a later edit added CLOSED to `_STARTED`, or counted closed units with a branch as in progress (the superseded unit keeps `branch` and `pr`), the change's groups would stay taken and the split would stall without any test failing.
  Done when: Add to `test_superseded_readers.py`, using `superseded_store`: (a) `in_progress(store.get("app/3"), store.all())` is False, and `start_room` does not count it; (b) the change's taken groups, through the public caller of `_taken_groups` (e.g. `abk replan --dry-run` or `plan_all` as other `tests/cli/test_replan_*` tests do), do not include 3 or 4 on account of `app/3`; (c) a `tasks.md` without groups 3 and 4 does not make `_gone_groups` report them for `app/3`; (d) the web server's unit summary for `app/3` has `state == "closed"` and `replaced_by == ["app/3-s1", "app/3-s2"]`.

Optional:
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_store.py:1262 — `supersede` calls `repointed(stored, unit_id, last)` before the pieces are in `stored`, so `direct_dependencies` reduces each dependent over a graph where `last` does not exist yet.
  Consequence: Take a dependent that names both the superseded unit and something the pieces already reach. It keeps a redundant dependency, because the reduction cannot see through `last`. That gives it an extra parent that `unrelated_open_parents` and `second_open_parents` may count.
  Done when: Add the pieces to `stored` before calling `repointed` and `_repoint_references`.
- [1.6] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:501 — The `retry_closes` docstring still says "each satisfied or retired unit's pull request", and the `on_closed` docstring (events.py) still explains only the satisfied case. Neither mentions a superseded unit.
  Consequence: The docstrings understate who these functions act for.
  Done when: Name the superseded unit in both docstrings.

description.summary: A unit held because it is too big for its review tier can be superseded by smaller pieces. Each piece has its own id. The held unit's pull request is closed, and every reader of the store treats the unit as closed and replaced.
changes: A split's pieces get ids of their own, such as `app/3-s1`. Ordering parses them through one function, `unit_id_parts`, and the shared `unit_file_prefix` names a piece's run logs and transcripts so they never mix with its parent's.

`UnitStore.supersede` closes a unit held for its size with the cause superseded and adds its pieces as planned, all in one write. Every dependency, `needs`, `merge_needs`, `waited_on` and `superseded_by` reference to the held unit is re-pointed to the last piece.
The superseded unit's pull request is closed after a comment that names its pieces and the size overage. A close that fails is retried, and the poller's closed event does not overwrite the cause.

Readers treat a superseded unit as closed. It holds no slot and is not in progress, nothing waits on it, it does not block archiving, and its task groups are free for replanning and are not required to stay in tasks.md.
The web view shows a superseded unit as closed with its replacements, and lists only a unit's own run logs, pieces included.

units.title: The planner takes a split request
Planner split request and split plan checks

description.summary: The planner can now re-plan a unit held as too big for its review tier as a chain of pieces, and refuses any split plan that does not keep the pins, the shape and the retired ids.
changes: The planner prompt can carry a split request. It lists the held unit's groups in order, the earned and planned tiers with their ceilings, the `<id>-s<k>` piece ids, the retired ids, and each run of adjacent driver groups to pin in a unit of its own.

A split plan is refused unless each driver run sits alone at the earned tier and every other piece is at the planned tier, each within its tier's ceiling. A single driver group over the earned ceiling is reported as too large.

A split plan is refused unless the pieces cover the held unit's groups in order as contiguous runs under `<held>-s<k>` ids. The first piece must depend exactly on what the held unit depended on, and each later piece only on the piece before it.
An accepted split keeps its pieces' `-s<k>` ids and edges instead of being renumbered. A split round plans only the held unit's groups and treats every other group of the change as built.
No plan of any change may reuse a superseded unit's id. A split request given without its held unit is refused.

Tick split step, rounds and holds for a person

description.summary: Each tick now splits units that were held for being too big for their review tier, counts the split rounds, and holds a unit for a person when it cannot be split or has no rounds left. Later plans keep the pins of units already split.
changes: After planning, a tick asks the planner to split every unit held for its size, in priority order. A successful split closes the unit as superseded by its pieces. A refused or invalid plan uses one of the lineage's `split_rounds` and is tried again next tick. An outage, or a branch held by a live process, uses no round.
A unit held for its size with a split pending now counts as work for a tick, so it is split even when nothing else is outstanding.

A unit is held for a person, with a note giving the reason, when it has no split rounds left, holds a single group (the note names the group), carries groups of another change, or has a started unit stacked on it. This happens even while the usage guard refuses planning, and no planner call is made.
While the usage guard refuses planning, no split is attempted and no round is used.
Every later plan of a change is given the pins of its superseded units whose pieces have not started, so a replan cannot regroup a pinned driver group or change its tier.

drivers: src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py (tick split step, has_work, holding units for a person)

units.title: A piece reuses commit pairs from the superseded branch
Pieces reuse commit pairs from the superseded branch
Pieces reuse commit pairs, and documents describe hold-and-split
units.feedback:
The predecessor (a-group-with-no-new-tests-gets-an-empty-tests-commit/1) has been squash-merged into main (71e88338), and this branch sits on origin/main. So the unit's diff is origin/main..HEAD (groups 11 to 13). I checked the tests against that base. They are still meaningful. None asserts behaviour the predecessor removed. None duplicates its coverage. The tests the tasks name for groups 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, 12.2 and 13.1 are all there. The test-side `land` helper change (an empty commit gets the `Already-built: yes` trailer) is justified by the new empty-feat reuse test. docs/configuration.md has no conflict markers and its review block reads coherently.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:2707 — Nothing in production writes `refs/spec-driven/superseded/<unit id>`, so `reuse_superseded` always returns at its `rev-parse --verify` and a piece is never given its parent's pairs.
  Consequence: `keep_superseded_branch` (pipeline/workspaces.py:256) has no caller anywhere in src/; only tests/pipeline/test_superseded_branch_ref.py calls it. `_plan_and_supersede` calls `store.supersede` without keeping the branch. Every real piece therefore finds no kept ref (nodes.py:1163) and is built from scratch by the agent. Group 11's done criterion ('a piece whose groups were built per group on the superseded branch has their pairs cherry-picked') is never met outside the fixture, which plants the ref by hand (piece_fakes.py:49). Three texts this unit adds become false: docs/architecture.md ('UnitStore.supersede then writes the pieces ... after keeping the old branch under refs/spec-driven/superseded/<unit id>'), docs/unit-graph.md ('Its branch is kept under refs/spec-driven/superseded/<unit id>') and the CHANGELOG bullet ('cherry-picked from the kept branch of the unit it replaces').
  Done when: The split step keeps the held unit's branch tip under the ref, in the unit's code repo, before `store.supersede` closes it. A split whose branch cannot be kept supersedes nothing. `branch_lock` is not re-entrant: a lock already held by the same live pid raises `BranchBusy`. `_split_one` already holds the lock for `unit.branch` around `_plan_and_supersede`, so calling `keep_superseded_branch` as it is from inside that block would always fail. Either give workspaces.py an unlocked core that the locked function and the split step share, or keep the ref before taking the lock. Add a test in tests/cli: drive `split_held_units` over a real temporary repository holding the held unit's branch, then assert that `refs/spec-driven/superseded/<unit id>` points at that branch's old tip and the unit is closed as superseded. A second assertion, or a second test, should show that a piece prepared afterwards (through `build`, as in the piece tests) has the pair on its branch with no agent call, with no ref planted by hand.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/commit_order.py:236 — `cherry_pick` rewrites the `Unit:` trailer with `git commit --amend`, which runs the worktree's commit-gate hooks. The call uses `check=True` and nothing catches a failure, which breaks the docstring's 'whole or not at all' promise.
  Consequence: A unit's worktree carries the repo's commit gate as git hooks (wiring.build_commit: 'every attempt commits everything with the hooks on'). `git cherry-pick` runs no pre-commit hook, but `git commit --amend -m` runs pre-commit and commit-msg. Take an installation whose gate has a hook that runs whatever is staged (for example a whole-tree type check with `always_run`). That hook can fail on a piece's tree, because a later group's tests picked without the earlier groups' code are exactly what will not type-check. The amend then exits non-zero and `git()` raises `CalledProcessError` out of `BuildPath.prepare`. The run fails instead of the agent building that group. The branch keeps a `test:` commit that still names the parent in its `Unit:` trailer, with no `feat:` commit after it. Even when the hook passes, the gate runs once for every picked commit for nothing.
  Done when: Rewrite only the message of a commit the gate already passed, without running the hooks. One way is `git commit --amend --no-verify --allow-empty -m ...` through `pipeline.shell.git` with `check=False`. Another is to build the commit with `git commit-tree` and move HEAD onto it. Treat any failure of that rewrite like a failed pick: reset to `start` and return False. Add a test in tests/pipeline over a temporary repository with an executable `.git/hooks/pre-commit` that exits 1. `cherry_pick(repo, shas, unit_id=...)` should still return True, the picked commits should carry `Unit: <unit_id>`, and the tree should be clean.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1158 — The superseded ref's name is spelled a second time as an f-string, beside the one in `keep_superseded_branch` (pipeline/workspaces.py:263).
  Consequence: The ref's writer and its reader are now two copies of one string. A change to the ref's layout in workspaces.py would silently leave `reuse_superseded` reading a ref that no longer exists. Every piece would then be rebuilt from scratch and no test would fail, because the fixture spells its own literal (tests/graph/piece_fakes.py:20).
  Done when: Define one named function in pipeline/workspaces.py, for example `superseded_ref(unit_id: str) -> str`, returning `f"refs/spec-driven/superseded/{unit_id}"`. `keep_superseded_branch` and `BuildPath.reuse_superseded` both call it, and piece_fakes.KEPT may use it too.

Optional:
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/commit_order.py:199 — `superseded_pairs` reads `base..kept`, so a parent that was stacked on a predecessor which has since been squash-merged is never reused.
  Consequence: The predecessor's original commits are still reachable from the kept ref but not from the piece's base after a squash merge. They appear as commits that belong to no group, so the branch is rebuilt with the message 'not a pair for each group'. The result is safe but needlessly loses the work, and the message misstates the reason.
  Done when: Optionally read the parent's own commits, for example only those carrying `Unit: <parent id>`, or those beyond the parent's recorded start, instead of everything beyond the piece's base. Otherwise leave it as it is and document it.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/commit_order.py:199 — The `git log --reverse ... {base}..{ref}` read in `superseded_pairs` repeats `branch_subjects` (commit_order.py:147) with hashes added.
  Consequence: There are now two log readers of a branch's commits, one for HEAD and one for any ref, which must change together if the subject reading changes.
  Done when: Optionally give `branch_subjects` a `ref` parameter, or add one shared reader of (sha, subject) pairs that both use.

units.title: The e2e_before_merge setting and the recorded e2e state
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/init/scaffold.py:207 — The `abk init` template adds a second, commented top-level `global_limits:` block after the dumped config. Its instruction is to uncomment it, but the generated file usually already has an uncommented `global_limits:` section (scaffold.py:181 always sets `generated_files` from the detected lock patterns).
  Consequence: I rendered `dump_with_notes` for a workspace with `global_limits.generated_files: ['*.lock']` and uncommented the new two lines. `yaml.safe_load` (the loader `config.load` uses, config.py:1576) then gave `global_limits == {'e2e_before_merge': 'required'}`. The duplicate key silently replaces the earlier one, so `generated_files` is lost and the lock files are no longer treated as generated. No error is raised. The lines also sit inside `REVIEW_BLOCK`, whose comment (line 205) and `dump_with_notes`'s docstring both say it is the `review` section, so both are now false. The new template test (`test_the_init_template_has_the_setting_commented_out_with_its_default`) only covers a workspace with no `global_limits`, so it cannot catch this.
  Done when: The commented `# e2e_before_merge: required` line, with its note, goes inside the dumped `global_limits:` section when there is one, indented as its child. Only when the dump has no `global_limits` key is a commented `# global_limits:` header written with it. Move this text out of `REVIEW_BLOCK` into its own step, or its own constant, so `REVIEW_BLOCK` and its comment again describe only the review section. Add a test in tests/cli/test_config_cmd_e2e_before_merge.py, or beside the scaffold tests, that does three things. (a) It renders `dump_with_notes` for a workspace with `generated_files` set. (b) It asserts there is exactly one `global_limits` key, commented or not. (c) It uncomments the setting's line and asserts the loaded `global_limits` holds both `generated_files` and `e2e_before_merge: required`. Keep the existing assertion for the case with no `global_limits`.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_store.py:313 — The field comment says `e2e_state` is the state of the head last pushed, but the code does not keep it that way. nodes.py:1064 clears it when any run starts, before anything is pushed, and the e2e node records `failed` for a head that is never pushed.
  Consequence: Example: a deferred or passed unit's rework run stops or is held before it pushes (a HostMoved hold, a build stop, a rate limit). The stored state is then None, while the remote head, unchanged, still has its result. A reader of group 4 (verify names units whose state is `deferred`) would trust the comment and miss that unit. The changelog's wording ('reset when a new run begins') matches the code; the comment does not.
  Done when: Reword the comment (and the one at nodes.py:1063) to say what the code does. Something like: the outcome of the unit's latest e2e-test step, cleared when a run begins and written by that run's result; None when no result is known. Alternatively, move the reset to the push so it really belongs to the pushed head.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/events.py:2167 — When a parent merges, the restack in events.py runs only the unit-test checks and then pushes a new head with `record_push`. `e2e_state` is left as it was, so the new head carries the old head's `passed`.
  Consequence: This matches how the restack treats approval today, so it is not wrong for this unit. But it means 'the state belongs to the pushed head' does not hold after a moved base. Group 3 (deferred on a moved base) and group 5 (verdict reads the state) should decide explicitly whether a restacked head keeps its state.
  Done when: Nothing required here. Group 3 should state whether this out-of-graph restack keeps, clears or re-records the state, with a test.

description.summary: Adds the `e2e_before_merge` setting, global with a per-repo override, and records each unit's e2e-test state in the unit store.
changes: `global_limits.e2e_before_merge` (`required` or `deferred`) chooses whether the e2e-test runs before a PR merges or is left to verification after the merge. A repo's tests block can override it.

Each stored unit has an `e2e_state` field holding the outcome of its latest e2e-test step. A build run clears it when it begins, the run's result writes it, and records from before the field existed read as `None`.

The `abk.yaml` written by `abk init` shows the setting commented out at its default, with a note. The line goes inside the generated `global_limits` section when there is one, and under a commented `global_limits:` header otherwise, so uncommenting it never produces a duplicate key.
The commented `review` block in the init template is again only the review section. The e2e note has moved to its own constant and step in `init/scaffold.py`.

units.title: The e2e_before_merge setting and a unit's recorded e2e state
Deferred units skip the e2e node and say so in the pull request

description.summary: A repo can set `e2e_before_merge: deferred` so its e2e-test units skip the live test step before merge. Their pull request and any failed verification say so.
changes: An e2e-test unit in a repo, or under a global setting, with `e2e_before_merge: deferred` skips the e2e node before merge. It also skips it when its base moves or a resumed run finds its head approved, and its e2e state is recorded as `deferred`. Scheduled whole-suite runs still run the node.
The `deferred` state is recorded before the pull request body is built, so the first pull request already says "e2e-test deferred to verify" in its verification section.
No e2e commit status is posted for a deferred unit, because there is no result to report. The required tier still posts one after its e2e run.
When `abk verify` fails, its detail starts by naming the change's units that deferred e2e-test to verify.

The abk-pipeline skill now describes the deferred setting, what the pull request says, and the verify message. The test recorder keeps pull request bodies and can refuse a status post when there is no e2e result, as the real poster does.

units.title: A deferred unit skips the e2e node and says so in its pull request
The verdict reads four e2e states

description.summary: The merge verdict reads the unit's e2e-test result as one of four states (passed, failed, deferred, not run). A unit whose e2e run was deferred to verify reaches `auto` only when the policy allows it.
changes: The verdict reads the stored e2e state of an e2e-test unit. A failed run gives `full` with 'the e2e-test gate failed'. No result in a final verdict gives `full` with 'the e2e-test gate has no result'.

A unit whose repo defers e2e tests to verify records its state as `deferred` when its pull request opens. The verdict holds it at `light` or higher unless the new setting `review.auto_land.allow_deferred_e2e` is true. The setting defaults to false.

A rework or an adapt (a restack port) that writes a new head clears the stored e2e state through one shared helper. A result recorded on an earlier head can no longer count for the head that was pushed.

The configuration docs, the abk-config skill, docs/architecture.md and the changelog describe the new setting and the four e2e states. Graph tests pin the deferred floor, the rework clear and the adapt clear.

It never says what the spec requires: that the hook does nothing against the pipeline's own merge.

units.title: A forge can squash-merge a pull request at a given head, on GitHub

description.summary: Adds a squash-merge-at-a-given-head operation to the forge protocol, with a GitHub implementation, a declared refusal and safe retrying, ready for a later landing step to call.
changes: The forge protocol has `merge_pr(repo, pr, head=...)`, which squash-merges only if the pull request's head is still the approved commit and returns the merge commit. It also has `merge_commit(repo, pr)`, which reads the commit a merged pull request produced, or None.
A host that will not merge (not mergeable, a protection rule or ruleset blocks it, the head moved, or the pull request is closed) raises a new `MergeRefused` carrying the host's message.
Each forge declares `merges`: GitHub declares True. Azure DevOps and the local forge declare False, and their merge methods are placeholders for later units.
GitHub sends `merge_method=squash` with the approved head as `sha`. Answers 405, 409 and 422 are refusals, and any other failure is the ordinary transport failure.

The retrying forge layer treats the merge as a create that lands on `merge_commit`. After a transient failure it asks whether the merge happened: if so it returns that commit without merging again, otherwise it tries again. A refusal is never repeated.
The shared stand-in forge can produce a merge commit, refuse a merge, or fail transiently before or after merging, for the tests and later units.

units.title: The local forge refuses a merge and the merge denial is unchanged

description.summary: The local forge now refuses a merge as a person's job, and tests pin every route that denies an agent a merge to what it was before the pipeline could merge.
changes: The local forge's merge operation raises a merge refusal saying a local pull request is merged by a person, with git, instead of NotImplementedError; the repository, branch and pull request are left untouched.
A test checks that the local forge declares it does not merge and that a refused merge changes nothing in a real git repository.
Tests check that the policy hook and the command policy still deny each GitHub and Azure DevOps merge or completion route, including raw API calls.
Tests pin each forge's denied commands and requests, their combined prefixes and the Claude Code runtime's disallowed tools to their values from before this change.
A source search checks that nothing outside the forges and the landing step calls the merge operation.

units.title: Azure DevOps completes a pull request by squash

description.summary: The Azure DevOps forge can now squash-merge a pull request at an approved head and says that it merges.
changes: `merge_pr` completes the pull request with the squash strategy and sends the approved head as the last merge source commit. It returns the commit of the completed merge.

When the host answers the completion with 400, 405, 409 or 412, or leaves the pull request active or abandoned, `MergeRefused` is raised with the host's failure message or merge status. Other failures stay ordinary transport errors.
`merge_commit` returns a pull request's merge commit once its status is `completed`, and None before that. The retry layer reads it after a transient failure so a merge is never repeated.
The Azure DevOps forge now declares `merges = True`, and its pull request model reads `lastMergeCommit`.
`docs/code-forges.md` documents `merges`, `merge_pr` and `merge_commit` for each forge.

description.summary: The pipeline can now record a merge it made itself under its own cause, `auto_landed`. A second merge report for the same unit is ignored.
changes: `Cause` gains `AUTO_LANDED` (`auto_landed`). `events.on_merged` takes a `cause` argument, `Cause.MERGED` by default, and records it on the merged unit.

A pipeline landing does the same follow-up work as a person's merge: it restacks and retargets children, releases a child held for depth once it is within the cap, and removes the worktree and branch once nothing builds on them.

A merged event for a unit already recorded merged returns True and logs that there is nothing to do. It does not record, restack or clean up again, whichever of the landing and the poller reported first.
The depth-cap test graph `deep_store` now lives once in tests/factories.py. The rebase-cap tests and the new auto_landed tests share it.
The changelog gains an Unreleased bullet for the new cause and the merge-once behaviour. It notes that nothing lands a unit on its own yet.

units.title: An intent record names a landing in progress
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:3383 — The real poller dispatch `_dispatch` never passes `landing_path` to `build_dispatch`, so in production `on_merged` never reads the intent.
  Consequence: Suppose an intent is still on file after a crash between the forge's merge and the record. The poller's merged event then goes through `_dispatch` with `landing_path=None` and is recorded with cause `merged`, as a person's merge. That is the exact case task 7 and the spec's "A crash between merge and record" scenario exist for. It also makes the new CHANGELOG sentence ("a merge the poller reports after a crash is still recorded as the pipeline's own") and the docs/architecture.md row false. `test_the_poller_s_merged_event_reaches_the_intent` passes only because it calls `build_dispatch` itself with the path set, not the wiring the poller actually uses.
  Done when: `_dispatch` passes `landing_path=inst.state_dir / landing_intent.LANDING`, next to `waiting_path`. Preferably also drop the `None` default on `build_dispatch`'s `landing_path`, so a caller cannot silently turn the read off. Add a test through a public surface that drives the installation's dispatch, for example `deliver_hold_event`'s sibling path or whatever public entry builds `_dispatch`. With an intent written to the installation's state dir, it asserts that a merged event records cause `auto_landed`.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/events.py:279 — `on_merged` reads the intent but never removes it once the merge is recorded.
  Consequence: The spec (auto-land: "SHALL remove it once the merge is recorded") and task 7.1 ("removed once the merge is recorded") ask for this. In the crash-recovery path the poller's event is the only record that will ever be made, and nothing else clears the intent, so it stays in landing.json forever. The same happens when the landing records the merge and crashes before clearing: the poller's later event takes the 'already recorded merged' early return and leaves the intent. The docs/architecture.md row says the record is 'removed once the merge is recorded', which is false for both paths. The only removal test calls `clear_intent` directly, not through a merge record.
  Done when: Once `_record_merge` has recorded the unit merged, and also in the `merged.state == MERGED` early-return branch, `on_merged` calls `clear_intent(landing_path, repo=repo, pr=pr)` when `landing_path` is given. Do not clear on the `BranchBusy` deferral, because the event comes again. Add tests in test_landing_intent.py: (a) after a merged event for a PR with an intent, `has_intent` is False and the cause is `auto_landed`; (b) a merged event for a unit already recorded merged also removes its intent.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/landing_intent.py:35 — `record_intent` and `clear_intent` read, modify and write landing.json without holding a file lock.
  Consequence: `atomic_write_text`'s own docstring (file_lock.py:52-58) says writers on two threads of one process share the temporary name and must hold the file lock. With the clear added to `on_merged`, the poller's dispatch (lane worker threads, overlapping ticks) and the landing pass write this file concurrently. One writer's read-modify-write can drop another's freshly recorded intent, and that landing's merge is then recorded as a person's. Two same-process writers can also collide on `landing.json.<pid>.tmp`.
  Done when: Wrap the read-modify-write in `record_intent` and `clear_intent` in `file_lock(path.with_name(f"{path.name}.lock"))`, as `label_sweep._record` does (label_sweep.py:31-36) and as `tier2_holds` does. Keep the `IntentNotWritten` wrapping around any OSError, including the lock's mkdir/open. Update `test_the_file_is_replaced_atomically`'s directory listing so it allows the lock file and still asserts no `.tmp` is left.

Optional:
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/landing_intent.py:23 — An unreadable or corrupt landing.json reads as 'no intents': `has_intent` answers False, and the next `record_intent` overwrites every other intent.
  Consequence: If the file cannot be read (permissions, or a hand edit), a crash-recovered merge is silently recorded as a person's, and the other landings' intents are lost on the next write. Atomic writes make a torn file unlikely, so this is a robustness point rather than a reproducible bug.
  Done when: Treat only a missing file as empty. Make `record_intent` raise `IntentNotWritten` for an unreadable or corrupt file, and have `has_intent` log or raise, rather than answer False, when the file exists but cannot be parsed.
- [1.5] tests/pipeline/test_landing_intent.py:46 — `test_the_intent_names_the_unit_and_pull_request` asserts the unit and repo but not the pull request number, and the stored record carries the number only inside the key.
  Consequence: The test's name claims something it does not check. A record that stopped naming the PR in its body would still pass.
  Done when: Store `pr` in the record value beside `repo` and `unit`, and assert on the parsed JSON (the entry has repo 'app', pr 7, unit 'c/1') rather than on substrings of the text.

description.summary: Before the pipeline asks the forge to merge a pull request, it writes a landing-intent record. A merge reported for that pull request, whether by the landing or by the poller after a crash, is then recorded as the pipeline's own (`auto_landed`), not a person's.
changes: Adds `pipeline/landing_intent.py`: `landing.json` in the state directory holds one record per in-flight landing, keyed by repo and pull request. Each record names the repo, the PR number and the unit.

Writes to the intent file are atomic and taken under a file lock, so concurrent dispatch threads and overlapping ticks do not lose each other's records. A record that cannot be written raises `IntentNotWritten`, so no merge is asked for, and an unreadable file is never written over.

`on_merged` records cause `auto_landed` instead of `merged` when an intent exists for the pull request. It removes the intent once the merge is recorded, and also when the unit was already recorded merged.
The installation's poller dispatch passes the state directory's `landing.json` path, so the poller reads the intent and clears it when it records a merge after a crash.
Tests cover writing and removing intents, removal through a merge record, the installation's dispatch reading the intent, refusing to overwrite an unreadable file, and atomic replacement.

units.title: Landing decision, checks as evidence, and the landing pass
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/landing.py:31 — The landing pass decides each unit from a snapshot taken before the pass started: the `StoredUnit` from the outer `store.all()` and a pull-request listing cached per repo in `pulls`. A merge earlier in the same pass changes both of these, and the pass never re-reads them.
  Consequence: Take a parent unit P and its stacked child C in the same repo. Both are in review, both have a final `auto` verdict of a listed class, and both have passing checks. P comes first in `store.all()`. P lands, and `dispatch("merged")` records it merged, then restacks or retargets C (with a lane these moves can be deferred). The pass then reaches C. `unmerged_parents` is computed from a fresh `store.all()`, so P now counts as landed and the parent condition passes. `head` is the stale `unit.pushed`, which still equals `approved`. `state` is the stale IN_REVIEW, even if dispatch has moved C on since. `pull` is the cached listing from before P merged, so its base is still P's branch. The decision allows C, and `merge_pr` is called on C's pull request while that PR still targets P's branch, or after C's head was force-pushed. In the first case the squash lands in the parent's branch rather than the trunk, and C is recorded `merged`/`auto_landed`. In the second, the host's head guard is the only thing that stops it.
  Done when: Base each unit's facts on the current state. At the start of `_land_unit`, re-read the unit with `store.get(unit.id)` and skip it unless it is still IN_REVIEW. After any landing in a repo (any path that calls `dispatch("merged")`), drop that repo's entry from `pulls` so the next unit's pull request is listed fresh. A simpler alternative: leave any unit alone whose parent landed earlier in the same pass, until the next tick. Add a test to `tests/pipeline/test_landing_execution.py` with a parent and its stacked child, both landable, the parent first. It asserts that one pass merges only the parent (`forge.merge_calls == [(parent_pr, HEAD)]`) and the child is still IN_REVIEW.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/landing.py:53 — The landing pass gets pull requests from `forge.list_prs(repo_id)` directly. The poller gets them through `with_ui_review(...)` (`cli/pipeline.py:5613`), which adds the web UI's review decisions. As a result, a request for changes a person makes in `abk serve` never shows up in `changes_requested`.
  Consequence: A person requests changes on a unit in the web UI. The poller sees it and the unit is reworked. It is approved again with a final `auto` verdict and its checks pass. The UI's latest decision is still `request_changes`, and the poller's wrapped listing reports `review_decision == "changes_requested"`. The landing pass reads the bare host listing, sees `""`, and merges the unit without the person ever approving. On the host itself the same sequence is held, because the host keeps CHANGES_REQUESTED. That is the spec's 'a request for changes' condition, enforced for one review source and not the other.
  Done when: Have the landing pass use the same listing the poller uses. Extract the `with_ui_review(lambda: forge.list_prs(repo_id), review_of=...)` construction in `poll_all` into one function that both callers use, or have `land_units` take a `list_prs(repo)` callable that `run_round` builds from it. Add a test that writes a UI review with a `request_changes` decision for an otherwise landable unit and asserts the pass declines it with `Condition.CHANGES_REQUESTED` and calls no merge.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/landing.py:91 — A declined landing is recorded as a history entry, and that entry replaces `unit.note` for every unit in review, including units the landing step is not concerned with (a `light`/`full` verdict, an unlisted class).
  Consequence: With `auto_land.classes: [docs]`, a `full` unit of class `code` in review gets a `landing_declined` entry. Its review card body (`notify/cards.py:67`) and `abk serve` note change from their earlier note (for example 'hold label removed' or 'depth 2 is within the cap') to 'the verdict is full, not auto'. Task 11.3 says status shows nothing for a unit the landing step is not concerned with, and the full design for that belongs to group 11.
  Done when: Record `landing_declined` only for units whose final verdict is `auto` (the ones a person might expect to land), or leave how declines are recorded to group 11 and log the rest only.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/landing.py:109 — No test covers the path where `merge_pr` raises after the host has merged. `StandInForge(merge_lands_before_failing=True)` already supports it.
  Consequence: If the `merge_commit(...) is None` check were inverted or dropped, the intent would be cleared after a real merge, and the poller would record the landing as a person's merge. No test would fail.
  Done when: Add a test to `test_landing_execution.py` with `merge_failures=[RuntimeError(...)]` and `merge_lands_before_failing=True`. It asserts the intent is still present after the pass and the error is logged.

description.summary: The pipeline now runs a landing pass after each poll and merges, without a person, each unit in review that the landing decision allows. It records the merge the same way as a person's merge, with the cause `auto_landed`.
changes: A landing pass runs after the poll on each tick. For each unit in review it reads the final verdict, the pull request's checks, labels and review state, and the unit's parents, then asks the landing decision whether the unit may land.

A unit allowed to land gets an intent record first. Then the forge squash-merges it at the approved head, and the merge is recorded through the poller's own dispatch with the cause `auto_landed`, which restacks children and clears the intent. A refusal from the host leaves the unit in review with the reason, and an error after the host may already have merged keeps the intent so the poller can record the merge.
Each unit's facts are read fresh during the pass. A unit whose parent landed earlier in the same pass waits for the next tick, and the pull-request listing is re-read after each landing.

The landing pass and the poller read pull requests through one shared listing (`ui_listing`) that includes reviews made in the web UI. A request for changes made in `abk serve` therefore declines landing just as one made on the host does.
A pull request a person already merged is recorded as merged and not merged again. Declines are recorded where `abk status` shows them, but only for units whose final verdict is `auto`.

Return "" when no decline comes after that entry. Add a test to tests/cli/test_status_landing.py: decline the unit by hold label through `landed.land()`, call `store.set_state(UNIT, IN_REVIEW, note="rework")`, write a LIGHT verdict, and assert the status line has no `not landed` and no `held by label`.

Required:
- [2.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/landing.py:142 — `declined_reason` still returns the last `landing_declined` entry in the unit's whole history, so a decline that is no longer current keeps showing after a rework and re-review. `_will_land` in notify/cards.py reads the same out-of-date entry.
  Consequence: Take an `auto` unit declined because `changes are requested on the pull request`. It is reworked (`set_state` writes a new state entry) and re-reviewed as `light` or `full`. The landing step no longer records anything for it, yet `abk status` still prints `— not landed: changes are requested on the pull request`. That breaks 11.3 ('shows nothing for a unit the landing step is not concerned with'). If the unit is re-reviewed as `auto` and is now landable, `_will_land` in cards.py returns False from the old decline, so it raises a review card for a unit that is about to land.
  Done when: Have `declined_reason` consider only `landing_declined` entries recorded after the unit's latest state-change entry, meaning the last history entry with no `event` key (`set_state` writes one on every rework or re-entry to review). Return "" when no decline follows that entry. Add a test to tests/cli/test_status_landing.py: decline the unit by hold label through `landed.land()`, call `store.set_state(UNIT, IN_REVIEW, note="rework")`, write a LIGHT verdict, and assert the status line contains neither `not landed` nor `held by label`.

description.summary: When the pipeline merges a low-risk unit itself, it says so on the pull request, shows the landing or the reason it declined in `abk status`, and makes digest cards report what landed without hiding an auto unit that will not land.
changes: After the pipeline merges a unit itself, it comments on the merged pull request with the unit's class and the review's reason, and adds a label. Each step is best effort, and a failure is logged.

`abk status` shows why the landing step declined an auto-classified unit, for example `held by label` or changes requested. It shows nothing while the unit only waits for checks, and nothing for units the landing step does not handle.
A decline counts only until the unit's next state change, so a reworked or re-reviewed unit no longer shows an out-of-date `not landed` reason (`declined_reason` in pipeline/landing.py).
Digest cards say what landed without a person. An auto unit that the landing step declined still gets a review card instead of being treated as about to land.
The verdict-shadow allowlist now includes notify/cards.py, which reads the latest verdict.

A sampled share of landed units is audited, with a command and a card
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/review_rates.py:57 — The rule for auto-landed units in `class_rates` reads `record["auto_landed"]` and `record["audit"]` from the verdict records, but nothing writes either field. `with_outcome` (pipeline/review_outcome.py:57) adds only `outcome`, `reworks` and `revert_checked`, and audit results go only to audits.json.
  Consequence: In a real installation, a unit landed by the pipeline that no one has audited still counts in its class's samples and clean rate as an ordinary `clean` merge, and the class's agreement rises with it. An `abk review audit <unit> wrong` never reaches the rates. Group 13's done-when ('an auto-landed unit enters the rates only when audited or reverted') and the CHANGELOG sentence 'a unit landed without a person counts in a class's rates only once audited or reverted' are both false. tests/pipeline/test_review_rates_auto_landed.py passes only because it builds records with fields production never produces.
  Done when: Fill both fields from what is actually recorded. (a) In `with_outcome`, derive `auto_landed: bool` from the unit's history: true when an entry has cause `Cause.AUTO_LANDED`. (b) Read the audit result from audits.json when the rates are computed, not by copying it into the verdict record during the outcome sweep: the sweep stops at HORIZON_DAYS and an audit can be recorded after that. One way is to have `recorded_gates`/`class_gates`/`class_rates` take the audit records (`audit_record.read_audits`) and look up `state in ("ok", "wrong")` by unit id. Pass them from `abk review report`, from `cmd_status` and from every other caller of `recorded_gates`. Add a test that starts from real writers: a unit recorded merged with cause `auto_landed`, `with_outcome` applied, and an audit recorded with `audit_record.record_result`. Through `recorded_gates`, it should show no sample before the audit, one clean sample after `ok`, and one not-clean sample after `wrong`.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:812 — `abk status` calls `audit_status_lines`, which calls `read_audits` and then `json.loads`, with no guard. The other new readers have the same problem: the card reconcile and `abk review audit`.
  Consequence: If audits.json exists but cannot be read (truncated, or edited by hand), `abk status` stops with a traceback before it lists any unit. landing_intent.py:_read handles the same situation by treating an unreadable file as unreadable rather than crashing.
  Done when: Give `read_audits` the behaviour of landing_intent's `_read`: return a value that means unreadable, or raise a named error. Have `audit_status_lines` and the card code log one line and carry on. `record_result` should refuse with a message rather than write over the file.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/landing.py:162 — The audit time comes from `datetime.now(UTC)` here and in cli/review_report.py:91, not from the injectable `spans.clock.now()` that the reconcile and the other pipeline code use.
  Consequence: A test cannot pin the time recorded for an audit. The current test only checks that a timezone is present.
  Done when: Use `spans.clock.now()` in both places, and assert the exact time in test_audit_record.py using fake_clock.

description.summary: A sampled share of the units the pipeline lands without a person is recorded as awaiting audit. A person records each result with `abk review audit`, and an auto-landed unit counts in its class's rates only once it is audited or reverted.
changes: When the pipeline lands a unit, a configured share of them is picked and recorded in audits.json as awaiting audit, with its class and the time.

`abk review audit <unit> ok|wrong` records a person's result. It refuses a unit that is not awaiting audit, a second result, and an audit file it cannot read, and in every refusal it leaves the file as it was.
Units awaiting audit appear as cards and in `abk status`. An unreadable audit file is named there instead of crashing the status.

The outcome sweep marks each verdict record with `auto_landed`. The class rates, the auto-land gates and the class history the reviewer sees all read audit results from audits.json, so an unaudited auto-landed unit is no sample, `ok` counts as clean, and `wrong` or a revert counts as not clean.

units.title: A demotion is recorded, holds a class at light, and is not landed
A demotion is recorded, holds a class at light, and is lifted by reinstate
units.feedback:
Groups 15 and 16 are implemented and their tests pass: 173 passed across the reinstate, notify, demotion-record, landing-demoted, verdict-floor, landing-conditions and status-landing tests. One point blocks approval. When demotions.json cannot be read, the demotion is silently ignored, which is the opposite of what the code's own docstring promises.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/demotion_record.py:98 — `demoted_classes` returns `()` when demotions.json cannot be read. That ignores every demotion, so the class lands again, and its docstring claims the opposite ("a broken file never lands a unit by being unread").
  Consequence: Demote `docs`, then corrupt demotions.json (a hand edit or a truncated write). The landing step (`pipeline/landing.py:87`) gets `demoted_classes=()` and lands the `docs` unit. `BuildPath` (`graph/nodes.py:2115`) records the next `docs` verdict at `auto` with no demotion floor. The spec says a demotion 'SHALL only ever raise the review a unit gets' and that only `abk review reinstate` lifts one. Here a broken file lifts it with no sign beyond a status line, and the docstring tells the next reader the code fails closed when it fails open.
  Done when: Make an unreadable file fail closed in both callers. In `landing._land_unit`, if demotions.json raises `UnreadableDemotions`, decline the unit with a reason naming the file (for example 'demotions.json cannot be read'), log it through `say`, and merge nothing. In the verdict's recording caller, an unreadable file holds the unit's class at `light`, with a reason saying the demotion file cannot be read. `compute_verdict` must still read no file: pass that in as a fact, for example by putting the unit's own class into `demoted_classes` or adding a flag. A simple way is a function that raises (or returns a sentinel) and is used by those two callers, keeping `demoted_classes` only where ignoring the file is wanted. Correct the docstring to match. Add tests: (a) in `tests/pipeline/test_landing_demoted.py`, an auto unit of a listed class with demotions.json holding 'not json' is not merged and a log line names the file; (b) a verdict recorded while the file is unreadable has tier `light`.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/notify/reconcile.py:55 — `desired_cards` now receives the demotion file but still takes `demoted_classes` as a separate argument, and reconcile never passes it. `_will_land` therefore never sees a live demotion.
  Consequence: An `auto` unit approved before its class was demoted has its review card hidden until the next landing pass records `landing_declined`. Only that recorded decline makes `_will_land` false. The card rule from group 12 ('an auto unit whose class is demoted has a review card') holds only because of the order of steps within a tick.
  Done when: In `desired_cards`, when `demotions` is given, derive the demoted classes from it with `demotion_record.demoted_classes(demotions)`, failing closed as in the first finding. Remove the separate `demoted_classes` parameter or let it default from the file. Add a test: with a demoted class and a unit with no `landing_declined` event, an auto unit of that class has a review card.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/demotion_record.py:90 — `demotion_status_lines` and `cards._demotion_cards` index `record['triggers'][0]` and `record['since']` with no guard, while `demoted_classes` does check `isinstance(record, dict)`.
  Consequence: A hand-edited record with an empty `triggers` list or a missing key raises IndexError or KeyError in `abk status`, and in card reconciliation on every tick. `read_demotions` only promises that the file is a table, so the readers handle malformed records differently.
  Done when: Read each record through one helper in demotion_record (for example `standing_demotions(path)`, yielding name, first trigger and since for each well-formed standing record). Use it for status, cards and `demoted_classes`, and report a malformed record as one status line instead of raising.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:2112 — `VerdictFacts` is built and then immediately rebuilt with `model_copy(update=...)` to add `unit_class` and `demoted_classes`, which skips pydantic validation of those fields.
  Consequence: A wrongly typed value (for example a list instead of a tuple) would not be caught, and the facts are put together in two places.
  Done when: Compute `verdicts` and `unit_class` before building `VerdictFacts`, and pass `unit_class=` and `demoted_classes=` in the constructor.
- [1.5] docs/cli.md:1 — docs/cli.md describes neither `abk review reinstate` nor `abk review audit`. Only the runbook mentions reinstate.
  Consequence: Someone reading the CLI reference does not learn the only command that lifts a demotion.
  Done when: Add `abk review reinstate <class>` (lifts a standing demotion, refused for a class that is not demoted) beside the other `review` subcommands in docs/cli.md.

description.summary: Review classes can be demoted and reinstated: a demoted class's units are held at `light` and are not landed without a person, and a demotion file that cannot be read fails closed.
changes: A demotion is recorded in `demotions.json` in the state directory. Further triggers are added to a standing demotion, and only `abk review reinstate <class>` lifts it. Reinstating a class that is not demoted is refused.
The verdict holds a unit of a demoted class at `light`. The landing step leaves an auto unit of a demoted class in review and records why.
If `demotions.json` cannot be read, or holds a malformed standing record, no auto unit is landed (the decline names the file), every verdict is held at `light`, and the review card is not hidden.
A standing demotion has a notification card until it is lifted, a lift shows a 24-hour notice with no reminder, and `abk status` lists each demoted class with its trigger, unit and since when.
`docs/cli.md` documents `abk review audit` and `abk review reinstate`, including what happens while the demotion file cannot be read.

units.title: A revert or low agreement demotes the class
A revert, low agreement, a failed verify or a failed audit demotes the class

description.summary: A review class that auto-merge is allowed for is demoted back to person review when a unit in it is reverted, its reviews agree too rarely, or a unit fails live verify or an audit. A lift made by a person is not undone by evidence they already weighed.
changes: A revert of a merged unit in a class, or low agreement over the class's recent samples, records a demotion of the class.
A failed live verify or a failed audit of a unit also demotes its class, and every trigger is recorded through one shared demotion path.
Once a person lifts a demotion, it is not demoted again by the same unit or by agreement samples that merged before the lift.
When a lifted class is demoted again, the demotion record keeps the earlier trigger units in an `earlier` list, so units weighed at any past lift never demote the class again.
A standing demotion still reports the trigger and unit that caused it, and a new trigger on a standing demotion is added to that demotion rather than starting a new one.

units.feedback:
Groups 1 and 2 are mostly there. The split policy digest, the per-line reasons, the tick and has_work behaviour, and the report's counts, total and no-write guarantee are correct, and the 34 targeted tests pass. Three things block approval. (1) The outage record that task 1.2 relies on is built by hand in a shape the real code never writes. (2) The report copies plan_all's decision ladder instead of sharing it. (3) The abk-pipeline status row that task 2.2 names is not updated.

- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:3985 — When a plan meets an outage, plan_all writes the waiting record with the current `sizing_digest()`, not the digest of the plan that still stands.   Consequence: A change planned under `ceilings.full: 750`, then `ceilings.full: 900`, then `abk replan alpha` (or a tick after a tasks.md edit) meets a network or service outage. Task 1.2 ('still prints the lines for a plan that waits for an outage') is false against the real path. tests/cli/test_status_stale_plans.py:54 hides this by passing `sizing=standing`. Lines 68 and 82 pass `sizing={}`, a dict no code path ever writes.

Use the current digest only when there is no earlier record. A plan that later succeeds still records the current digest. Rewrite test_status_prints_the_line_of_a_stale_plan_that_waits_for_an_outage so it drives a real `abk replan alpha` after the ceiling change, with the stand-in planner raising the outage the driver can script (ServiceUnavailable, say). description.summary: Finds plans made under a review policy or size ceilings that have since changed, reports them in `abk status` and the `abk replan` listing, and adds `abk replan --report` to show what a replan would do without doing it.
changes: `abk status` prints one line for each change whose standing plan was made under another policy. The line names the reason (the ceilings changed, the `review:` section changed, or the plan predates the review policy) and points to `abk replan <change>`.

A replan that meets a network or service outage keeps the policy digest of the plan that still stands. A stale change waiting for an outage therefore stays reported as stale, and the `abk replan` listing marks such waiting lines `stale: …`.

`abk replan <change> --report` lists each change's plan state and stored units. It says whether a replan would be refused, would record the change without asking the planner, or would call the planner once, and totals the planner calls. It writes nothing.

plan_all and `--report` decide 'no planner call' through one shared function, `_without_planner` (broken task groups, groups gone from tasks.md, tag problems, or every group taken), so the report cannot drift from what a replan does.
The abk-pipeline skill's `abk status` row documents the stale-plan lines and `--report`.

replan --dry-run with kept units, joins and refusals
units.feedback:
Reviewed against origin/main; the local main is one merge behind, so `git diff main...HEAD` also shows unit 2's commits. Groups 3 and 4 are this unit's. I ran the four new test files plus a probe: all pass. The probe showed that the main scenario (four 150-line units replanned as one 600-line `light` unit) prints a false join line: `feature/1: would take in a join, 150 lines before, 600 after`.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:5898 — Joins are detected as 'any planned unit whose estimate changed'. That catches the change's own re-estimated units, and the check is not scoped to the change, so it fires again for every change in the loop.
  Consequence: In the spec's own scenario (feature/1..4 at 150 lines, planner returns feature/1 with groups 1-4 at 600 lines), the dry run prints `feature/1: would take in a join, 150 lines before, 600 after` beside `feature/1: would be stored`. No join exists. And with two planned changes selected, one real join onto another change's unit is printed twice, because the `elif` branch does not check `unit.change == change` and runs once per change.
  Done when: A join line is printed only for a unit whose `joined` members (or `members()`) gained a member of the change being printed that it did not have in `before`. It is printed once, under the change whose groups were joined, naming the unit joined onto and the estimate before and after. Add an assertion to `test_a_dry_run_lists_the_unit_with_its_tier_and_the_old_units_as_unplanned` that no output line contains `join`. Add a test that runs a dry run over two planned changes, one of which joins onto a third change's unit, and asserts the join line appears exactly once.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:5880 — A refused plan prints only the stored failure reason, not the unit ids the planner returned (spec: 'the output gives the refusal reason and the returned unit ids'; task 4.2/4.3).
  Consequence: Take a reply that returns `feature/a` (claiming merged group 1) and `feature/b` (group 2). The output names `feature/a` only because the PlannerError text happens to name it; `feature/b` is never printed. The test `test_a_reply_claiming_a_built_group_prints_the_reason_and_the_returned_ids` uses a one-unit reply whose id is in the reason itself, so it passes whether or not returned ids are printed.
  Done when: On a refused or failed plan with a parsed reply, the dry run prints the ids of every unit the planner returned, as a line of its own, for example `feature: the planner returned feature/a, feature/b`. The plan_all/planner path has to expose the parsed ids, for instance on PlanResult or in the record. The refused test uses a reply of two or more units where only one breaks the rule, and asserts every returned id appears in the output.
- [1.3] tests/cli/test_replan_dry_run_refused.py:1 — Task 4.2's outage case is not tested. Nothing asserts that a dry run during a planner outage prints that the change waits, uses no attempt and writes nothing.
  Consequence: The `waiting` branch (pipeline.py:5878-5879) and its wording could be removed or changed and no test would fail. `test_a_dry_run_writes_nothing_when_the_planner_fails` in test_replan_dry_run.py uses `raises(service())` but asserts only the byte snapshot and the call count, not the waits line or the attempts.
  Done when: Add a test to test_replan_dry_run_refused.py with `run.runtime.act = raises(service())`. It asserts that the output has the line saying the change waits and no attempt was used, that `run.records['feature']['attempts']` is what it was before, and that `snapshot_tree(run.inst.root)` is unchanged.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:5875 — The dry run uses its own copy of the replan's output instead of the replan's difference printing. The design says 'the preview uses the same printing as the replan's differences, with the review tier, the estimate against the tier's ceiling, and the joins added'.
  Consequence: There are now two printers for one plan outcome, and they must be changed together. They already disagree. A dropped unit prints `would become unplanned (groups 2)` in the dry run but `now unplanned, replaced by feature/1` in the replan. A started unit prints `feature/1: kept, merged; not replanned` against the replan's `kept: feature/1, merged` (pipeline.py:5826; the design specifies `kept: <unit>, <state>`). The waiting line drops the replan's `next try`. Three things the replan reports are never printed by the dry run: `recorded_only` (a change whose every group is taken prints nothing at all), `results[change].kept` with its `abk retire` hint, and `dropped_joins`. So a preview can silently differ from what the replan then reports.
  Done when: Extract one function that, given `before`, `after`, the results and the changes, returns the lines `cmd_replan` prints after planning: the per-change outcome lines (`recorded_only`, waiting, failed/refused, `dropped_joins`, kept), `_replan_differences`, and the kept lines. Extend it with the review tier and `estimate of ceiling` (through `unit_ceiling`) on new and re-estimated units, and with join lines. Both `cmd_replan` and the dry run print through it. The dry run only changes the verb ('would'), or adds a heading saying nothing was stored. Existing replan tests keep passing.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:5850 — Task 3.3 is not done. Asking for and checking a plan is not separated from storing it. The dry run reruns `plan_all` against a scratch copy and throws it away, and nothing lets a plan that has been asked for be shown and then stored without a second call.
  Consequence: Group 3's done line ('planning a change can be computed apart from being applied') and the design ('one planner call serves both a preview and, when it is allowed, the application: a replan never calls the planner twice') are unmet. The copy-and-plan block is inline in a print function and cannot be reused. Group 5 (`--accept-unplanned`, hold back application) has to build the separation from scratch, or call the planner twice.
  Done when: Move the copy, plan and link steps into a named function. It plans the selected changes against copies in a temporary directory and returns the outcome: the results, the units before and after, the records, and the reasons. The dry run prints that outcome and discards it. A second function can apply the same outcome to the real store and plan records, by copying the scratch files back under the store and `planned.lock` locks or by an equivalent store write, with no planner call. Add a test that asks once, applies the outcome and finds the stored units equal to those a plain replan stores, with `run.calls == 1`. The tick's planning pass stays as it is.

Optional:
- [1.6] docs/cli.md:586 — The Previewing bullet describes group 3 only. It does not say the dry run prints the started units it keeps, the joins, the returned unit ids of a refused plan and the waits line for an outage, or that `--dry-run` with `--forget` is refused. The changelog bullet does mention the joins and the `--forget` refusal.
  Consequence: A reader of the CLI reference does not learn about the `--forget` usage error or what an outage prints.
  Done when: Add those to the Previewing bullet, one clause each.
- [1.7] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:5869 — In a dry run, plan_all's own log lines claim effects the dry run does not have: `planning feature failed (1/3) — \`abk replan\` plans it again now` and `next try 17:59`. Neither the attempt nor the wait is recorded.
  Consequence: A person reading a refused dry run sees '(1/3)' and may believe an attempt was spent.
  Done when: Either let plan_all take a flag or logger that words these as a preview, or have the dry run print a closing line saying no attempt or wait was recorded.
- [1.8] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:5852 — Only units.json and planned.json are copied into the scratch directory. `_write_join` decides 'a live process holds this branch' from `state_dir/locks`, and the scratch copy has no locks.
  Consequence: While a build holds a planned unit's branch lock, the dry run prints a join onto that unit that the real replan would drop as started.
  Done when: Point the scratch installation's lock lookups at the real `locks` directory (read-only use), or note this limit in the docstring and the docs.
- [1.9] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:5841 — The `store` parameter of `_print_replan_dry_run` is unused. The function reads `inst.state_dir / 'units.json'` directly instead of `store.path`.
  Consequence: A reader assumes the passed store is the one copied.
  Done when: Copy from `store.path`, or drop the parameter.

description.summary: `abk replan --dry-run` previews a replan through the same printer the replan uses, and planning a change can now be computed apart from storing it.
changes: A replan and its dry run print through one function. The dry run shows the same lines in the conditional: units it would store with their groups, review tier and estimate against that tier's ceiling, units that would become unplanned, kept and started units, and dropped joins.
Joins are reported once, under the change whose groups joined a unit of another change, with that unit's estimate before and after. Re-estimating a change's own units no longer looks like a join.
A refused or failed plan prints its reason and the ids of every unit the planner returned. During a planner outage the dry run says the change would wait and uses no attempt.

`plan_apart` plans changes against copies of the unit store, the plan records and the branch locks in a temporary directory, and `apply_planned` stores that outcome under the store and plan locks without a second planner call.
Replan difference lines now include each new or re-estimated unit's review tier and its estimate against the ceiling, along with changes to its groups and review tier.

units.title: Replan accept-unplanned, keep old plan, and stale --limit migration
replan --accept-unplanned, refused plans and --stale --limit

description.summary: Makes `abk replan` safe to run over open changes when they move to review tiers: it reports what a new plan would drop, keeps the old plan when the new one is refused, and with `--stale --limit N` re-plans the most urgent stale changes first.
changes: A replan lists the stored units the new plan would remove. It keeps the existing plan and units when the new plan is refused or the store changed underneath it, using a new compare-and-replace in the unit store. `--accept-unplanned` allows the drop.

`abk replan --stale` picks the changes whose plan predates the current sizing. It skips changes that have given up or are waiting out an outage, with a reason, and reads plans recorded before the test-kind tag rename by their recorded hash.
`--limit N` caps how many changes one run plans, ordered by urgency and then by name. A limit below 1 is a usage error.

A replan that meets a network or service outage writes the same pause a tick would. The pause is copied without adding the resume grace a second time, through the new `pause.record_pause`. A dry run writes no pause.
Replans keep a group-owned sizing, promote held splits, and handle partly started changes and joins that remove a unit. docs/cli.md, the abk-pipeline skill and the changelog describe the new flags.

units.title: abk tags --fix and tag-spelling-stable digest
abk tags --fix and a tag-spelling-proof tasks.md digest

description.summary: Adds `abk tags --fix`, which rewrites the old test-kind tags in open changes' group headings, and makes the plan digest ignore the tag's spelling so the rewrite never makes a plan stale.
changes: `abk tags --fix [CHANGE | --all] [--dry-run]` replaces each old test-kind tag in a group heading with `[unit-test]` or `[e2e-test]`. Every other byte is kept, including prose, code spans, titles, CRLF line endings and a missing final newline. It prints the count per change, or "unchanged", and writes each file atomically under the tasks.md lock.

A change is refused, with the reason and nothing written, in any of these cases; the other selected changes are still handled and the exit status is 1:
  - it has another tag error or is on a `Needs:` cycle
  - the file is missing, cannot be read, is read-only or is not valid text
  - the rewritten text parses to different groups

The plan digest now hashes the specification with tags in their current spelling. A hash recorded by an earlier release, whether from text with every tag old or with both spellings mixed, still counts as current. After a rewrite, the plan record's hash moves to the new text's digest, so no tick plans the change again.
`abk tags` with `--dry-run` but no `--fix` is a usage error. A tasks.md that is not valid text no longer turns off the `Needs:` cycle check for the other changes.
`compat_names.old_tag` gives the old spelling of a current tag. `old_spelling` now raises `ValueError` for a kind that has no old spelling.
`docs/cli.md` and the changelog describe `abk tags --fix`.
