units.title: Config key rename migration and migration docs
Config migrate renames the old test-kind settings
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/config_migrate.py:275 — `_rename_test_kind_keys` crashes with a bare AssertionError when an old key comes into a block through a merge key or alias higher up the tree. It should refuse with a ConfigMigrateError.
  Consequence: `old_setting_blocks` works on the constructed document, where merges are already applied, but `_block_node` and `_pair` walk the composed node tree, where they are not. Take `repos:\n  app: &app\n    path: app\n    tests:\n      tier2_schedule: weekly\n  platform:\n    <<: *app\n    path: platform\n`. It reports the block `('repos','platform','tests')`, `_pair(platform_node, 'tests')` returns None, and `assert isinstance(block, yaml.MappingNode)` raises AssertionError. I reproduced this with `migrate()` on the branch. `cmd_migrate` catches only ConfigMigrateError, OSError and UnicodeDecodeError, so the user gets a traceback, not the documented 'exit 2 when it refuses' (docs/cli.md). The spec also says it SHALL refuse, naming the file and the key. Under `python -O` the asserts are stripped and it fails later with an AttributeError. The plain alias case (`platform: *app`) does refuse, but for the wrong reason: 'it is quoted or written across lines'. The first pass has already renamed the shared lines, so the second path's column check fails.
  Done when: Replace the three asserts with refusals. When `_block_node(root, path)`, its parent or `_pair(parent, path[-1])` doesn't resolve to a MappingNode written at that path, raise `_refuse(where, "the block comes from a merge key or an alias, which cannot be renamed by lines")`. Also refuse when the same block node or key node is reached by two paths (keep a set of seen node ids), so an alias above the block gets that same reason, not the 'quoted' one. In tests/test_config_migrate_test_kind_keys_refused.py, add a case for a merge key at the repo level and one for a repo that is an alias of another. Each asserts ConfigMigrateError naming the block (`repos.platform.tests`) and matching `merge|alias`.

Optional:
- [1.2] tests/test_config_migrate_test_kind_keys_refused.py:12 — Two refusals in the new rename path have no test: a quoted old key (`"tier2_lock_wait_seconds": 600`) and the parse-back check `written != read_new_settings(old)`. Task 9.2's 'several documents' case is listed only in the older limits refusal test.
  Consequence: The quoted-key and verification branches could be dropped or broken and every test would still pass.
  Done when: Add a quoted-key case to CASES, asserting the key and `quoted`, and a several-documents case with only a tier key, asserting `several documents`.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/config_cmd.py:28 — The `cmd_migrate` docstring still says it moves the file 'to the new limits blocks' and exits 0 when it had 'nothing to move'. It now also renames the test-kind keys.
  Consequence: The next reader of the command misses half of what it does.
  Done when: Say it moves the limits blocks and renames the old test-kind setting keys.
- [1.4] tests/test_config_migrate_test_kind_keys.py:22 — The fixture's `tier2_splits.slow.tier2_schedule: nightly` is a key that `E2eSplitEntry` (marker, hold, gate) does not have, so the file it pins would not load.
  Consequence: A reader may take a split entry to have a schedule setting that the rename deliberately leaves alone.
  Done when: Use a real split field (e.g. `marker: slow`), or add a comment saying the nested key is there to show that nested values are not touched.

description.summary: `abk config migrate` now renames the old numbered test-kind setting keys, in the limits block and in each repo's `tests` block, as well as moving the limits blocks. It edits by text and refuses any file it cannot edit line by line.
changes: Renames each old test-kind setting key (for example `tier2_schedule`, `tier2_lock_wait_seconds`) to its new spelling on its own line. Comments and layout are kept, and nested split fields are left as they are.

Refuses with a ConfigMigrateError, so the command exits 2 and names the block or key, when a block holding an old key: is brought in by a merge key or an alias higher up, is reached by two paths, has an anchor, is written in flow style, or uses a merge key itself.
Refuses an old key that is quoted or written across lines. Also refuses a file with several YAML documents, and an edit whose result would parse to anything other than the renamed settings.
The `cmd_migrate` docstring now says the command renames the old test-kind keys as well as moving the limits blocks, and exits 0 when there is nothing to change.
Adds tests for the rename (with comments and nested splits) and a table of refusal cases, including the merge-key and repo-alias inputs.

units.title: The verdict function over plan floors, recorded results, classification and history

description.summary: Adds a deterministic, model-free verdict that decides how much review a unit needs (auto, light or full) from facts already recorded about it.
changes: `compute_verdict` takes a unit's recorded facts: its planned estimate, protected paths, flags, red-first, unit-test and e2e-test gate results, open required findings, the reviewer's classification and whether the round is final. It returns the highest floor those facts give and the rule that decided it.
The class's history (number of samples and clean-merge rate, measured against the auto-land policy) can only raise the evidence tier, never lower it.

A missing classification, a failed or missing gate, an open required finding, a protected path or a floored flag forces `full`. An e2e-test result still pending is accepted in an interim verdict but counts as missing in a final one.
The review-tier order is defined once, as `REVIEW_TIERS` derived from `ReviewTier`, and the planner, the stack runner and the verdict all use it.
Tests check that each floor alone gives its tier, that no pair of floors lowers either one, that the verdict is repeatable, and that an `auto` verdict says no recorded fact raised it.

units.title: The review reply carries a focus list and a skippable list
Review reply carries focus and skippable lists, and the prompt asks for them
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_store.py:237 — The prompt and the parser spell the boundary reason differently, and the parser matches it exactly, so a reviewer that follows the prompt gets no kind.
  Consequence: REVIEW_BRIEF_PROMPT (wiring.py:705-209) tells the reviewer to write the reason `boundary another system depends on`. `_parse_focus` (stack_runner.py:617) looks the reason up with `kinds.get(reason)` against the enum values, and FocusKind.BOUNDARY is the bare string "boundary". A reply that does exactly what the prompt says, {"place": "src/events.py", "reason": "boundary another system depends on"}, is stored with kind=None. The match is also case-sensitive, so "Behaviour change" gets no kind either. The spec says a reason that names one of the four kinds is kept with that kind. The tests pass only because they send the enum values ("boundary") and never the wording the prompt asks for.
  Done when: Make the enum value and the prompt one text, with a single source. For example, set BOUNDARY = "boundary another system depends on" and have REVIEW_BRIEF_PROMPT build its four reasons from `FocusKind` rather than repeat them. Match after trimming and folding case. Add a test in test_review_brief_parse.py that takes each reason exactly as REVIEW_BRIEF_PROMPT spells it, sends it as a focus reason through parse_verdict, and asserts it comes back with the matching FocusKind.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/stack_runner.py:660 — When the drivers are merged into the focus list, a driver that the reviewer listed as skippable stays in the skippable list. The reviewer's own duplicate focus places are not removed either.
  Consequence: `_parse_skippable` filters against the reviewer's focus places before the drivers are merged in. Example: drivers=["src/a.py"], focus=[], skippable=[{"place": "src/a.py", "reason": "renamed"}]. The stored description has src/a.py at the head of focus and also in skippable. The spec requirement 'A place SHALL NOT appear in both lists; the focus list SHALL win' fails. Separately, a reviewer focus of [{place: a}, {place: a}] with no drivers is stored twice, which breaks 'no place SHALL be listed twice'. `_drivers_lead` returns early when there are no drivers, and `_parse_focus` never removes duplicates.
  Done when: Remove duplicate places in `_parse_focus`, keeping the first. In `_drivers_lead`, also drop from `skippable` every place that ends up in the merged focus list. Add tests to test_review_brief_drivers.py: (1) a driver named in the reviewer's skippable list ends up in focus only; (2) a reviewer focus list that names one place twice is stored once.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/stack_runner.py:629 — The skippable list is cut to five before places that are in focus are removed, so it can keep fewer than five valid entries.
  Consequence: Take six skippable entries where the first is also a focus place. Only four are kept, although five distinct valid entries were given. A minor shortfall against the 'at most five' cap.
  Done when: Remove the focus places first, then apply MAX_BRIEF_ENTRIES (for example, have `_brief_pairs` take an `exclude` set).
- [1.4] tests/pipeline/test_review_prompt_brief.py:74 — Task 2.2 says the brief-off prompt is identical to the prompt before this change, but the test only checks that each sentence of the off prompt appears somewhere in the on prompt.
  Consequence: If something were added to the brief-off prompt, this test would still pass as long as the text left out `focus` and `skippable`.
  Done when: Assert that the brief-off prompt equals REVIEW_PROMPT + review_changelog_paragraph(...), with the classification prompt in front when review is enabled, or that it equals the brief-on prompt with REVIEW_BRIEF_PROMPT removed.
- [1.5] CHANGELOG.md:9 — This change has two Unreleased bullets, one per unit, although the convention asks for one bullet per change.
  Consequence: AGENTS.md's changelog section says 'One change is one bullet, even across several pull requests: fold later work into the bullet that already describes it.' The bullet at line 9 and the one at line 20 both describe reviewers-are-told-where-to-look.
  Done when: Fold the prompt bullet into the reply-lists bullet as a single entry.

description.summary: Review replies now carry a ranked list of places a person should read first and a list of places safe to skip. The review prompt asks for both lists, and a unit's recorded drivers lead the first.
changes: An approving review reply's description can carry a `focus` list (place, reason, and a kind when the reason names one of four kinds) and a `skippable` list (place and a required reason). Each is capped at five entries and read defensively, so bad entries are dropped, and a reply without them parses as before.
A focus reason is matched to its kind after trimming and folding case. No place appears twice in a list, and a place in focus is dropped from skippable.
When review is on and the `review.brief` setting allows it (default on), the review prompt asks for both lists. It names the four reasons straight from the `FocusKind` enum.

Points 1.2 and 1.3 are fixed. Add a test in tests/graph/test_pr_description_wiring.py: after an approved build, the opened body's Start here section says 'seen to fail first', 'unit-test result: passed' and the round count. Then assert the opened body's Start here section has no 'Review tier' line and that a pull request was still opened.

units.title: A tool renames the old spellings over the paths it is given, by token
units.feedback:
The tool is well shaped and its tests cover what task 1.1 and 1.2 ask for. Three things block it. On real code it turns bare lowercase identifiers into hyphenated words, which is invalid Python. It crashes on the `__pycache__` files that sit next to the `tier2*` modules it will first be run over. And both its table of names and its test helper copy code that already exists.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/rename_test_kinds.py:54 — A bare lowercase `tier1`/`tier2`, with no `_`, `.` or `-` beside it and no space before the digit, falls through to the prose form (`unit-test`/`e2e-test`). In code that turns an identifier into one with a hyphen in it, which is a syntax error.
  Consequence: Checked with `_rewrite`. `def tier1(self):` becomes `def unit-test(self):`, `tier2: bool = False` becomes `e2e-test: bool = False`, and `(tier2,) = x` becomes `(e2e-test,) = x`. These all occur in the tree today: src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1669 and :1727, graph/state.py:137, tests/time_limit.py:34, tests/profiles/test_node_npm_tier2.py:83 and tests/pipeline/test_wiring.py:1550. So a slice run in groups 3 to 13 produces code that does not parse, and the task says the builder should fix by hand only what the tool cannot rename.
  Done when: A bare lowercase spelling in an identifier position becomes the identifier stem (`unit_test`/`e2e`). The prose and tag form (`unit-test`/`e2e-test`) is kept where the spelling is delimited as a tag or value: inside `[...]`, inside quotes, after `/`, or written `tier 2` with a space. Add a test in tests/test_rename_test_kinds.py that rewrites a .py file holding `def tier1(self):`, `tier2: bool = False` and `x = "tier2"`. It asserts `def unit_test(self):` and `e2e: bool = False`, asserts the tag value becomes `"e2e-test"`, and asserts `ast.parse` succeeds on the result.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/rename_test_kinds.py:69 — `_files` walks every file on disk under a folder with `rglob`, including untracked and ignored ones. It then calls `git mv` on any file whose name carries an old spelling, and `git mv` fails on a file git does not track.
  Consequence: src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/__pycache__/ holds tier2.cpython-314.pyc, tier2_exclusive…, tier2_holds…, tier2_schedule… and tier2_times…, all untracked. Running the tool over `src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/`, as group 3 does, reaches `git mv` on one of them. `pipeline.shell.git` then raises CalledProcessError partway through the run, after some files have already been rewritten. The same happens with node_modules or .venv under any path it is given. An ignored text file would also be rewritten silently.
  Done when: Enumerate files with `git ls-files` under the given paths (through `pipeline.shell.git`), so that only tracked files are read, rewritten and moved. Add a test that seeds a tracked `pkg/tier2.py` and an untracked, git-ignored `pkg/__pycache__/tier2.cpython-314.pyc`, runs the tool over `pkg`, and asserts three things: it returns without raising, `pkg/e2e.py` exists, and the .pyc is untouched.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/rename_test_kinds.py:23 — `_FORMS` restates the old-to-new table that compat_names.py already holds (`_STEM` at compat_names.py:31 and `_FILE_STEM` at :32 give the same `unit_test`/`e2e` and `unit-test`/`e2e`, and `_KIND_OF_TAG` at :30 gives the prose form). The spec says the tool rewrites "from the compatibility module's table".
  Consequence: The spec (test-kind-names, "The rename is applied by a repeatable tool") and design.md ("from the table in the compatibility module") say there is one table. With two copies, a change to one spelling has to be made in both. If one is missed, the tool writes names the reading side does not recognise.
  Done when: Give compat_names.py a public, documented accessor for the forms of each old spelling (for example a frozen mapping from `tier1`/`tier2` to its identifier stem, file stem and tag value). Have both `new_spelling` and the tool read it, and derive the CamelCase form from the identifier stem. Remove `_FORMS` from the tool.
- [1.4] tests/test_rename_test_kinds.py:14 — `seed` is the same function as `commit_files` in tests/factories.py:222 (write each file, making its folders, then `git add -A` and commit). It is also copied a second time in tests/test_rename_test_kinds_idempotent.py:11.
  Consequence: The change adds two copies of an existing helper, so three copies now have to change together.
  Done when: Remove both `seed` functions and call `commit_files(repo, "seed", {...})` from tests.factories.

Optional:
- [1.5] tests/test_rename_test_kinds.py:28 — Nothing asserts that a renamed file is recorded as a rename in git's index, which is what task 1.3's "renaming files with `git mv`" is for. The tests would pass just the same with a plain `Path.rename`.
  Consequence: If this regressed to a plain rename, the old path would show as deleted and the new one as untracked, and a slice's commit could leave out the new file.
  Done when: In the first test, assert that `git status --porcelain` shows `R  pkg/tier2_gate.py -> pkg/e2e_gate.py`, or that `git ls-files` lists `pkg/e2e_gate.py` and not `pkg/tier2_gate.py`.
- [1.6] src/agent_build_kit/rename_test_kinds.py:89 — `read_text`/`write_text` use universal newlines, so a CRLF file the tool rewrites comes back with LF line endings on every line.
  Consequence: Every line of such a file shows as changed, and the slice's diff grows beyond the rename.
  Done when: Read and write with `newline=""` (or work on bytes decoded as UTF-8) so line endings are kept.

description.summary: Adds a repeatable tool that rewrites the old `tier1`/`tier2` test-kind spellings to `unit-test`/`e2e-test` (and their identifier and file-name forms) over the tracked files under the paths it is given.
changes: `python -m agent_build_kit.rename_test_kinds --paths ...` rewrites the old spellings token by token and keeps each one's case style. `tier2_gate` becomes `e2e_gate`, `Tier2Result` becomes `E2eResult` and `TIER2` becomes `E2E`; a bare identifier takes the stem (`e2e`), and a quoted, bracketed or spaced value takes the tag (`e2e-test`).
It touches only files git tracks under the given paths, so caches and ignored files are never read, rewritten or moved. Files whose names carry an old spelling are renamed with `git mv`.
It refuses a path outside the repository root and changes nothing. A second run reports no change. Line endings are kept, and the compatibility module, the tool and their tests are exempt.
`compat_names` now exposes a single public `KIND_FORMS` table, giving each old spelling's stem, file-name stem and tag. The read-side `new_spelling` and the rename tool both use it.

units.title: The tool leaves aliases behind, takes another root and can list its changes
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/rename_test_kinds.py:192 — The shim left at the old module path is `from .<new> import *`. That makes a second module object holding copies of the new module's public names, not an alias of the module.
  Consequence: The spec (test-kind-names) says the old module stays importable 'as an alias for each module', and group 3 needs 'callers elsewhere still import, and the suite passes'. A star import breaks that in three ways. (1) `tests/tier2_lock_fakes.py:17,52` does `from agent_build_kit.pipeline import spans, tier2` and then `monkeypatch.setattr(tier2, "time", sleeping)`. Once group 3 renames `pipeline/tier2.py` to `e2e.py`, that patch lands on the shim's copy of `time`, while `e2e.py` keeps calling the real `time.monotonic()` and `time.sleep()` (see `pipeline/tier2.py:324-344`). The fake sleep is skipped without any error, so the lock test sleeps for real or fails. (2) A star import skips names that start with an underscore, so `from pkg.tier2_gate import _helper` and `tier2_gate._helper` both fail. (3) In a module that defines `__all__`, the rewrite turns the old names listed there into new names. The star import then exports only the new names, so `from old import Tier2Thing` fails even though the alias line exists.
  Done when: Make the shim alias the module itself on one line, still ending in the marker. For example: `import importlib, sys; sys.modules[__name__] = importlib.import_module(".<new_stem>", __package__)  # abk-shim`. The import system then binds `pkg.tier2_gate` and `from pkg import tier2_gate` to the new module object. In `tests/test_rename_test_kinds_shims.py`, give the fixture module a private name (for example `_helper = 1`) and a module-level `import time`. Extend the consumer to assert that `pkg.tier2_gate is pkg.e2e_gate`, that `from pkg.tier2_gate import _helper` works, and that setting an attribute on the old module is visible through the new one (`old_module.TIER2_MARKER` patched means `e2e_gate.TIER2_MARKER` changes). Keep the existing assertion that the shim is one line naming `e2e_gate`.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/rename_test_kinds.py:194 — With `--dry-run --shims`, the tool lists only the renamed target. It leaves out the shim module a real run would write and `git add` at the old path.
  Consequence: Someone checking a shimmed slice with `--dry-run` before running it does not see that the old path will be recreated as a shim, so the dry-run list is shorter than what the real run changes.
  Done when: When shims are on and a `.py` file is renamed, also add the old path (relative to root) to the returned list, in dry runs and real runs alike. Assert this in a dry-run test with `--shims`.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/rename_test_kinds.py:162 — Passing `--shims` and `--remove-shims` together is accepted, and removal silently wins.
  Consequence: A mistyped command removes shims when the person meant to add them, and nothing reports the conflict.
  Done when: Put the two flags in an argparse mutually exclusive group, or make `rename_paths` raise when both are set.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/rename_test_kinds.py:192 — The shim uses a relative import, which only works when the renamed module sits inside a package.
  Consequence: A renamed module that is imported as a top-level module, with no parent package, raises 'attempted relative import with no known parent package' when its old name is imported. Today `tests/` is reached as the namespace package `tests.`, so this is a latent edge case.
  Done when: Fall back to an absolute import when `__package__` is empty, or document that shims are only for modules inside a package.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/rename_test_kinds.py:199 — The docstring of `main` still describes only `--paths` and the injected `root`.
  Consequence: A reader of `main` does not learn about `--root`, `--shims`, `--remove-shims` or `--dry-run`, or that `--root` takes precedence over the injected root.
  Done when: Name the four new flags in the docstring and say that `--root` overrides the `root` argument.

description.summary: The internal test-kind rename tool can now leave the old module names behind as real aliases, take away those aliases later, work under a different root, and list what it would change without writing anything.
changes: With `--shims`, each renamed Python module leaves a one-line file at its old path. That file makes the old module name the renamed module object itself, so `is` checks, private names and monkeypatching behave the same through either name.
Each renamed top-level name stays bound under its old spelling in the renamed module, and the rewriter skips any line carrying the shim marker.
`--remove-shims` deletes the shim modules and the old-name aliases. It cannot be combined with `--shims`: `rename_paths` raises `ValueError` and the command line refuses the pair.
`--root` picks the repository to work under, and `--dry-run` lists every path that would change without writing anything, including the old paths that `--shims` would recreate.
A shim for a top-level module (no package) imports the new module by its bare name.

units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:2237 — This unit's commits record none of the hand fixes, which task 4.2 requires. The least visible one is `_E2E_COMMANDS = "tier" + "2_commands"`: the profile method's old name is built from parts and called through `getattr` (line 2245) so that neither the progress guard nor the rename tool can see it.
  Consequence: Task 4.2 says to fix by hand only what the tool cannot rename, "recording each in the group's commit message". Both commit messages (a820120c, 1e718510) hold only the title and the `Unit:` trailer. Group 6 converts `profiles/`. The tool will rename `tier2_commands` there, but it cannot see this string-built name, and pyrefly cannot check a `getattr` call. So once `--remove-shims` runs, every full e2e-test run raises AttributeError, and nothing in the record tells the next unit that this line needs undoing. The same applies to the other hand-added forwards this unit made outside `pipeline/`, none of them recorded: `E2eUnitScope` and `e2e_unit_scope` (config.py:346, :355), `e2e_base_runs` and `unit_test_repeat_runs` (config.py:571-572), `e2e_lock` (installation.py:102).

Also reword the comment above `_E2E_COMMANDS` to say the line is temporary and must become a direct call when `profiles/` is converted, rather than that it is "built from parts so the name is not spelled out here".

The same tool artifacts appear elsewhere: "a second unit's e2e-test tests" (2673), "Post a e2e-test result" (1741) and "What a e2e-test run executes" (2214).

If reading a checkpoint that still carries the real old keys `tier2` and `tier2_ran_none` broke, this test would still pass. The docstring also says something false about the earlier release.

This is the pattern this branch already uses in `tests/pipeline/test_unit_store_test_kind_values.py:14`: for example `OLD_FLAG = "tier" + "2"`, then `{**values, OLD_FLAG: True, f"{OLD_FLAG}_ran_none": False}`. units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] tests/config/test_config_text_edit.py:252 — `test_a_file_written_with_the_old_key_is_edited_under_that_key` was rewritten to write and assert `e2e_splits`. No other test calls `set_hold` on a file written with the old key.

Config load then refuses the file for setting both keys. The suite stays green, which goes against the convention that a renamed setting keeps its old name working for one release.

Follow the existing pattern (`tests/config/test_e2e_runtime_lists_refused.py:18`, `tests/pipeline/test_work_graph_test_kind_tags.py:17`): `OLD_SPLITS = "tier" + "2_splits"` with a comment saying it is the key an installation still has. Write `f"tests:\n  {OLD_SPLITS}:\n    acp:\n      marker: runtime_acp\n"` and assert `loaded(path)["tests"] == {OLD_SPLITS: expected}`. The test should fail if `_OLD_SPLITS` handling is removed.

units.title: Rename README, AGENTS.md, changelog and skills text
Remove aliases and make the old-name guard strict
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/config.py:502 — `TestKindSettings.__getattr__` is an old-name alias that was kept. Its `# abk-shim` marker was taken off, so `--remove-shims` skipped it. Python code can still read `tests.tier2_marker`, `tests.tier2_splits`, `limits.tier2_schedule` and the like as the new fields. The test that does this, `tests/config/test_test_kind_settings_aliases.py`, was put on the guard's exempt list instead of being converted.
  Consequence: Task 23 says it is done when 'no shim module or alias remains' and 'an import of an old name fails', and the spec allows old names only in the compatibility module, the tool and their tests. Reading old keys from `abk.yaml` is a separate job, done by `_read_old_names` and the compat table. `__getattr__` serves only code that uses old attribute names. Right now `tests/config/test_test_kind_settings_aliases.py:96` (`loaded.repos["my.app"].tests.tier2_marker`) and `:105` (`old.tests.tier2_splits.keys()`) depend on it. So the guard's exemption is hiding an alias that is still in use, and new code can bring back `config.<old_name>` reads without any check failing. The class docstring at config.py:479-480 ('still reads, as its new one, until the aliases are removed') is also false once this unit lands.
  Done when: Delete `TestKindSettings.__getattr__` (config.py:502-506) and keep `_read_old_names`. In `tests/config/test_test_kind_settings_aliases.py`, read `tests.e2e_marker` at line 96 and `tests.e2e_splits` at line 105. Reword the docstring at config.py:479-480 to say that an old key name in a file is read as the new one, with a warning, and that the old names are not attributes. Add a test, for example in that file, that loads a block written with `tier2_marker` and asserts that `getattr(block, old_name)` raises `AttributeError` while `block.e2e_marker` holds the value. Build the old name with `old_spelling(...)` or from parts, as the other compat tests do. The `uv run poe test` suite, including `test_the_repository_carries_no_old_spelling`, should still pass.

Optional:
- [1.2] tests/old_test_kind_names.py:28 — `test_test_kind_settings_aliases.py` is exempted by name, but neither the compatibility module nor the tool owns it. The exempt-paths parametrization in `tests/test_old_test_kind_names_guard.py:62-71` doesn't list it, and doesn't list the two terminology documents either.
  Consequence: The spec's exempt set is the compatibility module, the tool and their tests. A config-edge test that writes old keys as literals is a reasonable addition, but nothing pins it, and the parametrized test does not describe the full exemption.
  Done when: Either build the old keys in that file the way the other compat-edge tests do (`old_spelling(TestTier.E2E_TEST)` + suffix, or a `"tier" + "2_..."` constant) and drop it from `EXEMPT_NAMES`, or add it and the two documents to the guard test's exempt parametrization.
- [1.3] tests/old_test_kind_names.py:17 — The guard scans `src`, `tests`, `web/src`, `docs` and the root `*.md`, but not `scripts/` or `pyproject.toml`. This unit fixed an old spelling in `pyproject.toml` by hand, and nothing now stops one coming back there or in `scripts/ci_scope.py`.
  Consequence: An old spelling reintroduced in a pyproject comment or a CI script passes the guard.
  Done when: Add `scripts` to `SCANNED` and scan `pyproject.toml`. Optionally scan `.github/` as well.
- [1.4] tests/profiles/test_node_npm_e2e.py:35 — Spelled-out forms the guard pattern doesn't match are still there: `test_tier_two_*` / `_run_tier_two` in tests/profiles/test_node_npm_e2e.py and test_python_uv_e2e.py, and `test_tier_one_*` in test_python_uv_changelog.py and test_python_uv_parallel.py. A follow-up on group 12 raised the same gap.
  Consequence: AGENTS.md says to use `unit_test`/`e2e` and never the earlier numbered spellings. These names slip through because `OLD_SPELLING` only matches digits.
  Done when: Rename these to `unit_test`/`e2e` and widen `OLD_SPELLING` to `ti`+`er[-_ ]?([12]|one|two)`, plus a guard test case for the spelled-out form.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/work_graph.py:454 — The missing-tags error that `abk tags`/`abk check` show still writes the heading as `[<tier>]` and says 'tier one of unit-test, ...'. The skills were changed to `[<kind>]` in group 22, and AGENTS.md keeps 'tier' for review tiers.

units.title: Profiles declare stub support and a types-inclusive clean check
Profiles declare stub support, a types-inclusive clean check and a stubbed red reading
Profiles declare stub support, read red in a stubbed mode, and the per-group commits setting with a paired commit-order check

description.summary: Toolchain profiles can now declare whether they support test stubs, the red check has a stubbed mode where a test failing on a missing name means a stub is still needed, and a per-group commits setting comes with a check that a branch's test and implementation commits are paired in order.
changes: A toolchain profile can declare `supports_stubs`. `supports_stubs()` reads it tolerantly, so a profile that does not declare it counts as not supporting stubs.

In stubbed mode, the red check rejects a test that fails on a missing attribute, module or name, and names the test as needing a stub. python-uv reads these failures from the pytest JUnit report. An assertion failure or NotImplementedError still counts as red in both modes, and the reading without stubs is unchanged.
In node-npm, the stubbed clean command runs the project's type check after lint and format, using the same argv as the project check so the two cannot drift apart.

A new `builders.per_group_commits` config setting comes with a paired commit-order check in pipeline/commit_order.py that expects alternating `test: ` and `feat: ` subjects. The build now writes its commit subjects from those same prefix constants.
New recorded pytest reports, for failures on a missing attribute, module or name, back the tests of the stubbed red reading.

units.title: The per-group commits setting, a paired commit-order check and a stubbed push gate
Stubbed push gate and the check-and-fix loop after the test step
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1283 — Task 5.2 asks for a test that 'a second group's loop starts again from zero'. None exists: no test reads `stub_rounds` after the loop passes, and none checks that the saved checker output is cleared (`set_feedback(unit.id, "")` when `state.stub_rounds` is non-zero).
  Consequence: If either reset in `stub_checks` is removed (the `"stub_rounds": 0` in its update, or the feedback clear), every test still passes. Once group 7 builds groups one after another, a second group would then start its loop with the first group's rounds already used, and could stop early on `max_check_rounds`. Stale lint output would also stay saved on the unit after its tests commit.
  Done when: Add the test to tests/graph/test_stub_check_rounds.py. Drive `BuildPath.stub_checks` directly, built the way tests/pipeline/test_no_remote.py:192 builds a BuildPath, or through `build` if its outcome exposes the final state. Give it a `UnitRun` with `stub_rounds=2`, saved feedback on the unit, and `run_stub_checks` answering `(True, "")`. Assert that the update has `stub_rounds == 0` and `stub_loop is False`, that the stored feedback is now "", and that a `commit:test` was made.
- [1.2] tests/stub_gate_support.py:72 — `repo_on_branch`, `commit_tests` and `commit_feat` copy, almost line for line, the `repo` fixture, `add_tests` and `add_feat` in tests/pipeline/test_commit_order_pairs.py:19-34. Same base commit, same `spec/change/1-unit` branch, same `test: <title>` / `feat: <title>` subjects, same `tests/test_<name>.py` and `src/<name>.py` paths.
  Consequence: Two copies of the branch shape that paired-commit tests build must now change together. Groups 7 to 10 will change that shape (commit bodies, the `Unit:` trailer), and a copy that is not updated will test a branch the pipeline no longer writes.
  Done when: Keep one copy. Change tests/pipeline/test_commit_order_pairs.py to import the `repo` fixture and the commit helpers from tests/stub_gate_support.py. Give `commit_tests` the optional `content` argument `add_tests` has, then delete the local copies. All assertions stay as they are.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/stack_runner.py:1248 — `_no_stub_checks` is the default for both `run_stub_checks` and `tree_state`. Its signature does not match either field, so both need `# type: ignore[assignment]`, and it raises a bare `NotImplementedError`. The existing `_no_reset` next to it raises a `RuntimeError` with a message.
  Consequence: A runner built without `tree_state` fails with an unnamed NotImplementedError raised by a function named for stub checks, which points the next reader to the wrong field.
  Done when: Use one default per field, typed to match its field so neither type ignore is needed, each raising `RuntimeError("this runner was not given ...")` like `_no_reset`.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/gate.py:122 — Whether a build is stubbed is decided from the repo's profile only (in `cmd_gate` and in `BuildPath.stubbed`). The types-inclusive clean command and the stubbed red reading are then asked of each project's own profile (`profiles.for_project`), here and in `wiring.build_stub_checks`.
  Consequence: In a repo with a project whose profile does not support stubs, that project would be asked `clean_command(types=True)` and `interpret_red(stubbed=True)`, which it may not accept. Both built-in profiles support stubs today, so this is not reachable yet.
  Done when: Either decide stubbed per project (setting on and that project's profile supports stubs), or state in the docstring of `check_branch` that the repo's profile decides for every project.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1287 — `stub_checks` repeats the budget test from `checks`: `budget = active().global_limits.max_check_rounds; if budget is not None and rounds >= budget`.
  Consequence: Two copies of the rule for what `null` and 0 mean in `max_check_rounds`.
  Done when: A small helper, for example `out_of_rounds(rounds) -> int | None` returning the budget when it is spent, used by both.

description.summary: A stubbed build's test step now runs lint, format and type checks over the agent's stubs and tests, with a bounded fix loop, before it commits the tests, and the push gate understands stubbed branches.
changes: When a build is stubbed, the test step no longer commits right after the test agent writes. A new stub-checks step runs lint, format and types over the working tree (no test run) and makes the `test:` commit only once they pass.

A failing stub check saves its output on the unit and starts a fix round. The rounds are limited by `global_limits.max_check_rounds` and counted apart from the pre-review check rounds. The unit stops with the output kept when the budget runs out or a fix round leaves the tree unchanged.
A pass resets the round count to zero and clears the saved checker output, so the next group's loop starts fresh.

In stubbed mode the push gate (`check_branch`) requires paired test/feat commits, runs the clean command with types, and reads the red run as stubbed. Its cached check results are kept apart from those of unstubbed runs.
Both check loops now read the shared round budget through one helper, `out_of_rounds`, where null means no limit and 0 means the budget is spent at once.

- [2.1] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1320 — Line 1320 (`self._leftovers, self._stub_leftovers = self._stub_leftovers, ()`) wipes the node's own leftovers when FIX_STUB_CHECKS is itself resumed after being killed mid-agent.
  Consequence: Take a fix_stub_checks run killed mid-agent, which a later tick resumes at FIX_STUB_CHECKS with a new BuildPath and `_tree` None. `self.tree()` at line 1313 is called with `_own` True, so it sets `self._leftovers = dirty.paths`. Because of `if not self._own`, it leaves `_stub_leftovers` at (). Line 1320 then replaces `_leftovers` with (). If the session cannot be continued and the fix runs in a new session, `agent()` adds no LEFTOVERS_NOTE and records no 'resuming over uncommitted work' trace. The agent is not told the uncommitted files are an interrupted run's work. Before this rework, the own-leftovers path worked for FIX_STUB_CHECKS as it does for every other node in EDITING_NODES. The rework added the line, so it could not have been seen in round 1.
  Done when: fix_stub_checks keeps leftovers found under `_own`. For example, use `self._leftovers = self._leftovers or self._stub_leftovers; self._stub_leftovers = ()`, or set `_stub_leftovers` whenever the stub-loop branch is taken, not only when `not self._own`. Add a test that kills FIX_STUB_CHECKS mid-agent over a dirty tree and resumes it in a new session. It asserts the fix prompt carries LEFTOVERS_NOTE with the paths. description.summary: A stubbed build now runs static checks on its stubs and tests before committing them, and loops on fixing those checks. That loop survives being stopped or killed while there is uncommitted work in the tree.
changes: A stubbed build runs lint, format and type checks (no test run) over what the test agent wrote, and makes the tests commit only once those checks pass. If they fail, it stores their output as STUB_CHECKS feedback and runs a fix round, up to the configured round budget.

A unit requeued after its check loop stopped with uncommitted tests in its worktree is no longer held for a dirty tree. The tree is accepted as the unit's own, and the fix prompt names the leftover files. A tree dirtied by a chat's changes is still held as attached.
A fix_stub_checks run killed mid-agent and resumed in a new session keeps the leftovers it found itself. The resumed prompt carries the leftovers note with those paths.
A fix round that changes nothing stops the unit with a message that says so. A fix that passes clears the stored stub-check feedback.

units.title: The build writes a tests and an implementation commit per group, with reasons and carried groups
A stubbed build resumes at the first group without its pair
Per-group commit messages, carried groups, resume and pair count
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:2530 — `after_prepare` checks `had_feedback` before `resume`. A stubbed branch that is only part built and has saved feedback therefore goes to REWORK, then CHECKS and REVIEW, and its remaining groups are never built. The new pair count does not catch this, because it runs only inside `implement`.
  Consequence: When the branch already has commits, `standing` treats a person's note (`saved.guidance if existing`, line 1062) as feedback. Restack-conflict feedback (line 1023) is treated the same way. Take a unit of three groups whose branch holds the pairs for G1 and G2, requeued with a note or after a restack that conflicted. It gets `had_feedback=True` and `resume='tests'`. The router returns REWORK, then `after_rework` goes to CHECKS and REVIEW, and a PR opens without group 3. This breaks the spec requirement that 'a requeue SHALL continue at that group' and 'a count short of the groups SHALL stop the unit'. It also contradicts the comment at line 1445 that the note is kept so that every group's prompts carry it.
  Done when: In `after_prepare`, check `state.resume` before `state.had_feedback` (after `stub_loop`), so a part-built stubbed branch continues at its next group. The note still reaches the group prompts through `person_guidance` and is cleared after the last group, as it is today. Add a test in `tests/graph/test_per_group_resume.py`: seed the branch with the G1 and G2 pairs and call `store.set_guidance(UNIT, NOTE)` before the build. Assert that the first agent call is group 3's tests and carries the note, that `claude:rework` is not in the events, and that the branch ends with three pairs.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1439 — The pair count runs only after the last group. If a group before the last makes no implementation commit, the build carries on, and the stop message then names every group from that one onward. A requeue then writes the later groups' tests a second time, so the unit can never finish.
  Consequence: Example: group 1's implement makes no commit (the agent made no change, or committed under its own subject). The build continues: `test: G1`, `test: G2`, `feat: G2`, `test: G3`, `feat: G3`. `missing_pairs` uses `group_progress(...).done == 0` and reports 'group 1, group 2, group 3', but groups 2 and 3 have their pairs. On requeue, `resumed` gives group 0 / implement. After that, `implement` sets `group=1` and routes to TESTS, so group 2's tests are written again. The branch never reaches `done == 3`, so every run stops again.
  Done when: Run the check after every group's implement, not only the last. After `r.commit(...)`, when `group_step` is not None and `group_progress(branch_subjects, titles).done != state.group + 1`, stop naming this group: `group N (title)`. The last-group count then comes from the same code. Add a test in `tests/graph/test_per_group_pair_count.py` with `no_commit_for="1"` that asserts: the outcome is failed, the detail names group 1 and not groups 2 or 3, no `claude:tests` call is made after group 1's implement, and nothing is reviewed.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/commit_order.py:140 — The new `branch_subjects` produces the same list that `check_structure` already builds at line 270 with `[_subject(repo, sha) for sha in _commits(repo, base)]`: the subjects of `base..HEAD`, oldest first.
  Consequence: This leaves two ways in one module to read a branch's subjects, and the paired gate check and the build's resume/count must agree on them. If one changes (say, to a merge-aware range or a different format) and the other does not, the gate and the build can disagree about whether a pair exists.
  Done when: In `check_structure`, call `_pair_problems(branch_subjects(repo, base))` and delete `_subject` (it has no other callers).

Optional:
- [1.4] tests/runner_fakes.py:112 — `Recorder.commit` decides a commit's kind with `"test" in message`, and it now receives the whole message. Every stubbed `feat:` commit's body contains `CODE_BODY` ('...makes its tests pass'), so each one counts as a tests commit and `commits_from_impl` is ignored.
  Consequence: A stubbed-build test that uses `Recorder(commits_from_impl=0)` to stand for an implementation that made no commit would still count one commit and pass whatever the code does. No current test combines the two.
  Done when: Classify on the subject's prefix: `count = 1 if subject.startswith(TESTS_PREFIX) else self.commits_from_impl`, where the subject is the line already split off for `self.subjects`.

description.summary: A stubbed build now gives each task group commits under its own title, resumes a part-built branch at the next group, and stops at the first group that lacks a tests-and-implementation pair.
changes: In a stubbed build, each group's commits use the group's title as the subject. The body says what the commit holds and repeats the group's "Done when" sentence.

A requeued stubbed branch that is only part built continues at the first group without a pair, even when a person's note or restack feedback is waiting. The note is passed to every remaining group's prompts and cleared after the last group.

After each group's implementation step, the build checks that the branch holds a tests and implementation pair for that group and for every group before it. If one is missing, the build stops and names that group, so a later group's tests are never written over a gap.
Resuming, the pair count and the commit-order gate's paired check all read the branch's commit subjects through one function, `branch_subjects`, so they cannot disagree.

- [1.3] docs/unit-graph.md:337 — The two new steps appear only in the diagram. The node table (lines 335-344) has no rows for `stub_checks` and `fix_stub_checks`, and the opening list of graph callables (lines 6-9) does not name them.

  Done when: Add both names to the list at lines 6-9. Add a table row for `stub_checks` (stubbed build only: lint, format and types over the stubs and tests with no test run, then commits `test:`; on failure saves the output as `stub-checks` feedback and stops once `max_check_rounds` is spent; wraps `run_stub_checks`, `commit`). Also say in the `tests` and `implement` rows that a stubbed build makes one pair per group, with each commit's body holding the fixed sentence and the group's 'Done when'.

units.title: The review.ceilings setting and the ceilings in effect
Review ceilings setting, repo override and the ceiling in effect
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/config.py:1503 — The workspace check and the per-repo check order the `full` ceiling differently. `_ceilings_ordered_above_floor` checks the workspace against the literal `review.ceilings` object, so an unset `full` counts as the default 750. A repo's check goes through `repo_ceilings`, whose inherited `full` comes from `_full_ceiling`, which is `max_unit_lines` when `ceilings.full` is unset. So a repo can fail on a relation between two values it did not set and that the workspace check accepts.
  Consequence: I ran this against the branch: `global_limits.max_unit_lines: 3000` with no `ceilings` loads. Adding only `repos.app.review.ceilings: {auto: 6000}` then fails with `repos.app.review.ceilings: light (2000) must not be below full (3000)`. Neither value is the repo's, and both are inherited from a workspace that loads. Overriding just `auto` should not stop the configuration loading, and the message blames the repo for something it does not set. The spec says an *override* that breaks the order fails, naming the repo.
  Done when: Check the repo's merged ceilings so that it only refuses an ordering pair (auto/light, light/full) where at least one side is the repo's own value. The floor check already works this way (`own.full is not None`). Add a test to `tests/config/test_review_ceilings_repo.py`: `max_unit_lines: 3000` plus a repo override of `{auto: 6000}` loads, and `review_ceiling(app, config, ReviewTier.FULL)` is 3000. The existing refusal tests must still pass, for example `{auto: 1500}` against a global `light: 2000`.
- [1.2] CHANGELOG.md:5 — The new bullet says what each tier's ceiling is, but nothing reads `review_ceiling` yet. The planner, the join check and the size comparison still read `global_limits.max_unit_lines` (`pipeline/planner.py:239,441,1001`, `pipeline/unit_size.py:57`, `pipeline/wiring.py:1920`).
  Consequence: The sentence 'With `review.enabled` off every tier gets the `full` ceiling…' implies that setting `review.ceilings.full: 1000` resizes units today. It does not: plans are still held to `max_unit_lines`. A reader who sets the key will see no effect.
  Done when: Reword the bullet to say the keys are accepted and checked when the configuration loads, and that units are not sized by them yet. Group 11 later folds in the final wording.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/config.py:365 — The design names the resolver `ceilings_in_effect(workspace, repo)`. The code calls it `repo_ceilings(repo, config)`, which reads like the repo's own `RepoCeilingsConfig` rather than the merged ceilings in effect.
  Consequence: The name is easy to confuse with `repo.review.ceilings`, the repo's own unmerged override, and it does not match the design the later units are written against.
  Done when: Rename it `ceilings_in_effect`, keeping the `(repo, config)` argument order that `e2e_unit_scope` uses.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/config.py:1508 — At the workspace level, a `full` ceiling in effect that comes from `max_unit_lines` is never ordered against `light`. With `max_unit_lines: 3000` and `review.enabled` true, a unit expected to get `full` review may be larger than a `light` one.
  Consequence: This only matters once per-tier sizing is on. Refusing it now would stop existing files with a large `max_unit_lines` loading, so it belongs with group 3's handling of `max_unit_lines` (a later unit).
  Done when: Decide this in group 3: either a notice, or refusing it only when `review.enabled` is true.

description.summary: Adds per-review-tier changed-line ceilings to the `review` config. A repo can override them, and they are checked when the configuration loads, but units are not sized by them yet.
changes: The `review` section accepts `ceilings` with `auto` (5000), `light` (2000) and `full` (750) changed lines. They are refused at load unless auto >= light >= full, and `full` is checked against `min_unit_lines` when it is set.

A repo's `review` block can override any tier. An override that breaks the order or the floor is refused with a message naming the repo. A repo is never blamed for a relation between two values it only inherits from the workspace.

`review_ceiling(repo, config, tier)` gives the ceiling in effect for a unit: the tier's own ceiling when `review.enabled` is on, otherwise the `full` one. `full` falls back to `max_unit_lines` when it is not set. `ceilings_in_effect` merges a repo's overrides with the workspace values.
The changelog says the keys are accepted and checked, and that plans are still held to `max_unit_lines` for now.

units.title: max_unit_lines is deprecated and read as the full ceiling
Deprecate max_unit_lines and migrate it to review.ceilings.full

description.summary: This branch deprecates `global_limits.max_unit_lines`. It is still read as the full-review ceiling, `abk config` and `abk doctor` warn about it, and `abk config --migrate` moves it to `review.ceilings.full` without changing anything else in the file.
changes: `max_unit_lines` (under `global_limits` or the old `limits` root key, in the base file or its overlay) is read as `review.ceilings.full` when that is not set. A file that sets both keys to different values is refused.
The minimum unit size (`min_unit_lines`) is checked against the full ceiling that is actually in effect, whichever key sets it. A raised floor with a larger `review.ceilings.full` now loads.

`abk config` and `abk doctor` report each deprecated key the file or its overlay sets, once each, including `max_unit_lines` kept under the old `limits` root key. `abk config` prints the full ceiling actually in effect.

`abk config --migrate` moves `max_unit_lines` (with its comments) into `review.ceilings.full`, creating the `review`/`ceilings` blocks if needed. When both keys already agree it removes the old key and keeps its comments. It refuses anchors, flow style, merge keys, conflicting values and any result that would not load with the same ceiling, and says to raise `light`/`auto` when the moved ceiling would exceed them.
The line-editing migrations share one set of steps for moving lines, restoring a missing final newline, and refusing blocks that cannot be edited line by line (`config_migrate.py`).

units.title: The plan check holds a unit to the ceiling of its expected tier
Plan check and planner prompt use the tier ceiling
units.feedback:
the reviewer's reply was not readable as a verdict

Still open from earlier rounds:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/planner.py:443 — With review.enabled on, a planner reply that leaves out `review_tier` is held to the ceiling of its floor tier, not to `full`. `_with_review_tier` (line 221) fills in the floor, which is `auto` for unflagged groups, before `_check_ceiling` runs. `unit_ceiling` then returns 5000.
  Consequence: Flag on, unflagged groups, and a reply `{"groups":[1,2,3],"estimated_lines":4000}` with no review_tier: the plan is accepted against 5000. The spec (review-tier-ceilings: 'a unit with no expected tier SHALL be held to the `full` ceiling', scenario 'No expected tier' at 800 refused against 750) and design.md ('a reply that omitted the tier and was given its floor, is never sized more loosely') say it should be refused against 750. The prompt this branch adds ('a unit with no `review_tier` is held to the `full` ceiling', `_ceilings_text`) and the changelog ('a unit with no tier to `full`') are therefore false. `test_a_unit_with_no_expected_tier_is_held_to_the_full_ceiling` misses this because it flags every group `contract`, so the floor is already `full`.
  Done when: The plan check sizes a unit whose reply gave no `review_tier` against the `full` ceiling, even though the recorded tier is still the floor. For example, keep whether the reply named a tier (raw value before `_with_review_tier`) and pass `None` to the helper for those units, or run `_check_ceiling` on the unfilled tiers. Add a test in tests/pipeline/test_planner_tier_ceilings.py: flag on, unflagged GROUPS, a reply with no review_tier at 800 raises PlannerError naming 750. Rename or keep the existing contract-flag test as a test of a `full` floor.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/planner.py:241 — Three places still read `global_limits.max_unit_lines` directly instead of the one helper: the join check's `ceiling=` (line 241, which task 5.4 names), the prompt's `max_lines` (line 1137) and the new flag-off branch of `_largest_raw_figures` (line 946). AGENTS.md says not to add a new reader, and tasks 5.4 and 6.4 say to route these through the helper.

Meanwhile the planner is told 'Never combine groups into a unit estimated over 750 changed lines', the join check allows a join up to 750, and the calibration's 'largest raw estimate' is worked out from 750, all with the flag off. The planner then plans to a figure the check refuses, and a join accepted at 700 contradicts the plan check.

After this, `grep max_unit_lines src/agent_build_kit/pipeline` finds nothing. Per-tier join sizing stays with group 8; this unit only has to make the join's argument come from the helper. The same KeyError would replace a PlannerError in `_check_ceiling` when `known_repos()` is empty (parse_plan only checks the repo when that list is non-empty).

The spec's 'no prompt differs from today's' is then unenforced.

description.summary: With review.enabled on, the plan check, the planner's instructions and the pull-request size comparison use the ceiling of each unit's expected review tier; with it off they behave as before, reading the one full ceiling through the same helper.
changes: The plan check holds each unit, after its calibration ratio, to the ceiling of its expected review tier in its repo. A reply that names no tier is held to `full` but recorded at its floor. A refusal, including a single group too large for any unit, names the tier and the ceiling.
The planner's instructions list the auto, light and full ceilings and each repo override. With review on, the calibration section gives each kind's largest raw estimate per tier.

The prompt's single ceiling, the join check's ceiling and the calibration figures now come from review_ceiling, so an installation that sets only review.ceilings.full is planned and checked against that value. With the flag off the prompt is pinned byte for byte by golden files.

A pull request landing over its unit's tier ceiling is logged with that figure, and `abk status` names the figure when review is on. A stored unit of a repo no longer configured falls back to the workspace's ceilings instead of crashing.
review_ceiling and ceilings_in_effect in config.py accept a missing repo, which gets the workspace's ceilings.

units.title: A plan records the sizing digest it was made under
Plan sizing digest and stale plan reporting
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:4255 — `stale_plans_line` walks every record in `planned.json`, including changes that are no longer open (archived or deleted), so it reports plans that can never be planned again.
  Consequence: Nothing removes a change's record from `planned.json` when the change is archived: the only removals are in `retire_cmd`, `split/remove` and orphan cleanup. `inst.tasks_files()` lists only open changes. So once `review.enabled` is turned on, every archived change's old record (`ok: true`, no `sizing`) counts as stale. The tick and `abk status` then print, on every run and with no end, a line such as `N plan(s) stale ...: <archived>, ... — abk replan CHANGE plans one again`. Following that advice fails: `abk replan <archived>` refuses with "is not a change", so the line can never be cleared. It also disagrees with `abk replan` with no argument, which lists only `inst.tasks_files()` (pipeline.py:5609), and with `has_work`, which also walks only `tasks_files()`.
  Done when: `stale_plans_line` considers only open changes, the same set the listing and `has_work` use: walk `inst.tasks_files()` and look up `planned_hashes(inst).get(change)`, keeping records that are `ok` and `plan_is_stale`. Add a test, in `tests/cli/test_status_stale_plans.py` or the tick test, where `planned.json` holds a stale, ok record for a change with no directory under `changes/` (or one only under `changes/archive/`), and assert that `abk status` prints no stale line for it. The change in the existing status test should also get a `tasks.md`, so the test still passes once the line is filtered to open changes.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/split/copy.py:85 — Plan records that `abk split` copies into the destination are written without `sizing`, so a plan the split moves reads as stale there whenever the destination has review enabled.
  Consequence: Task 9.2 says the digest is stored on every recorded plan. The spec says a record with no digest reads as empty, so with `review.enabled` true in the destination every moved change is reported stale by its tick, `abk status` and the `abk replan` listing right after the split. That holds even when source and destination share the same sizing and the plan was made under it. The source record's `sizing` is dropped in the copy.
  Done when: `_plans_to_write` carries the source record's digest: `"sizing": planned_hashes(source)[name].get("sizing", "")` beside `hash`, `attempts` and `ok`. This is the sizing the plan was actually made under. A split test asserts that a moved record keeps the source record's `sizing` value, and that `outstanding` stays false after the copy (idempotent).

Optional:
- [1.3] tests/cli/test_status_stale_plans.py:45 — `assert "2" in line` checks the count loosely: a '2' anywhere on the line passes it.
  Consequence: A line that printed the wrong count and happened to contain a '2' elsewhere (for example a change name or a digest) would still pass, so the count that task 10.3 asks status to give is only loosely pinned.
  Done when: Assert the count's position, for example `line.lstrip().startswith("2 plan")` or a regex on `\b2 plan\(s\) stale`, after stripping any log prefix.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:4252 — `plan_is_stale` recomputes `sizing_digest()` (a model dump plus sha256 of the review config and every repo) for each record, and `stale_plans_line` calls it once per change on every tick.
  Consequence: The cost is small but grows with changes × repos on every tick and every status. Each call also reads `config.active()` again.
  Done when: Compute the digest once in `stale_plans_line` (and in `plan_all`, which calls `sizing_digest()` per record write) and compare against it, for example with an optional `current: str | None = None` parameter on `plan_is_stale`.

description.summary: A plan now records the sizing it was made under. A plan made under other sizing is reported as stale by the tick, `abk status` and `abk replan`, with the command that plans it again.
changes: Every plan record written to `planned.json` now carries a `sizing` digest of the sizing settings it was made under. This covers successful plans, failures, waits and plans that were only recorded. `plan_all` works out the digest once per run.
A plan is stale when its recorded `sizing` differs from the current digest. A record with no `sizing` counts as the empty digest.
The tick and `abk status` print a line that counts and names the open changes whose ok plan is stale and says `abk replan CHANGE` plans one again. Changes that are archived or deleted are ignored.
The `abk replan` listing marks a planned change as `planned, stale: made under other sizing` when its plan is stale.

`abk split` copies each moved change's recorded `sizing` into the destination's plan record. A moved plan therefore does not read as stale there, and running the split again has nothing left to write.

units.title: The pull request carries a label for its review tier
Review-tier labels on pull requests and the queue ordered by tier
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:468 — No test covers the production wiring of the review label. `labels.follow_review(unit, inst.state_dir / VERDICTS)` in `store_for` is the only place a review label is ever written, and every test in this branch calls `StateLabels.follow_review` or `set_review` directly.
  Consequence: If this line is deleted, or passed the wrong path (for example `inst.state_dir / "units.json"` or a planning-root path), the whole suite still passes, but no pull request ever gets `review-auto|light|full` in production. That breaks the spec scenario 'A verdict is recorded … WHEN the unit's labels are brought in line THEN the pull request carries review-light', and task 1.4 asks for this call to be made.
  Done when: Add a test to `tests/cli/test_state_label_wiring.py`, beside `test_the_store_the_cli_builds_labels_a_pull_request_as_its_unit_changes`, that uses the same `inst`/`forge` fixtures with review enabled. It should: write a `light` verdict for `add-marker/1` to `inst.state_dir / VERDICTS` with `tests/verdict_fakes.write_verdicts`; call `cli.store_for(inst)`; upsert the unit; call `store.set_state(UNIT, IN_REVIEW, pr=PR, branch=...)`; assert that `forge.on_pr[PR] & review_label_names() == {"review-light"}`; then write a `full` verdict, make another state write (for example `set_state(UNIT, IN_REVIEW)`), and assert that only `review-full` remains. Optionally assert that with review disabled no review label appears.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/labels.py:94 — `follow_review` works out the recorded tier itself (`latest_verdict(...)` then `.tier` if not None), which is exactly what `review_order.review_tier` (src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/review_order.py:16) does.
  Consequence: If the definition of a unit's recorded tier changes (for example, to ignore a non-final round's verdict), two places have to change together.
  Done when: Have `follow_review` call `review_tier(unit, verdicts)` and pass the result to `set_review` when it is not None.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:926 — `cmd_status` re-reads and re-parses verdicts.json for every unit in review twice: once inside `review_order`'s sort key and once more per printed line through `review_tier`. It also calls `config.active().review.enabled` again on every printed line.
  Consequence: With n units in review, `abk status` parses the file 2n times. That is harmless at today's sizes, but grows linearly with the queue for no reason.
  Done when: Work out each in-review unit's tier once (a dict from unit id to tier) and use it both for ordering and for the printed tier, for example by letting `review_order` accept or return that mapping.
- [1.4] tests/pipeline/test_scheduling_ignores_review_tier.py:44 — The 'without' baseline is computed while the verdicts file already exists, not 'with no verdicts'. Because `ready_units` is pure and has no verdict input, the test only shows that `ready_units` does not depend on where in-review units sit in the list.
  Consequence: If the scheduler started reading verdicts.json, this test would not catch it. The source guard in `tests/graph/test_verdict_is_shadow.py` is what actually protects against that.
  Done when: Either add a line to the module docstring saying the guard in `test_verdict_is_shadow.py` is what keeps the scheduler from reading verdicts, or compute the baseline before `write_verdicts` so the test matches what task 2.3 describes.

description.summary: When review is enabled, a unit's pull request gets a label for its recorded review tier, and `abk status` lists units in review with the highest tier first.
changes: Each time a unit's state labels are brought in line, its pull request gets one `review-auto`, `review-light` or `review-full` label matching its latest recorded verdict, and that label is replaced when the verdict changes. Nothing is written when review is disabled or no verdict is recorded.
`abk status` lists units awaiting review as `full`, then `light`, then those with no verdict, then `auto`. Within each group they stay in arrival order, and units in other states keep their places.
Each line for a unit in review in `abk status` shows the unit's recorded tier (` — tier light`).

`review_tier` and `review_tiers` in `pipeline/review_order.py` are the single place where a unit's recorded tier is read. The labels and the status listing both use them, and the verdicts file is read once for each status run.
Tests check that the store the CLI builds puts the review label on a pull request, and that ordering by tier never changes which unit the scheduler starts next.

units.title: Forge merge-commit reads and verdict outcome with revert detection
units.feedback:
Groups 6–8 are almost all in place, and the 69 tests across the touched files pass. Most of the forge read (groups 6 and 7) was already on main: the protocol method, its retry entry, and the GitHub and Azure DevOps implementations. This branch makes GitHub answer empty for a pull request it cannot find and makes the local forge answer empty. It also adds the outcome derivation and the revert search. One correctness gap in the revert-check flag blocks approval, and two cases the tasks name have no test yet.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/review_outcome.py:46 — `revert_checked` is set true as soon as the forge names a merge commit, even when the checkout could not be searched. `reverts_merge` returns False when `git log <merge>..<trunk>` fails (`review_revert.py:17-18`), and that False reads the same as 'no revert found'.
  Consequence: Take a checkout that has not fetched since the merge, or a trunk name that does not resolve there. The forge answers a sha, `git log` exits non-zero, and the record holds `outcome: clean` with `revert_checked: true`. The spec requires that 'the record SHALL also say whether a revert could be checked', and here it says checked when nothing was searched. A revert that does exist upstream is then counted as a clean sample by the later rates and gates. `tests/pipeline/test_review_outcome.py` takes exactly this path: the stand-in answers `'a'*40`, which is not in the checkout. The comment `# the checkout does not hold the merge commit: nothing to find` states the wrong conclusion.
  Done when: `reverts_merge` lets its caller tell 'searched, none found' apart from 'could not search'. For example, it returns `bool | None` with None when `git log` fails, or it raises a named error that `with_outcome` catches. `with_outcome` then sets `revert_checked` true only when the search actually ran. Add a test in `tests/pipeline/test_review_revert.py`: the forge answers a 40-hex sha that is absent from the checkout, and the record has `revert_checked is False` with the outcome taken from the history (`clean`). Fix the comment to match.
- [1.2] tests/forges/test_github_merge_commit.py:18 — Task 6.2 asks for a closed-but-unmerged pull request to answer empty. Neither this file nor `tests/forges/test_github_merge.py:115-126` covers that case. Only merged, open and missing are tested.
  Consequence: Suppose the GitHub read keyed on `state == 'closed'` instead of `merged`. A closed-unmerged pull request would then answer a merge commit and could be searched for a revert as if merged, and no test would fail.
  Done when: Add a test where the host answers `{"number": 7, "state": "closed", "merged": false, "merge_commit_sha": "c"*40}` and `merge_commit(REPO, 7)` is None.
- [1.3] tests/forges/test_azure_merge.py:152 — Task 7.1 asks that an abandoned Azure DevOps pull request answer empty. Only completed and active are tested, and the file the task names, `tests/forges/test_azure_merge_commit.py`, was not created.
  Consequence: The abandoned case only works because of `status != "completed"` at `azure_devops.py:892`. A rewrite that checked `status == "active"` would let an abandoned pull request that carries a `lastMergeCommit` answer a commit, and no test would catch it.
  Done when: Add a test, either in the named `tests/forges/test_azure_merge_commit.py` or beside the existing ones, where a pull-request document with `status: abandoned` and a `lastMergeCommit` set gives `merge_commit(REPO, 162) is None`.

Optional:
- [1.4] docs/code-forges.md:99 — The `merge_commit` row says 'the commit a merged pull request produced, None while it is not merged'. That is now untrue for the local forge, which answers None even after a person merges, and for a pull request GitHub cannot find.
  Consequence: A reader takes None to mean 'not merged', but on the local forge it means 'cannot say'. The spec calls this the forge that cannot say, and the revert check relies on that reading.
  Done when: Reword the row: None when it is not merged or when the forge cannot say (the local forge always; a pull request the host cannot find).
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/forges/azure_devops.py:890 — GitHub's `merge_commit` now turns a missing pull request (NotFound) into an empty answer, but the Azure DevOps copy still raises on a 404. The two forges disagree on 'cannot say'.
  Consequence: For a deleted or unreachable pull request, the outcome sweep (group 9) gets an empty answer on GitHub and an exception on Azure DevOps. The sweep's own guard will log it, but the record will not say 'unchecked' the same way on both hosts.
  Done when: Catch the 404 in Azure DevOps `merge_commit` and answer None, with a test like `test_a_missing_pull_request_answers_empty`. Or record why the two forges differ.
- [1.6] tests/pipeline/test_review_outcome.py:4 — The module docstring says the repository has 'no commits on it', but the `checkout` fixture commits `base.txt`. The real reason only the history decides is that the stand-in's sha `'a'*40` is not in the checkout.
  Consequence: The next reader is misled about why these tests never reach the revert search. This also ties in with the first finding.
  Done when: Say that the forge answers a commit the checkout does not hold. Once the first finding is fixed, these tests could also assert `revert_checked is False`.

description.summary: Records how each reviewed unit turned out after merge (clean, reworked, reverted or still open). Every forge can now say which commit a merged pull request produced, so the record can look for a revert of that commit.
changes: A unit's verdict record gains an `outcome` (`open`, `clean`, `reworked` or `reverted`), a `reworks` count taken from the unit's history, and `revert_checked`.

A merged unit counts as reverted when a trunk commit after its merge commit says `This reverts commit <full sha>` or `Reverts <owner>/<repo>#<pr>`. Both are matched exactly, so a longer sha or a longer number does not count.

`revert_checked` is true only when the forge named the merge commit and the checkout could actually be searched. A checkout that lacks the merge commit or the trunk now reads as unchecked, not as free of reverts.

`merge_commit` answers None, instead of raising or guessing, for a GitHub or Azure DevOps pull request that is missing, unmerged, closed without merging or abandoned. The local forge always answers None.
docs/code-forges.md describes when `merge_commit` answers None.
