units.title: A test that needs the OpenSpec CLI fails with one message when it cannot be run
units.feedback:
Two points from task 1.5 are still open. First, the design's UNVERIFIED note on the time limit was never settled: the probe runs with no timeout. Second, two of the four files send their CLI work through a path that `require` never sees. The helper, the fixture, the four markers and the guard test are otherwise sound, and the 11 new tests pass.

Required:
- [1.1] tests/openspec_cli.py:30 — `probe` calls `openspec.run` with no timeout, so a CLI fetch that hangs fails with the time-limit message and not with 'the OpenSpec CLI is not installed'.
  Consequence: The first test to request the session fixture pays for it in its setup phase, and `tests/time_limit.py` caps setup at 60 seconds. If `npx` stalls while it fetches the package (the incident's flake-fix test died exactly this way: 'test exceeded the time limit of 60 seconds'), the probe gets interrupted by `TimedOut`. Every test that requests the fixture then errors with 'test setup exceeded the time limit of 60 seconds'. That breaks the task's done-when, which says the four files fail with 'the OpenSpec CLI is not installed' plus the status when the CLI cannot start. design.md flagged this as UNVERIFIED and told the builder to keep the probe under the limit with a timeout passed to the runner. That was not done, and the design was not corrected either.
  Done when: Give `probe` a timeout below `time_limit.DEFAULT_TEST_TIME_LIMIT`, for example a module constant around 45 s. When `run` is None, pass the runner as `functools.partial(subprocess.run, timeout=...)`, and catch `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` (it is not an `OSError`). Fail with `not_installed('timeout', <the expired command's stderr or its str>)`. Add a test in `tests/test_openspec_cli_probe.py`: a `FakeRunner` that raises `subprocess.TimeoutExpired(['npx'], 45)` makes `probe` fail with a message that starts with MESSAGE. Also update design.md's UNVERIFIED note on the time limit to say what the code does.
- [1.2] tests/integration/test_scheduled_tier2_change_validates.py:26 — The `abk check` results never go through `require`, so a status 127 from validate there still shows up as `assert 1 == 0`. `test_init_end_to_end.py` has the same gap for the `openspec init` that `abk init` runs.
  Consequence: The spec says 'A command of a test that exits with status 127 SHALL be reported with the same message and not as a failure of what the test checks'. Task 1.5 and design.md say to pass the `abk check` results through `require`. In both tests of this file, `cli.cmd_check(...) == 0` hides validate's `CompletedProcess`. If the probe passes and the later validate exits 127, the test reports `assert 1 == 0`, which is one of the five different messages the incident showed. In `test_init_end_to_end.py`, a 127 from `openspec init` inside `main(['init', ...])` still surfaces as 'abk init: openspec init failed' and not as the shared message.
  Done when: Pick one. (a) Make the check visible to `require`: in each `abk check` test, before `cmd_check`, run `require(openspec.validate(inst.root))`, the same command `cmd_check` runs, so a 127 fails with MESSAGE; or wrap `cmd_check` so its printed output is checked for status 127. (b) Correct design.md, as task 1.5 asks where the code differs, to say that the `abk check` and `abk init` paths are covered by the session probe alone, and why that is enough. Either way, the code and the design must agree on which commands in the four files `require` covers.

Optional:
- [1.3] tests/test_openspec_cli_probe.py:80 — The 'probe runs once per session' test uses its own copy of the fixture in a generated conftest, not the real one in `tests/integration/conftest.py`.
  Consequence: If the real fixture lost `scope='session'`, this test would still pass. Only the AST check in `test_openspec_cli_users.py`, a substring match for 'session' in the decorator, would catch it. That covers the case, but the two tests split one fact between them.
  Done when: Optional: have the generated conftest import the real fixture, with the runner swapped through a monkeypatch or a parameter, so one behavioural test pins the real fixture's scope.

description.summary: Tests that need the real OpenSpec CLI now fail with one clear message ('the OpenSpec CLI is not installed', plus the status and the last stderr lines) when the CLI cannot be run, instead of a scatter of unrelated assertion failures.
changes: A new test helper, `tests/openspec_cli.py`, adds `probe` and `require`. `probe` asks the CLI for its version once, in a temporary directory, under a 45-second timeout. It fails with the shared message when the exit status is non-zero, when the program cannot start, or when the fetch stalls. `require` passes a command's result through and fails with the same message on exit status 127.
A session fixture `openspec_cli` in `tests/integration/conftest.py` runs the probe once. The four integration test files that use the CLI request it.

Those files pass their OpenSpec results through `require`. This covers `abk check`'s validate and the `openspec init` that `abk init` runs, so a missing CLI is reported as missing, not as `assert 1 == 0` or 'abk init: openspec init failed'.
Unit tests cover the helper with a fake runner: each failure path, the message format, and the five-line stderr tail. Another test checks that the four files use the fixture.

units.title: The integration job fetches the pinned OpenSpec once, with a bounded retry, from the pin the kit defines
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] .github/scripts/warm-openspec.sh:6 — The script accepts an empty or missing spec. The workflow builds the spec with `$(uv run ... python -c ...)`, and a failing command substitution inside an argument does not trip `bash -e`.
  Consequence: Suppose the Python snippet fails: `PACKAGE` is moved or renamed, an import breaks, or uv fails. The step then runs `warm-openspec.sh ""` and the script calls `npx --yes "" --version`. Either that exits 0 without fetching anything, so the warm-up passes silently and the tests go back to failing one by one (the incident this change exists to prevent), or it fails three times with a message saying an empty spec 'could not be fetched', which hides the real cause. The workflow tests only look for the substrings `PACKAGE` and `settings.openspec_version` in the step, so they don't catch this either.
  Done when: Have the script refuse a missing or empty argument before any npx call, e.g. `spec="${1:?usage: warm-openspec.sh <package>@<version>}"`, which exits non-zero and names the usage. Add a test in tests/test_ci_openspec_step.py that runs the script with `""` as the spec, using the same fake npx. It should assert a non-zero status and that `calls_made()` is empty.
- [1.2] tests/test_ci_openspec_step.py:118 — `test_neither_the_workflow_nor_the_script_spells_the_pin` uses bare `assert PACKAGE not in text`. When it fails, it does not name the offending line, which the spec scenario 'A hand-copied pin is caught … THEN it fails naming the line' requires.
  Consequence: If someone hand-copies `@fission-ai/openspec@1.13.1` into ci.yml, pytest shows `assert '...' not in '<whole file, truncated>'`, with no file or line number. The spec says the failure names the line.
  Done when: Collect the offending lines, e.g. `hits = [f"{name}:{n}: {line}" for name, text in (("ci.yml", ...), ("warm-openspec.sh", ...)) for n, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1) if PACKAGE in line or settings.openspec_version in line]`, then `assert hits == []`, so the failure lists each file:line. Keep the `assert warm_steps("integration")` precondition.

Optional:
- [1.3] tests/test_ci_openspec_step.py:106 — The pin test only checks that the step's `run` text contains `uv run`, `PACKAGE` and `settings.openspec_version`. It never runs the command, so it would pass if the snippet were broken (a typo in the import, a bad quote from YAML folding).
  Consequence: Example: `from agent_build_kit.openspec import PACKAGES; ... settings.openspec_version` passes this test. I ran the folded command by hand and it currently prints `@fission-ai/openspec@1.13.1`, so today's code is correct. Only the test is weak.
  Done when: Optionally, take the `$(...)` substitution from the parsed step, run it with `bash -c` as `echo` in place of the script path, and assert the output equals `f"{PACKAGE}@{settings.openspec_version}"`. Together with the empty-spec guard above, a broken snippet would then fail both locally and in CI.
- [1.4] tests/test_ci_openspec_step.py:39 — `jobs()` is a third hand-rolled loader for ci.yml, after `workflow()` at tests/test_repo_gates.py:37 and the inline load at tests/test_parallel_suite.py:94-95. tests/ci_workflows.py already exports `WORKFLOWS` and is the natural shared home.
  Consequence: Three places parse the same file and have to change together if the workflow moves or is split.
  Done when: Optionally, add a `ci_jobs()` (or similar) to tests/ci_workflows.py and use it here. Repointing the two older callers is not required in this unit.
- [1.5] .github/scripts/warm-openspec.sh:13 — The script relies on GNU `timeout`, so the unit tests that run it fail on a development machine without coreutils `timeout` (stock macOS).
  Consequence: On such a machine every attempt fails with 'timeout: command not found', and the test expecting status 0 fails. CI and Linux are unaffected.
  Done when: Optionally, skip the script-running tests when `shutil.which("timeout")` is None, or note the requirement in the script header.

description.summary: The CI integration job now fetches the pinned OpenSpec CLI once, with a bounded retry, before its tests run, so a failed download shows up as one clear failure instead of many failing tests.
changes: A new step in the integration job, placed after uv is set up and before pytest, runs `.github/scripts/warm-openspec.sh` with a 10-minute limit. The package and version come from the kit's own `PACKAGE` and `settings.openspec_version`, not a copy in the workflow.

The script tries `npx --yes <spec> --version` up to three times. Each try has a 120-second limit, the npx cache is cleared between tries, and the wait between tries grows each time. If all three fail it reports a `::error::` saying the OpenSpec CLI is not installed. It refuses a missing or empty spec with a usage message before calling npx.

New tests in `tests/test_ci_openspec_step.py` use a fake npx. They cover where the step sits and that no other job has it, retry counts on success and failure, cache clearing, the empty-spec refusal, and that the step's own command prints the right spec. They also fail, naming the file and line, when the pin is typed into the workflow or the script by hand.
`tests/ci_workflows.py` gains a shared `ci_jobs()` loader for the jobs in ci.yml.
AGENTS.md notes that CI fetches the pinned OpenSpec CLI once, with a bounded retry, before the integration tests.

units.title: Every action runs on Node 24 at an exact release, the runner is pinned, and a test fails on anything else
units.feedback:
The workflow edit (ci.yml) matches task 1.4 exactly. The four actions are at v7.0.1, v7.1.0, v7.0.0 and v10.3.0, all four jobs run on ubuntu-24.04, and python-version, node-version and enable-cache are unchanged. tests/test_ci_workflows.py passes: 15 tests. Three things block approval. First, the spec's own scenario for actions/checkout@v4 gets the wrong message. Second, a runs-on list with no -latest label is never checked against ubuntu-24.04. Third, no test checks that the step is named, although the spec and task 1.2 both require it. The AGENTS.md 'CI workflows' section the message points at belongs to task group 3, a later unit, so it is not asked of this one.

Required:
- [1.1] tests/ci_workflows.py:36 — A floating reference below the Node 24 major (the spec's own example, `actions/checkout@v4`) gets only the format message. It never says the first major that runs on Node 24.
  Consequence: The spec scenario 'An action below its Node 24 release' gives `actions/checkout@v4` and requires a failure that 'says the first major that runs on Node 24'. Today `check_workflow` returns only 'actions/checkout@v4 is not owner/name@vX.Y.Z or a full commit SHA; see AGENTS.md, CI workflows', with no v5 in it. `test_an_action_below_its_node_24_release_fails_naming_file_job_and_step` avoids the gap by using `@v4.2.0` instead of the spec's `@v4`.
  Done when: In `_check_uses`, when a reference fails EXACT, still read a major from a `@vN` / `@vN.M` form of a listed action. If that major is below the table's entry, the message names both problems, for example '... is not owner/name@vX.Y.Z or a full commit SHA, and is below actions/checkout v5, the first major on Node 24'. Change the below-major test to use `actions/checkout@v4`, as the spec scenario does, and assert that the message contains 'v5'. Keep a second case with `@v4.2.0`.
- [1.2] tests/ci_workflows.py:61 — A `runs-on` list is checked only for `-latest` labels, never against `ubuntu-24.04`, so `[self-hosted, linux]` passes. Matrix values are checked strictly against RUNNER, so the two rules disagree.
  Consequence: The task's Done-when says the test fails on 'a *-latest or unlisted runner'. The spec says every job 'SHALL name its runner by a fixed label, ubuntu-24.04'. Running `check_workflow` on a job with `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]` returns [] (checked by running it). Because of the `scalar` flag, a list escapes the pin that a string or matrix value gets.
  Done when: A list passes only if it contains RUNNER and no label ending in `-latest`, or else it is checked the same way as a scalar. Pick one and drop the `scalar` special case. Add a test that `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]` fails naming the job, beside the existing `[self-hosted, macos-latest]` case.
- [1.3] tests/test_ci_workflows.py:12 — No test asserts that a failure names the step, although task 1.2 and the spec scenario require file, job and step. The test named `..._naming_file_job_and_step` checks only the file and the job.
  Consequence: The step label in `check_workflow` (`step.get('name') or step.get('id') or f'#{number}'`) could be dropped or broken and every test would still pass. The `workflow()` helper's step has no `name:`, and none of the failing-case tests (below-major, missing-from-table, floating/branch/latest/expression) assert the step label.
  Done when: Give the generated step in `workflow()` a `name:` (for example 'Check out'). In the below-major, missing-from-table and floating/expression tests, assert that the message contains 'ci.yml', 'build' and that step name. Also tighten `assert "5" in problems[0]` to `assert "v5" in problems[0]`.

description.summary: Pins every GitHub Actions action in CI to an exact release that runs on Node 24, pins the runner to ubuntu-24.04, and adds a test that fails on any workflow that drifts from either.
changes: The CI workflow uses actions/checkout v7.0.1, actions/setup-node v7.1.0, astral-sh/setup-uv v7.0.0 and actions/setup-python v10.3.0, and every job runs on ubuntu-24.04 instead of a -latest label.

A new checker in tests/ci_workflows.py reads each workflow and reports any action reference that is not an exact vX.Y.Z or full commit SHA. Each report names the file, job and step and points to AGENTS.md.

An action below the first major that runs on Node 24 fails with a message naming that major. A floating reference such as `@v4` gets both reasons in one message, and an action missing from the table fails with a request to add it.
A runner fails when it ends in -latest. A string or matrix value must also be ubuntu-24.04 exactly, and a label list must include ubuntu-24.04.
Local actions (`./...`), `docker://` references and reusable-workflow jobs are skipped, and the shipped workflows are checked by the suite.

units.title: Checkpoint test states hold tuples, a pydantic serializer warning fails the suite, and the CI workflow policy is documented
units.feedback:
With the new filter in place the whole suite passes: `uv run poe test` gave 9051 passed and 1 skipped in the parallel pass, 106 passed in the serial pass, and 0 'Pydantic serializer' lines. The 42 tests the branch changes or adds pass on their own as well. Task 2.4 asks for two results to be recorded in the commit: whether any other test raised the warning, and whether a production path puts a list in a tuple field (design.md marks that UNVERIFIED). Neither commit message records either one. Put both in the next commit message or in the reply to the pipeline, so the design's UNVERIFIED note can be corrected in the planning repo.

Required:
- [1.1] tests/test_pydantic_warning_filter.py:1 — Task 2.3 says to extend `tests/test_warning_filters.py` with these tests. The branch instead adds a separate file, which repeats that file's `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` (tests/test_warning_filters.py:9) and its pytester-child-run pattern (`run_with_the_guard`, tests/test_warning_filters.py:54).
  Consequence: The suite's warning policy is now pinned in two files that a reader has to keep in step, against the task's explicit instruction. Because the repo has two copies of `ROOT` and two near-identical child-pytest runners, a change to how the child pytest is run (for example `-p no:cacheprovider`) has to be made twice.
  Done when: Move the four tests and the `SERIALIZES` / `OTHER_USER_WARNING` sources into `tests/test_warning_filters.py` and delete `tests/test_pydantic_warning_filter.py`. Reuse the existing `ROOT`, and widen the module docstring to cover both guards: the fork plugin and the scoped pydantic `filterwarnings` entry. Keep the assertions as they are: the entry starts with `error`, matches the message and `UserWarning`; a list in a tuple field fails; a tuple passes; any other UserWarning gives `passed=1, warnings=1`.

Optional:
- [1.2] tests/graph/test_checkpoint_state_quiet.py:35 — The test filters `updates` down to `UnitRun.model_fields` before calling `state_from_updates`. The helper already does that filtering (tests/checkpoint_types.py:80).
  Consequence: The redundant filter suggests the helper needs pre-filtered input, so the next caller may copy it. Its sibling call at tests/graph/test_held_state_plain_text.py:57 passes the updates unfiltered.

description.summary: The suite now fails on a pydantic serializer warning instead of passing it by quietly. The checkpoint tests' states hold tuples where the model expects them, and the CI workflow policy is written down.
changes: pyproject.toml has a scoped `filterwarnings` entry that turns pydantic's 'Pydantic serializer warnings' UserWarning into a test error. Every other UserWarning is still only reported.

tests/test_warning_filters.py now covers both warning guards: the fork plugin and the serializer entry. The serializer tests read the entry from pyproject.toml and run it in a child pytest. They show that a list in a tuple field fails, a tuple passes, and an unrelated UserWarning gives one pass and one warning.
The checkpoint-state tests build their states with tuples, as the model expects, so serialising a held unit's state gives no warning. A test asserts this.

AGENTS.md documents the CI workflow policy that tests/test_ci_workflows.py enforces: actions pinned at an exact Node 24 release or a full SHA, the runner pinned to ubuntu-24.04, and how to bump either.

units.title: A moved-base run is named, and a unit owed one is found
units.feedback:
One required point. The rest of the unit matches group 1: the new cause and stored flag exist, `owed_a_moved_base_run`, `moved_base_units` and `clear_answered_feedback` follow the spec's rule, `READMITTED_CAUSES` is widened with a comment, and the tests cover each scenario in 1.1–1.3. The sentence in docs/architecture.md:583 that lists the readmitted causes is now incomplete, but updating the docs is task group 8, so it does not block this unit.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_store.py:543 — `UnitStore.upsert` rebuilds each stored unit field by field and does not carry `moved_base_run` over, so a re-plan resets the flag to False.
  Consequence: Task 1.4 says the flag is "kept by the store's writes". `upsert` is one of those writes, and the planner calls it on every tick. Take a unit that is `running` with `moved_base_run=True` (the lane is making its run). If its change is re-planned, `upsert` writes it back with the flag False and the state still `running`. Group 2 tells lane-owned runs apart from build-worker runs by this flag: flagged units are kept out of `resumable_units` and resumed by the lane's scan. After a re-plan, an interrupted lane run would be resumed by a build worker and take a build slot. The new test `test_the_flag_is_kept_by_the_stores_other_writes` only checks `set_feedback` and `record_step`, so it misses this.
  Done when: In `upsert`, keep the flag the way the other work-in-progress fields are kept: `moved_base_run=existing.moved_base_run if existing else False`. Add a test to tests/pipeline/test_moved_base_run_stored.py that takes the `flagged` store (unit `running`, flag set), calls `store.upsert([new_unit(UNIT)])`, and asserts `UnitStore(store.path).get(UNIT).moved_base_run is True` and that the state is still `running`.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/restack_lane.py:145 — `has_commits` counts `base..branch` with its own `rev-list --count`, but `wiring.branch_commits` (src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:864) already answers "how many commits the branch carries beyond its base".
  Consequence: There are now two ways to count a branch's commits beyond its base, and they differ: the existing one counts from `HEAD` and raises on a git failure, the new one names the branch and returns False. A change to how the base is resolved (for example after a squash merge of a parent) has to be made in both places.
  Done when: Give `branch_commits` an optional head ref (defaulting to `HEAD`) and call it from `has_commits`, catching its error at this call site so the scan still treats an unresolvable ref as no commits. Or say in a comment why the scan needs its own count.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/restack_lane.py:134 — Inside `moved_base_units`, `usable` repeats the `is_dir` check that `head_of` already makes. `head_of` also runs the same `rev-parse --verify --quiet <branch>` that `owed_units.holds_base` runs (line 182). Each judged unit gets `rev-parse` twice: once through `usable`, once through `head=`.
  Consequence: Each candidate unit costs one extra git call per scan, and the branch-resolution rule exists in two places in the same module.
  Done when: Pull out one module-level `_branch_head(checkouts, unit) -> str` used by both scans, and have `has_commits` reuse the head it already resolved instead of calling `usable` first.
- [1.4] tests/pipeline/test_moved_base_run_feedback.py:267 — `test_feedback_over_an_approved_head_is_answered_and_is_not_rework_input` makes exactly the first assertion of the test above it, so it adds nothing.
  Consequence: A reader may think the 'answered' case is covered by its own test when it is only repeated.
  Done when: Drop the duplicate test, or have it check something the other does not, such as the case where the approved head differs from the current head after a move.

description.summary: Adds a moved-base cause and a stored `moved_base_run` flag, and a rule plus a scan that find which units are owed a moved-base run.
changes: Units gain a new readmitted cause for a moved-base run. The store keeps a `moved_base_run` flag through its writes, including the re-plan `upsert`.

`owed_a_moved_base_run` decides from recorded facts whether a unit is owed a moved-base run: whether the branch has commits, whether its base has moved, and whether saved feedback is answered by an approval of the current head.
`moved_base_units` (in restack_lane.py) checks the repositories' branches once per unit and returns the ids of the units owed a run.
`clear_answered_feedback` clears feedback that review has already answered when the run starts, so the old feedback is not given to the rework as input.
`wiring.branch_commits` takes an optional `head`, so it can count the commits on a branch that is not checked out.

units.title: The lane runs the unit's whole moved-base run in one worker and resumes interrupted ones
units.guidance:
Two things to do on this unit.
1. Fix the one required review finding [2.1]: the new test for the unclaimed-run fix does not reach the changed code. The reviewer swapped the older restack_lane.py back in and test_a_run_the_usage_window_refused_is_not_made_again_by_the_next_scan still passed. Rewrite or add a test that FAILS against the old code and passes with your fix (prove it by running it against the old restack_lane.py), and keep point 2.2 as it is.
2. The pull request now conflicts with main. Rebase onto the current main and resolve the conflicts. Since this branch was built, these merged: #427 (rename of cli/, config.py and forges/), #428 (ready units start by priority; handoff; priority 0), #430 (a tick that builds nothing says why, per unit) and #431 (a failed unit requeues itself when its wait ends). Expect conflicts in src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py and CHANGELOG.md. Keep both sides' behaviour; do not drop their changes. Re-run the unit's tests and the full tier 1 suite after the rebase.
The unit landed at about 900 lines against an estimate of 340; do not add scope.

description.summary: A unit whose only reason to run is that its base moved now runs its whole moved-base run inside the restack lane's worker, and the lane resumes such runs when they are interrupted.
changes: After the lane moves a unit and the move leaves a restack conflict or deferral, the same lane worker goes straight on into the unit's run (`build_unit` with `moved_base_run=True`). The unit holds one lane worker and no build worker.

The unit is flagged as being in a lane run only once its run holds the branch. A run the process lost, or one a usage pause interrupted, is therefore found by the lane's scan (`in_a_lane_run`) and resumed there, never offered to a build worker.

A lane run that went ahead is noted like a move, whatever its outcome (rate-limited, paused, interrupted, ended). A later scan leaves it alone until its head or base changes or a pause that stood has ended, so a usage-window refusal no longer makes the pass spin.
A run skipped because a tab holds the unit's lease, or because another run holds its branch, raises BranchBusy and stays un-noted. The lane runs it as soon as the branch is free.
Tests cover the lane run, resuming it, the held-branch retry, the wait for a usage pause, and the tick sending moved-base runs to the lane and only builds to the pool.

history.note: rounds spent with work outstanding: Point 2.2 is done. The tick test now goes through cmd_tick with a counting ThreadPoolExecutor and checks three things: the pool was made, only first/1 was submitted, and MOVED ran on a 'restack' thread. The code fix for 2.1 is also right: `_go_on` notes an unclaimed run whatever its outcome and skip

requeue: rework — Two things to do on this unit.
1. Fix the one required review finding [2.1]: the new test for the unclaimed-run fix does not reach the changed code. The reviewer swapped the older restack_lane.py back

units.title: A lane run stops before non-moved-base work and hands the unit back

description.summary: A moved-base run in the restack lane now stops before any step that is not moved-base work and hands the unit back to a build worker, which carries on from that step without moving the branch again.
changes: When the lane's run of a unit reaches a step that is not moved-base work, such as a rework after the conflict was resolved, it stops and records the unit as `planned` with cause `restack_handed_back`. The unit keeps its thread at that step.
Each tick readmits a handed-back unit as ready, and a regular build worker resumes it at the stored step instead of rebuilding from tests and implementation. The lane does not touch it.
A worker resuming a handed-back unit marks it `running` before the thread resumes, as for parked units. `abk status`, the graph page and later passes then see it as being built, not as planned.
`RunOutcome.handed_back` carries the hand-back note, and callers check it before `status`, which means nothing for a run that was handed back.
New graph and CLI tests cover the hand-back at each step, the readmission, and the worker's resume. They check that the branch head is unchanged and that no lane thread ran the rework.

units.title: Moved-base attempts are counted at the base tip and spent attempts end in a hold
units.feedback:
All four round-1 points are fixed. Attempts are now forgotten only when no agent streamed anything, and the resume of a forgotten start counts as attempt 1 through the new `moved_base_uncounted` flag. `_last_ended` skips the entries the run did not write (`running`, `base_changed`). `read_base_tip` is now the single reading of a unit's base tip. `hold_for_conflict` is the one hold, shared by the handler and the lane, and both log it. One new problem came in with this rework: `owed_units` now also returns everything `moved_base_units` returns. That change is not in the earlier rounds' diff, so it could not have been raised before. I could not run the suite here because the command needed approval; the finding below comes from reading the code.

Required:
- [2.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/restack_lane.py:285 — `owed_units` now returns `... | moved_base_units(inst, units)`. `moved_base_units` takes `Cause.RESTACK_HANDED_BACK` as owed (MOVED_BASE_CAUSES, line 67), so a unit the lane handed back with no rework input of its own is owed to the lane again, and the build pass skips it.
  Consequence: Take a lane run that stops before `e2e`/tier 2, `tests` or `implement`. It leaves the unit `planned`/`restack_handed_back` with no feedback, so `_rework_input` is false. The unit has commits, so `owed_a_moved_base_run` is true and the unit is in `owed_units`. `_evaluate_round` (cli/pipeline.py:2077) puts every PLANNED unit in `owed` into `for_the_lane` and starts none of them (line 2105), so no build worker takes the handed-back unit. The lane's scan hands it over as a run instead. `_build_unit` records an attempt and runs the thread, which stops before the same step and hands the unit back again. After `max_review_rounds` of this, `hold_if_spent` holds it with 'restack held: 3 attempts … did not settle it'. That breaks group 3's settled requirement that a handed-back unit is not continued by the lane and is taken by a build worker from its step. It also turns a unit with no conflict into a spurious hold for a person. `tests/cli/test_lane_hand_back_readmit.py` misses this because it only covers a hand-back at `rework`, where the review feedback is rework input and keeps the unit out of `moved_base_units`.
  Done when: Keep handed-back units out of the set `owed_units` hands to the lane and that the build pass leaves for it. For example, leave out units whose cause is `Cause.RESTACK_HANDED_BACK` when you add `moved_base_units` to `owed_units`. Or add only what this unit needs for the lane to find a unit its run left `planned`/`restack_conflict`. Either way, a handed-back unit becomes owed again only when its base moves again and the cause is rewritten to `base_changed`, which is what test_lane_hand_back_resume pins. Add a test in tests/cli/test_lane_hand_back_readmit.py with the e2e scene (`Scene(graph, tmp_path, tier="e2e-test")`, `scene.told_its_base_moved()`, `scene.lane_moves()`, `handed_back_at(scene, Node.E2E)`). It asserts that OTHER is not in `cli.owed_units(...)` and that `cli.run_round(...)` returns `[OTHER]`. Keep `test_the_note_names_the_conflict_the_last_run_left_when_nothing_else_was_written` passing, because it needs a `restack_conflict` unit to be found again with no `owe()` in between.

Optional:
- [2.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:4233 — When the base tip cannot be read, the lane run now ends 'skipped, its base cannot be read' and leaves the unit owed, so every later scan takes it, locks the branch and skips it again, logging a line each time.
  Consequence: If a parent branch or trunk ref stays missing, the run journal fills with the same skip line on every scan and nothing tells a person. Before this rework the run went ahead and was simply never counted.
  Done when: Optional. Either leave such a unit out of the lane's owed set while its tip is unreadable, or log the skip once per tip instead of on every scan.

description.summary: Moved-base runs in the restack lane now count as attempts at the base branch's current tip, and a unit whose attempts at that tip run out is held for a person instead of being retried forever.
changes: When the lane starts a moved-base run, it records one attempt at the base's current tip, in the same counter the conflict handler uses. When the base moves to a new tip, the count starts again from zero.
If a run stops before any agent produced output, its attempt is forgotten and the resume counts as the attempt instead. A unit is never charged for a run that did nothing.

Once `max_review_rounds` attempts at one tip have not settled a unit, it is held with a note naming the base, the tip and how the last run ended. The lane and the conflict handler share one hold for this, and both log it.

A unit the lane handed back to a build worker, and one whose base tip cannot be read, are no longer in the lane's owed set. The build pass picks a handed-back unit up from its step, and the lane takes it again only when its base moves again.
A unit's base tip is read in one place, shared by the conflict handler and the lane.

units.title: Every agent call of a lane run asks the usage guard and a refusal defers the run
units.feedback:
The code for 5.4 and 5.5 does what the tasks ask. The resolver in `graph/nodes.py` now asks `may_start` under `starting(unit.id)` and raises `AgentRateLimited` with the guard's `resume_at`. When the thread's own move is refused, `move_unit` records `restack_deferred` and calls `defer_until`. A run that a usage pause stops tells the lane through `on_pause`. Two things block approval. First, three things tasks 5.1–5.3 ask to be tested are not tested. Second, the guard check is now written out a second time instead of being shared with `gated_resolver`.

Required:
- [1.1] tests/graph/test_lane_run_usage.py:25 — Task 5.1 has three gaps. No test runs a thread parked at `prepare`, under a pause, through a move that applies cleanly. No test checks that a conflict rework in the lane is asked of the guard. The refusal test does not check that the thread is left where it was.
  Consequence: Task 5.1 says that under a pause a move that applies cleanly goes ahead in the lane and the guard is not asked. Only the stack-move path (a unit with no thread) is tested for this, in `tests/pipeline/test_restack_lane_usage.py:64`. The thread path is a different one: `advance_thread_through_prepare` followed by `run_of` and `build_unit`. If a gate at the node boundary, or the new check in `resolve`, refused a clean move under a pause, every test would still pass. Likewise, `test_under_a_pause_a_conflict_in_the_move_is_not_resolved_and_defers_the_run` checks only the cause and the attempt count. A refusal that moved the thread off `prepare`, or left the unit in a state the scan never picks up, would pass it. The spec says the refusal leaves the unit and its thread where they are. Nothing tests that this deferred thread-path move is moved again once the guard allows.
  Done when: Add three tests to `tests/graph/test_lane_run_usage.py`. (1) With the lane shut and a move that applies cleanly (no `Failing`), `lane_moves()` leaves the branch on the new base, makes `lane.decisions == []`, and the unit ends in review. (2) In the existing refusal test, also assert that `lane.graph.next(OTHER) == (Node.PREPARE,)` and that the stored state is `RUNNING`. Then open the lane, move a `Moving` clock past the `resume_at` that was refused, scan again, and assert the resolver is asked again and the run goes on. (3) Run a conflict rework (feedback whose source is the conflict) in the lane and assert it is asked of the guard and attributed to the unit, as the port and the review are.
- [1.2] tests/cli/test_lane_run_usage_pause.py:93 — `test_a_runtimes_own_refusal_at_the_port_does_the_same` checks only where the unit stops. It does not check the timing that 'does the same' covers in task 5.2: no retry before the time the runtime gave, and a resume at the port once the pause ends.
  Consequence: `_build_unit`'s `except RateLimited` branch (cli/pipeline.py:4321) never calls `on_pause`, so `defer_until` is never called for a runtime's own refusal. Whether the lane holds the run back then depends only on the stamp of the last try and the pause marker. No test pins that. A change that made the lane retry at once, or never resume after a runtime refusal, would pass.
  Done when: Extend the test along the lines of `test_the_lane_waits_for_the_guards_resume_at_and_then_resumes_at_the_port_asking_again`. Raise the runtime's refusal with a `resets_at`. Assert that a scan before that time makes no new agent request. Assert that a scan after the pause ends, or after that time, resumes the run at the port (`ADAPT`) and asks the guard again. If the test fails, call `on_pause(when)` from the `RateLimited` branch so that both kinds of refusal defer the run alike.
- [1.3] tests/pipeline/test_lane_run_ledger.py:41 — Task 5.3's 'a clean move writes none' is not tested.
  Consequence: Task 5.3 lists three things: the resolver and port rows, the review rows, and no rows for a clean move. Only the first two are tested. A clean move that started writing `restack` rows, or that called an agent at all, would pass.
  Done when: Add a test to `tests/pipeline/test_lane_run_ledger.py`: a clean move in the lane (the scene without `Failing`) leaves no row with node `restack` or `adapt` in the ledger.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1130 — The new check in `resolve` repeats `gated_resolver` in `cli/pipeline.py:3600-3606`. Both enter `starting(unit_id)`, call `may_start()`, and on a refusal raise `AgentRateLimited(reason, resets_at=resume_at())`.
  Consequence: There are now two copies of the rule 'ask the guard before a resolver call, and raise the model's rate limit with the guard's time'. Task 5.4 states its aim as 'so a thread's own move and the lane's stack move ask alike'. That only holds while the two copies are kept in step, for example if the reason text, the attribution or the time source changes in one of them.
  Done when: Extract one function both call, for example in `pipeline/usage_guard.py` or beside `starting`. It takes `unit_id`, `may_start` and `resume_at`, asks under `starting(unit_id)`, and raises `AgentRateLimited(reason, resets_at=resume_at())` on a refusal. `Gated.__call__` catches the error only to tell `refused`, then re-raises it. `BuildPath.resolve` calls the function with `self.runner.may_start` and `self.runner.resume_at`.

Optional:
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/restack_lane.py:411 — The docstring of `defer_until` still says 'The usage guard refused the unit's resolver'. It is now also called when a usage pause stops a lane run (`on_pause` in `build_restack_lane`).
  Consequence: The next reader will think only a refused resolver defers a unit. A run paused at the port or at review is deferred by the same call.
  Done when: Reword it: 'The usage guard refused an agent call of the unit's move or run and expects to allow it from `resume_at` ...'.

description.summary: Every agent call of a run in the restack lane, the conflict resolver of a thread's own move included, asks the usage guard first. A refusal, from the guard or from the runtime, defers the unit in the lane until the time it was given, and the run resumes where it stood.
changes: A thread's own conflict resolver in the lane asks the usage guard before each call, as the lane's stack move already did. Both go through one shared `ask_before_call` in `pipeline/usage_guard.py`, and a refusal is raised as the model's rate limit carrying the guard's resume time.

When the guard refuses a lane run before its first agent call, the unit stays RUNNING with cause RESTACK_DEFERRED at the same thread node. No conflict attempt is counted, and the lane tries again only once the guard's resume time has passed.
When the runtime itself rate-limits a lane run, the lane also defers the unit until the runtime's reset time and then resumes the run at the port. The lane never retries before that time.
Under a pause, a move that applies cleanly is still made in the lane without asking the guard. Only the agent calls that follow, such as the review, are put to the guard.
Lane runs write the usual ledger rows for the resolver, the port and the review, and a clean move writes no restack or adapt rows. The changelog bullet describes the guard-first behaviour.

units.title: A conflict rework starts with the move and the handlers hand the unit to the lane

description.summary: When a unit is sent back for its pull request's conflict, its rework now starts by moving the branch onto the new base in the restack lane, and the conflict and rework handlers hand the unit to that lane instead of a build worker.
changes: When a conflict or rework event arrives for a unit sent back for its conflict, the unit goes to the restack lane, which moves its branch onto the moved base. This covers a unit whose review thread is parked as well as one without a thread.
When the move ends without a conflict, `prepare` clears the conflict's saved feedback, so the conflict the move settled does not start a billed rework agent.
A lane run keeps the cause it was planned with, so `prepare` can tell that a run is a conflict rework even when the unit had no thread.

One predicate, `StoredUnit.sent_back_for_conflict`, decides whether a unit was sent back for its conflict. The lane's scan, the lane's run start, `_build_unit` and `prepare` all use it, so they cannot disagree.
An event for a unit a person holds is left for the next poll and taken once the hold lifts.

units.title: A lane run counts toward slot occupancy and the whole run shows as restacking
units.feedback:
Round 1's four points are done, and the five touched test files pass (24 tests). I could not delete my scratch files: /tmp/r2scratch/test_scratch_lanewait.py and /tmp/r2_lane7.diff are still there.

Required:
- [2.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:1649 — The rework passes `lane_waiting` into `_evaluate_round`'s `idle`. That marks every unit waiting behind the lane's cap as `HELD` in the evaluated view, including a unit stored `planned` that is owed a restack. Such a unit then drops out of `for_the_lane`, and so out of `startable`, and `_planned_wait` gives it `slot` or `queue_full`. This is the misreading finding 1.3 fixed for units the lane is running, now brought back for units waiting in the lane.
  Consequence: Take `max_concurrent_restacks` 1. One run is in the lane. A unit stored `planned` with `cause=base_changed` and a branch is handed over and sits in `lane.waiting`. In `_evaluate_round` (line 2093) it becomes `HELD` because it is in `idle`, so it is not in `for_the_lane` (line 2111). `run_round`'s `startable` is `evaluated | for_the_lane | lane_running`, and the unit is in none of them. `_waits_in` reads its stored state, `PLANNED`, so `_planned_wait` (line 5526-5531) records `WaitReason.SLOT`, or `QUEUE_FULL` when the queue has no room. Before this round the unit stayed `PLANNED` in the view, sat in `for_the_lane` and read `ready`. The decision log now says a unit waiting for the restack lane waits for a build slot, which contradicts the rule that a restack takes no build slot. I traced this through the code but could not run a probe test (the sandbox refused the command).
  Done when: Mark as idle only the lane-waiting units stored `running`, which are the ones that need it for the worker count: `idle=(idle - resumed) | {unit.id for unit in units if unit.id in lane_waiting and unit.state == RUNNING}`. Alternatively, add `lane_waiting` to `startable` in the `_waits_in` call next to `lane_running`. Either way, a planned unit waiting in the lane must read as it did while owed. Add a test beside `test_a_planned_unit_the_lane_is_moving_reads_as_ready_not_as_waiting_for_a_slot` using `Slots(..., restacks=1, flagged=["run1/1"])`. Run `run1/1` in the lane. Set `moved/1` to `PLANNED` with `branch="spec/moved/1"` and `cause=Cause.BASE_CHANGED`, call `hand_over("moved/1")` and assert `lanes.waiting == ["moved/1"]`. After `slots.started()`, assert `slots.reasons()["moved/1"]` is neither `slot` nor `queue_full`. Keep `test_a_waiting_lane_unit_whose_branch_is_held_still_takes_no_slot_from_a_ready_unit` passing.

description.summary: Moved-base restack runs in the restack lane now count toward slot occupancy, and the whole run shows as restacking, without counting units that wait behind the lane's cap or units no run holds.
changes: A unit the restack lane is running counts as occupying a slot in the round's occupancy, in the sample row and in the gauges. A unit waiting behind the lane's cap does not, and nor does a unit stored running that no run holds.
The decision log no longer says a unit the lane is running or holding waits for a build slot (`slot`) or a full queue (`queue_full`). Such a unit reads as it did while it was owed a restack.
Only lane-waiting units stored running are treated as idle when the round counts workers. A unit stored planned and owed a restack stays planned and startable for the lane.
Occupancy is counted per project, so a project whose slots are full starts nothing while another project with room still starts work.
New tests under tests/cli/ cover lane occupancy, the sample row and gauges, and the wait reasons of planned units that are moving in the lane or waiting in it.

units.title: Make test_stopping_still_awaits_the_builds_in_flight deterministic
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] tests/cli/test_tick_stop_ordering.py:23 — The new test module never warms the unit-graph database (`warm_unit_graphs`), even though it runs several builds at the same time. Every other module that installs the scripted `Builder` warms it, including `tests/cli/test_tick_scheduling.py:78` (`warmed`) and `tests/cli/test_tick_readmission_ordering.py`.
  Consequence: `warm_unit_graphs` (tests/tick_pass.py:30) exists because builds that open the unit-graph database together race to switch its journal mode to WAL and fail with `database is locked`. This test starts `quick/1`, `slow/1` and `stops/1` at once with `max_concurrent=3`, then starts `later/1`, against a cold database. It passes alone, but under parallel workers and load it can fail in exactly the way this unit is meant to remove. The unit is about removing a flake, and it adds a new flaky test.
  Done when: Add an autouse fixture to `tests/cli/test_tick_stop_ordering.py` that calls `warm_unit_graphs(tmp_path)`, imported from `tests.tick_pass`. Copy the `warmed` fixture at `tests/cli/test_tick_scheduling.py:77-79` exactly, so this module sets things up the same way as every other Builder-driven tick test.

Optional:
- [1.2] tests/cli/test_tick_stop_ordering.py:1 — The module docstring describes the case by naming another test (`test_stopping_still_awaits_the_builds_in_flight`) and calls itself what that test 'must rule out'. It should state the behaviour it pins.
  Consequence: If the other test is renamed or moved, this docstring points at nothing. A reader has to open a second file to learn what this one checks.
  Done when: Rewrite the docstring as the behaviour itself, for example: 'Once a build has started it runs to completion, even when another build records the model's refusal after it started; a freed slot is refilled at once, so the unit started into it is not undone.' Do not name the other test.

description.summary: Makes the tick test that stops on a model refusal deterministic, and moves the ordering it used to allow into its own event-driven test.
changes: test_stopping_still_awaits_the_builds_in_flight now plans only stops/1, slow/1 and later/1 with two slots. No slot frees before the refusal is written, so the test always asserts that later/1 never starts and stays planned, while slow/1 still finishes and reaches review.

A new module, tests/cli/test_tick_stop_ordering.py, covers the other ordering: a slot frees and is refilled before another build records a refusal. The unit started into that slot still runs to completion and reaches review.
The new test sequences its builds with wait_for on events (later/1 starting, then the pause file appearing) rather than on timing.
The new module warms the unit-graph database before each test, like the other tick tests that use the scripted Builder, so builds starting at the same time do not race to switch its journal mode.

units.title: The integration-test tag is accepted, and a unit takes the widest kind of its groups

description.summary: Accepts the `integration-test` tag on a task group and gives each unit the widest test kind of all the groups it carries, its own and those joined onto it.
changes: A task group may be tagged `integration-test`, and planning and tag checks accept it beside the existing kinds.

A unit's kind is the widest kind of every group it builds. When work is joined onto a unit, through `Unit.taking`, which both the join check and the unit store use, the unit widens to cover what it took.

When a change is re-planned, a started unit's stored kind is compared with the widest kind across all the groups it carries, joined groups of other changes included. A difference names the group that sets the kind and its change.
If a group the unit carries can't be found (its change archived, or the group removed), the stored kind is not compared, so a unit is not reported for a tag nobody changed.
Tests in tests/cli/test_tag_drift_widest_kind.py cover agreement, retagging the wider group, joined groups across changes, and a missing group.

units.title: Calibration pools integration-test with unit-test, and the kind-listing tests name the third
Documents, skills and changelog describe what the lane runs and hands back
units.feedback:
The docs test, the leak check and the docs and skills suites pass (143 passed). The branch is held back by gaps against group 8's done-when: the conflict event's route in unit-graph.md, the readmission and hold text in the abk-pipeline skill, and the changelog bullet. There is also one sentence in unit-graph.md that is false, and the list of where a lane run stops is incomplete in five places. All of these are wording fixes in docs, the skill and the changelog.

Required:
- [1.1] docs/unit-graph.md:399 — The events table still sends every merge-conflict event `await_review` → `rework`. Group 6 changed this: for a unit owed a moved-base run, a conflict-kind rework now goes to `prepare`, the move runs first, and the rework agent is called only for what the move and port leave. Task 8.2 asks unit-graph.md to say the conflict event starts at `prepare`, and that was not done. The same gap is in the paragraph below the table (line 410): `rework` for a rework, `prepare` for a moved base or a requeue.
  Consequence: Readers are told that a conflicting pull request always runs the rework agent. `route_after_await_review`/`on_event` in graph/nodes.py and tests/graph/test_conflict_rework_starts_at_move.py show it starts at `prepare`, and that a clean move or a resolved move calls no rework agent.
  Done when: Line 399's row, or a separate row for a merge conflict, says that a conflict for a unit owed a moved-base run is routed to `prepare` with the conflict's feedback kept, and that the rework runs only for what the move and the port leave. A conflict for a unit with rework input of its own stays `→ rework`. The paragraph at line 410 names `prepare` for a conflict of a moved-base unit.
- [1.2] docs/unit-graph.md:414 — The new sentence says a thread the lane runs from `prepare` 'is left planned (`restack_handed_back`) at the node it stopped before for a worker'. That presents a hand-back as the only way a lane run ends.
  Consequence: The sentence is false for most runs. A run that needs no rework, fix or e2e ends waiting in review having pushed (task 3.1). Others end held, satisfied, or `running` and flagged after a usage interrupt. Only a stop before a step outside the run is handed back (`_run_in_lane` in graph/unit.py returns an empty note when the run reaches a wait or the end).
  Done when: Reword it to: the lane runs the thread to its next wait or end; only when the thread reaches a step outside a moved-base run is the unit left `planned` with `restack_handed_back` at that step, for a build worker.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/skills/abk-pipeline/SKILL.md:100 — The `planned` row still says a pass lets a unit back in only when it was sent back for rework, its base changed, or it was parked for host/network/service unavailable, and that 'any other cause waits for the next pass'. Task 1.6 added `Cause.RESTACK_HANDED_BACK` to `READMITTED_CAUSES` (cli/pipeline.py:2566). Task 8.3 also asks for the held unit's note, and the skill only says 'then the unit is held for a person'. It does not say the hold is a review-loop hold (`held_by` review, `needs_human`), what its note names, or that the exit is the review-loop exit (requeue).
  Consequence: An agent following the skill expects a handed-back unit to wait for the next pass, but the running pass starts it within the same pass (tests/cli/test_lane_hand_back_readmit.py). It also cannot connect a moved-base attempts hold to its exit in 'Holds and their exits'.
  Done when: Line 100 names `restack_handed_back` among the causes a pass readmits: a unit the lane handed back is started by a build worker in the same pass. The Restacks section (or the review-loop row at line 290) says that a unit whose attempts at one tip are spent is held by the review loop with `needs_human`, with a note naming the base, the tip, the count of attempts and how the last run ended, and that its exit is the review-loop exit (decide, then `abk requeue`), after which it is owed a run again with the count kept for that tip.
- [1.4] CHANGELOG.md:68 — Task 8.4 (fold this group's points into the restacks bullet) left CHANGELOG.md untouched on this branch. The existing bullet does not give the cause a handed-back unit carries (`restack_handed_back`). It does not say that `project_limits.max_concurrent_restacks` now bounds whole moved-base runs rather than only moves, or that these limits are counted for each project. Group 8's done-when lists all three for the changelog.
  Consequence: A user reading the changelog keeps thinking `max_concurrent_restacks` caps short moves only. With this release it caps full runs, review included, which changes how they should size it. They also cannot match the new `restack_handed_back` cause they see in `abk status` to an entry.
  Done when: Extend the bullet at lines 68-88, without adding a new bullet. Say that `max_concurrent_restacks` now bounds the whole moved-base run in each project's lane, that a handed-back unit is `planned` with the cause `restack_handed_back`, and that slot occupancy and the limits are counted for each project.
- [1.5] docs/architecture.md:283 — The list of steps a lane run stops before is incomplete. The docs name a rework that answers a reviewer, a fix of failing checks and the end-to-end tests. The code (`OUTSIDE_A_MOVED_BASE_RUN` in graph/unit.py:315) also stops before `tests` and `implement`, and before a rework of any feedback that is not the conflict's (a failing CI check, a comment, `agent-rework`), not only a reviewer's. The same three-item list appears at docs/unit-graph.md:147 and :256, docs/configuration.md:534 and CHANGELOG.md:72.
  Consequence: A unit with only its tests commit whose base moves is handed back before `implement`, with the note 'it is new work, not a moved base'. A unit with saved CI feedback is handed back before `rework`. The docs say neither happens, so an operator reading a hand-back note for `implement` or for CI feedback finds nothing that explains it.
  Done when: In each of the five places, name the steps as the code does: a rework of feedback other than the conflict's, a fix of failing checks, the end-to-end tests, and the tests or implementation steps of unfinished work. A short form such as 'any work that is not about the move (a rework of other feedback, a fix of checks, the end-to-end tests, tests or implementation)' is fine.

Optional:
- [1.6] tests/test_docs_moved_base_lane.py:65 — The pattern `work after a move runs in a build worker` matches no text that existed before this change, so it guards nothing. The old unit-graph wording it was meant to catch was 'drives the thread through prepare only, then leaves it positioned at the next node for a worker' and 'outside the build slots'.
  Consequence: If the old account came back in unit-graph.md, this test would not catch it.
  Done when: Replace the dead pattern with ones that match the removed text, for example `through prepare only` and `outside the build slots`.
- [1.7] docs/cli.md:125 — The docs say limits are counted for each project, but `_slots_line` prints one total across projects (`taken` summed over projects, `cap` = `max_concurrent_stacks` × unfinished projects). cli.md does not say the slots line is a total.
  Consequence: With two projects, `slots: 5/8` reads as one pool of 8, although each project is gated at 4.
  Done when: Say that the slots line totals every project, like the restacks line does, and that the cap shown is the per-project cap times the projects with unfinished work.
- [1.8] docs/architecture.md:868 — The stack-move paragraph still says a conflict left by the stack-move handler is `planned` with `restack_conflict` and 'the unit's next run' starts the resolver order, and that anything else 'goes back to planned to be reviewed'. It does not say that the lane's same worker goes straight on into that run and review (group 2).
  Consequence: A reader may think a conflicted move waits for a build worker.
  Done when: Add that the lane's worker continues into the run, which starts the order from its first step.

description.summary: Documents, the abk-pipeline skill and the changelog now describe the restack lane running a unit's whole moved-base run, and handing work outside it back to a build worker.

units.title: The documents say how the kit's tests are tagged and split and how a split is held
A group declares its tier 2 split with a Split line, and a unit carries one

description.summary: A task group can declare its e2e-test (tier 2) split with a `Split:` line. Each planned unit carries exactly one split, and the planner is told about splits and enforces them.
changes: A task group's `Split:` line names the e2e-test split it belongs to; a group without one is in `rest`. A line naming an undeclared split is refused, and the group stays in `rest`.
The planner refuses a unit or a join that mixes groups from different splits. Every stored unit records its split.
The planning prompt states the one-split rule and adds 'the same e2e-test split' to the join constraints. It marks each group heading outside `rest` with `(split <name>)`.
