units.title: A planned unit whose tier 2 split is held is not started and waits on the split reason
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:5588 — The wait detail reads "waiting for e2e-test split <name>", but the spec and the changelog both say "waiting for tier 2 split <name>".
  Consequence: split-start-gate spec, Requirement 'A unit not started because of a hold waits on a reason of its own' and Scenario 'The reason', fixes the text as "waiting for tier 2 split acp". Task 2's done-when says the same, and so do the later task 3.1 (status line) and task 4.1 (the skill-text test asserts `waiting for tier 2 split`). The CHANGELOG bullet added here also says "waiting for tier 2 split <name>", which the code does not do. AGENTS.md says a name a change's spec fixes stays as the spec says, so the test-kind naming rule does not override it here.
  Done when: Change the detail to f"waiting for tier 2 split {unit.split}: {hold_text(gate)}". In tests/cli/test_wait_reasons_split.py, assert "waiting for tier 2 split acp" in wait.detail. The changelog then matches without an edit.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wait_log.py:35 — Adding `detail` to `Wait` changes its equality. WaitRecorder.record treats any change in the whole Wait as a new wait, but `_resume` rebuilds waits without `detail`.
  Consequence: The recorder's contract (docstring, line 40) is to append only when a unit's reason or what it waits on changes. A new process (every `abk tick` run) resumes the log, giving `Wait(reason=SPLIT, waits_on=())` with detail "". The round then produces the same reason with a non-empty detail, so `before[0] == wait` is false. Each gated unit then gets a spurious transition record on every restart, and again whenever a gate rewrites its entry with a new deadline, source or origin, even though the reason has not changed. The decision log fills with false transitions, and wait-duration readings are cut at every tick.
  Done when: In WaitRecorder.record, compare only (reason, waits_on): `if before and (before[0].reason, before[0].waits_on) == (wait.reason, wait.waits_on): continue`. Alternatively, keep detail out of Wait equality another way. Add a test in tests/pipeline (beside the existing wait_log tests): write a log, start a fresh WaitRecorder on it, and record the same SPLIT wait with a non-empty detail. Assert no line is appended. Assert also that a second record with a different detail appends nothing.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:3523 — The plan-time `_promote` now leaves gated units out via the new `excluded` parameter of `promote_ancestors`. No test exercises it, and it stores a lack of promotion that a release never undoes.
  Consequence: `_promote` runs only from `plan_all` and the replan command (lines 3517 and 5052), never in a round. test_a_gated_unit_lends_no_priority_to_the_unit_it_waits_on only calls run_round, and passes on the round's `excluded` set in `_evaluate_round`, so it would pass with this hunk and the planner.py change reverted. The new `excluded` argument of promote_ancestors has no test in tests/pipeline/test_promote_ancestors.py. Also, if a plan runs while `acp` is held, the parent's stored priority stays unpromoted after `abk tier2 release acp` until some later replan, but the spec limits the no-lending rule to "while it is left out".
  Done when: Remove the `gated` set from `_promote` and the `excluded` parameter added to `promote_ancestors`. The round's `excluded` already keeps a gated unit from lending priority while it is left out, as the existing test shows. If the builder keeps it instead, it needs a promote_ancestors test asserting that a waiter in `excluded` gives no priority. It also needs a way for the promotion to come back on the first round after a release, with a test for that.

Optional:
- [1.4] tests/split_start_support.py:46 — `scratch(tmp_path, name)` is defined but nothing uses it, and it is not in `__all__`.
  Consequence: Dead helper code that the next reader has to work out is unused.
  Done when: Delete the function and the `Path` import if nothing else needs it.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:1977 — `_split_gate` calls `repo_holds` (which reads the hold state file) once per unit, on every `_evaluate_round` call and in `_planned_wait`. It also calls `inst.repo(unit.repo)`, which raises KeyError for a repo that is no longer in abk.yaml.
  Consequence: A pass reads the state file O(units × evaluations) times. A planned unit whose repo was removed from the configuration now raises out of the whole round, not just failing its own build.
  Done when: Compute the held set once per repo per round, for example a dict passed into the loop, as `_holds_of_parked` callers could share. Treat a unit whose repo is unknown as not gated.

description.summary: A planned unit that has never started is no longer started while its e2e-test split is held. It waits with its own `split` reason and starts in the first round that finds the hold gone.
changes: A round leaves out a never-started planned unit whose split is held for its repo, reading the held set once per repo from the state file and configuration without asking a gate. It shows the unit as held, so it takes no slot or place under the limit. A started or parked unit is unaffected, as is a unit whose repo the configuration no longer has.
Wait reasons gain `split`: a gated unit reads "waiting for e2e-test split <name>: <hold>", given after its dependency reasons and before the usage-pause and ready reasons.

A gated unit lends no priority to the units it waits on, both in the round and when a plan or replan stores promotions. `promote_ancestors` takes an `excluded` set for this, and the round's effective priority restores the lending once the hold ends.

The decision log's WaitRecorder treats a wait as unchanged while its reason and what it waits on stand. A restart, or new detail text such as a changed hold deadline, no longer appends spurious transitions.
The changelog bullet for e2e-test splits now describes the start gate and its wait text.

units.title: Listings, graph, check warning, documents and skills show and explain the split gate
The Claude Code runtime delivers the prompt on standard input, chosen and size-checked in one place
units.feedback:
Most of the work is right: `build_argv` no longer contains the prompt, both spawn paths pass it on standard input, the feeder thread prevents a deadlock on a full pipe, the one size check runs at the start of `run` in both runtimes, and the tests cover the sizes and the stand-in executable as tasks 1.1 to 1.4 ask. Three things block approval. The runtime protocol is missing `prompt_transport`. The prompt pipe uses the locale's encoding rather than UTF-8. Task 1.5's `refresh_login` assertion was never written.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/base.py:309 — Task 1.6 asks for a `prompt_transport` attribute on the runtime protocol, but the `AgentRuntime` Protocol was not changed. Only `ClaudeCodeRuntime` and `AcpRuntime` declare the attribute.
  Consequence: A runtime written against `AgentRuntime` is never required to say how it carries a prompt. Code that holds an `AgentRuntime` (such as `runtimes.active()`'s result) cannot read `runtime.prompt_transport` without a type error. So the spec sentence 'A runtime SHALL declare how it carries a prompt' is not part of the interface.
  Done when: Add `prompt_transport: PromptTransport` to `AgentRuntime`, with a one-line comment like its neighbours (e.g. how this runtime carries a prompt to its agent; `check_prompt_size` holds a request to that transport's safe size). pyrefly passes with both runtimes still satisfying the protocol.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/claude_code.py:124 — Both spawn paths encode the prompt with the locale's preferred encoding, not UTF-8. One is `spawn`'s `subprocess.run(..., text=True, input=input)`. The other is `stream_run`'s `Popen(..., text=True)` at `pipeline/claude_stream.py:138`. Meanwhile `check_prompt_size` counts UTF-8 bytes and `_run` decodes them straight back to str, so the bytes checked are not the bytes delivered.
  Consequence: Take a host whose preferred encoding is not UTF-8 (a Latin-1 locale, or Windows cp1252) and a prompt containing a character outside that charset, such as `✓` from the test's own prompt. On the plain path, `communicate` raises UnicodeEncodeError after `claude` has started. On the streamed path the error is raised in the feeder thread, and `_feed` catches only OSError. The thread dies, the pipe closes, and `claude` runs on a cut-off or empty prompt with no error reported. The spec requires the prompt 'delivered whole and unchanged', and design.md says sizes are 'bytes of UTF-8'.
  Done when: Pass `encoding="utf-8"` (in place of relying on `text=True`'s locale default) to both the `subprocess.run` call in `spawn` and the `Popen` call in `stream_run`. The bytes on the pipe are then the UTF-8 bytes the check counted. `claude`'s output is UTF-8 too, so reading stdout the same way is correct. The existing `é✓a` tests keep passing. No new test is needed, since the parent's locale cannot be changed from a test.
- [1.3] tests/runtimes/test_prompt_delivery_callers.py:1 — Task 1.5 asks this file to assert that `refresh_login`'s fixed prompt is still an argument. No test does, here or elsewhere: `tests/runtimes/test_claude_refresh_login_env.py` checks only the environment.
  Consequence: A task-required test is missing. If a later change dropped `refresh_login`'s prompt or moved it to stdin, the suite would still pass. Its `run=subprocess.run` gives no input, so the login refresh would then send `claude -p` with no prompt.
  Done when: Add a test that imports `refresh_login` from `agent_build_kit.runtimes.claude_code` at module level, as `test_claude_refresh_login_env.py` does (the autouse guard patches the module attribute). Call it with a recording `run`. Assert that `argv[argv.index("-p") + 1] == "Reply with OK and nothing else."` and that no `input` keyword was passed.

Optional:
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/claude_stream.py:161 — `feeder.join()` runs after the `with subprocess.Popen(...)` block exits. `Popen.__exit__` closes `process.stdin` while the feeder may still be inside `pipe.write`.
  Consequence: Suppose a child closes its stdout but stays alive without reading stdin. The main thread's close then races the feeder's write, which can raise ValueError (I/O on a closed file). `_feed`'s `except OSError` does not catch that, so it surfaces as an unhandled thread exception.
  Done when: Call `feeder.join()` inside the `with Popen` block, after the stdout loop, so stdin is closed only by the feeder itself.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/runtimes/base.py:71 — `check_prompt_size` returns 'the UTF-8 bytes to deliver'. The only caller that uses them, `ClaudeCodeRuntime._run`, decodes them straight back to str, and `AcpRuntime._call` ignores them.
  Consequence: A 2 MB prompt is copied twice for nothing. The docstring suggests the checked bytes are what reaches the process, when the pipe re-encodes the text.
  Done when: Pick one: (a) make the check return nothing (or the str) and drop the `.decode()` in `_run`; or (b) pass bytes all the way down to the process, which would mean binary stdin.

description.summary: The Claude Code runtime now sends an agent's prompt on standard input as UTF-8 instead of as a command-line argument, and refuses a prompt that is too large for its runtime's transport before any agent starts.
changes: `build_argv` no longer puts the prompt in the `claude` argument list. Both the plain path and the streamed path write it to the child's standard input as UTF-8.
The streamed path writes standard input from a feeder thread and joins it before the pipe closes, so a prompt larger than the pipe buffer cannot deadlock the run.
Each runtime declares a `prompt_transport` (argument, stdin or protocol) as part of the `AgentRuntime` protocol, and each transport has a fixed safe size in UTF-8 bytes.

`check_prompt_size` runs once at the start of both the Claude Code and ACP runtimes' `run`. A prompt over its transport's safe size raises `PromptTooLarge` naming the role, size and limit, and nothing is started.

The login refresh still passes its fixed short prompt as an argument, and a test now covers that, alongside tests showing that the planner, the reviewer, the restack resolver and the tracks send their prompts as input.

units.title: The planner omits landed units of other changes, names the parts of an oversize prompt, and the documents state how a prompt reaches the agent

description.summary: The planner's prompt stays small as the store grows, and a prompt that is still too large fails the attempt before any process starts, with a message saying where the bytes went.
changes: The planner's list of units in flight leaves out merged and satisfied units of other changes and puts one line in their place giving how many there are. Units of the change being planned, and units of other changes still in flight or planned, are still listed.
A `Needs:` line that names a group built by a unit left out of the list still adds its dependency edge, and a plan that depends on such a unit still passes the plan check.

Before making the graph call, the planner checks the prompt's size against the runtime's prompt transport. A prompt that is too large fails the attempt with a `PlannerError` naming the change, the size, the limit, the transport, and the bytes in each part (template, tasks.md, relationships, calibration, in-flight list).
`abk replan` lists that failure as `failing n/3: the generic prompt for <change> is N bytes; the stdin transport carries at most M`, and it uses up attempts like any other failure.

`docs/agent-runtimes.md` gains a section on how a prompt reaches the agent: standard input for Claude Code, the `session/prompt` message for ACP. The runtime table and `docs/architecture.md` now say the same thing, and new docs tests check those statements.

units.title: Usage guard switch and Claude Code scratch setup with the guard off

description.summary: Adds an environment-only switch, ABK_USAGE_GUARD=off, that turns off the usage guard for one process, and makes Claude Code live-test scratch installations run with it off.
changes: A new per-machine setting `ABK_USAGE_GUARD` accepts `on` (the default) or `off`. Any other value is refused, and `abk.yaml` cannot set it because the config schema forbids the key.

With the guard off, `decide_start` lets every start go ahead without taking a usage reading or applying any threshold, allowance or estimate. This covers the tick, the checks between graph nodes and the scheduled tracks, so no usage pause is written.
`abk tick` prints `usage guard off (ABK_USAGE_GUARD) — no usage is read and no start is held for usage` as its first line when the guard is off, and `abk status` shows the same line.

The test helper `runtime_scratch` sets `ABK_USAGE_GUARD=off` for Claude Code scratch installations, even over a value set in the test's own process. A `usage_guard=True` argument opts a test about the guard back in, and the ACP setup is unchanged.
A changelog entry describes the switch and why live tests use it.

units.title: Scratch tick skips on a usage pause, and the documents say so

description.summary: When a live scratch tick builds nothing because the installation's usage limits paused it, the test is skipped and names the pause; any other failure to build fails with the full scratch state as before.
changes: `commits_on_unit_branch` (tests/scratch_tick.py) skips the running test when the unit's branch never reached the remote and an unexpired `usage` or `rate_limit` pause marker is in the scratch's state. The skip reason quotes the pause. A `network` pause, or no pause at all, still fails with cause hints, the tick's output and the scratch dump.

A new test helper, `write_pause` (tests/usage_condition.py), writes pause markers in the pipeline's shape with an explicit kind. The branch-check and failure-dump fixtures now use it with `network`, so their failure paths run instead of being skipped.
The check of whether a branch is on the remote is now one function, `branch_on_remote`, used by both the failure dump and the usage skip.
A structural test fails when a live test runs `run_tick` without ending through `commits_on_unit_branch`, so every live tick goes through the guarded branch check.
The CLI and configuration docs, the abk-pipeline skill and the changelog now describe the usage guard switch and the usage skip. A docs test pins that wording.

units.title: A unit parked on a split holds no place whatever its cause field says, and a replan keeps the park

description.summary: A unit parked on a held e2e-test split no longer takes a place under max_units_in_progress, whether it is planned or unplanned and whatever its cause field says, and a replan no longer drops the park.
changes: A new parked_on_split rule in pipeline/units.py: a planned or unplanned unit with parked_splits, whose latest cause is empty or split_held, is not in progress, so it leaves room to start other units. A planned unit with cause split_held stays exempt as before.

UnitStore.upsert carries parked_splits, parked_sha, parked_snapshot and parked_attempts over from the existing record. A replan that includes, demotes or plans a parked unit again no longer wipes the park, and no longer lets the unit be released while its split is held.

abk status lists unplanned parked units as well as planned ones. An unplanned unit reads 'unplanned, parked on e2e-test split …', and once the split is released it says it is left alone because the plan no longer has it.

Releasing a split still resumes only planned units with cause split_held. An unplanned parked unit keeps its state, branch and park until a replan plans it again, and the ordinary round then starts it.
The in_progress docstring, docs/architecture.md, docs/unit-graph.md, the abk-pipeline skill and the changelog describe the new rule.

units.title: A replan keeps a started unit the plan omits and refuses a plan that gives its group to a second unit
units.feedback:
One required fix. `_new_collisions` decides that a collision was "already in the store" by asking whether the claimant's old record listed the group, even when that record owned nothing. The new tests passed when run (41 passed). I could not run the reproduction script below because the sandbox refused it, so that finding comes from reading the code. The scratch file /tmp/abkrev/probe.py is still there because the sandbox refused its removal. Everything else in group 1 is present and matches the tasks. Demotion is now limited to `unstarted` units, `owns_groups`/`has_work`/`GroupOwned` are added, the store is left untouched on refusal, `plan_all` records the failure with every attempt spent and an `owned` list, and `abk replan` prints the kept line, the retire line and exits 1 on a refusal.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_store.py:1144 — `_new_collisions` skips a claimant whenever `_carries(before.get(claimant.id))` contains the group. It does not check whether that earlier record owned the group. A work-less `unplanned` unit that the plan brings back, or an unstarted unit that already listed the group, is therefore treated as an existing collision and let through.
  Consequence: The spec says a work-less `unplanned` unit owns no group and a collision must be new to be refused. Reproduction: plan A gives group 16 to `app/4`. Plan B gives group 16 to `app/3` and leaves `app/4` out, so `app/4` becomes `unplanned` but its record keeps groups (16,). `app/3` then gets a branch. Plan C omits `app/3` (kept, since it has work) and lists `app/4` with group 16 again. `upsert` brings `app/4` back to `planned`. Because `app/4`'s old record listed 16, the claimant check skips it and no `GroupOwned` is raised. The store ends up with two planned owners of group 16, one of them started: the exact state this change exists to prevent. Planners reuse ids like `app/4` regularly, so this will happen. A second form of the same gap: unstarted `app/4` carries 17 and started `app/3` carries 16. A plan that gives `app/3` (16, 17) and keeps `app/4` with 17 is also accepted, because `app/4` listed 17 before and `app/4` is not started, so it is never counted as an owner.
  Done when: Decide "already in the store" by ownership, not by what a record lists. Simplest fix: build the same collision set from `before` (groups carried by `owns_groups` units, counting only owners that are not `unstarted`), key it by `(change, group, owner, claimant)`, and raise only on the collisions in `after` that are missing from `before`'s set. Add one test to `tests/pipeline/test_group_ownership.py`. It should reach a store where `app/4` is `unplanned` with no work and groups (16,), and `app/3` is `planned` with a branch and group 16, by real upserts as in the reproduction above. Then `upsert([app/4 with (16,)], change="app")` must raise `GroupOwned` naming `app/3`, `app/4` and 16, and the store bytes must be unchanged. The existing `test_a_collision_already_in_the_store_is_not_refused`, where both units owned the group before, must still pass.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:3502 — `plan_all` now has a local `kept` (attempts kept across a wait) next to the new `PlanResult.kept` (unit ids kept by the replan), and the `PlanResult(..., kept=left_out)` call sits on the line right after it.
  Consequence: A reader sees `kept = record.get("attempts"...)` immediately followed by `kept=left_out` and can easily confuse the two.
  Done when: Rename the local to something like `attempts_kept`, or name the field `kept_units`.
- [1.3] tests/factories.py:61 — `own_group` now gives every `unit()`/`stored_unit()` that does not set `groups` a group derived from its id, using a CRC32 offset of the id prefix. This changes the default for every test in the suite.
  Consequence: The new default is hard to read: a failing test's group number (for example 734016) gives no hint where it came from. Tests that depended on the old `(1,)` default silently get different groups.
  Done when: Optional. Add a short note in the docstring that the offset only needs to be unique per fixture, or have the colliding fixtures pass `groups` explicitly.

description.summary: When a replan leaves out a unit that has already started, the unit is kept with its task groups instead of being dropped. A plan that would give a started unit's group to a second unit is refused, and nothing is written.
changes: Only `unstarted` units (planned, with no branch, commit, pull request or approval) are demoted when a plan leaves them out. Units with work stay as they are and are reported as kept.

The unit store refuses a merge that adds a new collision with a started owner of a group, raising `GroupOwned` with both units and the group named. The store file is left unchanged. Collisions that were already in the store are let through.
Who owns a group is decided by `owns_groups` and `has_work`, so a work-less `unplanned` unit owns nothing, and planning it again is treated as a new claimant.
`plan_all` records a refused plan as a failure with every attempt spent and the `owned` collisions listed. `abk replan` prints the kept and retire lines and exits 1 when a plan is refused.
Test fixtures now give each unit its own group number, so no fixture shares a group with a started unit by accident.

units.title: A retired unit is finished: it holds no place, nothing waits on it, and a plan cannot reuse its id
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_store.py:72 — Task 2.6 asks for `Cause.RETIRED` and `UnitStore.retire(unit_id, reason)`, and the branch adds neither. The `Cause` enum has no `RETIRED` member, `UnitStore` has no `retire` method, and every test makes a unit retired with `store.set_state(..., UnitState.RETIRED)`, which records no cause and no reason.
  Consequence: Group 2's done-when says 'a unit can be stored `retired` with the cause `retired` and a history entry carrying the reason and `by: abk retire`'. Nothing on this branch can produce that record, and group 3's `abk retire` (task 3.6) would have to write the state, the cause and the history ad hoc.
  Done when: Add `Cause.RETIRED = "retired"` to `Cause` in pipeline/unit_store.py. Add `UnitStore.retire(unit_id, reason)`, marked `@_exclusive`, that writes the state `retired`, the cause `retired` and one history entry with `state: retired`, `cause: retired`, the reason when one is given and `by: "abk retire"`, in a single `_write`. Use the existing `_with_state`/`set_state` history path, not a parallel one. Add a test, for example in tests/pipeline/test_upsert_retired.py or a new test_unit_store_retire.py, that calls `store.retire("app/3", "built in app/4")` and asserts the state, the cause, the reason and `by` in the last history entry, that no user name is recorded, and that the file is written once (count calls through `on_write`).
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:1795 — The `Needs:` paths still treat a retired unit as building its groups. `awaiting_planning` (line 1795) leaves out only `UNPLANNED` units, `link_needs` builds `live = [... if unit.state != UNPLANNED]` (line 2940) and passes it to `declared_needs`, and `_drop_cycle_edges` keeps `u.state != UNPLANNED` units (line 3533). Each of these left out `unplanned` precisely because it builds nothing, and `retired` builds nothing too.
  Consequence: A retired unit `feat/2` was the only carrier of feat group 3, and the group was released. description.summary: A unit can now be retired: it builds nothing and holds no group, nothing waits on it, it is recorded with its own cause and reason, and a replan keeps a started unit the plan leaves out.
changes: Adds the `retired` unit state and an event cause of the same name. `UnitStore.retire(unit_id, reason)` records the state, the cause, the reason and `by: abk retire` in one history entry and one write, and leaves the branch and the pull request as they are.

A retired unit counts as building nothing, like an unplanned one. Its groups are not counted as planned, a `Needs:` line is never linked to it, it is left out of cycle checks and priority promotion, and a unit that waited on it has its wait ended.
Join checks and the retire assessment both read one `FINISHED_STATES` set (merged, satisfied, closed, retired) from pipeline/units.py, so they agree on which units are finished.

The retire assessment (pipeline/retirement.py) reports, for each group, who else carries it. It counts the group as already built only when another carrier merged, or was satisfied and actually landed. It refuses a unit that is finished or running, or that a started unit is stacked on.
`abk status` and `abk replan` stop reporting retired units as live work. The architecture and unit-graph docs list `retired` among the event causes.

The spec says a branch with commits after its last pushed commit (after its base when none was pushed) SHALL refuse `--delete-branch` alone; here an unreadable count lets the deletion through.

Without `--discard-unpushed`, refuse and exit 1 before anything changes, printing that the commits on BRANCH since SINCE could not be counted and that `--discard-unpushed` accepts losing them. description.summary: Adds `abk retire`, which takes a unit out of the plan for good, and adds status lines that suggest retiring a unit when two started units carry the same task group.
changes: `abk retire UNIT` marks a unit retired in the unit store and records `abk retire` as the actor in its history. If the unit has an open pull request, the command closes it with a reason through the repo's forge. When the close fails, the close is recorded as pending and retried on the next pass.

`--delete-branch` removes the unit's local branch, worktree and remote branch. It refuses when the worktree has uncommitted changes. It also refuses when the branch has commits after its last pushed commit, or after its base when none was pushed, unless `--discard-unpushed` is given. `--discard-unpushed` without `--delete-branch` is refused.

If git cannot count the unpushed commits, for example because the base branch is not in the checkout, the count is treated as unknown rather than zero. `--delete-branch` alone then refuses and exits 1 without changing anything.

`abk status` lists each task group that two started, unfinished units both carry, and suggests retiring the one further from done. Ties go to the unit later in plan order. A group shared with a unit that has not started is not listed.

units.title: Ready units start by priority, handoff units break ties, and the status marks them

description.summary: Ready units now start in effective-priority order. Among units of equal priority that have never run, handoff units go first, and a new priority 0 is an emergency lane that starts before everything else.
changes: `ready_units` sorts all ready units with one key. Units that have never run go by effective priority, and within the same priority the handoff units (those that take the place a blocked unit frees) go first. A handoff unit no longer jumps ahead of a more urgent unit.

The priority scale is now 0 to 5. Priority 0 is an emergency lane: such a unit starts before priority 1, and its prerequisites take priority 0 with it. It bypasses no slot or in-progress limit and stops no running unit.

In the `abk status` ready queue, a handoff unit is marked `(handoff)`, but only while some unit is blocked. A priority-0 unit is listed first with its reason, and so is a prerequisite that inherits priority 0 (shown as `from <unit>`).
Task parsing, the unit store, `abk tags` and the unit diagram accept priority 0 and report it. A `Priority: 0` line in a group that cannot be read is the same error as any other bad priority line.
The abk-authoring and abk-pipeline skills, docs/architecture.md, docs/unit-graph.md and the changelog describe the new order and the emergency lane.
Shared test helpers: `worked_unit` in tests/factories.py and `ready_queue` in tests/conftest.py replace copies that were scattered across test files.

units.title: The planner is shown priorities and a plan with an unexcused edge onto a less urgent unit is refused

description.summary: The planner now sees each task group's priority and refuses a plan in which a more urgent unit waits on a less urgent one without a stated reason, sending that reason back on the next attempt.
changes: The planner prompt shows each group's priority, and in-flight unit headings carry their marks in the order priority, project, built-by, so the planner can see urgency when it orders units.

A planned dependency from a unit onto a less urgent one is refused unless the plan gives an excuse for it. The target's urgency comes from the priority of its groups. Started, merged, closed, satisfied, held and unplanned stored units are skipped (src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/planner.py).

When a plan is refused, the reason is fed back into the next planning prompt. This happens only while the recorded refusal still matches the change's current digest and holds unit ids. An outage or a failed call replaces the record, so nothing stale is fed back.

Join checks stay independent of priority. A priority-1 group joining a priority-5 unit is judged only by the ceiling and by whether the target has started, and the rule against joining two units merely because both are small is kept.
A changelog bullet describes the new refusal for people running the pipeline.

description.summary: A tick that builds nothing explains why for each unit, and a live test whose scratch tick did not produce the expected branch fails with a diagnosis of what the scratch tick did.
changes: A tick that starts nothing, and is not held by a pause, a deadlock, a full queue or a failed blocker, prints `nothing ready to build` and then one line for each planned, held or failed unit with its reason and what it waits on. Actionable units come first, up to 10 are shown, and the rest are summarised; docs/cli.md describes it.

When the branch is missing, the failure opens with one `cause hints:` line: the tick's exit status, the missing branch, whether the pause marker is absent, present or unreadable, and the unit's latest wait reason. units.title: Failed live tests print scratch state, and live tests move onto the shared helpers

description.summary: When a live (`local_stack`) test fails and has a scratch installation, its failure report now ends with a bounded, redacted SCRATCH STATE section, and the live tests use the shared tick helpers.
changes: A failed or errored `local_stack` test that has a scratch gets a `SCRATCH STATE` section. The scratch can be a `scratch` fixture argument, the `scratch` attribute of any fixture value (including module-scoped ones), or one passed to `register_scratch`. The section opens with a `cause hints:` line naming the tick's exit code, whether the first open unit's branch is on the remote, the pause marker, and that unit's wait reason.

The section holds the last tick's output, the units with their wait reasons, the pause marker, lease holders, the e2e lock holder (read from its file without taking the lock), the remote's heads, the tails of the decision log, the usage ledger and the run log, the fake host's latest requests, and the environment. Each source has its own cap and everything goes through the redactor.
One dump is at most 20 480 characters. A dump that would take the session past 61 440 is replaced by one 'left out' line, and only what is printed counts toward the budget.
`cause_hints`, `newest_run_log` and the git runner and timeout now live in `tests/scratch_tick.py`, shared by the guarded branch check and the dump.
The live build and telemetry tests now include the tick's output in their assertion messages, and the telemetry scratch carries its fake host so the dump can list the host's requests.

units.title: A failed unit requeues itself once when its wait ends

description.summary: A failed unit that was waiting on another unit is now requeued once by the pipeline when that wait ends, in a mode chosen from its record, and `abk status` reports what the end of a wait did.
changes: A new tick step (`requeue_wait_ended`) records which units a failed unit is waiting on. When all of them reach review, merge or satisfied, it requeues the unit once through `requeue`. On a thread, the event's reason is the wait-ended text; without a thread, the history note says `requeue: its wait ended (waiting on <group> is now merged)`.

The mode is chosen from the unit's record. A saved unit-test or e2e-test failure with feedback is reworked. An environmental cause, no saved failure, or a review, CI or conflict failure is resumed. A person's note is kept as guidance. Held units, units in flight and failed units that never waited are left alone.

When a prerequisite is closed or unplanned, the unit stays failed and `abk status` shows `wait ended: <group> closed, requeue to retry`. Only a requeue that takes effect clears that line; a refused one leaves it. The status also counts the failed units resumed today because their wait ended.
A new setting, `global_limits.wait_end_requeue` (`auto` by default, `resume`, `rework` or `off`), forces a mode or turns the step off. `rework` falls back to resume when nothing is saved.

The unit store gains `waited_on` and `wait_ended` fields; stores written before them still load. The history-stamp parser in `units.py` is now public as `history_stamp`. The description of the FAILED state, in both the code comment and the diagram legend, now says the pipeline retries such a unit once when a wait ends.

units.title: The documents, the skills and the changelog describe the automatic requeue when a wait ends

description.summary: Documents the automatic one-time requeue of a failed unit when the unit it waited on lands, together with the `global_limits.wait_end_requeue` setting, and adds a test that keeps those docs in step with the code.

docs/configuration.md and the abk-config skill list `wait_end_requeue: auto` in the `global_limits:` example, where the config schema accepts it.

units.title: emergency_extra setting and the emergency lane start rule
The status shows the emergency lane, and the documents and skills describe it
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:2652 — The `abk.slots.emergency_used` gauge counts only lane units that are running (`lane_units(...) & running`), but the lane use is every recorded unit still in progress.
  Consequence: Take a priority-0 unit that started in the lane, finished its build and went `in_review`. It still holds the lane: `_lane_use` counts it, status prints `emergency room 1/1 used by <unit>`, and `ready_units` refuses a second priority-0 start. The gauge still reports 0. The spec (unit-scheduling, 'The status shows the emergency lane') says the gauge SHALL report the lane use summed over the projects, so it disagrees with the status and with what the scheduler enforces.
  Done when: Make the gauge count the recorded ids that are in flight or in progress in the stored units. That is the predicate `_lane_use` applies, with in-flight builds counted as running, as `prune` does at line 1596. Use one shared helper, not a second copy of the predicate. Add a test to tests/cli/test_emergency_lane_sample_row.py (or a new one) where a lane-recorded priority-0 unit is `in_review` when a sample is taken, and assert the gauge is 1.
- [1.2] tests/cli/test_status_emergency_room.py:68 — Task 3.1 asks for the case where only a restack run takes the project over the cap. This test seeds five ordinary running builds instead, and its comment claims restack runs that are not there.
  Consequence: Nothing pins the rule that the room line reads the emergency lane's record and not the occupancy margin that a restack-lane run creates, which the spec forbids ('SHALL NOT be a margin shared with the restack lane'). A change that derived lane use from occupancy beyond the cap, counting a restack run, would pass every test here.
  Done when: Seed a restack-lane run for a unit of the full project, so the occupancy goes over the cap because of the restack. The fakes in tests/restack_lane_fakes.py, as used by tests/cli/test_emergency_lane_round.py, can do this. Assert that no `emergency room` line is printed and that the queue-full line still carries the 'a priority-0 unit may still start' sentence. Fix the comment so it describes what is seeded.
- [1.3] CHANGELOG.md:33 — The existing Unreleased bullet still says priority 0 'bypasses no limit'. The new bullet above it says a priority-0 unit starts past the places and workers.
  Consequence: The same Unreleased section now makes two contradictory claims about unreleased behaviour. Group 3's done-criterion says no text should still say priority 0 bypasses no limit.

- [1.4] docs/architecture.md:244 — 'Only a unit that has never started is stopped by the limit, and no more of them start than leave room' is now false for a priority-0 unit in the emergency lane.
  Consequence: A reader of the units-in-progress text (task 3.5 names it) is told that no never-started unit starts past the room. The new paragraph at line 210 says the opposite.

- [1.5] tests/emergency_lane_support.py:83 — `status_output` copies the tail of `status_lines` in tests/conftest.py:316-318: patch `current_usage`, run `cmd_status`, split the captured output.
  Consequence: Two copies of the way a test runs `abk status` must change together. A future change to how status is invoked in tests (another patched dependency, say) would update one and miss the other.

- [1.6] tests/cli/test_status_emergency_room.py:19 — `app_only` here and `single_project` in tests/cli/test_emergency_lane_sample_row.py:58 are two new copies of the same thing: `repos_declaring(root)` with `platform` deleted. The pattern already appears in tests/cli/test_status_queue_full_single.py:20.

Optional:
- [1.7] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:2202 — `_emergency_room_lines` sorts by `item[0].repo` only, while `_queue_full_by_project` sorts by `(repo, project)`. It also names the project as a trailing `(app/web)`, where the queue-full line uses a leading `app/web: `.

description.summary: Priority-0 units get a per-project emergency lane, and status, telemetry, docs and the changelog now show and describe it consistently.
changes: `abk status` prints an `emergency room n/cap used by <units>` line for each project whose emergency lane is in use, and names the project when the workspace has more than one.

When a project's queue is full but its emergency lane still has room, the queue-full line adds that a priority-0 unit may still start. A restack-lane run that pushes occupancy past the cap does not count as use of the lane.

The `abk.slots.emergency_used` gauge counts every unit recorded in a lane that is still in progress, including units in review and builds in flight. It uses the same `emergency_lane.users` helper that pruning and status use.
The changelog and docs/architecture.md no longer say priority 0 bypasses no limit. They describe a priority-0 unit starting in its project's emergency lane past the normal room.
Test helpers were consolidated: a shared `run_status` in tests/conftest.py and an `app_only_repos` workspace helper for the lane tests.

units.title: The emergency_extra setting, and a ready priority-0 unit starting in its own lane
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:2066 — The lane is decided in two places against two different caps. `ready_units` decides it against `cap + owed_most`, and `owed_most` is the maximum over all projects. The `_within_workers` slice then holds every unit to `cap`, and for never-started units it counts running units without the lane's units. Task 2.8 says to give `_within_workers` the same helper (`emergency_start`), and that was not done, so in a workspace with several projects the two checks disagree.
  Consequence: Two projects. Project A has a planned unit owed a restack, so `owed_most` is 1 and `ready_units` runs with `max_concurrent` 5 for every project. (a) Project B has four normal builds at a cap of four, places free, `emergency_extra` 1, and a ready priority-0 unit that has never started. `ready_units` admits it as a normal start (busy 4 < 5), so it is in `ready_with(0)` too, and `in_the_lane` is empty. `_within_workers` then drops it (4 >= 4). The priority-0 unit does not start, which breaks the scenario 'a place free but the workers full still starts a priority-0 unit in the lane'. (b) Project B has three normal builds and one lane unit running at a cap of four, places free, and a ready priority-1 unit that has never started. `ready_units` admits it (busy 4 including the lane unit, < 5). `_within_workers` admits it too, because `running` there excludes the lane units (3 < 4). An ordinary unit starts at an occupancy of 4/4, which breaks 'while ... its occupancy is at or above the cap, no never-started unit that is not of effective priority 0 SHALL start'. In a single project, `_start_rank` puts the owed unit first and it absorbs the slack, which is why the existing tests do not catch this.
  Done when: The slice and `ready_units` must agree at the real cap. Prescribed fix: have `_within_workers` take the view, the excluded set, the lane ids and `emergency_extra`. A unit that does not fit `cap` is admitted, without taking a worker, when `emergency_start(unit, view, excluded)` holds and the project's lane use (in-progress lane units plus those admitted so far) is below `emergency_extra`. Return those ids as the round's `lane_starts`, so the `ready_with(0)` second evaluation can go. For a unit that draws on room, count the lane's running units in `taken`; for a unit already started, leave them out. Add two tests in `tests/cli/test_emergency_lane_round.py` over a two-project workspace where project A has a planned unit owed a restack (`Cause.BASE_CHANGED`): (a) project B with four builds in flight, places free and a ready priority-0 unit; `run_round` returns it and `emergency_lane.lane_units` names it; (b) project B with three normal builds plus a lane unit in flight, places free and a ready priority-1 unit; `run_round` does not return it.
- [1.2] tests/cli/test_emergency_lane_pool.py:92 — `run_blocked_pass` gives up after 12 calls to `poll_all`. Those calls come from the pass's refresh timer (`REFRESH_SECONDS` 0.05, real time), so the test races the clock. In the `extra=1` case the lane build's thread must reach `lane_build` before roughly 0.65 s of refreshes has passed since the pass began.
  Consequence: On a loaded machine, starting four blocking builds, evaluating the round with `zero/1` and getting its pool thread running can take longer than 13 refreshes. The give-up branch then records `in_flight == [4]` and sets the release before `zero/1` builds. `lane_build` appends a second entry afterwards, so `test_a_priority_zero_unit_runs_beside_four_blocked_builds_in_the_lane` fails (`in_flight == [5]`) even though the code is right. It passes alone and fails under load. If the four builds are slow to start, `zero/1` may not even be upserted before the give-up fires. This breaks the rule against waiting on the clock.
  Done when: Make the give-up depend on a scheduling decision, not on a count of refreshes. For example, wrap `cli.run_round` (or `_evaluate_round`) to record each round's result, and in the `extra=0` case release the builds once a round has run with `zero/1` in the store and has not returned it. In the `extra=1` case, have no give-up path: only `lane_build` sets the release, and `wait_for(..., timeout=WAIT)` is the safety net. The `extra=0` assertions stay as they are.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/emergency_lane.py:25 — Record file names are built with `re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "_", ...)`. Two projects whose names differ only in replaced characters (for example `a b` and `a_b`) map to the same file. The existing per-project record in `pipeline/restack_lane.py:198` (`record_path`) hashes `repo/project` and avoids that.
  Consequence: Today the records are only ever read as a union, so a collision changes no count. Group 3's status line names the lane's units per project, and it would then see another project's units in this project's file.
  Done when: Name the file the way `restack_lane.record_path` does: a short sha256 of `f"{key.repo}/{key.project}"`. Optionally share one helper for both lanes.

description.summary: Adds an emergency lane per project: up to `emergency_extra` ready priority-0 units may start beyond a project's places and workers, in pool threads of their own, while ordinary starts wait.
changes: A ready priority-0 unit that has never started (or waits for room like a new one) starts even when its project's places or workers are full, as long as the project's lane holds fewer than `emergency_extra` units in progress.
Units in the lane count as in progress and running for never-started units, so ordinary starts wait while the lane is in use. A unit already started is held to the workers the lane leaves.

The lane's units are recorded per project under the state directory and dropped once they finish or disappear. The round uses this record to tell lane starts from normal ones, and the worker slice admits lane starts without taking a worker.

The extra workers a project gets for units owed a restack now apply to that project only (`ready_units(extra_workers=...)`), so an owed unit in one project no longer lets another project go past its cap.
The build pool gets `emergency_extra` threads per live project on top of the workers, so a lane unit builds at once beside a full set of builds.

units.title: A standing cause and a unit's runtime fields survive a replan; a cause change closes the gate in the same write

description.summary: A replan, a vanished change and a join no longer erase why a unit stopped or the runtime state a run left on it, and a gate's saved requeue is cleared in the same write that changes the cause.
changes: When the store moves a unit itself (a replan demoting it to `unplanned` or promoting it back, marking a vanished change's units `unplanned`, or joining another unit onto it), the new history entry repeats a standing cause such as `split_held`, `gated` or `base_changed` and the previous note, and is marked `carried`. An event cause such as `requeued` is not carried. Causes are split into two sets, `STANDING_CAUSES` and `EVENT_CAUSES`, which together cover every `Cause`.

`StoredUnit.cause_since` gives the time of the entry that actually set the current cause, skipping carried entries. The parking backoff is measured from it, so a replan does not restart a backoff but a second parking does. A carry is not counted as another parking and keeps the step a parked unit resumes at.

Every state change that records a cause other than `gated` clears the unit's saved gate requeue in the same write. On its non-delivered path, `release_gated` now records `requeued` in one write, so the store never shows `gated` without its requeue.

`UnitStore.upsert` now keeps runtime fields it used to drop on a replan: `service_attempts`, `gated_requeue`, `waited_on`, `wait_ended`, `close_pending`, `step`, `guidance`, `ready_at` and `first_human_activity_at`. Gated and split-parked units therefore stay parked across a replan, and a pending close is still retried.
A running pass logs its 'not started again' skip once per cause, keyed on `cause_since`, so a carried entry written mid-pass does not log it again or readmit the unit.
A changelog bullet under Unreleased describes the carry, the kept backoff, the kept runtime fields and the one-write requeue clear.

units.title: A gate is released by its saved requeue, a deferred conflict move stays owed, and the documents define standing and event causes

description.summary: A gate is now released by the unit's saved requeue whatever its cause, a deferred conflict move keeps its restack owed, every reader of a cause is pinned over a replan, and the docs and skill define standing and event causes.
changes: `release_gated` and `awaits_release` key on a planned unit having a saved requeue, not on its cause being `gated`, so an older record with a requeue is still released. The `abk status` dependency-wait line follows the same rule.
A conflict move that comes back deferred records the cause `restack_deferred` on its in-review entry. The restack lane still owes the restack, and following predecessors leaves the unit alone.

New regression tests show that the restack lane's owed checks, `why_branch_is_changing`, `follow_predecessors`, `gate_sent_back`, waiting for room, `in_progress` and the parked resume in `build_unit` give the same answer after a demotion and promotion and after a plain replan. Only comments change at those sites.
`abk status` is tested to list a held or started planned unit with no recorded cause, and not one a replan carried a standing cause onto.

docs/architecture.md, docs/unit-graph.md and the abk-pipeline skill define standing and event causes with both sets. They cover the carry through a replan, the `carried` mark and `cause_since`, and that `upsert` keeps runtime fields. The existing changelog bullet is extended.

units.title: Unstarted prerequisites take their dependents' urgency; warnings and displays show effective priority
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:682 — The tick's and `abk status`'s `priority:` line does not use `priority_note`. It adds its own ` (promoted from X)` suffix to `unit.priority` and still filters on `unit.priority != Priority.NORMAL`, so it never shows the effective priority of a unit that a more urgent waiter covers without a stored promotion.
  Consequence: Group 4's done-when says the tick's `priority:` line and `abk status` show a unit's effective priority with `promoted from <unit>` or `from <unit>`, and task 4.5 says to use `priority_note` in the tick's priority line. Take a started priority-3 unit with a priority-1 waiter: the ready queue and the graph label say `priority 1, from app/9`, but the unit is missing from the `priority:` line entirely. That line also shows a promoted unit as `base/1 1 (promoted from fix/1)` instead of the shared text. The 'promoted from' wording now lives in two places (`units.priority_note` and here), and both would have to change together. The test module's docstring says the `priority:` line carries the note `priority_note` makes, which is not true.
  Done when: Build each entry of the `priority:` line from `priority_note(unit, units)` (pass the same `excluded` the ready queue uses if one is in scope), e.g. `f"{unit.id} {note}"` for every unit that is not merged or closed and whose note is non-empty. Remove the inline `promoted from` suffix. Add a test in `tests/cli/test_status_effective_priority.py` where a started priority-3 unit has a priority-1 waiter and no promotion, and assert the `priority:` line contains `<id> priority 1, from <waiter>`. Keep the existing assertions: a promoted unit reads `priority 1, promoted from fix/1`, and `plain/1` is absent. Update any older test that pinned the `<id> <n>` form.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/units.py:421 — `priority_note` names `unit.promoted_from` as the source whenever it is set, even when a different, more urgent waiter now sets the effective priority.
  Consequence: Take a unit that started while promoted to 1 by `app/9`, then gets a new priority-0 waiter `app/12`. It is labelled `priority 0, promoted from app/9`, which names the wrong unit as the source of the 0.
  Done when: When `effective_priority` is more urgent than the stored priority, name the most urgent waiter (`from <id>`), and use `promoted from <promoted_from>` only when the stored promotion is what sets the effective value. Pin this with a test in `tests/pipeline/test_priority_note.py`.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/planner.py:260 — `own_priority` falls back to `unit_priority` for a unit that has `promoted_from` but none of whose groups is in the catalog. `unit_priority` then returns `Priority.NORMAL`, not the priority the unit had before it was promoted.
  Consequence: Take an unstarted unit whose own priority is 1, promoted to 0, whose change's groups are not in the catalog at that pass. When its waiter lapses it is written at 3 rather than 1, until the catalog has its groups again.
  Done when: Either document that fallback in the docstring, or keep the stored priority when no group is known, whatever `promoted_from` says. Add a test for the chosen behaviour.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/work_graph.py:731 — `inverted_group_warnings` runs `validate_tasks` on the same file that `inverted_groups` validates again, just to look up the heading lines.
  Consequence: Each `abk tags` and `abk check` run validates every tasks file once more. This is only a cost, with no wrong result.
  Done when: Have `InvertedGroup` carry the dependent group's heading line (or have `inverted_groups` accept already-validated groups), so the warning does not validate a second time.

description.summary: Unstarted units that a more urgent unit depends on now take that urgency, and warnings and status displays show each unit's effective priority and where it came from.
changes: A unit that has not started is promoted to the priority of its most urgent waiter on every planning pass. The promotion lapses when the waiter goes away, and a unit that has started keeps the priority it had.

`priority_note` gives one shared wording for a unit's effective priority: `priority N, from <waiter>` when a more urgent waiter covers it, `priority N, promoted from <unit>` for a stored promotion, and nothing for a normal unit with no source.

The `priority:` line in the tick and in `abk status`, the ready queue and the graph labels all use that note. So a started unit with a more urgent waiter is now listed, and a promoted unit shows where its promotion came from.

`abk tags` and `abk check` warn about each task-group edge where an urgent group depends on a less urgent one, pointing at the dependent group's heading line. The edges come from `inverted_groups`, which now carries that line.
A promoted unit whose groups are not in the catalog goes back to normal when its promotion lapses. An unpromoted one keeps the priority it was stored with.

units.title: Skill, architecture, unit graph docs and changelog describe the priority rule, refusal and promotion

description.summary: Documents the planner's priority rule: what the planner is shown, which plans it refuses and the `needs_less_urgent` excuse, how unstarted prerequisites are promoted, and that already recorded plans need `abk replan` only to drop avoidable edges.
changes: The `abk-authoring` skill's Priority section says a group should be at least as urgent as every group that depends on it, that `abk tags` and `abk check` warn when it is not, that such a prerequisite is promoted, and that groups sharing no code belong in an `Independent:` group.

units.title: Make the moved-base running-pass test deterministic
units.feedback:
The diagnosis is right. The failing run logged `back/1: skipped, spec/back/1 is held by pid <the test's own pid>`, which means a `branch_held` probe claimed the lock (old `branch_lock` acquire-and-release) at the moment the second build of back/1 tried to take it. Reading the lock through `lock_holder_gone` removes that window. The new test fails on the old `workspaces.py` and passes on the new one. I checked this by restoring HEAD~1's file. The probe test, test_moved_base_run_stored, test_restack_lane_run_unit and test_restack_lane_runs (30 tests) all pass. The only blocker is one docstring the change has made false.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:2821 — `branch_is_held`'s docstring still says "`branch_lock` already distinguishes a crashed holder from a live one by its pid; acquiring and releasing is the cheapest way to ask", but the function it delegates to (`workspaces.branch_held`) no longer acquires anything.
  Consequence: The docstring now describes the very behaviour this change removed as the right way to probe. A reader of `branch_is_held` (used by `parked_units` and the views) is told the probe takes the lock, and the next person writing a probe is pointed at the pattern that caused the flake.
  Done when: Rewrite the docstring to match `workspaces.branch_held`. Say it reads the lock's pid without taking the lock, so it never turns away a run starting on the branch, or just say it defers to `branch_held`. Do not mention acquiring or releasing.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/events.py:599 — This is a second probe of the same kind: `with claim(dependent): pass` takes and drops the dependent's branch lock only to learn whether a build holds it. Its own comment says a build starting in that instant gets `BranchBusy` and is skipped for the pass. That is the race this change removes from `branch_held`.
  Consequence: When a base unit merges while a dependent's build is starting, that build is skipped and left `planned` until the next pass. The behaviour is documented and tolerated, but it is the same kind of turn-away the changelog bullet says no longer happens.
  Done when: Optionally, switch the probe to `branch_held(branch_name(dependent), root=locks)`, or `lock_holder_gone(...) is False`. The ordering argument in the comment above still holds, because MERGED is already written before the probe. Then drop the 'probe holds the lock for an instant' paragraph. Check that `claim` does nothing beyond `branch_lock` that this site relies on before replacing it.
- [1.3] tests/pipeline/test_branch_held_probe.py:17 — The test finds a lock claim by swapping `workspaces.os` for a spy and recording `os.open` calls that carry `O_EXCL`. That reaches into the module's imports rather than a public surface, and it only sees one way of spelling a claim.
  Consequence: A later probe that claims the lock another way, such as `open(path, 'x')`, `Path.touch(exist_ok=False)` or a helper in another module, would pass this test and bring the flake back.
  Done when: Optionally, assert something observable instead. For example, pre-create a lock file for the branch whose pid is the current process, call `branch_held` and assert `True`. Then assert the file is still there with the same contents (the old code would also leave it, so pair this with the claim check). Or check that no lock file or directory is created under a fresh `root`. Keep the spy only if nothing observable can tell the two implementations apart.

description.summary: Asking whether a branch is held now reads the lock's recorded pid without taking the lock, so a build starting at the same moment is no longer skipped.
changes: `workspaces.branch_held` now asks `lock_holder_gone` and never acquires or releases the branch lock. Before, it briefly claimed the lock, and a build trying to start on that branch at the same instant was turned away as 'held by' the probing process.
A probe no longer creates the lock directory, and no longer deletes a lock file whose holder has not yet written its pid.
The docstring of `branch_is_held` in cli/pipeline.py (used by `parked_units` and the views) now describes the read-only probe.
A new test, tests/pipeline/test_branch_held_probe.py, asserts that asking about a free branch returns False and leaves nothing on disk.
CHANGELOG.md gets an Unreleased bullet explaining that a concurrent build is no longer skipped by the held-branch check.

units.title: The rename tool is deleted
units.feedback:
Group 5 deletes the module, its five test files and the guard's exemption for them, and the new guard tests would have failed before the deletion. Three things still need changing: an earlier Unreleased changelog bullet still says the tool stays, a source comment still names the tool, and the new search helper duplicates the guard's existing file walk while scanning fewer files. Also, the group's own Done line says a person must run the tool over the planning repository before this merges. Nothing in the branch can check that, so the person merging has to confirm it.

Required:
- [1.1] CHANGELOG.md:569 — An earlier bullet in the same Unreleased section still says `python -m agent_build_kit.rename_test_kinds` stays for rewriting a planning repository's text, while the new bullet at line 5 says the tool is deleted.
  Consequence: This branch deletes src/agent_build_kit/rename_test_kinds.py, so the next release's notes would both promise the tool and announce its removal. A reader who trusts line 569 runs a module that no longer exists.
  Done when: Fold the deletion into the existing bullet: replace its last sentence ('`python -m agent_build_kit.rename_test_kinds` stays for ...') with one saying the rename tool has been removed too, and that old spellings in a planning repository are now found with `git grep` and replaced with a reviewed edit. Then drop the separate bullet at line 5, so the change has one bullet, as the changelog convention says.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/compat_names.py:41 — The comment above KIND_FORMS still says it is 'the one table the readers and the rename tool share'.
  Consequence: Group 5's Done line says 'nothing refers to them'. This comment refers to the deleted tool and tells the next reader that a second consumer of KIND_FORMS exists, which it no longer does. The new search misses it because it looks only for the module name, not for 'rename tool'.
  Done when: Reword the comment so it names only the readers, for example '# The two kinds, by the old name each had: the one table the readers share.' Running `git grep -n 'rename tool' -- src` should then return nothing.
- [1.3] tests/test_old_test_kind_names_guard.py:30 — `naming_the_tool` re-implements the file walk that `candidates(root)` in tests/old_test_kind_names.py:42 already provides, and it scans less: no root `*.md` files, no `pyproject.toml`, and it does not skip the built web bundle.
  Consequence: There are now two copies of the guard's file walk that must change together. Because this copy skips root files, a mention of `rename_test_kinds` added to README.md or AGENTS.md passes `test_no_file_of_the_repository_names_the_rename_tool`. That breaks the 'nothing refers to them' rule for exactly the files a user reads first.
  Done when: Have `naming_the_tool` iterate over `candidates(root)`, imported from tests.old_test_kind_names. The CHANGELOG stays exempt there, as it must for its history. Drop the private SCANNED/SKIPPED_PARTS walk and those imports if nothing else uses them. Add a parametrized case where the module name is written in a root `README.md` in tmp_path, and assert that it is reported as `README.md:1`.

Optional:
- [1.4] docs/runbooks/migrate-to-risk-tiered-review.md:51 — The step after the rewritten line 50 still says 'Read the preview', and the next one says 'Apply'. Both wordings came from the tool's `--dry-run` preview and apply flow, which no longer exists.
  Consequence: A person following the runbook is told to read a preview that the new instruction (git grep plus a manual edit) does not produce.
  Done when: Reword to fit the grep-and-edit flow, for example 'Read the matches. `tier 1` and `tier 2` in prose become ...' and 'Make the edit, run `openspec validate --all --strict` and `abk check`, and commit ...'.

description.summary: Deletes the test-kind rename tool and its tests, and makes the old-spelling guard fail any file that still names the tool.
changes: `python -m agent_build_kit.rename_test_kinds` and its five test files are gone. The compatibility readers in `compat_names.py` are now the only users of the `KIND_FORMS` table.
The strict old-spelling guard no longer exempts the rename tool or its tests, so an old spelling in those paths is now reported.

units.title: Calibration pools integration-test with unit-test, and the kind-listing tests name the third
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] CHANGELOG.md:5 — This branch adds a second Unreleased bullet for the integration-test change. The change already has one at CHANGELOG.md:209 ("New group tag `[integration-test]`, a label between `[unit-test]` and `[e2e-test]` ..."), written by the earlier units.
  Consequence: AGENTS.md's changelog convention says "One change is one bullet, even across several pull requests: fold later work into the bullet that already describes it instead of adding another." Right now Unreleased describes the tag twice: at line 5 and at line 209.
  Done when: Delete the new bullet at lines 5-8. Add one sentence about calibration to the end of the existing bullet at line 209, with the same two-space continuation wrapping, e.g. "Estimate calibration pools `integration-test` with `unit-test`, so samples of both feed one ratio and a unit of either is checked by it." Leave the rest of that bullet as it is.

Optional:
- [1.2] tests/config/test_test_kind_settings_aliases.py:230 — Task 4.5 asks for a test that the `unit_test_*` settings are the ones read for a unit of kind integration-test. This test only checks that those field names exist on the config models. Its last assertion (`TestTier.INTEGRATION_TEST.value == "integration-test"`) is already pinned by the TestTier tests and adds nothing here.
  Consequence: No current code picks a limit by kind (wiring.py:289 and :1276 and environment.py:101 read the `unit_test_*` limits whatever the kind), so nothing breaks today. If someone later adds a branch that picks limits by kind and leaves integration-test out, this test would still pass.
  Done when: Optional: drop the trivial last assertion. If cheap, also drive the unit-test runner's limit (`_run_limited`'s caller) for a unit of kind integration-test and assert it uses `unit_test_command_seconds`.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/joins.py:185 — When a join onto an integration-test unit is refused, the message now names the pooled calibration kind. It reads "the largest raw estimate for app unit-test ..." even though the unit being joined onto is tagged integration-test.
  Consequence: The text is accurate, because the ratio really is the unit-test one. But someone reading it may not see why their integration-test unit is called unit-test.
