description.summary: Estimate calibration treats `integration-test` units as `unit-test`, and the tests that list the test kinds now include the third kind.
changes: A new helper `pooled_kind` in `model.py` maps `integration-test` to `unit-test` and leaves every other kind unchanged.
Both calibration keys go through `pooled_kind`: the planner's `plan_kind` and `unit_size.kind_of`. Merged units of either kind feed one size ratio, and a unit of either kind is checked against it.

New tests cover the pooling in the planner, in joins and in unit size. Further tests check that the unit store, the work graph's tag parsing, the metrics ledger and the compat names accept `integration-test` as a value.
A config test pins that no setting is named for `integration-test`, and that the `unit_test_*` settings are the ones a unit of that kind reads.
The existing Unreleased changelog bullet for `[integration-test]` gains one sentence on calibration pooling.

units.title: Status, tier 2 status, graph and check show held-split waits; documents and skills describe the Split line and start gate
units.feedback:
Groups 3 and 4 are mostly in place. The status lines, the graph state and legend, the docs, the skills and the changelog bullet match the spec, and the new tests plus the leak and ecosystem guards pass (60 passed). Three things block approval. (1) The `abk e2e-test check` warning finds a unit's own tests in a way that differs from how the e2e-test run finds them, and its tests use a fake that returns a shape the real lookup never returns. (2) `abk e2e-test status` decides which units are gated with its own workspace-wide rule, not the per-repo gate the round uses. (3) A no-declared-split test that task 3.1 asks for is missing. The change's design.md still lists 'how abk tier2 check finds a unit's own tests' as UNVERIFIED. Its guess (`own_tests.py`) is not what the run uses: the run uses `touched_tests` and `_ids_for` in pipeline/wiring.py. A person should correct that line in the planning repo.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/e2e_cmd.py:54 — `unit_own_tests` diffs the default branch's current tip against the unit's branch (a two-dot tree diff through `defined_tests_in_range(checkout, default_branch, branch)`), not the point the branch forked from. It also returns bare function names, which `_split_declaration_warnings` matches with `test == own or test.endswith('::' + own)`.
  Consequence: Three wrong results. (a) Unit `feature/1` is declared `rest` and forked from main. Another unit then merges `tests/integration/test_live.py::test_acp`, marked for `acp`, into main. `abk e2e-test check` sees `test_acp` as removed in `git diff main feature/1`, so `defined_tests_in_range` counts it as one of feature/1's own tests, and the check wrongly warns 'feature group N is declared rest but its test test_acp is in acp'. `restack.py` and `wiring.py` pass the real old base, which is why they don't hit this. (b) A parametrized own test is listed by the profile as `path::test_acp[a]`. That id does not end with `::test_acp`, so a real mismatch gets no warning. (c) Bare names collide across files: a test with the same name in another file counts as the unit's own. The task asks the check to use the same own-test lookup the e2e-test run uses. The run uses `touched_tests` and `_ids_for` (pipeline/wiring.py:3262, 1504), which give file-qualified ids for added or changed tests and only for test paths, and leave deleted tests out.
  Done when: Compute the unit's own tests from the merge base of the default branch and the unit's branch (`git merge-base`, through `pipeline.shell`), not from the default branch's tip. Keep only tests that exist on the branch and sit in a profile test path (`toolchain.is_test_path`), and give them file-qualified ids in the shape the run uses (`<path>::<Class>::<test>`, relative to where the listing runs). Match a listing id to an own id after removing a trailing parameter id (`[...]`), or reuse whatever the run's narrowing relies on. Do not compare bare names. If the run's `touched_tests` cannot be pointed at a ref range as it stands, add one named helper beside it that takes a range, so the run and the check share one definition of a unit's own tests.
- [1.2] tests/cli/test_e2e_check_split_declaration.py:18 — The fake `Lookup` returns fully qualified node ids (`ACP = 'tests/integration/test_live.py::test_acp'`), but the real `unit_own_tests` returns bare names (`test_acp`). No test drives `unit_own_tests` or the real matching at all.
  Consequence: The warning tests pass through the `test == own` branch, which the real lookup never reaches. The real path (the `endswith('::')` match and the base used for the diff) is untested, so every defect in the finding above passes the suite. The fake is a stand-in at a boundary that returns what the implementation expects, not what the real lookup returns.
  Done when: Add a test that builds a real git fixture repo (neutral names, a `tmp_path` per test). Create a branch for a unit declared `rest` that adds an e2e test listed under `acp`, including a parametrized one. After the fork, commit another test listed under `acp` on the default branch. Run `cmd_e2e_check` with the default lookup and the `Pytest` listing stand-in, returning ids in the real `--collect-only` shape (`path::test_x[a]`). Assert there is exactly one warning, for the branch's own test, and none for the test that only main added. Keep the fake `Lookup` tests, but have the fake return the shape the real lookup returns.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/e2e_cmd.py:325 — `cmd_e2e_status` lists units under a held split with its own rule: `unit.unstarted and unit.split == split.name`, and `parked_on_split(unit) and split.name in unit.parked_splits`. It tests that rule against `current_holds`, which combines every repo's declarations. The round gates a unit with `_split_gates` (cli/pipeline.py:2012), which reads `repo_holds` for the unit's own repo and leaves out a split the repo no longer declares; parked units are handled by `_holds_of_parked`.
  Consequence: Example: `app` declares `acp` with `hold: true`, and `platform` declares its own `e2e_splits` with `acp` and no hold, or no longer declares `acp`. An unstarted `platform` unit in `acp` is not gated: the round starts it, and `abk status` does not list it. `abk e2e-test status` still lists it as 'not started' under `acp`. The spec says a unit whose split its repo no longer declares SHALL NOT be gated, and the listing should show the units the hold keeps from starting. The same gate predicate now exists twice, and the two copies already disagree.
  Done when: Move the per-repo gate (`_split_gates`, and `_holds_of_parked` for parked units) into a pipeline module both commands can import, e.g. a public `split_gates(config, state_dir, units)` in `pipeline/e2e_holds.py`. A pipeline module is needed because `cli/pipeline.py` already imports `e2e_cmd`. Make `gated_units`, `_split_wait_lines` and `cmd_e2e_status` all use it: 'not started' under split S lists the gated units whose gate is S, and 'parked at e2e-test' lists the parked units whose held splits for their own repo include S. Add a test with two repos where the split is held for one and not for the other (or not declared by it), asserting only the held repo's unit is listed.
- [1.4] tests/cli/test_status_split_waits.py:1 — Task 3.1 asks for a test that a workspace with no declared split prints nothing new in `abk status`. There is none.
  Consequence: A change that makes the split lines appear for repos with no declared split, for example a unit in `rest` whose last recorded wait was `split` showing 'released, starts this round', would pass the suite, although the spec says a repo that declares no split shows none of this.
  Done when: Add a test that uses an installation with no `e2e_splits` and fresh units with split `rest`, runs a round, and then runs `run_status`. Assert that no line contains 'e2e-test split'.

Optional:
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/vocabulary.py:188 — The new `if unit.id in gated` check sits between the comment about a run stopped part-way through its loop (the `paused_rework` case) and the code that comment describes.
  Consequence: The next reader takes the comment as describing the gate.
  Done when: Put the gated check above the comment, or give it its own one-line comment, so the existing comment stays attached to the `waiting_on` branch.
- [1.6] tests/cli/test_e2e_check_split_declaration.py:1 — Task 3.4 also asks this file to assert that a started unit declared `rest`, found at e2e-test to hold `acp` tests, parks for `acp` exactly as before. That path is unchanged and covered by tests/pipeline/test_e2e_split_groups.py, where units default to `rest`, but this file does not pin it.
  Consequence: Nothing the change touches can break it today. The task's checklist is just not met literally.
  Done when: Optionally add one test, or a pointer in the module docstring to the existing parking tests that cover the backstop.
- [1.7] src/agent_build_kit/cli/e2e_cmd.py:328 — `abk e2e-test status` names a unit's place as `(repo)`, while `abk status` uses `unit_label` (`repo/project`).
  Consequence: A unit in a project beside the repo root shows as `(app)` in one listing and `(app/web)` in the other.
  Done when: Optionally use `project_tag(unit.repo, unit.project)` in both lines.

description.summary: A unit in a held e2e-test split is not started, and status, tier 2 status, the graph and `abk e2e-test check` show these waits, judged against the unit's own repo.
changes: The round's gate for a held split now lives in one place, `split_gates`/`parked_holds` in pipeline/e2e_holds.py. It reads each repo's own holds, so a unit whose repo does not hold its split, or no longer declares it, is not gated.

`abk status`, the waits view and the graph show a line for each unit that a held split keeps from starting or has parked: which split, why, until when, and whether it was released and starts this round. A workspace with no declared split shows none of this.

`abk e2e-test status` lists, under each split, the units that split's hold keeps from starting and the units parked at e2e-test for it, using the same per-repo gate as the round, and names their project.

`abk e2e-test check` warns when a unit is declared in one split but its own tests are listed in another. Its own tests are the ones its branch added or changed since it forked from the default branch, as file-qualified ids with parameter ids removed, defined the same way as the e2e-test run's narrowing (`own_test_ids`).
`touched_tests` can compare a ref against a commit instead of the working tree, so code that does not run tests can read a branch's own tests.

units.title: Profiles name the agent's commands, build prompts carry them, docs describe them
units.feedback:
The implementation matches the change across all three groups. The six full prompts carry the section as a pure insertion, and the continuations, COMMIT_FIX_PROMPT and RESOLVE_PROMPT do not. The matcher moved to tool_patterns.py, and acp re-exports the same function object. The load check refuses an override the allow-list refuses, and doctor reports ok, info, FAIL and warn. I confirmed that agent_commands.refused and commands_note work with sys.modules['acp'] = None. The 96 new and guard tests pass, including the ecosystem-names and no-installation-leaks guards. What blocks approval is two test helpers the change copies instead of sharing.

Required:
- [1.1] tests/cli/test_doctor_agent_commands.py:906 — `ok_run` and `planning_with` copy the existing helpers in tests/cli/test_doctor_python_tools.py: `ok_run` at line 19 line for line, and the body of the `planning` fixture at about line 68 (the planning and app repos, CHANGELOG.md, .gitattributes, the env-sync/env-check EnvironmentConfig, the dump, render_openspec_config and skills.install), with only `**fields` added.
  Consequence: The change adds a second copy of a fake `run` and a doctor planning builder. The next time doctor needs another fake command answer or another file in the fixture app, both copies have to change together. If only one does, the other file's doctor tests start reporting unrelated FAILs or stop covering the case.
  Done when: Move `ok_run` and a planning builder that takes the RepoConfig fields (`planning_with(tmp_path, **repo_fields) -> Path`) into one shared, non-test module, for example tests/doctor_fakes.py, with no `test_*` names. Make test_doctor_python_tools.py's `planning` fixture call it, and import both in test_doctor_agent_commands.py. Neither test file defines its own copy afterwards, and both files still pass.
- [1.2] tests/agent_command_fakes.py:842 — The new tests build the same default repo four times: `repo_of(tmp_path, **fields)` returning `RepoConfig(path=tmp_path, slug="example/app", **fields)` is defined in tests/config/test_agent_commands_config.py:1114, tests/graph/test_nodes_commands_note.py:1304 and tests/pipeline/test_agent_commands_note.py:1494, and spelled inline in tests/pipeline/test_build_prompts_commands.py `python_note` and tests/pipeline/test_agent_commands_no_ecosystem.py.
  Consequence: The change brings in its own shared fakes module, tests/agent_command_fakes.py, but still copies one helper into three files plus two inline spellings. When the fixture repo needs another field (a forge, a profile), five places have to change together.
  Done when: Define `repo_of(path, **fields) -> RepoConfig` once in tests/agent_command_fakes.py, beside `command`, and import it in the three test files that define their own. Use it for the inline RepoConfig(...) in test_build_prompts_commands.py and test_agent_commands_no_ecosystem.py too. No new test file defines its own `repo_of` afterwards.

Optional:
- [1.3] tests/pipeline/test_agent_commands_note.py:1511 — The spec scenario 'Another toolchain' says a node-npm repo's section lists its npx commands. The parametrized bound test only checks the heading and the length for node-npm, so nothing asserts that the rendered note holds the node commands.
  Consequence: If the node-npm profile's commands were dropped from the note (for example by a dedupe or ordering bug that only affects the second profile), the 600-character test would still pass.
  Done when: For node-npm, also assert that `npx vitest run` and `npx vitest run <path>` appear in the note.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/agent_commands.py:399 — `_SCOPE_WORDS.get(item.scope, "one test")` and `_SHOWN.get(item.scope, "")` use a fallback to cover a scope missing from the dict: NODE_ID in the first, WHOLE in the second.
  Consequence: If a fourth scope is added, it is rendered silently as 'one test', or with `{path}` turned into an empty string, instead of failing.
  Done when: Give both dicts an entry for every AgentScope member and index them directly.

description.summary: Toolchain profiles now name the test, lint and format commands a build agent may run, each full build prompt lists them, and config loading and `abk doctor` check them against the command allow-list.
changes: Each toolchain profile declares the commands an agent may run to test, lint and format, each with a purpose and a scope (whole repo, one file, or one test). A repo can override them with `agent_commands` in abk.yaml.

The six full build prompts (tests, implement, checks, review feedback, rework, adapt) gain a bounded section listing those commands, with a placeholder shown for the file or test the agent picks. Continuation, commit-fix and resolve prompts are unchanged.

Loading abk.yaml refuses an `agent_commands` override that the command allow-list would refuse. The pattern matcher behind that check moved to a shared `tool_patterns` module, and the ACP runtime re-exports it.
`abk doctor` reports each repo's agent commands as ok, info, FAIL or warn. It flags commands that would be refused, a profile that names none, and commands that reach outside the repo.

Docs describe the new profile field and prompt section. Shared test helpers (`repo_of`, `ok_run`, `planning_with`) live in tests/agent_command_fakes.py and tests/doctor_fakes.py, so the test files do not each keep a copy.

units.title: A parent that builds nothing holds no child; repeated bounces are logged and listed as looping; docs and skills updated

description.summary: A unit's dependency on a unit the plan dropped or a person retired no longer stops, holds or pauses it, and a unit that keeps being put back from running with the same cause is logged once and listed as looping.
changes: The build's upstream check (`build_upstream_incomplete`), the branch-changing check, the follow pass and the room rule for paused units (`_parent_went_back`) skip a parent that is unplanned or retired, so it no longer stops or holds its child.

Each tick's `link_needs` removes a stored dependency, of a unit still to be built, on an unplanned or retired unit that no `Needs:` line declares, and logs `<unit>: dropped dependency <parent>: it builds nothing`.

The unit store counts consecutive short runs put back from `running` to planned or held with the same cause (`bounces`, `bounce_cause`, `bounce_at`). The count resets after a long run, a different cause, a person's requeue, review, failure or a finished state, and the fields are omitted from the file while zero.

When the count reaches `global_limits.bounce_limit` (default 3; runs shorter than `bounce_span_seconds`, default 120, count), the tick logs `is looping` once. `abk status` lists the unit under `looping:` and marks it `(looping)` in the ready queue, and an upstream_went_back note gains `held repeatedly by <parent>`. It is a notice only and holds nothing.
`requeue()` takes a `by` argument. `abk requeue` and the web UI pass `abk requeue`, which ends the unit's run of bounces and is recorded in its history; the pipeline's own requeues leave it empty.
The changelog, docs/unit-graph.md, docs/architecture.md and the abk-config and abk-pipeline skills describe the new settings, log lines and what to do about a looping unit.

units.title: Unit ids come from the groups: program-assigned ids, reuse on same groups, planner labels, stable replans and docs
units.feedback:
The id assignment (`unit_ids.py`) and how `parse_plan` uses it match the spec. The only blocker is that `abk requeue --restart` no longer gets a stuck unit going again: a person told to run it is then refused on every replan.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_ids.py:14 — A unit requeued with `--restart` (state `planned`, branch kept) is not reusable, so a replan can no longer rewrite it with the new tags; tests/cli/test_replan_started_tags.py was changed to expect the refusal instead of the old behaviour.
  Consequence: `plan_all` tells a failed or held unit whose group was retagged to run ``abk requeue --restart <id>``, which 'rebuilds it from the new tags' (cli/pipeline.py:3144). On main, the replan after the restart returned that unit's id and `upsert` rewrote its tier in place. Now `is_reusable` is false because `has_work` is true (the branch is kept). The old label `feature/1` is refused as taken. Any other label gets the fallback `feature/2`, and `upsert` then raises `GroupOwned`, which spends every attempt (`attempts: max_attempts`). The change stays stuck until tasks.md is edited, so the advertised way out is a dead end. `test_a_unit_requeued_with_restart_takes_the_new_tags_and_the_report_ends` now asserts `code == 1` and `tier == 'unit-test'`: the opposite of its name, with the old behaviour dropped and no test for it.
  Done when: When a stored unit of the change is in state `planned` and has work, and its own group set exactly equals a plan unit's, reuse its id in the exact-match step (step 1) of `assign_unit_ids`. `upsert` already keeps its branch and progress and takes the new shape, as on main. A label equal to that id need not be refused, but it may be. Restore the requeue test to its original assertions: with a reply that labels the unit anything (e.g. `retagged`) for group 1 at `e2e-test`, it gets `code == 0`, `store.get('feature/1').tier == 'e2e-test'` and `records['feature']['ok'] is True`. Add a unit test in tests/pipeline/test_unit_ids.py: a `planned` `x/1` with a branch for [1] plus a plan unit for [1] gives `x/1`. Keep the started-states guarantee: running, in-review, failed, held and merged units still keep their ids and are never matched. If this makes tests/cli/test_plan_all_group_owned.py stop colliding (the plan gives [1, 2] to a unit while a planned-with-branch `feature/1` holds exactly [1, 2]), change that test so the planner splits the groups differently (e.g. [1] and [2]), so it still tests the collision. Say in the PR body that this narrows the spec's 'no branch' condition for reuse to the `planned`-with-work restart case, so the spec can be brought in line.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/unit_ids.py:14 — `is_reusable` partly repeats `StoredUnit.unstarted` (unit_store.py:334, `state == PLANNED and not has_work`), and its `state != UnitState.RETIRED` clause can never be false after `state in (PLANNED, UNPLANNED)`.
  Consequence: If 'unstarted' changes, the two copies have to change together. The dead clause suggests a case that cannot happen.
  Done when: Write it as `(stored.unstarted or (stored.state == UNPLANNED and not stored.has_work)) and stored.id not in retired`, adjusted for the required finding above.
- [1.3] docs/architecture.md:125 — 'A refused plan keeps the unit ids returned' now means the planner's labels, not ids.
  Consequence: A reader expects the plan record's `units` to hold `<change>/<n>` ids, but after a refusal it holds labels such as `u1` (the spec's modified 'A refused plan keeps its reason' requirement says labels).
  Done when: Say 'keeps the labels the planner gave its units'.
- [1.4] tests/cli/test_replan_kept_and_refused.py:26 — Removing `with_branch(run, "feature/4", 1, 2)` leaves the docstring's second half ('the unit in the plan has work too and is not named') untested, and `"kept: feature/1" not in out` is true whatever the code does, because `feature/1` is new and has no work.
  Consequence: A regression that named a planned unit with work as 'kept' would no longer fail this test.
  Done when: Seed a planned-with-branch unit whose groups match the plan unit (once the required fix allows reusing it) and assert it is not named 'kept'. Otherwise drop the assertion and that half of the docstring.
- [1.5] tests/pipeline/test_unit_ids.py:136 — `test_a_started_units_record_is_not_touched` compares a frozen pydantic model with its own copy, so it passes whatever `assign_unit_ids` does.
  Consequence: It cannot catch a started unit being renamed or regrouped. Only the `plan_all` tests check that.
  Done when: Assert on the returned units instead: no returned unit has id `x/2` and none carries groups 3 or 4.

description.summary: Unit ids are now assigned by the program from the task groups each unit carries, not taken from the planner's reply, so a replan keeps ids stable.
changes: The planner's reply names its units with labels that are used only inside that reply. The program names each unit `<change>/<lowest group>` and rewrites `depends_on` from labels to ids (pipeline/unit_ids.py).

A plan unit whose groups exactly match those of a stored unit of the same change that is not started, or is planned with a kept branch after `abk requeue --restart`, keeps that unit's id, so a replan renumbers nothing and a restarted unit picks up the new tags.
When the rule's id is retired, started or finished, the unit takes the smallest free integer above every number the change has used, including split-suffixed ids.
A refused plan records the labels the planner gave, and running, in-review, failed, held and merged units are never renamed or given another unit's groups.
docs/architecture.md describes the new naming.

units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:2302 — `_skipped_reason` lists every touched path the runner does not collect, source files included, though its docstring and the design say it lists the touched *test* files left out.
  Consequence: `touched_tests` comes from `_changed_tests`, which reads every changed `*.py` file (wiring.py:3283), so a `def test_*` method in a source file is a touched pair. Take a unit that changes `src/app.py` to add `class Client:\n    def test_connection(self): ...` and touches no test. It now logs `e2e-test skipped: no e2e test added or changed; not collected by the suite: src/app.py`. That points a person at a source file as if it were a skipped test, and it breaks the scenario where a unit that touched no test gets the reason with nothing appended. The existing test misses this because its `src/app.py` holds only `x = 1`.
  Done when: In `left_out`, keep a path only when some toolchain in `work` says `is_test_path(path)` and none says `collects_path(path)`. Add a test to `tests/pipeline/test_own_test_ids_collected.py`: a unit whose only change is `src/app.py` with a class holding a `def test_connection(self)` method gets `scope.reason == SKIPPED` exactly.
- [1.2] tests/profiles/test_collects_path_not_is_test_path_callers.py:40 — Task 1.5 is only partly met. The unit-test step's split (`graph/nodes.py:944`, the build node's `outside_note`) has no test, and the push-gate test passes whatever predicate it is given.
  Consequence: Task 1.5 asks for a test that the push gate, verify's deploy filter and the unit-test step still treat a helper and `conftest.py` under `tests/` as test-side. The unit-test step is not exercised at all. `test_the_push_gate_classifies_a_not_collected_file_as_a_test_file` calls `classify_paths([path], PY.is_test_path)` directly. `classify_paths` already labels any path with a `tests` component as "test" through `TEST_DIR_NAMES` (commit_order.py:42), so the test would still pass if it were handed `PY.collects_path` or `lambda _: False`. It never reaches `pipeline/gate.py`, so a change of `gate.py:90` or `nodes.py:944` to `collects_path` would go through unnoticed in the nodes case.
  Done when: Add a test for the unit-test step that goes through the code `graph/nodes.py` runs. Either drive the build node's `outside_note` over a temporary git repo whose outside-session commit touches `tests/integration/replay_unit_build.py` and `tests/conftest.py`, or, if the node cannot be reached, call `outside_commits_note` with `is_test` built the way nodes.py builds it from `profiles.for_path(...)`. Assert both paths appear in the outside-tests note. For the gate, either drive `pipeline/gate.py`'s public check, or drop the claim and say in the test's docstring that for python-uv `classify_paths` already labels these paths by name. Do not keep a gate assertion that passes whatever predicate it is given.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/wiring.py:2302 — `_skipped_reason` types `work` as `Sequence[tuple[Any, Any, Any]]`, so the type checker never sees `tc.collects_path` as a profile call.
  Consequence: A rename of `collects_path` would not be caught by pyrefly at this call site. `own_test_ids` (wiring.py:3346) already types the same value as `Sequence[tuple[Path, ToolchainProfile, Any]]`.
  Done when: Type the parameter `Sequence[tuple[Path, ToolchainProfile, Any]]`, as `own_test_ids` does.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/skills/abk-pipeline/SKILL.md:280 — The abk-pipeline skill quotes the skip line, but not that it can now end with the files left out or that helpers and `conftest.py` are never named.
  Consequence: An agent reading the skill for why a unit ran nothing gets no hint that a touched helper was dropped on purpose. The docs say this; the skill an agent reads does not.

units.title: The drift test finds every live module, decides agent starts per test, and checks tags against runtimes and splits
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] tests/test_agent_start_signals.py:139 — `test_every_test_of_the_kits_live_modules_that_starts_an_agent_has_exactly_one_tag` is a word-for-word copy of the test with the same name at tests/test_live_tests_are_tagged.py:70. Both collect every live module with `inline_genitems` and assert `drift(items) == []`.
  Consequence: The branch adds a duplicate. Any change to the kit-wide check (for example, also reporting `agent_start_notes`) now has to be made in both copies, and every suite run collects the whole live tree one extra time.
  Done when: Keep exactly one kit-wide drift test. The one in tests/test_live_tests_are_tagged.py already exists, so delete the copy in tests/test_agent_start_signals.py. Task 3.4's 'real kit modules' assertion is then met by the remaining test, which now runs the per-test signals through `drift`.
- [1.2] tests/live_tag_drift.py:179 — `AgentStart.of` builds `set(callspec.params.values())`, which raises `TypeError` when a parametrised live test has an unhashable parameter value.
  Consequence: Suppose a `local_stack` module has `@pytest.mark.parametrize("argv", [["a", "b"]])` or a dict param. Then `drift()`, and with it the kit-wide test, the split test and every fixture test, crashes with `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` instead of reporting drift.
  Done when: Keep only hashable string values that name a runtime, e.g. `{v for v in callspec.params.values() if isinstance(v, str) and v in RUNTIMES}`. Add a fixture-module test in tests/test_runtime_tag_agrees_with_start.py: a correctly tagged live test parametrised with a list value, and `drifted(...)` returns `[]` without raising.
- [1.3] tests/live_tag_drift.py:244 — `agent_start_notes` is only called by its own unit test. The kit-wide drift test never reports the notes, so in the real run an unresolved fixture is still dropped without a word.
  Consequence: The design's Risks section says an unresolvable fixture is treated as not starting an agent 'and says so in a note line of the test output, not in silence'. As built, a kit test whose agent-starting fixture cannot be resolved passes untagged and nothing is printed.
  Done when: In the one remaining kit-wide test (tests/test_live_tests_are_tagged.py), emit `agent_start_notes(items)`. A `warnings.warn` per note would do, as would a single warning joining them. A note must never fail the test. Optionally, assert in the unit test that the kit-wide path warns, using a fixture module with an unresolved fixture.

Optional:
- [1.4] tests/live_tag_drift.py:163 — Protocol detection only matches the literal form `AcpRuntime().detect(...)`, where the owner is a call to `AcpRuntime`. `runtime = AcpRuntime(); runtime.list_models(...)` and a module-level `RUNTIME = AcpRuntime()` are not counted as starting an agent; the bare `AcpRuntime` name only adds the `acp` runtime and leaves `starts` false.
  Consequence: An untagged live test that holds the runtime in a variable before calling `detect`, `list_models` or `run` passes the drift test. This is the same kind of hole item 2 of the proposal set out to close, though every current kit test uses the literal form.
  Done when: Optional: count a call to a method in `PROTOCOL_METHODS` on any name bound from `AcpRuntime(...)` in the function or module, or treat any construction of `AcpRuntime` in a reached function as starting an agent. Add a fixture case for the variable form.
- [1.5] tests/live_tag_drift.py:210 — `requested_fixtures` reads pytest's private `item._fixtureinfo` and `name2fixturedefs`.
  Consequence: These are pytest internals with no compatibility promise. A pytest upgrade that renames them makes `getattr(..., None)` return None, and per-test detection then quietly stops following fixtures, so fixture-only signals are no longer seen and no test fails.
  Done when: Optional: if `_fixtureinfo` is missing for an item that has `fixturenames`, fail loudly rather than return `{}`. Or pin the behaviour with a test that fails when a fixture-borne signal is not found. The existing conftest-fixture test partly covers this.
- [1.6] tests/test_runtime_tag_agrees_with_start.py:55 — The callspec case asserts only that `runtime_acp` and the test name are in the message, not that `claude_code` is. Task 4.1 asks that each case be 'named with both runtimes', and the sibling cases do assert both.
  Consequence: Weak assertion only: if the message said something other than the runtime started, this case would still pass. Today the only message `drift` can produce for this module is the tag-against-start one.
  Done when: Add `assert "claude_code" in found[0]`.

description.summary: The live-test drift check now covers every live module in the kit and decides per test whether it starts an agent, including through fixtures. It checks each test's runtime tag against the runtime it actually starts and its parametrised split.
changes: One kit-wide test collects every live module and fails when a test that starts an agent does not carry exactly one runtime tag.
Agent starts are detected per test across the test body, the helpers it reaches and the fixtures it requests. This includes calls on a variable or module-level name that holds an `AcpRuntime(...)`.
Runtime tags are checked against the runtimes a test starts and against string values in its parametrisation. Unhashable parameter values (lists, dicts) are ignored instead of crashing the check.
A fixture that cannot be resolved is not counted as starting an agent. The kit-wide test reports it as a warning note and never fails on it.
If pytest stops exposing its fixture information, the check fails loudly instead of silently finding no fixtures.

units.title: Claude-only scenarios are listed, and the documents and changelog describe the drift test
units.feedback:
Five of the six round-1 points are done. The scrub leak is gone, and `scenarios_of`, `section_of` and `collected` each replace their copies. The docs wording on the compared tag is fixed. 1.2 is still open: the kit-level test now calls `warn_gap_list_drift`, but inside `warnings.simplefilter("error", UserWarning)`. That turns every gap-list difference back into a test failure. The 18 tests in the two touched test files pass on this branch.

Still open from earlier rounds:

That makes three statements false: the docs sentence 'A difference between this list and the tests raises a warning, not a failure' (docs/agent-runtimes.md), the changelog's 'a difference from the tests is a warning, never a failure', and the spec. Required:
- [2.1] tests/test_claude_without_acp_gap_list.py:135 — The kit-level test wraps `warn_gap_list_drift(items, DOCUMENT)` in `warnings.catch_warnings()` + `warnings.simplefilter("error", UserWarning)`, so the warning is raised as an exception and fails the test.

Round 1's done-condition said 'With `-W error::UserWarning` it passes today'. That means the test passes when someone runs it with that flag, not that the test hard-codes the error filter.

Keep the sorted and known-modules assertions. Then `uv run pytest tests/test_claude_without_acp_gap_list.py -W error::UserWarning` passes today because the lists match. units.title: Test-only groups: detection, commit-order check and push gate
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/commit_order.py:172 — `test_only_commits` matches the n-th `test:` commit to the n-th group by position only and ignores the subject's title (the docstring says "whatever the titles"). Any `test:` commit that lands at a test-only group's position is exempt from the pair rule, from the two-in-a-row rule and from the gate's red run, even when its subject names a different group.
  Consequence: Take groups [Drive (test-only), B (ordinary)] and a branch `test: B`, `feat: B`, where the build skipped Drive. `test: B` is flagged test-only, so `check_structure` passes and `check_branch` puts its sha in the `test_only` set, so B's red run is never made. A passing or never-red B test is then pushed, though the spec allows the exception only "when it is the commit of a test-only group". units.title: Cost settings, cost ledger reader and the calibrated cost fit

description.summary: Adds the settings, the ledger reader and the calibration that fit points of usage gained per dollar of recorded cost for each Claude usage window, and keeps the result in a versioned allowances file.
changes: The Claude limits take per-window `usage_estimate_basis` (`cost` or `units`, default `cost`) and `usage_estimate_intercept` (default on for the session, off for the week), plus `usage_cost_min_pairs` (8, not above `usage_allowance_window`) and `usage_cost_quantile` (0.9, in (0, 1]). Each can be set in `abk.yaml`, `abk.local.yaml` or an account's own limits block, and a bad value is refused naming the key.

The usage ledger can be read as one spend row per call (time, unit or blank, node, incremental cost, with absent, negative or non-numeric costs counted as zero). This includes calls that belong to no unit, such as plan or login refresh. The existing reader of `(time, unit)` pairs is unchanged.

For a window on the `cost` basis, each tick's calibration builds cost pairs and fits a non-negative line of points gained on recorded cost, plus hours when the intercept is on. It scales the line by a residual quantile clamped between 1 and 2 and rounds the kept figures up to 0.01. A cost pair is a gap with recorded cost whose units all have some cost, rows with no unit included.

The cost fit is adopted only when, judged walk-forward over the newest pairs, at least `usage_cost_min_pairs` gaps were judged and it has no more false allows than the flat per-unit allowance. Otherwise the window stays on `units` with a kept reason (too few pairs, too few judged, more false allows, no fit, or `basis_units`).

`usage-allowances.json` is now written as `{"version": 2, "windows": {...}}` with the basis, reason, cost figures and counts per window. A file of the previous shape is read as the flat calibration it was, and a missing, damaged or unknown-version file reads as no calibration.

description.summary: Adds the history-based usage forecast: what a unit of a given review tier is expected to cost, from the recorded calls of earlier units of that tier, plus the settings that tune it.
changes: New forecast settings in abk.yaml (config.py): a minimum number of runs before history is trusted, and the quantile used for the chance of reaching a step.

A tier's history is grouped into cells (role, node, round, model), each with a chance of being reached and a mean cost. A thin cell widens to the step's mean over all models, then to the node's mean. A step's total chance over its models never rises from one round to the next.

forecast_unit sums chance times cost over the tier's cells. It falls back to the window's flat allowance, flagged as the prior, when the tier has too few units or the window has no points-per-dollar rate.
forecast_step gives a later gate the one step it asks for, at its mean cost over every model. A step the tier never ran is priced at its node's mean, and a node it never ran at the prior.

forecast_remaining gives a running unit the expected cost of the rounds after the one it last ran, each weighted by the chance of reaching it given the unit got this far. It is zero past the last round the history recorded.
The verdict-reader guards allow the two new forecast modules to read the verdict record, since the history is grouped by planned tier.

units.title: A Needs line has a merge kind, and a merge edge holds a start until the parent merged and the next tick has it

description.summary: A `Needs:` line can now ask the dependent to wait for its parent's merge, and each dependency edge is either a review edge or a merge edge. A merge edge holds a start until the parent has merged and a later tick runs code that contains the merge.
changes: `Needs: <change> group <n> merged` is now a real merge dependency, accepted by `abk tags`/`abk check` without the old deprecation warning. A plain `Needs:` to a group in another repository is read the same way and gets an info note. `link_needs` records these targets on the unit as `merge_needs`, rebuilt from tasks.md each tick, and a replan keeps them.

New `edge_kind`/`EdgeKind`: an edge is a merge edge when it crosses repositories, when the author wrote `merged`, or when the dependent is a failed unit (or one a person requeued while it waited). Every other edge is a review edge, and a plain same-repo `Needs:` still starts on the parent's branch once the parent is in review.

Each tick writes `tick.json` (number, start time, the kit checkout and the head the process loaded, read before the planning sync). The poll records a merged unit's merge commit and the tick that saw it as `merge_sha`/`merged_tick`, and a replan keeps both.

`waiting_on` holds a merge edge until the parent has merged (or is satisfied and landed) and the merge is loaded. For a parent in the kit's own repository the merge commit must be in the tick's recorded head; for any other parent, or when either is unknown, a later tick than the one that saw the merge is enough.

Failed units, gated requeues and flake-parked units now resume only after the fix merges, not when it enters review. The status line, `abk requeue` and the send-back gate say 'to merge' for every merge edge.

units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:2348 — `note_merge_waits` prints its 'now waits ... (Needs: ... merged in tasks.md)' line at the start of every tick, and it prints it for cross-repo dependents whose `Needs:` line never said `merged`.
  Consequence: The spec (unit-scheduling, 'Existing `merged` lines delay no unit') says the *first* tick that reads a merge dependency prints the line, once. The design says it covers each live `Needs:` *merge line*. As written, it runs in every tick's first round (`first_round=True` in `_tick_with`) and walks `unit.merge_needs`, and `link_needs` (cli/pipeline.py:3784-3808) fills that from `d.merge`, which also includes plain cross-repo lines. Example: a planned `use/1` in `app` with a plain `Needs: lib group 1` on `platform` while `lib/1` is in review. Every tick logs `use/1: now waits for lib/1 to merge (Needs: ... merged in tasks.md)`. That is false twice over: the line says no `merged`, and the unit is not newly waiting, because cross-repo always waited for the merge. It also repeats every tick for as long as the parent is unmerged.
  Done when: Print the line only for a same-repo merge target (`parent.repo == unit.repo`, which is a written `merged`), and only in the tick that first records the pair. The simplest way is to emit it from `link_needs` for the targets it newly adds to `merge_needs` (`merge` minus `unit.merge_needs`) when the dependent is planned, failed or held and the parent is not `parent_landed`. That drops the `first_round` parameter and the separate step. Extend tests/cli/test_merge_need_migration_line.py: a second `tick(inst)` prints no line again, and a cross-repo dependent (parent `repo="platform"`, in review, with `merge_needs` set) prints none.
- [1.2] tests/cli/test_merge_need_migration_line.py:66 — Task 3.3's 'no unfinished unit gains a wait over the recorded units' check is missing.
  Consequence: Task 3.3 asks for a test that, over the recorded units with their `merged` lines, no unfinished unit gains a wait. That test is what pins 'Existing `merged` lines delay no unit': a merged parent with no `merge_sha`/`merged_tick` counts as loaded, and nothing is printed. Without it, a change to `merge_loaded`'s no-record rule could hold every unit behind an old `merged` line, and no test would fail.
  Done when: Add a test that loads tests/fixtures/stores/recorded_units.json (already in the repo and scrub-clean; do not copy any installation's tasks). For each planned, failed or held unit, record `waiting_on` with no tick record. Then set `merge_needs` to that unit's dependencies whose parent is `merged` (the shape of the existing `merged` lines). Assert that `waiting_on` returns the same ids for every such unit and that the migration line prints nothing.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/diagram.py:154 — The graph node adds a merge wait to units of any state, so a running or in-review unit that gained a merge `Needs:` is drawn as waiting.
  Consequence: `shown_waits` → `waiting_on` does not check the unit's state. Example: a `running` unit that gained a `Needs: p group 1 merged` line while `p/1` is in review. Task 2.5 says such a unit is not stopped, yet the graph draws it `running, waiting for p group 1 to merge (merge: the Needs: line says merged)`. That says a building unit is held when it is not. Before this branch the node carried no wait text in that state.
  Done when: Add the `dependency_wait` suffix only when `unit.state == PLANNED` (the state the `blocked` label covers). Add a test to tests/pipeline/test_diagram_merge_edges.py: a `running` unit with `merge_needs=("p/1",)` on an in-review `p/1` has a node with no `waiting for` text.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/diagram.py:151 — A failed unit waiting on a parent is drawn `failed, waiting on <id>` without the merge wording that `abk status` now gives it.
  Consequence: The spec says a wait's wording 'SHALL be the same in `abk status`, the pipeline log and the graph'. The changelog says 'a waiting node carries the same wait wording'. `_failed_waiting_lines` now appends `— waiting for fix group 1 to merge (merge: a failed unit resumes after the fix is merged)`, but the `failed_waiting` branch of the node label still shows only the ids. So the graph and status disagree for exactly the wait this change introduces.
  Done when: In the `failed_waiting` branch, append the same `dependency_wait(waits, merging=merge_parents(unit, waits, graph, repos))` text that `_failed_waiting_lines` uses, after `waiting on <ids>`. Add a test asserting a failed node waiting on an in-review same-repo parent contains `waiting for p group 1 to merge (merge: a failed unit resumes after the fix is merged)`.
- [1.5] docs/cli.md:119 — The documented history note does not match what the code writes.
  Consequence: cli.md says the note reads `requeue: its wait ended (waiting on <change> group <n> is now merged and loaded by tick <number>)`. `_requeue_ended_wait` (cli/pipeline.py:2439) writes `..., loaded by tick N`, and tests/cli/test_wait_ended_merge_need.py asserts the comma form, which is also the form task 3.1 gives. Someone searching unit history for the documented text finds nothing.
  Done when: Change the documented note to `requeue: its wait ended (waiting on <change> group <n> is now merged, loaded by tick <number>)`.

Optional:
- [1.6] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/diagram.py:266 — The graph legend still says a `needs` edge is released once the parent is in review (same repo) or merged (other repo). Both halves are now wrong in some cases.
  Consequence: A cross-repo `Needs:` is now always in `merge_needs`, so it is drawn `needs, merge`, never plain `needs`; the '(other repo)' case of the `needs` label no longer occurs. Separately, a failed unit's plain `Needs:` edge is drawn `==>|needs|` but waits for the merge, not for review.
  Done when: Reword the `needs` sentence: a `needs` edge releases a planned dependent once the same-repo parent is in review, and a failed dependent waits for the merge whatever the label says. Leave cross-repo to the `needs, merge` sentence.

description.summary: A `Needs:` line ending in `merged` holds its dependent until the parent has merged and a later tick has loaded that merge, and status, logs and the graph show the two kinds of dependency edge.
changes: A same-repo `Needs: <change> group <n> merged` line records a merge dependency. The dependent waits until the parent has merged and the next tick runs code that contains the merge, not just until the parent is in review.
A failed unit that waits on a parent resumes only after that parent's merge is loaded, and its history note reads `requeue: its wait ended (waiting on ... is now merged, loaded by tick N)`.

Linking prints one line, the first time it records a pair, for each planned, failed or held unit that now waits for an unmerged same-repo parent. It does not print for running units, cross-repo dependents or parents that have already merged, and old `merged` lines over recorded units delay nothing.

The graph draws a `Needs:` merge dependency as a `needs, merge` edge and an implicit cross-repo one as a dashed `merge` edge. Planned and failed nodes carry the same wait wording `abk status` gives, and running units are not drawn as waiting.
The docs, skills and changelog describe the two kinds of edge and when each releases its dependent.

units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/stack_runner.py:1506 — `commit_built` is built in wiring.py, but the runner never gets it: the runner type has no `commit_built` field and the runner assembly at wiring.py:3833 does not pass `build_commit_built(...)`.
  Consequence: Task 1.4 says to "expose it on the runner", and the group's Done-when says "the runner has `commit_built`". As written, nothing the graph can reach makes an empty marked commit. Group 2's `implement`/`stub_checks` code, which calls the runner's method, would have nothing to call and would have to add this wiring itself, outside the unit that owns it.
  Done when: Add a field `commit_built: Callable[..., int]` beside `commit` on the runner type in stack_runner.py. Give it a default, as `branch_subjects` has, so existing fakes keep building. Pass `commit_built=build_commit_built(unit_id=unit.id)` next to `commit=build_commit(...)` at wiring.py:3833. Add a test that the assembled runner's `commit_built`, called over a temporary repo, makes an empty commit carrying `Unit: <unit id>` and `Already-built: yes`. Simplest is to extend an existing test of the runner assembly; otherwise assert the field is set and is not the default.

Optional:
- [1.2] tests/pipeline/test_commit_order_recorded_built.py:90 — The gate test checks only `profile.cleans` to show no run is made for the empty `test:` commit. It never checks `profile.reads`, which records red-run readings.
  Consequence: Task 1.3 asks that no clean *or* red run be made for the empty `test:`. A gate that skipped the clean command for an empty tests commit but still ran and read the red command would still pass.
  Done when: In this test and the test-only test at line 99, also assert `profile.reads == [True]`, i.e. one stubbed red reading, for the real `test: G3` only.

description.summary: Lets a unit record a task group that an earlier group's work already built as an empty commit marked `Already-built: yes`. The push gate and a restack both accept such commits.
changes: A new commit builder, `build_commit_built`, makes an empty commit that carries the unit's `Unit:` trailer plus an `Already-built: yes` trailer. Hooks run, the gate does not, and there is one attempt; a rejected commit raises `CommitRejected`.

The assembled unit runner exposes this as `commit_built(message, *, cwd)`, so later build steps can mark a group as already built. The field defaults to a no-op that returns 0, so existing runner fakes keep working.

The commit-order gate accepts an empty, marked pair of `test:` and `feat:` commits after a real one, and also accepts a test-only group's empty marked `test:` commit with no implementation commit. It runs no red check on the empty commits.
A restack keeps the empty marked commits, with their subjects and trailers.
New tests cover the gate's handling, the restack, and the assembled runner making a real empty marked commit in a git repo.

units.title: A stubbed build records a group its agents left nothing to commit for, when its tests pass
units.feedback:
Optional:
- [1.1] tests/graph/test_test_only_group_built.py:107 — The 'setting off' test uses a fake whose agents commit a pair every time, so its implementation never 'commits nothing after a real tests commit', which is the case the spec names.
  Consequence: `built_unstubbed` (tests/graph/test_per_group_unstubbed.py:33) runs `with_three_groups`, whose tests and implementation agents both write files. `record_built` is never reached with `made == 0`. If the `step is None` guard in `record_built` (nodes.py:1515) were dropped, or the record ran with the setting off, `off.messages` would still hold no `Already-built` and `commit_built:test` would still be absent. The test passes whatever the code does for the spec scenario 'builders.per_group_commits off and a unit whose implementation agent commits nothing after a real tests commit'.
  Done when: Build the setting-off case with `per_group_commits` false, a real tests commit and an implementation agent that leaves nothing to commit. For example, use the branch fakes with `activate_with(builders={"per_group_commits": False})` and `no_commit_for` naming the unit's groups as the unstubbed prompt names them ("1, 2"), or give the unstubbed fake an option to skip the implementation write. Assert that no commit message carries `Already-built`, that `commit_built:test`/`commit_built:feat` are not in the events, that no `unit-test:whole_repo` run is made by the record, and that the outcome is what the old build gives for that branch. Keep the stubbed 'on' case beside it.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1546 — `tests_account` is added to `UnitRun`, set by `tests`, reset in the fresh update and passed into `record_built` from `stub_checks`, but it is never written. `record_built` uses `account` only when `not step.test_only`, and that is exactly when the value it got from `stub_checks` is ignored.
  Consequence: The new state field and its comment ('kept for a test-only group's record', state.py:147) claim the test-only `test:` commit keeps the tests agent's account. The design's test-only bullet says the same: 'Same marker, same account in the body (the tests agent's message here)'. In fact the empty `test: G2` body has no account. Every stubbed tests run also checkpoints the full agent message into graph state for nothing.
  Done when: Write the account in one place for both kinds of group. For a test-only group, the empty marked `test:` body holds the redacted account, cut to `ACCOUNT_LIMIT`, under `ACCOUNT_HEADING`, built by the same code that builds the `feat:` body (one small private helper, not two copies). For a non-test-only group, the `test:` commit stays without it. Add an assertion to `test_a_test_only_group_with_nothing_to_commit_and_passing_tests_is_recorded_empty` that `messages(repo)[-1]` holds the tests agent's last message under the heading. To do that, let `OnBranch.accounts` answer for `claude:tests` too, or add a `tests_accounts` mapping. If the account is instead meant to be dropped for test-only groups, remove `tests_account` from `UnitRun`, `tests`, `stub_checks` and the fresh update, and fix the state comment. The field must not stay half-wired.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1496 — The change adds two more copies of `group_progress(r.branch_subjects(tree, ref), [s.title for s in steps], [s.test_only for s in steps])`, in `half_recorded` (1496) and `record_built` (1520), beside the existing ones in `resumed` (1131) and `unpaired` (1480). `record_built` also computes it twice per call, once through `half_recorded`.
  Consequence: Four copies of how the branch's subjects map to group progress now have to change together. A change to how a group is matched (for example, the title list or the test-only flags) made in one copy and not the others would make resume, the pair count and the recorded-group decision disagree about which group the branch is on. Avoiding that disagreement is the reason the design gave for using one reading rule.
  Done when: Add one private method on `BuildPath`, e.g. `branch_progress(ref) -> GroupProgress`, that reads the group steps and branch subjects once and calls `group_progress`. Use it in `resumed`, `unpaired`, `half_recorded` and `record_built`. Have `record_built` compute it once and derive both the resume test and the `done`/`tests_made` checks from that value, for example by passing the progress into `half_recorded` or inlining the tip check `recorded_built(tree, r.head(tree))`.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1537 — `record_built` repeats the `unit_test` node's failure path (nodes.py:2172-2180): the environment re-check after a failed run, `self.say(output)`, then `r.store.set_feedback(unit.id, f"{UNIT_TEST_FAILED}\n{output}".strip(), source=FeedbackSource.UNIT_TEST)`.
  Consequence: Two copies now define what a failed unit-test run saves for the agent and how an environment fault is told apart from a failure. A change to the feedback format or source in `unit_test` would leave the recorded-group stop saving the old one, so a retried unit would be shown different feedback depending on which path failed. The copy already differs: `unit_test` counts the failure with `record_check_failure` (the `abk.checks.failures` metric) and this path does not.
  Done when: Extract one private method used by both, e.g. `failed_unit_test(output) -> Update | None`. It returns `self.blocked(...)` when `environment_problem()` reports a fault, and otherwise says the output and saves the `UNIT_TEST` feedback, returning None so each caller then picks its own stop: `unit-test failed` or rebase in `unit_test`, the pair message in `record_built`. Decide in that one place whether the metric is counted; counting it in both is the consistent choice. The existing tests of the unit_test node and test_per_group_built_pair_checked.py must pass unchanged.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/graph/nodes.py:1514 — `record_built` calls `half_recorded` (a `git log` of the branch's subjects plus a `recorded_built` read of the tip) before its cheap early returns (`step is None`, `made`), so every group of every stubbed build pays those git calls even when the commit step just made a commit.
  Consequence: This is extra git work on the common path (a group that committed its pair) that is never used. It is not a correctness problem.
  Done when: Return on `step is None or made` first, then on `not r.branch_commits(...)`, and only then read the progress and the tip (this falls out of the single `branch_progress` read above).

description.summary: In a stubbed per-group build, a group whose agents leave nothing to commit is now recorded on the branch as empty commits marked `Already-built: yes`, but only after the whole repository's unit tests pass. Before, the unit stopped as missing work.
changes: A test-only group in that situation is recorded with one empty marked `test:` commit and no `feat:`. That commit holds the tests agent's account.
The builder's account of why nothing was needed is kept in the recorded commit under the heading `Already built, the builder's account:`. Secrets are redacted and it is cut to 2000 characters.

A run killed between the two empty commits resumes at that group's implementation step and records only the missing `feat:`. Reading how far the branch has got and handling a failed unit-test run are each done in one shared place in `graph/nodes.py`.

units.title: The documents and the changelog say a built group is recorded with an empty pair

description.summary: When a stubbed build's agents leave nothing to commit for a group because the work is already built, the build now records that group instead of stopping, and the documents and changelog describe this.
changes: When a group's agents leave nothing to commit and the whole-repository unit tests pass, the stubbed build records the group as an empty `test:`/`feat:` commit pair marked `Already-built: yes`, and the agent's account goes in the `feat:` body. If those tests fail, the unit still stops, so a forgotten implementation is still caught.
A test-only group with nothing to commit is recorded as one empty `test:` commit marked `Already-built: yes` that holds the agent's account.
docs/architecture.md and the `stub_checks` and `implement` rows of docs/unit-graph.md describe the recorded empty commits, including the single-commit case for test-only groups.
The Unreleased changelog has one bullet for this behaviour: what is recorded, that a restack keeps the record and a squash merge drops it, and that a forgotten implementation still stops the unit.
Tests check the documents' wording, and the changelog-bullet parsing they use now lives in one shared helper, tests/doc_text.py.

units.title: CI installs the OpenSpec CLI from a lockfile and integration tests run the installed binary
CI npm fetch gets longer timeouts and the vitest test gets its own time limit
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] docs/agent-runtimes.md:887 — The docs on the test time limit still say every test without the `local_stack` marker gets `--test-time-limit` seconds. The new `time_limit(<seconds>)` marker is not mentioned here or in docs/architecture.md:1307-1311.
  Consequence: docs/agent-runtimes.md:887 says "A test without the `local_stack` marker has `--test-time-limit` seconds (default 60)". docs/architecture.md:1308 says the same: "`--test-time-limit` (sixty seconds) for a test without the `local_stack` marker". Both are now false for a test marked `time_limit(180)`, such as the vitest integration test, which gets 180 seconds. Anyone who reads these docs to find out why a slow test is not cut off at 60 seconds will not learn that the marker exists.
  Done when: In both places, add one sentence saying that a test without `local_stack` that is marked `time_limit(<seconds>)` gets that many seconds in place of `--test-time-limit`. Say also that a `local_stack` test keeps the e2e limit even when it carries the marker, and that the marker is for a test whose time is outside its control, such as a download. This matches the `tests/time_limit.py` docstring and the pyproject marker description.

Optional:
- [1.2] tests/time_limit.py:66 — `float(own.args[0])` assumes the marker always has one positional argument.
  Consequence: A test written `@pytest.mark.time_limit` with no argument, or `@pytest.mark.time_limit(seconds=180)` (the pyproject marker text spells the parameter `seconds`), raises IndexError inside the setup/call/teardown hook wrapper. That shows up as an internal error, not a clear message.
  Done when: Read `own.kwargs.get("seconds", own.args[0] if own.args else None)`. When there is no value, fail with a message that names the marker. Or keep positional-only and check for the missing argument with a clear error.
- [1.3] tests/test_vitest_test_time_limit.py:18 — This test nests an in-process `pytest.main` with a hand-written `Collected` plugin to read each item's marker. The repo already collects items with pytester for marker checks: `tests/runtime_tag_collection.py:37-46` uses `pytester.inline_genitems`.
  Consequence: That makes two ways of collecting items to inspect their markers. The nested `pytest.main` also shares the outer process's plugin and module state without the isolation pytester provides.
  Done when: Optionally, use `pytester.inline_genitems(str(VITEST_TEST), "-m", "integration")` (or `runpytest` for the strict-markers exit code) and assert `get_closest_marker("time_limit").args == (180,)` on each item.
- [1.4] CHANGELOG.md:8 — The bullet says "CI's npm fetches wait up to 300 seconds per attempt". Only the OpenSpec CLI fetch has a 300-second per-attempt limit. The vitest download inside the test has 180 seconds and no attempts.
  Consequence: A reader may think every npm download in CI now gets 300 seconds per attempt.
  Done when: Say instead: "CI's fetch of the OpenSpec CLI waits up to 300 seconds per attempt and the step allows 20 minutes".
- [1.5] tests/test_marked_time_limit.py:34 — Task 2.1 asked for these scenarios in tests/test_e2e_time_limit.py. Three of them were put in a new file that imports `SPIN` and `run_child` from that test module. Also, `test_a_marked_test_runs_past_the_default_and_passes` only checks that failure text is absent; it never checks that the test passed.
  Consequence: If the marked test errored or was not collected, `test_a_marked_test_runs_past_the_default_and_passes` would still pass. The third test's "1 passed" check covers this today, but only indirectly.
  Done when: Optionally, assert in that test that `PASSED test_child.py::test_marked_runs_past_the_default` appears (run the child with `-rA` or `-v`), or check the passed count directly.

description.summary: Gives the OpenSpec CLI fetch in CI longer timeouts and lets a test carry its own time limit, so a slow npm registry no longer fails CI or the vitest integration test.
changes: CI's OpenSpec CLI fetch (.github/scripts/warm-openspec.sh) gives each attempt 300 seconds instead of 120. OPENSPEC_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT can override this. The workflow step's limit goes from 10 to 20 minutes.

A test can be marked `@pytest.mark.time_limit(<seconds>)`, with the seconds given by position or as `seconds=`, to get that limit in place of `--test-time-limit`. A local_stack test keeps the e2e limit even with the marker, and a marker with no value fails the test with a clear message.
The marker is registered in pyproject.toml, and the vitest integration test that downloads vitest carries `time_limit(180)`.
New tests cover the per-test limit, the e2e precedence and the vitest test's marker. tests/test_ci_openspec_step.py checks the new CI limits.
The changelog and the time-limit sections of docs/agent-runtimes.md and docs/architecture.md describe the marker and the new CI fetch limits.

units.title: Make test_one_project_starts_its_next_unit_as_one_of_its_builds_ends_and_the_other_does_not deterministic
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] tests/cli/test_tick_scheduling_projects_starved.py:1 — The new test only zeroes `WAIT`, which the refill test no longer reads after the fix, but its docstring says it runs out every bound at once. It also passes `raising=False`, so it quietly does nothing if `WAIT` is renamed or removed.
  Consequence: The docstring says 'With every bound run out at once, that test must still give the same result', and that is false. `HANG_GUARD` is now the only bound the refill test reads, and setting it to 0 makes the test fail, because `next_started.wait(0)` returns False and `at_release` is captured before web5 starts. A reader will think the test shows the refill test holds up when all its time bounds run out, when it only shows that the refill test no longer reads `WAIT`. `WAIT` is still in the module only because `test_a_pass_starts_four_units_of_each_project_with_four_workers` uses it. If that test is later fixed and `WAIT` removed, `monkeypatch.setattr(scheduling, "WAIT", 0, raising=False)` does nothing and the file just runs the refill test a second time, still green and now guarding nothing.
  Done when: Remove `raising=False`, so the setattr fails loudly if `WAIT` goes away. Rewrite the docstring to say what the test actually pins: the refill test's result does not depend on `WAIT`, the short per-build bound whose running out under load used to look like the wrong project being refilled. Name `HANG_GUARD` as the one bound left, kept only so a hang ends. Do not claim that every bound is run out.

Optional:
- [1.2] tests/cli/test_tick_scheduling_projects.py:80 — The sibling test `test_a_pass_starts_four_units_of_each_project_with_four_workers` still ends each build after `everyone.wait(WAIT)` with `WAIT = 5`, which is the same clock-bounded pattern this unit removed from the refill test.
  Consequence: On a loaded machine where all eight builds do not arrive within 5 s, the earliest ones time out and leave `active`. `len(active)` never reaches `2 * WORKERS`, `peak` stays empty, and the test fails with 'only N of 8 units were building at once' even though the pass behaved correctly. This unit covers only the refill test, so the fix here is optional.
  Done when: Bound that wait with `HANG_GUARD` as well. It only waits on the `everyone` event, so a long bound changes nothing for a correct pass. Then `WAIT` can be removed.
- [1.3] tests/cli/test_tick_scheduling_projects_starved.py:25 — The new test copies the body of the target module's autouse `isolated` fixture and its `builder` fixture (`isolate(monkeypatch)`, `REFRESH_SECONDS = 0.05`, `install_builder(...)`) instead of reusing them.
  Consequence: If the scheduling module's isolation setup changes, for example a different refresh interval, the starved test keeps running the refill test under the old setup, and the two files have to be changed together.
  Done when: Import the `isolated` and `builder` fixtures from `tests.cli.test_tick_scheduling_projects` (with the `# noqa: F401 — fixture` import used in `tests/tracks/test_runner_network_outage.py:11`) and request them, rather than repeating their bodies.

description.summary: Makes the project-refill scheduling test deterministic: it waits on events instead of a short clock bound, so on a loaded machine it can no longer look as if the wrong project was refilled.
changes: The refill test (one project starts its next unit as one of its builds ends, and the other project does not) now waits on events and a refresh count. It no longer waits on the 5-second `WAIT`.
Adds a `HANG_GUARD` constant (120 s). It is the only time bound the refill test keeps, and it is there only so a hang ends; it never decides the result.

Adds tests/cli/test_tick_scheduling_projects_starved.py. It sets `WAIT` to zero and runs the refill test again, which pins that the refill test's result does not depend on `WAIT`. It reuses the sibling module's `builder` and `isolated` fixtures, and it fails loudly if `WAIT` is renamed or removed.

units.title: The text move lifts machine settings into abk.local.yaml
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/config_migrate_machine.py:164 — `_lift` finds the end of a moved setting with `node_end(...)` and leaves out `beside_dash=True`. A list-valued machine setting whose items are written as dashes at the key's own column therefore keeps its items behind in abk.yaml, and the move is refused.
  Consequence: This layout is valid YAML and is what PyYAML's default dump writes. With `runtimes:
  claude_code:
    command:
    - /opt/c/bin/claude
    - -p
    models:
      build: x
`, or a `verify.env.TOKEN.argv:` whose `- ~/bin/get` items sit at the `argv` column, only the `command:`/`argv:` line is lifted. The `- ...` lines are left under the parent, and `move_machine_settings` raises `abk.yaml: the new text would not parse`. I reproduced both cases. The spec moves `runtimes.<name>.command`, `policy_fix` and `verify.env.<NAME>.argv`, and all three are lists (machine_settings.py:42 and 51), so a valid file is wrongly refused.
  Done when: In `_lift`, call `node_end(lines, key.start_mark.line, key.start_mark.column, beside_dash=True)`, as `runtimes/policy_apply.py:313` already does. Add a test in tests/test_config_migrate_machine_move.py: an absolute `runtimes.claude_code.command` and a `verify.env.TOKEN.argv` holding a home path, each written as a block sequence with dashes at the key's column, with a sibling key after each. Assert that the whole sequence (key line and every dash line) is in the local text at the local depth, that the siblings stay byte for byte in abk.yaml, and that `merged(new) == merged(old)`.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/config_migrate_machine.py:247 — The line ending for the lines put into abk.local.yaml is taken from the tracked text. An existing local file with different line endings comes out with mixed endings.
  Consequence: With a CRLF abk.yaml `planning:
  worktree_root: ~/w
` and an LF local `repos:
  app:
    account: me
`, the new local text is `repos:
  app:
    account: me
planning:
  worktree_root: ~/w
` (reproduced). LF and CRLF lines end up in the person's own file. The reverse case (LF abk.yaml, CRLF local) mixes the same way. The spec ties the abk.yaml line ending only to a new local file ('the new local file's lines use CRLF'). An existing file should keep its own convention.
  Done when: Take the local `eol` from `request.local_text` when that text holds a line ending (`"
" if "
" in local_text else "
"`), and fall back to the tracked text's ending when the local text is None or has no newline. Pass that to `_place`. Add a test in tests/test_config_migrate_machine_place.py: a CRLF tracked text with an LF local text gives a new local text with no ``, and an LF tracked text with a CRLF local text gives a new local text whose every line ends `
`.
- [1.3] tests/test_config_migrate_machine_verified.py:46 — The refusal tests call `check_move` directly, so nothing proves that `move_machine_settings` runs the check before it returns. Task 2.6 asks for a stubbed placement.

A rework that drops or reorders the in-memory check would ship a move that can change the merged configuration, and no test would fail. That is the spec's 'compared in memory before anything is written ... SHALL be refused'.
  Done when: Add a test that runs `move_machine_settings` with a broken placement and expects the refusal. Monkeypatch a public name the move calls, such as `agent_build_kit.config_migrate_machine.shifted` or `insert_lines`, with a wrapper that drops a line, changes the value or adds a key. Assert that `ConfigMigrateError` is raised naming the differing key and that no result is returned. Cover the three cases task 2.6 lists. The direct `check_move` tests can stay.

- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/config_migrate_lines.py:660 — `shifted` with a negative shift slices off a fixed number of characters. A carried comment line indented less than the shift loses its own text, for example a column-0 `# note here` above an 8-space key moved to depth 4.

# note here

` is refused with `abk.local.yaml: the new text would not parse` because the comment became `te here`. I reproduced this. The check catches it, so no data is lost, but a valid file is refused with a misleading message. The same slice is used by `_move_models`.

- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/config_migrate_machine.py:189 — A parent the local file lacks is always written with `_FRESH_STEP = 2`, even when the local file's existing blocks are indented by 4.

`, the moved `repos.app.path` is added as `repos:

description.summary: Machine-specific settings (absolute or home paths, runtime commands, credential argv) move out of the tracked abk.yaml into abk.local.yaml by editing lines, and a move that would change the merged configuration is refused.
changes: A machine setting is cut out of abk.yaml together with its comments and nested lines, including list items written as dashes at the key's own column, and every other byte of the file stays as it was.

The setting is put into abk.local.yaml under the deepest parent the local file already has. Any parent it lacks is written in, indented the way the local file's existing blocks are, and a comment that sits less indented than the shift keeps its text.
An existing local file keeps its own line ending. A new local file takes the tracked file's line ending.
A setting the local file already sets stays in abk.yaml and is reported as a conflict. Layouts that cannot be edited by lines, such as flow style or several documents, are refused.
Before anything is returned, the old and new texts are merged in memory and compared, and a move that would drop, change or add a value is refused, naming the key.

units.title: A profile declares how its fixers are applied, and the runner applies them to the unit's own files

description.summary: Toolchain profiles can declare how their formatters and auto-fixers are applied, and the unit runner applies them to the unit's own changed files before a commit.
changes: A toolchain profile can provide `fix_command(files)`, the argv that applies its fixers. python-uv runs its pre-commit hooks, and node-npm runs `oxfmt` and then `oxlint --fix` over source files. A profile without it gets no fixer pass.
A repo can override the profile with `repos.<name>.tests.fix_command`. Unset follows the profile and `[]` turns the pass off. The setting is documented in docs/configuration.md.

The runner's fixer pass is given only the unit's modified and untracked files, per project, run in each project's directory. Deleted files are left out, and a renamed file is passed under its new name only.
Protected files are never passed to the fixers. If a command rewrites one, it is restored, and if a command creates one, it is removed. Both are reported.
The pass ignores exit status, reports the files it changed, never runs the type check, and makes a second pass only when the first changed something.

units.title: The estimate adds recorded cost, with the flat allowance where cost is unknown

description.summary: The usage guard's estimate can now add the cost recorded since a reading, at the window's learned points per dollar, and count the flat per-unit allowance only for units whose cost is not yet known.
changes: When a window's kept calibration holds an adopted cost fit, its estimate is the reading plus points-per-dollar times the cost of every ledger row of the account since the reading, with or without a unit, plus the per-hour intercept times the hours since the reading.

Units admitted on an estimate that have no ledger row yet, and units whose rows carry no cost, are counted at the window's flat allowance, and a unit that has a costed row is counted by its cost alone.
A window that has reset since the reading counts its climb plus the cost recorded since the reset, with no intercept.

A window with no adopted fit, a missing, damaged, old-shape or unknown-version calibration file, `usage_estimate_basis: units`, or calibration turned off keeps exactly the units-based estimate it had before, and each window is decided separately.

The reason line for a cost window says how much cost was counted and how many units were not yet recorded (`~69% estimated (61% read + 8% spent from $1.45 recorded)`), and the `abk status` estimate line shows the same text.
`decide_start` accepts a `step` and records it for an admitted unit under `estimate_steps` beside the list of admitted units, which is unchanged, and the start cap still counts units.

The estimator already has this test at src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_guard.py:1277-1283.

A window configured with `usage_estimate_basis: units` prints its flat allowance line unchanged, even when the kept calibration holds a cost fit.

units.title: Running units and due plan calls and tracks reserve what they will cost

description.summary: The usage guard's estimate now counts a running unit at what is left of its current step, and reserves the cost of track runs due before the window resets, from a forecast record of admitted steps and the installed track timers.
changes: When the guard admits a start for a known step and round, it appends a step row to a forecast record (`usage-forecasts.jsonl`) once per ask. The `usage_forecast` setting turns this off, and a cut-off last line is repaired before appending.

In a cost-basis estimate, a unit admitted on an estimate that has not yet written a ledger row is counted at the unfinished share of its step's mean cost, with a floor of 10%. A unit whose step has no costed history still counts at the flat allowance.
Track timers are read from `systemctl --user show`, including `LoadState`. A timer that is not installed is reported as missing, and none installed means the timers were not read.
A track whose timer fires before the reset, or that fired within three mean durations and has written no ledger row yet, reserves its node's mean cost (plus the propose step where it applies).
One `mean_cost` helper gives the mean incremental cost of a node, and of a round when one is given, for both the running remainders and the reservations; zero and missing costs are left out.
