units.title: The start decision applies the forecast and says what dominates
units.feedback:
Group 4's gate, track and estimate paths are wired and their tests pass: the four new test files, tests/pipeline -k usage/verdict/gate (1038 passed) and tests/graph, tests/tracks and tests/cli (3197 passed). Two parts of what the spec counts as 'the forecast' never reach the live decision. The planner's own ask is not forecast, and the plan and propose reservations are switched off where forecast_ask calls reserve(). Both are below. Nothing here belongs to groups 5 to 7.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/cli/pipeline.py:1788 — The planner's ask is never forecast in production. The round-level ask passes only `_lowest_tier(startable)` and never says that planning is due, and no caller anywhere passes `step="plan"` to `decide_start`. The test for the planner (`test_the_planner_s_ask_is_forecast_as_one_call_at_its_mean`) calls `decide_start(step="plan")` directly, so it passes whatever the round does.
  Consequence: Take a tick where `_needs_planning` is true, no unit can start, the session reading is 67% against a threshold of 80, and the `plan` cell costs $4 (10 points). `_lowest_tier([])` is None, so the Ask carries no tier, no lines and no step, `ask.forecast` is False, and the plan call is allowed. The spec (usage-pause, 'A track or plan ask SHALL itself be forecast as one call at its mean cost and judged like a unit') and task 4.4 say it is refused. When there are startable units as well, only the cheapest unit is forecast and the plan call adds nothing.
  Done when: When `planning` is true, the round's ask in `_may_build` forecasts the plan call. With no startable unit, the ask is `step="plan"`, its overhead forecast. With startable units, the plan call's mean is added to the lowest tier's forecast, for example through the plan reservation in the next finding. Replace or extend the planner test in tests/pipeline/test_usage_forecast_asks.py so it drives `cli.run_round` with a change to plan and a `plan` cell at $4.00 at 67%: the round is refused, the paused marker is written, and the reason names `plan`.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_forecast_ask.py:162 — `forecast_ask` always calls `reserve(..., plan_due=False, proposing=())`. A due plan call and a track's `track_propose` are therefore never reserved in any decision. Nothing in src/ sets either value; the only uses are this call and the reservations module.
  Consequence: Take the spec scenario 'A plan call due': a change to plan and a `plan` cell at $0.20. Group 3 computes the reservation, but the start decision never reserves those points for a unit's ask. Likewise, the improve track's timer reserves `track_health`/`track_improve` but never `track_propose`. The spec ('The guard SHALL reserve ... a plan call that is due ... `track_propose` being included with a track that proposes', which the refusal requirement counts in 'estimate plus the forecast of the unit, the running units' remainders and the reservations') is false for the live guard.
  Done when: Carry whether a plan call is due and which tracks propose into `forecast_ask`, for example as fields on `Ask` that the round-level ask sets from `_needs_planning`, with the proposing tracks taken from the track runner's own knowledge of which phases propose rather than hard-coded. Pass them through to `reserve`. Add a test through `decide_start` (or `run_round`) where a `plan` cell of $2.00 is due at 70%: an `auto` unit forecast at 2.5 points is refused, its reason names `plan reservation`, and it is allowed when no change is due.

Optional:
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_forecast_ask.py:259 — The subject of a track's forecast reads as a unit. `ask.unit` is `track:health`, so the refusal says 'unit track:health forecast 10.0% session'.
  Consequence: A person reading a track's refusal is told that a unit named `track:health` was forecast.
  Done when: Name an overhead ask by its step (for example 'track_health forecast …'), and keep 'unit <id>' for a unit's ask.
- [1.4] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_guard.py:436 — On a live or held reading, `_forecasted` builds `WindowEstimate(spent_pct=0.0)` and joins its `.text` into the reason. A live refusal therefore reads 'session ~70% estimated (70% read + 0% spent) + 8.6% forecast'.
  Consequence: A refusal on a fresh reading claims to be an estimate, which misleads whoever reads why a unit paused.
  Done when: Give the reading-path text without the 'estimated (… read + 0% spent)' part, for example 'session 70% read + 8.6% forecast is not 5 points under 80%'.
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/usage_guard.py:389 — Every gate ask that is forecast now re-reads the whole ledger, the verdict file and the forecast record, and runs `systemctl --user show` once per track (three processes) in `_ahead`. Before this change a gate on a live reading read none of these.
  Consequence: As the ledger grows, each agent step's gate gets slower and spawns three subprocesses. This is not wrong, but it costs time on every step.
  Done when: Optional: read the timers only when some window has a future `resets_at`, and consider caching the history per tick.

description.summary: The usage guard's start decision now applies the usage forecast in the live round, track and gate paths: it adds the due plan call and the tracks that will fire before the window resets, and a refusal says which part of the forecast is largest.
changes: Each round asks the guard for the lowest review tier that could start, and says when a plan call is due. With no unit to start, the plan call itself is forecast as one call at its mean cost, and the round pauses when that call would not fit.

A plan call that is due is reserved beside a unit's own forecast. A track that goes on to propose (improve, recommend) reserves its `track_propose` call as well; which tracks propose comes from one shared tuple that the track runner also dispatches from.

A refusal names its subject correctly: a track or planner call by its step, a unit by its id and tier. It also says which contribution (the unit's own forecast, a running unit, a reservation) is largest.
A decision made on a live reading reads 'N% read + X% forecast' instead of calling the reading an estimate.
The track timers are read only when some window has a reset still ahead, since nothing can be reserved otherwise.

units.title: abk config --migrate moves machine settings, with --include-defaults, and refuses or no-ops safely
units.feedback:
Groups 4 and 5 are built as the tasks describe, and the 142 config-migrate and doctor tests I ran pass. What blocks approval is four duplicates the branch adds, each a small local fix. The changelog bullet belongs to group 6. That later unit should fold it into the earlier `machine keys` bullet of this same change, because the repo's changelog rule is one bullet per change. That is not required of this unit.

Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/config_migrate_write.py:58 — `ignore_diff` recomputes the text that `append_missing_lines` (`src/agent_build_kit/pipeline/file_lock.py:84-92`) will write. It copies the separator rule and the 'one name per line plus newline' tail.
  Consequence: Two copies of how `.gitignore` grows have to change together, and they already differ. `append_missing_lines` skips a line that is already in the file as text. `ignore_diff` adds every name `git check-ignore` does not ignore. Take a `.gitignore` holding `abk.local.yaml` followed by a later `!abk.local.yaml`: the previewed diff adds a line, but the write adds nothing. The person then confirms a diff that is not what gets written.
  Done when: Extract a pure function in `pipeline/file_lock.py`, for example `with_missing_lines(text, lines) -> str` returning the text with the missing lines appended. `append_missing_lines` uses it to write, and `ignore_diff` uses it to build the `after` text it diffs. The separator and line-presence rules then live in one place. Add a unit test: for the same `.gitignore`, the preview's `after` equals the file `_ignore_local_files` writes.
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/cli/config_cmd.py:41 — `_diff` in `config_cmd.py` and `_diff` in `config_migrate_write.py:37` are two new copies of the same `difflib.unified_diff` join. The only difference is the `(new file)` label.
  Consequence: The output format of the three diffs the command prints (`.gitignore`, `abk.yaml`, `abk.local.yaml`) is defined twice, so a change to one, such as the labels or the line endings, leaves the other behind.
  Done when: Keep one function, for example a public `file_diff(path, before, after, *, new=False)` in `config_migrate_write.py`. Use it in `ignore_diff`, in `_ignore_local_files` and in `cmd_migrate` for both config diffs, and delete the other copy.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/cli/config_cmd.py:54 — `_machine_request` decides whether the abk.yaml is git-tracked and finds the top level its own way: `in_repository`, then `is_tracked`, then `rev-parse --show-toplevel`. `doctor._machine_keys` (`src/agent_build_kit/cli/doctor.py:994-997`) makes the same decision differently: `--show-toplevel` with `check=False`, then `is_tracked`.
  Consequence: The doctor's warning tells the person to run `abk config --migrate`. If the two decisions ever disagree (one is edited and the other is not), the doctor warns about a key that the migration silently leaves in place, as if the file were untracked.
  Done when: Add one helper, for example `tracked_toplevel(directory, name) -> Path | None` in `pipeline/shell.py`, returning the top level when git tracks `name` in `directory` and None otherwise. Use it in both `_machine_keys` and `_machine_request`, and drop the extra `in_repository` call there.
- [1.4] tests/cli/config_migrate_machine_fakes.py:67 — `merged(base, local)` is a line-for-line copy of `tests/config_migrate_machine_support.py:25`. That module also already defines `TILDE`, which these fakes instead import from the test module `tests.test_machine_settings`.
  Consequence: Two copies of the merged-configuration oracle that the command tests and the move tests both assert against have to change together. If the merge rule changes in one copy, the other suite keeps checking the old rule.
  Done when: Delete `merged` from `config_migrate_machine_fakes.py` and import `merged` (and `TILDE`) from `tests.config_migrate_machine_support` in the fakes and in the four test files that use them.

Optional:
- [1.5] src/agent_build_kit/cli/config_cmd.py:52 — `_machine_request` returns `(request, local_text)`, but `request.local_text` already holds that text. The tuple and the `wanted if wanted else (None, None)` unpacking add surface and hide nothing.
  Consequence: The return value is wider than it needs to be and gives a second name for one value; behaviour is unaffected.
  Done when: Return `MachineRequest | None`. In `cmd_migrate`, read `local_before` from the request, or from the file directly when there is no request.
- [1.6] tests/cli/test_config_migrate_include_defaults_cmd.py:19 — Task 4.4 names a root-level `tests.e2e_schedule: off`, but the command test uses only a repo's `repos.app.tests.e2e_schedule: false`.
  Consequence: At the command level, only the repo-level form of the schedule default is shown to move. The root form is covered only by the table tests of group 1.
  Done when: Add a root `tests: e2e_schedule: off` to `DEFAULTS`, written as text so the `off` spelling survives, and assert that it moves to `abk.local.yaml`.
- [1.7] tests/cli/test_config_migrate_machine_cmd.py:49 — No test pins that the `.gitignore` diff is printed exactly once. `write_both` is called with `show_ignore_diff=False` so that it does not print the diff a second time, but the order test finds only the first occurrence with `index`.
  Consequence: If a later edit dropped `show_ignore_diff=False`, the `.gitignore` diff would print twice after the question and no test would fail.
  Done when: In the confirmed-run test, assert that `terminal.out.count(f"+++ {ignore}") == 1`.

description.summary: `abk config --migrate` now moves the machine settings of a git-tracked abk.yaml into abk.local.yaml. `--include-defaults` also moves the defaults a team may commit. The command refuses what it cannot move safely, and a second run or a dry run changes nothing.
changes: For an abk.yaml that git tracks, `abk config --migrate` moves machine settings (repo paths outside the checkout, deploy keys, the worktree root, home paths) into abk.local.yaml. A key the local file already sets is reported and left in place, so the merged configuration never changes.
`--include-defaults` also moves the settings a team may commit, keeping how they are spelled (for example `e2e_schedule: off`). After that run, `abk doctor`'s machine-keys check reports nothing.

The command prints the `.gitignore`, abk.yaml and abk.local.yaml diffs in that order and asks one question naming both files. The `.gitignore` preview is built by the same function that writes the file, so it matches what is written.

It exits with an error, naming the key and the file, for an anchor, a flow-style parent or merge key, a local file that does not parse, or a tracked abk.local.yaml. A second run or a dry run writes nothing, and it names the units that are running before it writes.

`abk doctor` and the migration now decide whether abk.yaml is tracked, and where the repository's top level is, through one shared helper (`shell.tracked_toplevel`), so the doctor's advice and what the migration does cannot drift apart.

units.title: Archived units and no-directory units move; dependency check handles archive entries and foreign merged edges
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/split/copy.py:233 — The joined check only accepts the own change of units in `units_moved_no_directory`. A moved unit whose own change moves but which has a `joined` member with no directory anywhere is selected by `plan_split` and then refused by `preflight`.
  Consequence: Take a source with active change `moves` tagged `[app]` and unit `moves/1` (repo app, merged) with `joined=(Member(change='gone', groups=(1,)),)`, where `gone` has no active directory and no archive entry. `_units` treats `gone` as absent, adds it to `moves`, and selects the unit into `units_moved_active` with no refusal. `preflight` then builds `known_changes` from moved changes, destination changes, archive names and the own `change` of units in `units_moved_no_directory`. `gone` is none of these, so it reports `unit moves/1 joined names gone` and exit is 1. The spec says each joined member's change may be 'a change the moved units carry with no directory', and the design says 'A unit with an orphan member and a moving member moves (the orphan member needs no side)'. The plan says the unit moves and the dependency check refuses it. The same happens for a unit of another repo that has a moving member and an absent joined member, and for a no-directory unit whose second joined member is also absent.
  Done when: The allowed set in the joined check holds every member change name of every moved unit that resolved as absent, not only `unit.change` of the no-directory units. The cleanest way is for the plan to carry these names, for example a `changes_no_directory` tuple filled in `_units` from `absent` for moved units, so `copy.py` does not re-derive the resolution. Add a test in `tests/split/test_dangling_archived_edges.py`: a moved unit of an active moved change with a `joined` member whose change has no directory anywhere raises no `preflight` error. The existing staying-archive-entry test must still raise its one joined error.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/split/copy.py:230 — `preflight` runs `_satisfied_history` three times: once inside `unit_records`, once directly for `unloaded`, and once inside `dropped_edges`. Each run re-reads both unit stores and `moved_records`.
  Consequence: The results cannot disagree, but every preflight reads the stores three more times and the same decision is computed in three places. One call whose result is passed on would be simpler.
  Done when: Compute `_satisfied_history` once in `preflight` and pass the dropped map to private helpers behind `unit_records` and `dropped_edges`, keeping their public signatures. Alternatively return the dropped edges and the unloaded set from one call.
- [1.3] src/agent_build_kit/split/select.py:352 — `_sides` (twice) and the existing line 216 still spell `_ARCHIVE_DATE.sub("", ...)` inline, although the change adds `archive_change_name` for exactly that.
  Consequence: The rule for naming an archive entry by its change now has a named function plus inline copies. If the rule changes, every copy has to change with it.
  Done when: Use `archive_change_name(directory.name)` in `_sides` and at line 216.

description.summary: A split now carries the units of archived changes, and units whose change has no directory, to the destination, and its dependency check understands archive entries and a merged unit of another repo.
changes: Units whose change moves as an archive entry are selected to move beside those of moved active changes. A unit whose change has no directory anywhere moves when it belongs to the repo being split.
The split plan lists the moved units by where their change lives (active, archived, no directory). It also lists the changes the moved units name that have no directory.

The preflight dependency check accepts edges to archive entries in either installation, and joined members whose change has no directory. A joined member that is a staying change or archive entry is still refused.
A merged unit of another repo that a moved unit depends on is carried as satisfied history. It is no longer reported as a dangling edge.
Archive entry names are stripped of their date prefix in one place, `archive_change_name`. The satisfied-history computation runs once per preflight.

description.summary: `abk planning split` now moves the units of a moving repo's archive entries, along with any of its units that have no change directory, and its plan says where each moved unit came from.

units.title: Merged units of kept mixed changes and other projects are dropped like foreign ones
units.feedback:
Required:
- [1.1] src/agent_build_kit/split/copy.py:330 — The `Needs:` loop turns the line into a warning whenever every unit building the named group is merged and loaded. It never asks why the named change stays, so a `Needs:` on an unreadable change becomes a warning when it should be an error.
  Consequence: The spec says the line is a warning only "when the named change stays for one of those reasons" (another repo, another project, a kept mixed change). The design says the line is a note "exactly when the unit edge it caused is a dropped edge". Take a source with an active change `broken` whose tasks.md has an unparsed `## ` heading. `plan_split` lists it in `changes_unreadable` but does not refuse it. Its unit `broken/1` is of `app` and merged. A moved `g` group 1 has `Needs: broken group 1`. Today preflight gives the warning 'its group is merged history…' and does not refuse. Yet the unit edge `g/1 depends_on broken/1` is the dangling error, because `_stays_because` returns None for it, as `test_the_unit_of_an_unreadable_change_is_the_dangling_error` pins. The two rules disagree, and a `Needs:` on a change the tool cannot classify is copied with nothing but a note.
  Done when: The note condition should also require that every builder has a reason to stay: `all(_stays_because(u, plan, _kept_changes(plan)) is not None for u in builders)`, computing `kept` once as `_satisfied_history` does. Otherwise it falls through to `_dangling(what, need.change)`. This puts both rules on the one reason test. Add a test in tests/split/test_needs_on_staying_merged_group.py. Write `broken` with the UNTAGGED-style tasks.md (an unparsed heading), a merged loaded `broken/1` of `app`, and `g` group 1 `Needs: broken group 1`. Assert preflight has an error naming `change g`, `group 1` and `broken`, and that no warning names `broken`.

Optional:
- [1.2] src/agent_build_kit/split/copy.py:311 — `covering = UnitStore(source.state_dir / "units.json").all()` is a second load of the same store that `everything` loads a few lines below (line 344). `_satisfied_history` loads it a third time, and `loaded_code.current()` is also read twice.
  Consequence: preflight now holds two copies of the source's unit list under two names, and they must be read the same way. A reader has to check they are the same thing.
  Done when: Load the source store once, before the `Needs:` loop, and use that one list both for the covering-units question and for the staying-edge check below.

description.summary: When an `abk split` moves changes, a merged unit that stays behind because it belongs to a kept mixed change or another project is now dropped from the moved units' edges, the same way a merged foreign unit already was, and a `Needs:` line on such a group is kept as a note.
changes: A moved unit's dependency on a merged unit that stays for a kept mixed change or another project is dropped as satisfied history, as an edge into a merged foreign unit already was, instead of being reported as a dangling edge.

Preflight reports a moved change's `Needs:` line on a group that stays as a warning (merged history, the line is kept but does nothing in the destination) only when every unit that builds that group is merged, has a reason to stay, and its merge has been loaded by a tick.

A `Needs:` line on a group whose merge the tick has not loaded yet is an error that says to run a tick and try again; a line on an unmerged group, or on a change the split cannot classify (for example one with an unreadable tasks.md), is the dangling error.
Preflight reads the source's unit store once and works out the kept mixed changes once, sharing them between the `Needs:` check and the staying-edge check.

New tests cover kept mixed changes and staying merged groups (tests/split/test_kept_mixed_merged_edges.py, tests/split/test_needs_on_staying_merged_group.py), including a destination that already holds the copied change.

units.feedback:

Each copy slices the `### abk planning split` section of docs/cli.md and the `## N.` runbook steps with the same regexes. The only difference is the squash function each one calls.

Its assertions could then pass or fail on the wrong section. This is a duplicate that the change introduces.
